## THE WRITER WRITES NO PARAGRAPH FOR WHITESPACE (owner-reported 11 Sep 2026, C-8)

*"When I export a redlined contract to Word there are massive blank gaps between the clauses."* The owner had already measured it: 32 paragraphs, 21 of them empty — two or three before every heading, two after, more after each clause — each costing a line plus the Normal style's 8pt after-space. The cause was never the spacing: it was the page's own code layout. The negotiation page draws the contract from template literals that put every tag on its own indented line; a browser collapses that whitespace to nothing between blocks, and `docxRunsFromHtml` did not — `_dxSpace` collapsed each gap to a single space, `push()` made that space a run, and `close()` kept any paragraph that had a run with text. Proved in isolation before a line was written: two `<p>` inside a wrapper with no whitespace exported as 2 paragraphs; the same two laid out as the paper lays them out exported as 7. **The fix is one predicate in one place** — `close()` keeps a paragraph only where a run carries a visible character, or where the paragraph is `forced`. **The owner's question was whether a blank line somebody typed survives, and the answer is yes, by construction rather than by luck**: the clause editor writes a blank line as `<p><br></p>`, and `sanitizeRich` both removes any empty block that carries no `<br>` and strips the source indentation between blocks on the way to the record — so every deliberate blank line the record can hold carries a `<br>`, a `<br>` sets `forced`, and indentation sets nothing. The one shape the fix would drop, a paragraph of nothing but spaces or tabs, is a shape the record cannot contain. The styles' `after="160"` was right and stays; it was being applied to paragraphs that should never have existed. Two lessons from writing the net: **on the parent the junk paragraphs were not run-less** — each held one space — so "empty" had to be counted as *nothing Word draws* (no visible character, no page break), not as the absence of a `<w:r>`; and the rich reader carries no `<ins>`/`<del>` into its html (tracked changes keep their own feature), so the round-trip claim on marks is made on the reader's counts and on the text reading as-if-accepted. Proved as a loop on a pretty-printed body with a title, three headings, four markers, a stepped limb, a table and three tracked runs: 34 paragraphs with 26 empty in, 8 and 0 out, and the wording, headings by level, markers with their tabs, rows and cells, and tracked counts all read back. Tests: f288 (6) — 3 fail against the parent (7, 26 of 34, 6), the tight-markup control passes both sides.

## THE MAP COPILOT GETS EVERYTHING THE MAP KNOWS (C-1, owner-reported 11 Sep 2026)

The owner typed *"cluster by expiration date"* into the Contract Graph's panel. The panel answered *"All contracts · clustered by expiration date"*, the caption switched to *Grouped by Copilot grouping*, and every node stayed on its value-stream hub. Two turns earlier *"by timeline of when they were signed"* and *"by month they were created"* had been excused with *"I don't have those dates"*. Their words: *"it gave me an answer but as you can see from the nodes, it was not correct."*

**Three faults in one journey.** The tool's `groupBy` enum named six groupings while the dropdown drew ten; the card each contract travelled as carried `id · name · counterparty · folder · kind · value · status · expiry` and no other date; and `intelGraphAsk` took whatever came back on trust — `custom` with an empty `groups` map set `intel.groups` to nothing and `groupLabelOf`'s default drew the folder. Nothing checked that a grouping placed a single contract, and the chat line was Copilot's own sentence, never a reading of what the map did.

- **ONE LIST, TWO HOSTS.** `GRAPH_GROUPINGS` carries key, label and the `none` bucket. The dropdown maps it, the caption lower-cases its label (so "customer" for counterparty is the dropdown's own word), the cue table names only keys on it, the refusal quotes it, and the server's `GRAPH_GROUP_KEYS` is a declared mirror with the enum spread from it. Three tests that pinned the literal pair `['payterms','Payment terms']` (f267), `['decision','Renewal decision']` (f293) and the `gb` map's `payterms:'payment terms'` moved for that reason and were re-pointed in place — a literal where the claim was a relation.
- **FOUR TIME GROUPINGS, ONE READING EACH.** `contractSignedAt` (the one reading of when), `effectiveExpiry`, and `repRaisedAt` — the Reports page's reading of `_raisedAt`, which rides the light list, so *created month* is honest in production too (the standing question's "check"). A missing date is "Not signed" / "No expiry set" / "No created date", never folded in. Labels stay English literals like every other bucket.
- **THE CARD CARRIES EVERY FACT THE MAP DRAWS.** `graphCopilotCard` reads `graphNodeFacts` (A-1) for overdue / off-standard / unread, `renewalDecisionDate`, `payDays`, `contractCurrency`, `negWhoseMove` (reads `c.changes` raw — READING MUST NOT WRITE), `negoIsLive`, `obState` + `obligationDue` + `obligationBlocked` for the next due, `riskScore` only where a scan exists (null is "not scanned", never zero). The same card is what `where` is applied to, so what travels and what is filtered are one reading. f299 (7) stubs every reading with a sentinel and reads it back on the card, and sweeps every name against the publish lists (both shapes — a literal and jurisdiction's named `JX_API`). Wording is never on the card and the route deletes `text/body/wording/redlineText/extractedText/html` as a difference; `value` is deleted by `scopeAiPortfolio` and again in the route for a caller without `canViewValues` (f299 (8b) posts a card WITH a value from the no-values user and reads the model's prompt).
- **FILTERS ARE FIELDS.** The tool gained `where` (status · folder · kind · counterparty · valueAbove / valueBelow · expiringWithinDays · signedFrom / signedTo · overdueObligations · offStandard · notRead · move · archived); `graphWhereClean` on the server passes only those keys, typed; `graphWhereIds` applies them over the cards; a card without a value never matches a money cut (an absence is stated). Where both `where` and `visibleIds` come back, the field filter wins and the list is intersected.
- **THE ANSWER IS WRITTEN FROM WHAT THE MAP DID.** `intelGraphApply` is the one judge. A `custom` grouping is a grouping only if it places at least one contract the book holds under at least two labels; anything else, or a key not on the list, is first read by the product's own cue table — so the owner's exact journey (the model bailing on "cluster by expiration date") now lands on the six expiry windows — and REFUSED in words only where the cue names nothing: *"I could not group by that. The map can group by value stream, customer, …"*, with the map exactly as it was (no caption flip, no lens, `intel.groups` untouched — f299 (4) snapshots the three and compares). The line is composed off `buildGraphModel()`: *"Grouped 159 contracts into 6 groups by expiry window · 14 in “No expiry set”"*, *"Showing 23 of 159 · Leases"*, the cap said (*"Copilot read the first 600 of 700 contracts"*); Copilot's sentence rides as a second line only where `graphSaysMore` (differs from the note, does not open with Grouped/Regrouped/Clustered/Showing, names a contract or runs to six words). `graphInterpret` learned the same cues, and a pure grouping ask (*"cluster by expiration date"* contains "expir") no longer also trips the expiring-soon filter.
- **THE DROPDOWN FOLLOWS THE MAP** — found by measurement in section 18b, not in the source: the Group By control is drawn by the page header and had never been told when a typed command regrouped the map, so it said "Value stream" over expiry hubs. `igPaintGroupSelect` on every rebuild; a Copilot grouping has no option and the caption is its one carrier.
- **WHAT IS ON SCREEN TRAVELS, AND THE FULL COPILOT GETS THE GRAPH'S READINGS.** `graphAskScreen()` sends grouping, lenses (label, action, count), crowded quarters, the reader's language and the workspace currency; `graphScreenSays` on the server clamps every field (f299 (9a) hands it 500-character strings). `graphCopilotContext()` joins `ctx.graph` with `streams` (graphStreamFlow — a second, NAMED reader; f294's count re-pointed), `cliff` (`graphCliffQuarters`), `facts` (per live node with something to say, capped at `GRAPH_CTX_FACTS_MAX` 200 with the omission counted) and `lenses`; `aiGraphSays` and the server's `graphSays` are twins pinned equal on one fixture (f283's rule), each capped and saying what was left out.

Tests: f299 (13 — **all thirteen fail against the parent**); insights-panels-verify section 18 (7, browser — the owner's own journey with the scripted provider answering exactly what the real model answered that day; **all seven fail against the parent, 18a reporting the value-stream hubs verbatim, and the file finishes at 77/84 rather than timing out**); f267 (14), f293, f294 re-pointed in place. The two standing questions: *created month* BUILT (`_raisedAt` rides the light list); `custom` KEPT, walled — the owner's call whether to drop it.

### The map's Copilot did its own arithmetic (owner-reported 12 Sep 2026)

*"the copilot in contract graphs gives a completely different answer from the regular copilot. And the numbers are vastly different as well."* Three screenshots: the Home tile (159 live, SEK 833.01M), the map's Copilot ("333 contracts with a combined value of approximately 1.15 billion SEK", plus a grouping nobody asked for), the main Copilot (SEK 833,005,893 across 47 signed, 33 under review, 79 in draft; 2 in KES not converted).

THE CAUSE. The main Copilot never adds: since the audit its list tool carries `valueTotalInHomeCurrency` over the whole filtered set and `valueLeftOut`, and its rulebook says quote those. The map's Copilot is a different call (`/api/ai/graph`) handed up to 600 cards, each with `value` in the contract's OWN currency, plus `graphSays`' per-stream table with `in`, `out` and `net` — three tallies of one book, and it added them (in plus out is the same money twice; a KES figure is not a SEK figure) and invented a count on the way. Nothing in that prompt carried the figure the Home tile draws.

THE FIX is one fact handed over, not a second arithmetic: `graphPortfolioFigures(ctx)` reads the rows through `copilotRows` — factored out of `copilotList` so the two readings cannot count a different book — keeps what the Home tile keeps (not archived, not Declined), converts through `fxHome`, counts what `fxMissing` leaves out, and `graphPortfolioSays` writes it into the prompt ABOVE the cards with the rule: quote these for any count or total; never add up the cards; never add the streams' in and out. Money only for a reader with canViewValues (the wall asserted both ways), the scope the reader's own (a folder-scoped member is handed their own book's count). The cards and the stream table still travel — they are what the map filters and groups by.

Not done: the map's own printed line still says only what was grouped or shown; a money question on the map is answered in the model's sentence, now from HaTi's figure. Proved: f299 (11a–c) against a live server, with a scripted provider capturing the prompt; f305, f2, f1 green.

### One Copilot, one figure (owner's go, 12 Sep 2026; WORKORDER-copilot-one-figure.md)

The morning's second pair of screenshots: the main Copilot said SEK 833,005,893 across 159 active (4 KES contracts left out); the Insights panel a minute later said 851,005,893 across 161 including the two declined (1 left out); the Home tile said 833.01M over 159. And "list all the contracts inside hati" came back as a keyword match on "want, list, inside, hati" under "the Copilot engine could not be reached", then "I wasn't able to finish that".

WHAT WAS FOUND. The Insights panel's question box already used the main brain (`intelChatAsk` → `copilotAsk`); the two answers differed because "value under management" had no definition the model could read — the system line gave counts by status, `list_portfolio` gave a converted total over whatever filter the model chose, and the Insights context added `graphSays`' per-stream in/out/net table — so the model picked a definition per answer. The listing gave up because the chat loop allowed five model turns and the list tool forty rows a page: five pages plus a turn to answer is six. The stand-in answer could not say why the engine failed, because the server's error carried no kind, and it answered a listing with a keyword search.

WHAT WAS BUILT, five phases as ordered. (1) `portfolioFigures` / `portfolioSays` (server, the graph route's figure renamed) and `aiPortfolioFigures` / `aiPortfolioSays` (browser) — one body, pinned equal on a fixture — define the term the Home tile's way and ride every brain's system block, with the rule to quote and never add. (2) A whole-book ask is a count and a door: the rule in both HOW TO WORK blocks; `wholeBook` on `deliver_answer` on both hosts, carried through `normalizeDeliver` and both final sends; `aiWorklistHtml` draws "Open the Contracts page" onto the full register, no figure on the button. (3) `AI_CHAT_STEPS` 8 on both hosts, the 40-row page untouched. (4) The server's error carries `kind` (provider on the plain chat route's 502; rateLimit on every limiter's 429; spendCap on both budget refusals; noKey on the graph route's 400), api.js carries it onto the Error, and `aiDegrade` names it; a whole-book ask under a failure gets HaTi's own live count and the Contracts door — `aiWholeBookAsk` is narrow on purpose (a word for the book AND a word for all of it). (5) f299 asserts the graph route and the chat brain read one function.

Proved: f299 (11a–d) against a live server with the prompt captured; f305 "one figure, both hosts" (five claims, the sentence equality by vm on one fixture); answer-worklist-verify 6a–c (a scripted whole-book answer draws the door and pressing it lands on the register with nothing narrowing it) and 7a–c (two scripted provider failures: the stand-in names the cause and gives the count and the door). Not built: a reference-number range filter; a table answer type in chat; the basis line under an aggregate answer (the owner's call).

## THE UPLOAD IS ITS OWN PAPER — THE HEADER BLOCK IS GONE (C-7, Young ruled 11 Sep 2026)

The brief asked for three measurements before a line was written, and a proposal to wait on: *"the block above the wording does not look like the rest of the product … measure and advise … nothing comes off that page without my word."* Filed through the product's own store, three contracts with the same wording where a like-for-like was needed: an ordinary contract with stored wording, an upload with its structure stored, and a text-only upload. **The header block** — *EXTERNAL DOCUMENT · RECEIVED · MK-U2* in mono capitals over the name in the platform's face, on its own ruled line — measured 78 px plus a 24 px margin; the first line of the same wording sat at 372 on the ordinary contract and 563 on the structured upload. What it said that the room header twelve pixels above did not: nothing. The reference and the name are the room header's; "received" is what the file strip says, with the file, who filed it, Download original and Re-read document. **Whether it travelled**: yes, both ways. `docBody` dispatches to `uploadDocBody` FIRST for anything with `source:'upload'`, and `docBody` is what a share's `viewBody` is built from where there is no stored wording — the payload of a text-only upload was measured carrying the caption, the reading caption and the strip's markup — while an upload with stored wording carries `source` and `upload` on the payload, so the counterparty's page ran `uploadDocBody` ITSELF. Two real review links were minted and opened: both pages printed our filing language, in our typeface, over their paper. The same builder feeds `exportPDF` and the phone's document. **The wording size**: the text-only branch named 13 px against the sheet's `calc(14px × --doc-scale)`. The owner said *"Go with your proposal"*, which had recommended nothing at the top of an upload (the other side's paper carries its own title; the paper head says *Between us and them* and names OUR market) and keeping the reading caption. **Built**: the block removed from `uploadDocBody` with nothing in its place; because it is the one builder, the counterparty's page, the PDF export and the phone follow with the same edit — the two links were re-minted and re-opened, the phrase gone, the wording still there; `ct_external_received` left inert in both books and swept for a CALL (the builder's own comment names it, so a bare-mention sweep would have failed on the record of the removal); `documentTextHtml` learned `size:null` — the wrapper names no pixel size and inherits the sheet's, the heading and the ruled block take ratios of it (1.07em, .89em — the +1 / −1.5 relations as fractions of 14), and every other caller keeps its pixels. Measured after: 563 → 461 and 483 → 381, exactly the block; the text-only wording 14 px against the sheet's 14. A record already sealed keeps whatever copy it froze; records sealed after the change freeze the paper without the block. The file strip stays by the owner's word. Tests: f303 (the block absent on both shapes of upload, nothing drawn in its place, the strip and caption kept, the inherited shape, the key inert and unread — the node stage supplies `ocrBannerHtml`, which that builder reads unguarded); upload-party-verify C7a–C7e (a real link opened; against the parent C7a reports the caption, C7c 13px against 14, C7d the block first in the list above the wording, C7e the phrase on their page).

## THE EXECUTED PAPER IS READ, THE HEADINGS ARE DRAWN, THE SIZES ARE MEASURED (Part D, 11 Sep 2026)

The owner sent four screenshots of the Plain English edition and then three
more of the note window and the negotiation page, and asked for a review
before any code. The review is `WORKORDER-plain-english-four-reports.md`;
this is the story behind the rules that landed.

**Image 2 — the headings.** The section titles were in the answer HaTi stored
(8 items) and the screen drew 5. `docReadAnchors` kept a section only where
the reading had a body OR the item carried a model-written `head`; the 10
Sep ruling stopped asking the model for headings and the prompt tells it to
leave a section's reading empty, so both halves were false on every section
title. The server had kept them all along — two hosts disagreeing about one
row. Young chose option A: every row that was sent draws its heading, a
clause the model had nothing to say about included; the server's own drop of
an empty clause row went with it.

**Image 3 — "executed contracts come back with no reading".** Three faults on
one page, each measured on an executed template contract staged in a real
browser. Every clause of template paper is an `<h4>` over a `<p>`, so the walk
called every one a SECTION and the prompt told the model, in capitals, that a
SECTION reads EMPTY. The last clause's range ran to the end of the canvas
because a sealed record's signature card is `.seal-in`, not `.rl-paper-foot`:
743 characters ending "IPRS identity and CAK-accredited PKI are on the
roadmap" were sent as clause 4, e-mail addresses included, and image 4's own
reading printed them back. And when eight of eight echoes failed the route
only counted, so nobody could read why; the leading hypothesis — the doc line
read `[R0] SECTION 1. Purpose` while the prompt said "copied exactly as it was
given after the key", so a literal model echoed the label — is now tolerated
on both sides of the comparison, and every refusal is named on the record and
in the log so the next one can be read rather than guessed.

**Image 4 — the sizes.** A contract sealed before the 22 Aug size sweep carries
`text-[13.5px]` on its paragraphs and the compiled blob resolves that to a
flat 15px: at the 10 setting the sheet went to 9.34px, the sealed paragraph
stayed at 15, and the edition — which measures the SHEET — followed the sheet.
The fix is a screen rule in HaTi's own sheet scoped to the Document tab's
paper; the sealed markup, the hash, the export and the counterparty copy do
not move. The edition's headings were typed ratios (1.13em, 1em) against a
paper whose headings are 1.16, 1.04 and 1.05em; each entry now measures the
heading it faces, the way the body and the face already were. And one press on
the size control repaints both columns in the same frame, rather than waiting
for the canvas to change height.

**Image 1 — the wrap.** `text-wrap:balance` evened a wrapped title's lines by
breaking the first one early. Off. The two lines sitting on each other in the
owner's screenshot did not reproduce on the h3 shape staged here (17h measures
no overlap and every heading above its reading); it is said in the run log
and not called fixed.

**The note window (D-5, D-6).** Two lead sentences of different lengths made
the window jump on the room press; the lead now reserves one line and the six
sentences are written to fit it in both books, and the window's height is
measured equal across the rooms. Young then ruled Internal first — reversing
the 1 Sep ruling and C-3's default from the same morning, and both are written
beside the reading — and asked for a note per room in one window: a draft per
room, a dot on the other tab while it holds words, Add note posting each to
its own room through the one writer, Skip asking where either holds words.

**The change bars (D-7).** "Just like Microsoft Word": `right:-18px` became
`left:-18px` on the clause rule and its front-matter twin, one stylesheet
reaching the negotiation page, the clause editor, the counterparty's page and
the phone; redline-verify and parity-verify pin the relation — inside the
sheet, left of the wording — never a pixel.

**Already red at the parent, proved in a worktree-equivalent stash run:**
clause-door-verify 16d4/16d5, paper-grows-verify 5d/6, settled-ask-reopen-verify
"the adopted change has no card"; plain-english-verify 6c, which C-7 left red
by taking the upload's one painted h-tag, re-pointed to `painted <= 1`.


## NOTES ARE ONE SYSTEM — THREE DOORS, ONE DRAWER, AND THE THREAD GOES OUT TO WORD (Young asked 11 Sep 2026)

THE OWNER'S WORDS, in the afternoon of 11 Sep 2026, off the clause editor with a passage held in Copilot's rail and the Document tab's highlight menu:

> *"I need to reconcile something with your help. This is mostly related to the notes. I need your solution in how we can implement the comments ecosystem to be one. Maybe whenever you want to comment, the comments / chat slide panel slides in and you comment there instead. This for both commenting when you highlight a contract sentence and you want to comment or when you click on a pencil indicating you have finished you redlining. Currently when you highlight a sentence, it takes you to the copilot to redline ... Maybe it should be that when you highlight, you get a pop ... but you only have ask copilot and comment. If you choose ask copilot it brings you to copilot as it does today, if you choose comment, you are brought to the sliding comments / chat panel and you enter your comments there tagged to the CHG number. I want to go even further, the comments that are related to a CHG number can then be also exported to microsoft word document."*

And, off the design page: *"lets make sure when we implement it is clear that we also add the ability to reply to a comment vs just entering a comment which would be a different step. All comments to be time stamped as well."* And on the Document tab: *"you cannot ask copilot or comment whilst in the document page."*

WHAT STOOD BEFORE: three places a note could be written — the drawer (two rooms), the receipt window that came up after every filing (built 31 Aug, given two rooms and two drafts the same morning, D-5/D-6), and the card body's own composer — and no way at all to say something about words nobody had touched. The counterparty's notes sat on their card. The Word export carried redlines and no comments; the import read comments and pinned them to a clause by guessing the wording.

WHAT WAS BUILT, and the rulings inside it:
- THE MODEL grew four optional fields on a message (id, anchor, replyTo, done) and three readings (home, anchor state, threads) plus one writer (done). No migration: absent on every note on file. The home of an anchored note is a READING, so a note on words that a later change covers is drawn under that CHG without being moved.
- THE DRAWER took the window's job. Every ruling the window had survives on the pin: Internal lit at rest (D-6), a draft per room, Skip asks over a draft, the lead says "revised" where the fold happened. The design page had recommended External after a filing; the owner's explicit D-6 ruling ("always start with internal") was kept instead and said so in the summary.
- REPLY is a box under the note it answers with its own Send reply; the foot box never replies. DONE folds; the marker leaves the paper. The clock prints the day and the time on every row; the day goes through langLocale (the month follows the language rule).
- THE PAPER offers Ask Copilot · Comment on the negotiation page and in the clause editor; the Document tab was left untouched (the owner's sentence was a ruling that the Document tab offers neither; its existing Simplify / Ask Copilot menu was neither widened nor removed — reported, not fixed). In the clause editor a drag used to attach the passage to Copilot's rail by itself; it offers first now, which costs one press on the Copilot path and buys the comment door. f245's three attach claims were re-pointed.
- THEIR PAGE gained a notes aside of its own (the alerts panel's shape) drawing the same Chat panel with one room, a Notes row in More, Comment on highlight, and their channel post carries the note's meta. Their card composer was NOT retired (their seat's byte-identical rule; a follow-up).
- WORD: comments.xml and commentsExtended.xml are written only where there is a comment (the no-comment file is byte-identical, pinned); a note on a change sits on the change's inserted words (else struck words) with the CHG first; replies thread through paraIdParent; done is w15:done. The reader (docxComments) reads them back — proved in-process, and the import honours the CHG prefix before guessing by wording. No export dialog was added (cheapest channel: the toast counts the comments).
- THE SERVER: a `meta` JSON column on share_messages behind an allow-list; both post routes take it; two PATCH routes set done. `now()`/rlShare/scope as their neighbours.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the Document tab's highlight menu (untouched, see above); the counterparty's card composer (kept); an export dialog with a tick (the toast counts instead); Done on a channel-only note in local mode (says it cannot); marker placement inside the typing box (marker only, no wash — the wash could reach the record on the next pull).

Tests: f303 (38 claims across model, channel, drawer, doors, marks, Word, server), f302 rewritten against the drawer, f264 (4)(5) re-pointed, f266 caller count re-pointed, f245 attach claims re-pointed, clause-editor-verify 25 re-driven against the drawer, window-drag-verify 5 re-pointed, clause-door-verify helper re-pointed.

## COMMENTS, ROUND TWO — THREE VERBS, A PLAINER PIN, A MARKER THAT CLOSES (Young, 11 Sep 2026, evening)

The comments system went to main in the afternoon (NOTES ARE ONE SYSTEM). The owner used it for an hour and sent eleven reports with screenshots, then answered three questions and said "go, build all of them and merge to main. Do not build the multi party signing yet." WORKORDER-comments-round-two.md carries the reports verbatim.

**What was measured before a line moved.** The marker's number was inside its disc on the negotiation paper and OUTSIDE it in the clause editor: the rule set `font:var(--w-title) 10px/16px var(--n-font-ui)`, and a shorthand whose token cannot resolve is discarded whole at computed-value time, so every longhand inherited the paper's 15px/1.75 — a 26px line in an 18px disc. The editor's paper sits under no element defining `--n-font-ui`. Longhands with fallbacks now. The ruby bar the owner saw on a clause they had only opened was the editor's own live seam: `redlineDocHtml` drew the live clause `is-changed` unconditionally ("there is a draft on it"), and a draft equal to what stands is not a change. Leaving the editor filed nothing (measured on two clauses, typing on and off). The paper DID offer the menu on a two-paragraph selection; the silence the owner met was a real drag released a pixel past the last line, on the clause's pencil — a button, which the mouse-up filter read as a press on a control. In the EDITOR the refusal was real: the 31 Aug rule refused any selection across two sub-paragraphs.

**The three verbs.** Ask Copilot had been the editing path. Now: Ask is a question (the prompt asks for an explanation and no wording; the chips are questions; no cut; no Apply drawn anywhere; nothing recorded as proposed), Edit with Copilot is the old rail, Comment is the drawer. The owner's "Yes" to "may a question become an edit": the answer card carries Edit with this, which re-attaches the same words under the edit verb and, where the model volunteered wording with its answer, turns it into a card with Apply — recorded as proposed only then, because only then is it offered. On the paper both Copilot verbs land in the editor through its one door, the verb riding as `passageMode`.

**Several sub-paragraphs.** The draft carries a list's numbers as text ("2. Termination…") where the typing box draws them as list styling, so the second line never began with the selection's second part. The reading finds the run by tails and heads (a middle line ends with its part; the last part sits within a marker's width of its line's start) and carries the passage in the draft's own form — what the one replacement finds verbatim. The held mark is one span per text piece (one span round a range across two blocks throws, and extract-and-reinsert would pull the second paragraph's words into the first), and the selection is put back over the pieces, because splitting the nodes it sat in collapsed it (clause-editor-verify 21d caught that on the first run).

**The pin.** Two words, the tabs' own; no caption; Add note spends it, and a draft in the other room goes to its own room in the same breath rather than flipping the pin and waiting (the retired window's own behaviour, which the drawer had lost). A quote keeps its paragraph breaks through one reading; every word-finder joins with `\s*` because two paragraphs' text nodes touch with no space between.

**The rule the owner asked for.** "If you click an area that makes a panel appear, then the same location should also be able to collapse the appearance." The bell, Activity and Chat already did; the marker was written to open only (`force`), the card's row too, and their page's door. The marker keeps its own key (`_rlNpOpenKey`) because the focus key is spent by the paint that lands on the note.

Deliberately left: the Document tab's own highlight menu; their page's card composer; the Word export's choice of which comments travel; a Word range across paragraphs (Word opens and closes a range inside one paragraph here, so it goes on the quote's longest line and the comment carries the whole quote).

## COMMENTS, ROUND THREE — EVERY HIGHLIGHT OFFERS, THE PIN IS ONE SHAPE, THE NEGOTIATE PAGE BLURS (Young, 11 Sep 2026, late)

Minutes after round two went to main the owner sent seven more reports, then an eighth, an answer on the blur, and the principle that governs all of it: *"there should be a liberal approach to highlighting anywhere [in] a clause to have the dropdown with three options. Clicking a pencil should be minimal as possible and mostly when you really want to do manual typing / editing of a clause."* And a standing instruction: *"Ask how SAP would approach these issues when you are building them because in some cases they are nonsensical especially since I did not ask for those particular changes."* WORKORDER-comments-round-three.md carries the reports verbatim.

**What was asked of each item before it was built (the six questions, and SAP's shape).**
- *The filed pin.* Round two drew "CHG-006 filed · add a note" beside Skip over an empty body — a sentence about the reader's own act, which the rulebook already says is never a band. The general practice is one card shape wherever it is drawn: the pin is reference · the quoted wording · the switch, and a FILED pin quotes what the change proposes (`rlNpChangeQuote`, off the change's own body through the one wording builder). Nothing was added that the report did not ask for.
- *Equal halves.* A segmented control's halves size to the control, not the word: `inline-grid` with `grid-auto-columns:1fr`; measured equal at 153px each whichever half is lit.
- *The blur.* This reverses the 27 Aug ruling ("do not shade the contract, it has to remain active") for the negotiation page alone. SAP's distinction was put to the owner: a panel that needs the page dimmed is a modal task, a docked panel does not; the owner chose a SLIGHT blur that leaves the wording readable and a press on the blurred page that closes the drawer. Built as a class on the existing scrim (`is-blur`: transparent, 1.5px backdrop blur), asked of one function `notesBlurs()` so the clause editor — which covers the page — and every other page keep the old ruling. Measured: computed `blur(1.5px)`, transparent background.
- *Apply ends typing.* Measured which Apply the owner pressed: a passage card, whose `ceReplacePassage` held `keepView:true` by design (30 Aug, so the reader's next sentence costs one press). The reader's own typing still keeps the view; a card's Apply passes `keepView:false` and the clause drops out of typing showing its marks — the playbook standard's own behaviour.
- *No reading list under a question.* The three rows (playbook · precedent · wording) answer "what does this wording rest on", which matters where wording is about to move; under a question the answer alone is the answer. `read: []` under the ask verb.
- *The editor's paper offers on every clause.* `ceSelectionRead` answered only for the typing box; a drag over any other clause on the editor's canvas drew nothing. The negotiation page's reading was made the one reading — `rlPaperOfferFromRange` — and the editor's mouse-up hands a range outside the box to it, with Ask/Edit re-opening the page on THAT clause with the words in hand. While pinning this in the browser, the drag from the recital into clause 1 exposed a second thing: a highlight with words in one clause is not that clause's OWN words, and Edit would have opened the editor on words the box could not find; Edit is offered only where the whole highlight is one clause's share.

**One edge named to the owner, not built:** Edit with Copilot across two clauses or in the front matter. The editor opens on one clause; a highlight wider than that offers Ask Copilot and Comment. The clause editor does not blur behind the drawer (the owner said "the negotiate page"; the editor covers it).

**Measured before it moved, learned on the way:** `.nego-scroll` glides — a bare `scrollTop` assignment animates, so a probe that scrolls and measures in one breath measures the old place (H3 sat under the editor's foot bar on two runs). jsdom's Ranges have no rectangle; the offer refuses a highlight it cannot place, so the unit net stubs one as F96 always has.

Tests: f304 (8)(9), round-two-comments-verify H1–H5; f245, f302, f303, F96 (B3)(B8)(B8b), clause-editor-verify 25c re-pointed.

## COMMENTS, ROUND FOUR — REPLY ON ANY NOTE, DELETE BESIDE DONE, THE MARKS AT ONCE, THE BLUR OFF (Young, 11 Sep 2026, late night)

Two reports after round three, then five, then a correction, then an eighth; then "Start from the latest main. Fix all of them in an autonomous overnight work session." The owner went to bed with three choices open and the work order's proposals stood in for their answers: the blur goes AND the outside-press close goes with it (the 27 Aug shape); a root with replies is not deleted and an admin is not widened; a Copilot card's Apply still files nothing and the note comes at Save, with the Save control saying so.

**Measured before it moved.** The marker did not appear late by accident: posting a note repainted the DRAWER and the paper caught up on its next paint for some other reason (a probe, a refresh). The negotiation page, the clause editor and their page each paint their marks after their own canvas paints; none of them was told a note had been posted. One function now repaints every mounted canvas at the post and at every act. The marker press opened the drawer on the room it last showed; a note in the other room was listed nowhere, so the focus key found nothing and the reader stayed on the wrong tab — the room is read off the note before the paint. Suggest deleting "did nothing" because the refusal written for "you have struck the whole clause" fired on a whole PARAGRAPH: the line emptied, the clause had eight other lines, and the sentence went into a span the reader was not looking at. Only an empty clause is refused now. On the way: cutting the START of a paragraph leaves a lowercase remainder that the text-to-rich lift re-flows into the paragraph above — logged, not fixed.

**Reply on any note.** A thread stays FLAT (Word's and Google Docs' shape): the button on every note carries the root's key and its own, the box draws under the note pressed, the answer joins the root. Done stays on the root because it settles the thread. **Delete** is the one act that had a model and no door; it gained a null home (the contract's own thread) and a wall against a root with replies, and the drawer draws it on the reader's own notes only, greyed with the reason where the model would refuse. **The caret** reverses round two's rule in the other direction for the third time this fortnight: the held mark keeps the sentence on the paper, so the selection has nothing left to protect, and the owner wants to type at once. Four browser checks that pinned "attaching never takes the caret" were re-pointed; `ceHeldPassage()` is what the rail reads.

Tests: f304 (10) (seven claims), round-two-comments-verify I1–I6 (a real drag, Comment, Add note, the marker within 60 ms; a marker press landing in the external room lit; Reply on a reply; Delete with the marker going; the whole-paragraph cut; the Save hover), and the re-points named in the rulebook.

### The morning after (Young, 12 Sep 2026: "A lot is wrong")

Three reports off the first morning with round four, with two screenshots.

**"Edit with Copilot is now missing the feature with apply."** MEASURED with a real mouse: after the pick the rail held the words at mouse-up and had lost them 300 ms later; the answer came back as *Suggested wording* for the whole clause. The cause was two rules meeting: the selection menu picks on MOUSEDOWN (it always has — a click would collapse the selection first) and is gone by the mouse-up, which therefore lands on the paper underneath, inside `#ce-doc`; the paper's mouse-up handler reads the selection a tick later — and round four's `ceFocusAsk` had just moved the caret into the ask box, so it found nothing, no refusal reason, and cleared the passage (the "a plain click lets go" branch). Before round four the caret stayed on the paper and `ceMarkHeld` put the selection back, so the deferred read found the words and did no harm. The fix is at the cause: the pick stamps a time (`_ceMenuPickAt`) and a mouse-up inside `CE_MENU_PICK_MS` (600) ends that press, not a drag. A TIME rather than a flag, because a pick made by keyboard has no mouse-up to consume the flag and would have swallowed the next real drag. The first fix stamped the editor's OWN menu only, and the owner's second report the same morning ("when i click the pencil then highlight, it appears; if i simply highlight without clicking on the pencil first, it flashes and disappears") named the two other doors: the paper's offer inside the editor (`ceOfferOnPaper`, which on another clause re-mounts the page and attaches a tick later) and the NEGOTIATE PAGE's own highlight, which opens the editor with the words and attaches on a timer — so the mouse-up landed on the new paper BEFORE the attach and its deferred read cleared what the attach then held. One stamp (`ceStampPick`) at the one attach and at all three doors; the negotiate-page case measured with a real mouse: held at 150 ms and at 850 ms, lost at the parent. Not chosen: "never clear a held passage on a bare click" — that branch is the reader's own way of letting go and is asserted as such.

**"When I click reply it now brings up a pop-up when it should simply reply."** Round four routed a reply through `rlNotesSend`, whose confirm sits on the CROSSING (`ext && !pin`), so a reply under an external note asked "Send this to …?". A reply's room is the thread's own, chosen by pressing Reply under a note already sitting in that room with the other side named on the tab — the pin's reasoning exactly. `!reply` joins the guard; the new-note box still asks.

**"The delete button is not working."** The owner's note had already gone to the other side (an external note posts on a standing link the moment it is added), so the model refused and the button was drawn `disabled` with the reason on its hover — and NOTHING DRESSED IT: `.rl-np-act-b` had a `.g` shade and no `:disabled` rule, so a refused Delete looked exactly like a live one and did nothing when pressed. One rule in HaTi's sheet (`opacity:.45; cursor:not-allowed`). Delete on an undelivered note, on a reply, and on a root once its replies are gone was measured working; a root with replies greys with its own reason.

Proved: f304 (11–13); round-two-comments-verify J1–J3 with a real mouse (J1a/J1b red against the parent, 34/36); clause-editor-verify 257/257, notes-two-rooms-verify 73/73; the eight round-four items re-run green (I1–I6).

## THE COPILOT AUDIT — HONEST NUMBERS, REACH, PARITY, THE BLIND SPOTS (owner's order, 11 Sep 2026)

The owner measured Copilot against the code and wrote an eight-phase order (WORKORDER-copilot-audit.md, verbatim). What was found and what was done, phase by phase:

1. **Currency.** Both tool loops handed the model `value: Number(c.value)` with no code and no conversion while every screen converts through fxHome; the model added kronor to euros and printed the workspace code over the sum (918M against 833M, twice). Now every row carries its code, its converted figure and "no rate" as a fact; the list carries a converted total over the whole filtered set and what it left out, so the model never adds. The money wall was widened to every new key and asserted off a restricted member in both directions. The browser snapshot disagreed with itself (headline converted, streams raw) — the model had reported exactly that; the stream half converts now and names what it left out per stream.
2. **Archived** was on Copilot's list and in its workspace line while off every screen; off by default now, `archived:true` includes it.
3. **The id is a counter.** One line in both stable blocks.
4. **The graph's filter.** The fourteen-key `where` existed for the graph route only, applied in the browser over its cards. The predicate was lifted into `js/graphwhere.js` — the graph view asks it, the server asks it over its own reading of the record (`copilotCardOf`: whose move from the negotiation record, the signed day, overdue from the obligations' dates, off-standard from the stored review, read from the briefs table). The key LIST stays declared where each host declared it (f299 pins the set; f232 refuses a module declaring a name another publishes), so the shared file takes the list as an argument. On every script list the rulebook names.
5. **Paging.** `offset`; the cap stays.
6. **Search.** Scope was applied after taking `limit*2` rows, so a scoped reader silently got fewer; now the FTS query is paged with scope on every page, the limit is bounded, and the true in-scope count is stated. The conversation window went from eight to fourteen turns: two more rounds of question-and-answer, on a cached rulebook block, without paying for every earlier turn on every question — flagged to the owner as the judgement it is.
7. **Parity.** The browser lacked check_against_playbook and its system prompt disowned the check. It reads the stored review first and runs the product's rule-based review where none exists; the two tool-name sets are pinned equal.
8. **The blind spots.** get_obligations and get_contract_history on both hosts, every reading borrowed, folder scope through the one door, money walled (a trail line about money is dropped whole and counted for a no-values reader — coarse on purpose), pinned as writing nothing (the record byte-identical after both calls), never on the counterparty's page.

Tests: f305 (33 claims). Walls kept: no writing tool, no scope widened, fxHome/fxMissing/contractCurrency untouched, no screen changed, the named caps untouched.


## THE BUILD PLAN — GROUPS 1 TO 5 (13 Sep 2026)

The owner asked, on 13 September, for the whole HaTi Build Plan artifact to be
implemented, then narrowed it: *"continue building but do not build step 6"*.
Groups 1 to 5 were built in the plan's own order, one commit each, on a branch
started from the latest main.

**Why the order was cheapest-first.** Group 1 is three changes that need
nothing underneath them — no new store, no spend, no decision from the owner.
Group 2 is the send, which the owner had just redesigned with the Word channel
on it. Group 3 is the biggest coherent piece and rests on group 3's own phase 1
(the review's memory of what it read). Group 4 is the half that makes group 3
cheap to run. Group 5 is two items each with something new underneath.

**Three departures from the plan, each toward one of its own rules, each said
out loud rather than done quietly:**

1. *The round summary spends nothing.* The plan offered one Copilot call per
   round, cached on it. Writing the sentence out showed that every part of the
   worked example — what they accepted, what they refused, which clauses they
   countered, and even "start with clause 4" — is already on the record. A
   deterministic reading gives the whole sentence for nothing, and what a model
   could add on top is a judgement, which is a separate decision to take with
   its cost in view.

2. *The round summary adds no band.* The plan's picture put the line at the
   head of the change column. That is a new strip, and the owner's own rule
   makes a strip theirs to approve. The cheapest channel that carries the fact
   is the alert row that already says the round arrived, so the line rides
   there as a second line and nothing on any page grew.

3. *The template obligations refuse rather than guess.* Phase 7 asks for a
   hand-written table of what each built-in template promises. Reading the
   templates' own clauses showed their payment and rejection windows are
   counted from events HaTi holds no date for ("within 30 days of receipt",
   "within 3 days of delivery"). A single due date for those would be a date
   the product invented. So the table takes its first date from the contract's
   own start date and recurs, and a contract with no start date gets nothing.

**Two pieces were not built and are named as such**: the one-time code before a
guest's first Send (group 5.2) and the template baseline read once per version
(Part B phase 6). The guest code was stopped deliberately: the existing code
component is written into the signing screen, and shipping the server wall
without a prompt on the counterparty's workbench would have produced a refusal
with no way forward on the same screen — which is the one thing this codebase's
rules forbid above almost everything else.

**The server's half of the signing gate enforces two of three questions.** The
third — has the wording moved since the obligations were read — rests on
simhash64, which lives in the browser. A second implementation on the server
would have to agree byte for byte or it would answer "unread" for ever, and a
hash that drifts on that side refuses real signatures. So the card reports all
three and the wall enforces two, and the code says so in the place somebody
would otherwise discover it.

**What was re-pointed rather than deleted.** f180's claim that the counterparty
is told their answer has not travelled is unchanged; it is asked of the control
that carries the count now instead of the wall line that was printing it twice.
f42 and f45 described the send as two steps with a Next between them; their
real claims — you are shown what is going out before you send, and both routes
show the same manifest — are asked of the one screen.

## THE POP-UP DIET (13 Sep 2026)

The owner, with the send pop-up on screen: *"the pop ups have too many words
which are unnecessary and makes the card overwhelming. In artifact format,
review all the pops ups that have too many words and propose a current vs
proposed solution with an aim of keeping them clean or stripping them to just
the buttons and entry fields."* Then, on the first proposal: *"I did not want
to strip all the words but strip the unnecessary wording. Also update the
artifact and show real renders of how they appear in the platform of before
and proposed."* Then: *"Build all 26 as shown."*

**How it was measured.** A probe opened forty pop-ups on a real contract with
one change filed (thirty-five opened; the note window is a drawer now, the
signing window refused on a fixture with an approval outstanding, and the
playbook and webhook editors open only from inside Settings). Every word on
each face was counted — titles, sentences, labels and buttons — and each was
photographed. Twenty-six carried more words than they needed: 2,626 between
them. For the proposal, the new wording was placed into the same pop-up
INSIDE the real product by editing the DOM and photographed again, so the
"proposed" pictures were real renders in HaTi's own fonts and boxes, not
drawings. The owner approved every one.

**The rule that decided each sentence.** Anything a control already says goes
("Send for review" needs no sentence saying what a review is; a box with a
placeholder needs no "start typing" hint). How the machinery works goes —
fingerprints, versions, what the register reads — to the hover where somebody
might want it. One line that tells a first-timer what happens next stays
("Copilot picks the template that fits and fills in what you say"). A cost
stays, next to the button ("Saving here converts the document to plain text";
"the signature already given is discarded"). What the other side sees stays,
in one line ("Nothing can be signed on this link"; "Nandi Dairy sees one
name"). A hint arrives when it is needed: "a .doc must be re-saved" is said to
the person who drops a .doc, as the refusal, which the product already did.

**The send pop-up changed shape as well as words.** The build of 13 Sep had
joined the two old screens and hidden Next, so the reading order was the old
order concatenated and the dialog scrolled. The owner's approved drawing is
the order now: what travels first (the round line, the folded list, "Send
something else"), then what this round is for with ONE line under the chosen
answer, then the channel, then name and email, then the note, then the
warnings folded to a count, then the email-off line, then the link settings,
then Send — 724px against 1,254px on the same fixture. Two note boxes ("A note
to Nandi Dairy" on step 1 and "Personal message" on step 2, joined into one
message before they travelled) became one, under the recipient, keeping the
id `sh-summary` so every reader of it is unchanged. The sentence saying where
the address came from is gone; the SOURCE survives as `data-prefill-src` on
the email box because a test and a reader both have a right to it. The line
under the channel row and the line under the note box print only where the
channel costs something (a file has no page; a copied link mails nothing) —
"this note is sent in the email" under an email form was the control printed
twice. The "worth checking" strip folds to a count, but a BLOCK never folds:
it carries the tick that lets the send through, and a tick behind a fold is a
tick nobody sees. The email-off strip was four lines saying what else could
not be delivered on this workspace, which is the mail panel's job; it is one
line with the way forward now.

**Retiring a sentence means not calling it.** Every key whose sentence left
the face stays in both dictionaries, inert — the standing rule for keys — and
f310 (2) is the sweep: a builder that calls one of them again fails. Where a
sentence was shortened rather than dropped, the key's text changed in place in
BOTH books, so a Swedish reader gets the same diet.

## ONE LIST BEFORE THE SIGNATURE (Young's "go" on the signing audit, 13 Sep 2026)

The owner's report, with the page in front of him: *"So many layers of poor
flow prior to signing. First I am allowed to sign the contract without
resolving the fact that I need to resolve that accept the highlighted issues
first. Then at some stage I had a sign in red saying that I have 2 high
severity issues that prevented me from signing but the writing was not a link
where I needed to go to resolve the issues. Think best in class and give me a
seamless flow that also steers you towards what needs resolving."*

THE AUDIT (the artifact "Signing, audited") measured, on one real contract:
five different counts for "what stands before signing" on one visit (the
Checks card, the risk row, the check tiles, the red line, the gate's refusal);
the button leading with "tick intent to sign first" while an escalated
departure from standards was not on it at all; the red risk line and the gate
refusal printed as sentences with nowhere to press; the gate OFF by default so
the pad opened over four open findings; ESCALATE offering "Accept with a
reason" to the very person about to sign; the column upside down (obstacle
at the top, act at the bottom, the tick-box under the block); the head and
Home saying nothing about how much stood in the way. The owner said "go" and
took the defaults as written: escalations cleared by the colleague asked or
an admin; escalations, approvals, whose turn, blanks and unnamed signers hold;
departures and risk findings shown and acceptable with a reason; the intent
statement moved into the signature pad.

WHAT WAS BUILT, six pieces, one idea each:
1. `signReadiness(c)` — the one reading. It composes the rows `signBlockers`
   already carried (each holds), the check's own rows itemised
   (`signCheckRows`, each holding or shown by the gate), and the risk scan's
   open HIGH findings (shown, never holding). `opts.light` leaves the two
   hash-based rows out on a register row, because HEAVY strips the wording
   they hash and a guessed answer would be wrong on Home and the bell.
   READING MUST NOT WRITE: `signBlockers` reached negoSigningBlockers →
   negoAlignment → negoInit and CREATED a negotiation on every paint of the
   Signing tab (found by f308's byte-identical claim the moment the card read
   the list); it asks only where a table exists.
2. Rows are doors. The four tiles went; the card draws the rows in weight
   order (escalations first, then holds, then noted, then settled folded
   under their count). The `[data-sc-fix]` door had handed the FIELD NAME to
   focusKeyTerms, which takes the contract — dead on every press, found by
   reading it. "Read it" is `scanGoTo`, lifted out of the scan card's handler
   so both press one door. "Dismiss with a reason" writes the scan's own
   store with the reason it never asked for. "Take the paper's value" writes
   exactly where the Key terms editor writes (`c.value`, `fields.effDate`,
   `c.expiry`, `c.counterparty`).
3. Escalate means somebody else. `v.escalation` is the ask; `v.accepted`
   carries `byId` and `role`; `signCheckMayAccept` (who may, asked of the
   viewer) and `signCheckAcceptedProperly` (was it, asked of the STAMP) are
   the two readings, and the server's `scAcceptedProperly` mirrors the
   second and looks the role up on the users table by the stamped id. An
   escalated finding accepted by the wrong person is drawn as OPEN with the
   reason. The colleague is told through `POST /api/contracts/:id/escalate`
   — the mention route's own rule (ids in, addresses refused, scope checked)
   with a link onto the Signing tab. Ask a colleague leads every escalated
   row, an admin's included: an admin may decide it alone and may also hand
   it to whoever owns the standard.
4. The gate defaults to ADVISE. `signCheckRowHolds` is the one rule (off →
   nothing; advise → escalated standards rows; require → every open row) and
   the server reads the same three at both doors on every gate but off. The
   settings panel's three descriptions were rewritten in both books.
5. The column reads list → order → block → Sign; the tick-box left the page.
   `openSignaturePad({intent:true})` draws "I intend to sign electronically"
   with the statute line as the pad's first line and refuses Adopt & sign
   without it, flashing the row; the answer rides the result as `consent`
   and `signConsentStamp` writes the record and the same Consent audit line
   the box wrote. The counterparty's pad (portal.js) does not ask — their
   consent is their own page's.
6. Upstream. The button reads "Sign — N to settle" and is LIVE: the press is
   `signLandOnList`, onto the first held row, lit. "Sign — N noted" names the
   rows on the hover. The head's Sign says "Sign · N to settle" and its press
   lands on the list while anything holds ('sign-scroll' retired — it pointed
   at a box that no longer exists); `signPaintHeadLabel` re-words the head
   after every act, because the head is built once per render and a tab
   change never redraws it (measured: the head still said "1 to settle" after
   the admin's acceptance until this was added). The bell's signature row
   gains a sub-line and Home's "Needs your decision" a row, both quoting N.

MEASURED in signing-flow-verify with real presses (17 claims): the button
reads "Sign — 1 to settle" live; the escalated row leads and offers Ask a
colleague; the held press lands on the row and lights it; the dialog picks a
real colleague and the stamp lands; the server refuses a signature over the
open escalation; an admin's acceptance turns the button to "Sign — 1 noted"
and the head to "Sign"; the pad refuses Adopt & sign without the tick; with
it the signature lands and consent is on the record and the trail.

Tests: f311 (28 claims, 27 red at the parent), signing-flow-verify; f308 (3)
and (5), f256 (4), f167, sign-links-verify section 5 re-pointed in place.

## THE SEND OPENS ON THE SEND, AND THE RECORD IS ITS OWN LINK (Young reported it 13 Sep 2026)

Three screenshots, the day the one-screen send shipped: *"image 1, when I ask to send negotiation history i get the contract instead. When i click the share button, image 2 flashes quickly before image 3 appears."* Image 1 was the history screen leading with WHO SIGNS and a link bound to Juno Limited; image 2 was "What are you sharing?" for a fraction of a second; image 3 the send.

**THE FLASH.** The dialog "arrives once" (f178, 22 Aug): the first frame is painted before the share list is fetched, and until 13 Sep the first frame WAS the kind question, because that was the first step. The one-screen send made that question a door (`#share-other`) and folded it with `step(1)` — after the fill. So the opening frame still drew the question, live and pressable, and was swapped for a screen of a different shape when the fetch landed. The fix is one builder: `oneScreenHtml(pre, o)` is defined inside `openShareModal` before anything is fetched and draws both paints — the opening with empty boxes and a greyed Send, the settled one with the prefill. The kind step takes `{hidden}` so it is folded in the markup, never by the wiring. Two things were found on the way: the fill keeps the frame the opening made, so the 46rem width passed to `shareFillModal` (which takes one argument) had been silently ignored since 22 Aug — the dialog was 32rem wide — and is now the opening's; and the send form was drawn `hidden` for `step(1)` to reveal, which the first frame could not do (measured: `form:false` in the first frame), so it is drawn open. `shareWireOpening` holds a purpose press (repainting the row in place), the quiet door (folding the screens as the settled wiring would) and the kind cards; what was typed into the first frame wins over the prefill — the prefill is HaTi's guess, and a typed name is the answer. Measured with the fetch held 700ms: first frame `send:true form:true kind:false email:true other:true sendDisabled:true width:736`, settled identical but for Send live and the name kept.

**THE SIGNER CARD.** `#share-signers` was hidden at the draw for any purpose but Sign, and the purpose painter toggled it — but `setKind` (the kind switch) never did. A contract whose default purpose was Sign therefore kept WHO SIGNS on the history screen. `setKind` now hides it on the record and restores the purpose's answer on the contract.

**THE LINK.** "I get the contract instead" was the reuse rule: a durable send to an address that already held a standing link REFRESHED that link (`PUT /api/shares/:token/payload`) rather than minting a second — right for a round, and wrong here, because the server serves a link by the ROW's purpose and the PUT never touched it. A history send to Juno Limited's address wrote a `purpose:'history'` payload onto a `negotiate` row, and the recipient opened the contract. The dialog now never reuses for the record (`payloadObj.purpose!=='history'`) — a history link is a read-only pass the PUT already refuses with 403, so there is nothing of its own kind to reuse either — and the server refuses a history payload onto a contract link with 409 and the way forward. Payloads naming no purpose, or a contract purpose, pass as before: the round send names none, and the book may have moved to signing.

**PROVED**: f307 (5) — the card follows the kind (Sign → record → contract), the first frame is folded like the settled one, the 409 and the untouched 403 (three of four fail at the parent); f178 and f17 re-pointed (region, not byte count — the 700-byte window stopped short of the predicate's comment); n4 re-pointed (the question is behind its door in the settled html). share-recipient-verify 4b: the fetch held by `page.route`, the first frame measured, a change filed through `negoEditClause` so the history card is live, the record sent on the link channel by a real press, the share list read back (`["negotiate"]` → `["history","negotiate"]`, different tokens) and the new token fetched anonymously (`historyOnly:true`, no wording).

**NOTICED, NOT FIXED**: the history screen still carries the contract's readiness fold ("N things worth checking before you send") and its title says "Send round N"; a `view` payload can still refresh a `negotiate` row (same class of fault, contract-to-contract, not reported).

**THE WORD FILE (the same evening).** *"this is what i get in word format for negotiation history. It should be image 2. When i click on print or export history in the image 3 screen i get the right information."* The Word channel was built with ONE file builder, `wordTrackedFile` — the contract with its redlines as tracked changes — and `doSend` called it whatever the send was, so choosing the record and the Word channel delivered the agreement. Print history and Export history were right because they read `negoHistoryExportHtml`. The fix keeps that one report: `negoHistoryWordHtml` takes the export's body and drops only what the writer cannot use or Word draws itself (the page head and stylesheet, the circled event glyphs, the green/red legend — `<ins>`/`<del>` become real tracked changes), and `wordHistoryFile` verifies the record first exactly as Export and Print do, so the integrity line rides inside the file. Measured through the writer: the .docx reads *"Negotiation history — Warehousing…"*, the reference, the meta line, the proposed wording as a tracked change, and none of the clauses the negotiation never touched. The server's Word branch had one mail too ("mark it up in Word and reply with the file"); it reads the row's purpose now and describes the record. The dialog's channel line follows the kind (`paintChNote`, one painter for the channel press and the kind switch). Not built: a history file that is not Word (the channel is Word). Tests: f307 (6) — five claims, all red at the parent; share-recipient-verify 4b sends the record by Word file through the real dialog and reads the outbox back (`MK-B2-negotiation-history.docx`, the subject naming the history, no "mark it up").

**THE CHANNEL (the same night).** *"when i click share the blue highlight starts at email and then glitches and jumps to word. fix it so it stays at email and I can move to word if i want."* The first frame draws Email lit (it knows nothing yet); the fill read `pre.channel` — the channel of the LAST share on the record — and `setCh` moved the highlight to it. After the Word send of the record, every open jumped to Word. The dialog now opens on Email and the reader moves it; the remembered channel stays what it was for — the round send (`reshareToLastRecipient`) still posts by the channel the last round used. Proved in f307 (6) with a share list whose last row is a Word send (red at the parent) and in share-recipient-verify 4b, reopening the dialog after the real Word send.

**THE CHECKS (the same night).** *"what does the highlighted area have to do with sending negotiation history. Fix this because it is not necessary."* The readiness fold reads the agreement's own blanks and stage (a missing effective date, a Draft), which is a fact about the contract going out; a history send carries the record and no agreement, so the fold said nothing about what was being sent. It is wrapped (`#share-readiness-wrap`) and hidden on the record kind by `setKind`, back with the contract, and the send stops asking for the block's tick on that kind — a tick behind a hidden fold would have been a wall nobody could see. The owner asked for the removal by name, so the no-deleting-bands rule is satisfied. f307 (6) (red at the parent), share-recipient-verify 4b measures the fold off the history screen.

**THE TITLE (the same night).** *"fix the title so it says the history is being sent."* The one-screen heading was built once at the open — "Send round N to X" or "Send to X" — and the kind switch repainted everything under it but not the heading. `shareLeadTitle(c, s, purposeSel)` is the one reading now: the builder asks it for the first paint and `setKind` writes it back on every switch, so "Send the negotiation history to X" (`co_send_history_to`, both books) leads the record and the round leads the contract. f307 (6) (red at the parent), share-recipient-verify 4b reads the painted heading.

## PROMPT & BUILD — THE TEMPLATE BUILDER IS THE PAPER AND THE RAIL (owner's go, 13 Sep 2026; round two overnight 13–14 Sep)

Five screenshots, the day round one shipped: *"Image 4 and 5, maybe have copilot on the right hand side like in the contract workspace in image 5 and the idea is you tag each section which appears in the copilot and you collaborate and then you like the final output in copilot, you click apply which then appears on the contract builder. This goes section by section … truly think through this a propose a best in class solution because the current one is clunky and not innovative."* An artifact ("Tag, Talk, Apply") was drawn first, approved ("build it as agreed"), and built overnight.

**WHAT ROUND ONE GOT WRONG** was not the model or the routes — the outline, the drafting function, the library-first chip and the coverage arithmetic all survive — but the SHAPE: an ask box under every section made the builder a form with fifteen chat windows in it, and none of them knew about the others. The best-in-class shape in this space is the one the product already had two screens away: the clause editor, where the contract is the paper and Copilot is a rail beside it that knows which clause is in hand.

- **THE PAPER.** The template is drawn as a document (`tb-paperslot`): headings and wording blocks as contenteditable regions in the paper's own dress, a placeholder where a section has no wording yet, the blanks as chips. Typing reads back into the same block (`tbReadEditable` turns a chip back into `{{key}}`), so `tbSave` writes what it always wrote and the server sees no new shape. The paper and the rail are SLOTS, repainted separately, so a partial repaint never rebuilds the box the reader is typing in — the 30 Aug lesson from the clause editor, inherited rather than relearned.
- **TAG — FIVE DOORS, ONE READING.** ✦ on a section, the ◀▶ arrows in the rail's head, @ in the ask box (a picker over the section names), Next (the first section with nothing written), and Draft this on a placeholder. Every one presses `tbFocus`; `_tb.focus = ` appears exactly twice in the file (f306 counts it) — in tbFocus and at open — so "the section in hand" cannot come to have two answers. The rail's head names it; the paper marks it.
- **TALK — A THREAD PER SECTION.** `tbSend` posts into the focused section's thread; `tbTurn` builds the model's turn from the section's heading, its intent from the outline, the library clause where one matches (`tbLibraryFor`, spending nothing), the playbook's position (`tbStandardFor`), what the book usually signs (`tbPrecedentFor`) — and, new in round two, the OTHER sections, marked "for consistency only — do not rewrite them" (`o.others` in `copilotProposeTemplate`), which is what lets a definitions section and a payment section agree about a defined term.
- **APPLY — THE ONE WRITER.** A card's Apply (`tbAccept`) lands its wording on the block exactly as a keystroke does, through the same content write; Apply does not save — the builder's own Save does, as before. `tbAddBlock` is still the only push into `_tb.blocks`, `tbWordingBlock` the only splice, and block content is written in exactly three places; f306 pins all three counts so a fourth door is a decision.
- **WALK ME THROUGH IT** is ON after an outline (`tbSetWalk`): the rail moves to the first empty section and asks; Next takes you on. The outline (`tbOutlineAdd`) used to add "Payment terms" twice — once from the model and once as the playbook's required category — and "Liability cap" likewise; the playbook's additions are folded against the model's list and against each other now, so a heading is never added twice, and `tb_walk_std`'s trailing full stop is stripped so the sentence does not end "..".
- **PLAYBOOK AND BLANKS ARE TABS** (`tbSetTab`), in the rail, where the clause editor keeps its own. Below `TB_RAIL_MIN` (1024) the rail is not drawn (`tbRailFits`) and the paper takes the page — the clause editor's own rule at the same width.
- **THE FIVE DECISIONS** the artifact proposed were taken as proposed, and the owner did not overrule any: the paper replaces the block list; walk on by default; no rail below 1024; the two pop-ups stay two ("What kind of template?" and "New standard template" — see A DIALOG STATES ITS WIDTH ONCE); Apply does not save.

**THE TESTS** were where the cost went: f306's render claims read `#content`, but the paper and the rail paint into slots, and the fake DOM's `getElementById` creates any element it is asked for — so the claims had to be re-pointed at the slot elements or they would have measured an empty div the harness invented. f103's builder claim likewise. prompt-and-build-verify (27 checks) drives the whole journey — outline, walk, tag by every door, talk, apply, the tabs, the rail folding at 1000px — and writes its screenshots to `HATI_SHOT_DIR`, because `test/chromium/shots` is not writable in every sandbox. f148 learned that `tb_copilot` is the product's own name in both books.

## A DIALOG STATES ITS WIDTH ONCE, ON THE FRAME (Young ruled 13 Sep 2026)

*"image 1, this card is poorly designed with space not utilised well. Same with image 2. All pop ups should always have balance and centered. iMage 3, other is in the dropdown twice."* Image 1 was the approval route editor, image 2 "New standard template", both with a blank column down their right-hand side.

**ONE FAULT, MEASURED.** `openModal` drew every dialog as a 32rem frame, and the box handed to it carried its own `max-width` — 28rem here, 30rem there — left-aligned inside the frame. The frame was centred on the page; the box was not centred in the frame. So "balance" was not a design question at all: it was two declarations of one width disagreeing, and the second one being narrower and hugging the left.

- **THE WIDTH IS SAID ONCE, ON THE FRAME.** `DLG_W` (js/core.js, published) is the ladder — s 400 · m 520 · l 640 · xl 760 — and `openModal(html, { maxWidth })` takes it, defaulting to m. Every inner `max-width` came out (approvals.js's route editor, settings.js, intake.js, templatelib.js, library.js, the builder's field modal); the inner padding is one value, 24px. **A NET FAILS ON THE NEXT ONE**: f312 sweeps the dialog builders for an inner `max-width`, and dialog-balance-verify measures the box's left and right insets inside the frame and requires them equal, on eighteen dialogs.
- **"WHAT KIND OF TEMPLATE?"** is two equal tiles (`.tn-tile`, `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))`, the sprite's own symbols, the accent on hover and focus) rather than two rows of text with a button under each. The subtitle the artifact drew was omitted: the tiles say what they are.
- **"NEW STANDARD TEMPLATE"** puts Category and Value stream on ONE row (`tplLibCatStreamRowHtml`, shared with the details dialog so the two cannot drift), and **"Other" is listed once**: `tplLibCategoryOptions` builds the list with `other` first and never appends it again — image 3's duplicate was the list's own "Other" plus one the dialog added.
- **LEFT AS THEY ARE**: nine dialogs that name their own width explicitly for a reason of their own (the share dialog's 46rem among them). The rule is about saying the width twice, not about which width.

## THE LAYERED REDLINE — A COUNTER WRITTEN ON THEIR ASK STACKS (Young ruled 13 Sep 2026, "the Large option"; built overnight 13–14 Sep)

The brief, in the owner's own framing: *"When the other side sends a redline and you go to counter it, the clause you type in is built from the agreed wording plus changes that have been accepted. Their still-pending proposal is not in it. So their marks leave the screen the moment you start writing … Filing then replaces their ask … it means the record cannot say 'we accepted the shape of their redraft and moved two parts of it', which is the commonest move in a real negotiation."* Three rules: no pencil to start and the pencil means finished; marks never disappear; a counter stacks and the pair is decided together. Five pieces, a wholesale rule, and an order of work that began with a photograph.

**PROVED ON TWO PARAGRAPHS FIRST.** Five of their marks and five of ours on one clause — an edit inside one of their insertions, both sides deleting the same words, an edit straddling the edge of theirs — and a wholesale rewrite landing on a three-round clause. Composed from the two STORED op arrays (never re-diffed) by `redlineLayerOps`, drawn by the product's own renderer with two classes it did not have, photographed, and read: the layered picture was readable at 26 marked words against 81; the rewrite was not at 168 against 99, and the replacement rule was set from those two numbers rather than from a percentage.

- **PIECE 1 — SEEDING.** The editor already seeded from the LEAD change, so their pending ask was in the box; what it lacked was any record that the filing was written ON it. `ceStacksOn()` is the one reading of which ask this page writes on — their pending ask, or (after a first filing) the ask parked under our own counter, so a REVISION keeps measuring against their wording rather than falling back to the standing text and breaking the stack at the first correction.
- **PIECE 3 — FILING.** `negoEditClause` takes `opts.onTop` and measures against that ask's `newText`; `negoMeasuredAlike` already told "measured alike" (rivals) from "written on top", and the funnel now acts on the difference: their ask is PARKED (`status:'countered'`, `counteredBy`, `counteredAt`), the counter records `counterOf` and `bundle:[{id, was, counteredBy}]`. **A RIVAL STILL SUPERSEDES** — the playbook pass, Prepare redlines, Copilot's batch, the Word round trip and our own ask from another round all measure against the standing text and keep the 15 Aug behaviour, which the brief named as the wall: "they state our standards; they do not answer their draft." The first cut of the rule keyed wholesale on size ALONE and turned a same-side other-round rewrite of a tiny fixture clause into a bundle; f207's own claims caught it, and the rule was narrowed to a filing written on top.
- **PIECE 4 — THE PAIR RULE.** `negoResolve` refuses a decision on a parked ask, naming the counter to decide instead. `negoBundleFollow` is the one follower: ACCEPT supersedes everything under the counter — walked, because an ask of ours their counter had parked sits two deep, and the deeper ones KEEP `counteredBy` so a reopen can put them back under the counter they were under; REFUSE puts each back where it stood — under its own counter where that counter is still on the table (pending or itself parked), else onto the table — roots first, by depth read off the bundle's own links; REOPEN re-parks, to a fixpoint for the deeper ones. `negoRetractDraft` releases what an unsent counter parked. **THE TRAP the brief named** — `negoAdvanceRound` archiving a superseded ask while its counter is undecided — cannot arise: the round already refused to close over a pending change, and it now refuses over a parked one as well, so "a refusal in round 4 of a replacement filed in round 3" is a state the record cannot reach; the claim is pinned as the wall. `negoProgress` stopped counting a parked ask as decided ("3 of 4 decided" over one decision and two parked asks).
- **THE WHOLESALE RULE.** `redlineWholesale(before, after)`: the words carrying a strike or an underline exceed the words of the clause as proposed. A counter written on top that passes it is a REPLACEMENT (`replacement:true`) and a BUNDLE of every live ask on the clause, both sides', however deep it was parked — with `was` and `counteredBy` recorded per entry so the refusal restores the exact shape. Drawn as one struck block, one inserted block and `.rl-repl-on` saying what it stands on, on the block; never a band.
- **PIECE 2 — RENDERING.** `redlineOpsHtml` wears `who` as `rl-them` / `rl-us` and `under` as a nested mark (our deletion inside their insertion); `redlineOpsBlocks` had to spread the op (`{...o, text}`) or the who was lost between the walk and the paint — the proof rendered black until it did. The colours are the notes rooms' own — amber for the other side, the accent for us — and RELATIVE TO THE READER: parity-verify 12 measures our counter wearing our colour on our seat and theirs on their page, the same words swapping class while each class keeps its colour (one stylesheet). `rlLayeredHtml` is the one reading for both canvases; `negoLeadChange` leads with the top of a stack and never with a parked ask.
