## ANALYZE CONTRACT ON THE GRAPH — THE PAPER IN THE GRAPH'S COLUMN (Young ruled 26 Sep 2026)

**THE ASK.** *"In the contract graph page, I want to divide the highlighted button into two buttons. first one would be analyze contract and the other would be Open work space and the compare will remain as is. The analyze contract would be a button that when you press, the nodes disappear but the paper of the contract you had pressed which would be in the chat then appear on the page on the left or on top of the nodes … You can then query in the chat any questions regarding the contract. If it is respective to a clause or obligation the paper would jump to that location and highlight the specifics of what you are inquiring about."* Three options were drawn on the real page ("Analyze on the Graph": Sheet, Pinned, Focus); the owner asked *"if I am analyzing the page and I go back to graph, how do I go back to paper again?"* — the first drawing's only way back was the card's Analyze button, scrolled up the conversation — and then *"I want to have all three options in 1"*, then *"Build the all in one option and merge to main. Start from the latest main."*

**WHAT WAS BORROWED, so nothing is a second reading.** The paper is the working copy's one builder (docSheetHtml), asked for a read-only copy with its own canvas id; the pages are the Document tab's page-maker with the same options; the marks are the risk scan's own "take me to these words" (scrollToQuote) asked to HOLD; the map is the X-ray's own walk over the graph's canvas; the wording is this page's own reader (contractPlainText); the whole-contract message shape is the clause editor's (wholeDoc). Every widening is additive and every older caller is byte-identical, which f392 pins as walls.

**THE ONE THING THE SERVER HAD WRONG.** normalizeDeliver verifies a citation's quote against contractFullBody — the stored body — and drops one it cannot find. A DRAFTED contract's paper is template wording the server never renders, so every quote from it, copied character for character, verified against nothing and was dropped: no pin could ever have landed on a drafted contract. Under wholeDoc the last message IS the wording the model read, so both chat routes hand it to the check (`cx.sentText`) and a quote is kept where it appears in the stored body OR the sent copy. The wall stands: a quote in neither is still dropped, and the browser then finds a kept quote on the painted paper or marks the pin lost and says so on the chip's hover. analyze-on-the-graph-verify 2c is the claim, driven on MK-A2 (template paper, no stored wording) on purpose.

**FOUR THINGS ONLY THE RENDERED PAGE SHOWED.** (1) docXraySpineRows was not on contract.js's published list, so the graph file's typeof check bailed and the map drew nothing — THE FILES ARE ES MODULES, paid again. (2) The head strip states display:flex INLINE, which no stylesheet rule can outrank, so Focus hid only the grouped-by line; the fold is written on the element (never !important) and the markup's own value put back. (3) The X-ray strip has no width in the sheet — the Document tab writes it on the element — so the map had a block and no pixels; the graph writes the same constant the same way. (4) Three buttons overflowed the card at the panel's width and Compare was cut off; the row wraps.

**ONE FACT ONCE.** A dropped quote already prints the server's own amber notice under the answer; the "nothing to show on the paper" line is drawn only for an answer that quoted nothing.

**REFUSALS.** Q5 (one door): the same question can be asked on the Document tab and in the clause editor; the owner asked for this door by name, over the drawing that said so. Q2: no band — the strip is the column's own header and the box's placeholder carries the scope. Q3: this page never showed the agreement; the first line of the paper measured 241px from the top of the window in the column. Focus was drawn as a third full-window layer and built as a fold of the page's own head, so that cost was not paid.

**Said out loud.** A second Analyze on another contract starts a fresh paper and the first paper's pins go with it (per sitting). Pins are per sitting; keeping one is a note. Not on the phone (Insights is not drawn there). f277 (1) and (10) are red at the parent and left red.

Tests: f392 (35 claims, 33 red at the parent), analyze-on-the-graph-verify (26 checks); f364 (4) re-pointed in place. insights-panels-verify 84/84, two-copies-verify 28/28 unchanged.

## THE OVERNIGHT CLEAN-UP (owner-asked 26 Sep 2026: "review the entire platform … whatever bugs you find, fix them")

**THE ASK.** *"For the overnight job, review the entire platform for performance and functionality bugs that needs cleaning up. For instance, I was one of the very long contract when it is in the plain English loading phase, when the contract is loading the page says reading clause X and when the translation to plain English comes up, the words reading still display beneath the translation so they are on top of each other. Check all the presses, the pops ups, the loading, among other possibilities that may appear then whatever bugs you find, fix them. Also review the process flows and fix any processes flaws. After fixing and merging to main, share an output of all the fixes you managed overnight."*

**HOW IT WAS DONE.** Six audit passes over the product (the contract room; the negotiate page and its notes; signatures, sharing and the server; pop-ups and presses; Home, lists and counts; the other side's page and the phone), each finding reproduced by a probe in a real browser or against a real server before anything was changed, and each fix measured again after. Findings that turned out to be deliberate rulings, or questions only the owner can answer, were logged rather than changed.

**THE OWNER'S EXAMPLE, AND WHY IT HAPPENED.** The Plain English column copies the paper's front matter (title, parties, recitals) level with the paper so the column never starts on a blank — and it stopped copying at the first clause that had a READING. A long contract is read in pages, a few at a time, so a later page often lands first: every clause above it was then treated as front matter, copied in, and a "Reading…" line was drawn over each copied clause. The boundary is now the first clause ON THE PAPER (`docReadFront(c, rows)`, handed the sheet the painter already walked). A second overlap hid under it: a long preamble copied into a column narrower than the paper wraps onto more lines and ran under the first reading — it is now cut at a whole line above the first clause and fades. And the painter measured and placed each reading one at a time, forcing the browser to lay the page out again per entry: ~550ms a paint on a 300-clause contract, repainting every 1.5s while a reading runs. All reads first, all writes last: ~90ms.

**POP-UPS.** Every dialog added its own Escape listener to the document and it took itself off only on the next key press: twenty dialogs, twenty listeners (measured 13 → 33). Worse, a side panel (the brief, the memo) replaced by a guarded dialog left the PANEL's Escape behind, and that one called closeModal straight — measured on main: Escape closed an editing dialog with no "Discard these changes?" at all (`asked: 0`). And the dialog's own Escape took itself off BEFORE asking the guard, so after "Keep editing" Escape did nothing. `rootEscSet` is one Escape for the root, replaced on open and removed on close. A dialog replacing another read its opener after the old panel was gone — always `<body>` — so closing the second dropped a keyboard reader at the top of the page; the opener is read first now and handed to the trap. confirmDialog grew two honest options (`cancelLabel:''` for one way out, `multiline`) because the family check was asking for them under names nobody read, and three callers passed `confirm:` / `okText:` so their buttons said "Confirm". A second confirm or prompt settles the first rather than leaving its caller waiting for ever. Phone sheets said they were modal and trapped focus but offered no key out.

**THEIR PAGE.** Answers sent from the other side's page were remembered only in memory, and Send clears the held store — so a reload before the owner's browser collected them put the change back to "Awaiting you", a second, different answer was posted and applied after the first, and the owner's trail carried two "decided" lines (measured: two responses waiting, the change ending "rejected"). Sent answers and withdrawals are kept per link for the same month as held ones, dropped when the record catches up, and not read at all once the server says the last answer was applied (from then the link's copy IS the record, and a memory would hide a change the owner reopened). Proposals are deliberately not kept: the owner's copy re-files them under its own ids, so a remembered one could never be matched to its twin. Their decision buttons were 22px on a phone because the 44px rule named the old card class.

**THE CONTRACT ROOM.** Opening a signed contract created a negotiation on it (the History tab and the review gate read through the initialising functions), after which every save was refused — READING MUST NOT WRITE, paid again. Write the brief bound a listener per render, so one press after a few edits sent several paid requests. Editing an obligation erased its completion, chase and series. A slow reading landed on whichever contract was open when it came back. The room's More menu added a document listener per paint. The header kept the old name, value and term after an Overview edit until the reader left the contract (`roomHeadRefresh`, a paint of the four pieces that carry record facts). The fill counter changed shape and colour on the first keystroke; the arrival strip ticked "filled in" over fields still open.

**THE SERVER.** The dispute-hold guards sat inside the half-signed branch of the save, so they never ran on an unsigned or an executed contract. A signing link bound to one signer could be sent to any address, and the one-time code went there too. A revoked link could still make the server email a signing code. The daily send cap forgot a bucket's window after an hour. A crafted "signature" image ran script in the owner's session. A route that threw took the process down. The unused-file sweep had never been reachable (registered after `/api/files/:id`). A document that arrived by email filed a contract whose file could not be opened (`{name, type, data}` — a shape no screen reads). A deleted contract left its cached Plain English edition behind.

**WHAT THE BROWSER SET CAUGHT ON THE WAY OUT.** The whole browser set was run on the branch and at unmodified main, and every difference was chased to its cause. Four came from tonight's own fixes. (1) The Inspector now asks for a light row's trail — main answered "nothing recorded yet" for every contract the list had not loaded — but it asked with `ensureFull`, which copies the server's WHOLE record over the one on screen: a category set a moment before was gone the instant the panel asked (register-category-verify), and on Home's Map test a status staged a moment before read back as the stored one (home-page-verify 3c). The loader is `restoreHeavyFields`, the product's own inverse of the list's stripper, and the obligation history's loader took the same fix — and then one more measurement: that loader marks the record LOADED, and the contract room only fetches a record that is not, so the brief, the renewal advice, the Plain English edition and who must approve (all transport on the single-record route, never on the list) never arrived; a contract chosen in the list's side panel opened with no brief, where main showed it. `restoreHeavyFields` now copies every underscored key of that answer the record lacks — the server's readings, never a person's edit — which also closes the same hole in saveContract's light-row save. (2) Telling a turn notice kept in the outbox apart from a failure had taken away the row's *Try the email again* door; it is back, beside the honest IN OUTBOX. (3) signing-flow-verify 6 had been staging its "nobody named to sign" state on the contract that section 4 had just signed — the server refused that save with a 409 all along, and main kept the refused copy on screen, which is what the section had been measuring. With a refused save now putting the page back, the stage moved to a contract nobody has signed and asserts the stage landed. (4) upload-blanks-verify 9j asked the arrival tile for the words "still open" — the contradiction tonight removed (a tick over "4 still open") — and now asks the chip's number against the live count, still passing on both sides as the CONTROL it is.

**LEFT FOR THE OWNER, said in the run's summary and the log.** "See all N" on Home counts items while the list it opens counts contracts; the reference column is cut at 1024px wide (the widths are a ruled design); the other side's "accept the wording" answer is recorded but read by no screen; the bell row says "They are waiting for you to sign" where the act is their own readiness.

Tests: f393 (55 claims, 54 red at the parent 790b4d5; the one pass is a named wall), with the probes kept in the run's scratchpad.

## EXPLORER — THE NAME, THE DIVIDER, THE LEGEND AT REST (Young ruled 27 Sep 2026)

**THE ASK.** *"Let's just change the name to simply Explorer. Also, I need for you to bring the divider that is in the document and negotiate pages to the Explorer page as opposed to have the arrow button that is on the chatbot that expands and closes the chat window. Finally, when you open the explorer page, the legend should always be closed as the resting state."* Asked to confirm first; the one reading put back was which arrow — the panel's head carried two, » (widen/shrink) and › (fold to a strip). The recommendation was to remove » and keep ›, because a divider on the other two pages cannot hide a panel completely, so without › there is no way to give the map the whole width. The owner said go.

**THE NAME.** "Explorer" over three alternatives offered the day before (Contract Explorer, Contract Map, keep it). Only the tab's word moved: its key, the stored tab and Copilot's stable key are untouched, so no link and no conversation breaks. Swedish "Utforskaren", the definite form, as a tab name reads.

**THE DIVIDER, AND WHICH OF THE THREE IT COPIES.** The Document tab drags by distance travelled and stores a fraction; the Negotiate page stores a fraction but rests at a width; the clause editor drags by the pointer's position with a grab offset. The panel here is a fixed-purpose column whose cards were drawn at 380px, so it takes the Negotiate page's resting rule (a WIDTH, the panel's own) and the clause editor's drag (the handle stays under the finger — the Negotiate page once fell hundreds of pixels behind the cursor because its drag and its layout divided by different widths, which a stored width cannot do). The floors are the Document tab's column floor (420) and a panel floor at which the card's three doors still sit on one line (340). The panel's own width transition made the handle trail the pointer, so a drag turns it off.

**THE LEGEND.** It was per sitting: open it once and it stayed open until a reload. Now it folds on every ARRIVAL. The tell is whether a map is already on screen when the tab paints: an arrival (from another tab, or the page from elsewhere) replaces a page with no map; a repaint of the tab (a language change, the rail door pressed while here) replaces the map itself and keeps the reader's choice. No hook in setView, so the rule that nothing in app.js names the legend (f298) still holds.

**MEASURED.** A real drag of 160px widens the panel by 160px and moves the handle by 160px; far right stops at 340 with an amber grip, far left leaves the column 420; the paper beside the panel follows the drag (828px → 678px sheet). With the paper up the handle is on top and pressable.

Tests: f394, explorer-verify; insights-panels-verify 15e re-pointed (a legend row is measured as pixels, so it opens the legend with a press first).

## WHAT THIS CONTRACT NEEDS FROM YOU — THE CHECKLIST (Young picked "Checklist" by name, 27 Sep 2026)

**HOW IT CAME ABOUT.** The owner asked what Home's "Needs your decision" card means ("What attention needs to be paid to?") after a report that its "See all N" counted items while the list it opened counted contracts. The answer was six kinds of row, two of which (a contract merely sitting in review, and every renewal in the book) name nobody. The owner's reply was a different idea: *"What about adding a nicely designed banner in the contract's inspector side panel that explains what attention is needed. It would sit right under the party names and in color. Render how this may look like."* Three designs were drawn into the real Contracts page with the sample portfolio — Explained, Checklist, One line — on four example contracts, and the owner said *"Implement checklist."*

**ONE READING, AND IT IS HOME'S.** The checklist is not a second list of "things that need you". `needsYouOf(c)` asks Home's own five sources of a one-contract list, and Home's own lateness rules, so for any item both show, the two screens say the same thing. Two things were lifted out of Home to make that true without copying: the renewal-decision question (it was written inline over the whole book inside hmDashSlices; `hmRenewalDue` answers it for one contract and the slices are now built from it) and the review-lateness rule (`hmReviewLate`, with the 30-day renewal threshold as `HM_SOON_DAYS`). Home's card output is unchanged, byte for byte.

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT.** A contract sitting in review is not something anyone owes by name, and a renewal on a contract somebody else owns is theirs to decide. Home's card still shows both — that is the owner's call, asked at the end of the run, not made on the way past.

**WHERE IT SITS.** "Right under the party names" was built as under the whole name block — the party names and the agreement's own name — and above the status line, so the contract's name is never split in two by a coloured card. Said to the owner.

**ONE NUMBER FOR ONE THING ON ONE SCREEN.** The red row's "Waiting 9 days" is the asks table's own count further down the same panel (calendar days since the oldest of their asks), not the desk flag's working-day count, which would have printed a second number for the same wait. The five-working-day standard is the same words the table prints, and rides the hover: the first build printed it on the line and the line was cut off at every laptop width.

**THE DOORS.** Each button opens where its item is answered: their redlines and a review → the negotiation (the bell's own doors); a signature → the Signing tab; a renewal → the Overview, where the renewal card records it; a request to join → the room with the desk sheet open. Home's rows open the contract generally, and the bell opens renewal and join rows generally; neither was changed, and the owner was asked whether they should follow.

**THE APPROVALS & SIGNING PAGE.** Its signing panel leads with "what stands before signing", so its checklist leaves the signature out (`needsSkip`). The other kinds still draw there.

**THE CLOTHES.** The owner's Checklist render had buttons with tinted edges; they keep the platform's one light edge (26 Sep 2026) and take the row's colour on the word only. The rows are one line each; everything cut is on the hover.

**MEASURED.** The browser file stages every kind through the product's own acts (the desk claimed deliberately, a real review request, a real signing route, a renewal on an owned contract, a join request on the desk) and presses every button. At the parent 21 of 25 checks fail; three had first passed there vacuously (a panel with no checklist does not grow sideways, leaves out an unowned renewal and leaves the signature out) and were gated on the row having been drawn. At night the head reads 6:1.

Tests: f395 (26 claims, 25 red at the parent), inspector-checklist-verify (25 checks, 21 red at the parent).

### AND HOME'S CARD LISTS THE SAME FIVE (Young: yes, 27 Sep 2026)

Asked the same evening whether Home's "Needs your decision" should match the checklist, the owner said yes. Until then the card listed two things the checklist never did. **"Waiting on review"** was every contract in the book sitting at Under Review, longest first — a queue nobody owns, naming nothing the reader has to do; on the sample book it was all twelve of the card's rows. **A renewal** was listed on every reader's card, whoever owned the contract.

**THE CHANGE IS TWO LINES IN ONE FUNCTION.** `hmDecisionItems` stops reading `waitingLongest` and asks the renewal source `owns(x.c)` — `contractOwnedBy(c, me)`, the very question `needsYouOf` asks. The slice itself stays: the phone's own list (`mNeedsYou`) reads it and was not part of the ask. The bell still rings for every renewal inside thirty days, and the Map and the calendar still count them, so an unowned renewal is not lost — it is off the one list that is about the reader by name.

**MEASURED ON THE SAMPLE BOOK** (a fresh workspace, the sample ticked): before, 12 items, every one "Waiting on review"; after, none, and the card says "Nothing to decide — you're all caught up." No sample contract has an owner (they are raised by 'System', which the owner readings refuse on purpose), so no renewal there can be anybody's.

**THE TESTS THAT STAGED THE OLD ROWS WERE RE-POINTED, NOT DELETED.** f382 (3) staged five contracts in review to get five rows; it stages five renewal decisions the reader owns now, each put away from the desk — without that stamp the desk draws the nearest renewal and the one-door rule takes it off the card, which silently made every count one short on the first try. f381's one row was MK-4 in review and is MK-1's owned renewal. home-page-verify 11 stamps the reader as owner of its two renewals (the seeded book is owned by nobody, so every "it is on the list" claim would have been false for an unrelated reason) and 12 stages owned renewals instead of idle reviews. f274's filter regex and f395's 1d wall were re-pointed in place — 1d was a wall for exactly one commit, "Home's card is unchanged", and is reversed.

**RED AT a007cdb**: f382 (3)'s three new claims and home-page-verify 12h / 12i. 12i2 is the control: the same renewal owned by the reader IS on the list, so 12i was the owner question and not a renewal the reading could not see.

### AND THE OTHER TWO HOMES GO STRAIGHT THERE (Young: "Yes, make them go straight to the right place", 27 Sep 2026)

**WHAT THE OWNER WAS TOLD, AND WHAT HE ANSWERED.** The checklist's buttons each open the exact place an item is answered. Home's "Needs your decision" rows and the bell's renewal and "asked to join" rows did not: they opened the contract, and the room lands on whatever tab that contract last showed — the Document tab for a contract nobody has opened this sitting. So a signature row put the reader on the Document tab to go looking for Signing, a renewal row a tab away from the renewal card, and a request to join on a page with nothing to answer it on. The owner was asked whether those should go straight to the right place too, and said yes.

**ONE DOOR, THREE HOMES.** Nothing new decides a destination. Each Home row now carries its `kind` — the checklist's own five — and a press hands it to `needsYouGo`, the checklist's door. The bell's request-to-join row and both of its renewal rows (the decision coming due, and the agreement ending inside thirty days) press the same door through one small helper in `buildAlerts`. `needsYouGo` learned one thing to make that safe: it now answers whether it found the contract, so a press it cannot answer (a row with no kind, a contract that has left the list, a stage without the door) still opens the contract the plain way instead of going dead. That fallback is what the two named controls measure.

**WHAT WAS NOT SWEPT.** The bell's review, quiet-negotiation and signature rows already landed on the negotiation and the Signing tab, so they were not touched — but they carry their own copies of those destinations beside the door, which is the two-doors-drift fault in waiting. Logged, not fixed. The phone's own list (`mNeedsYou`) opens contracts its own way and was not part of the ask.

**MEASURED.** The node claims build the card and the bell for real — `buildAlerts` is lifted out of js/app.js whole, with the kind table and its rank, and run over slices handed in — and compare every landing with what `needsYouGo` does for the same kind, so the claim is a relation and never a destination typed twice. The browser file presses Home's real rows and the real bell on a staged workspace. **Before every press it opens the room on another contract**, because the room remembers its tab per contract: section 3 had left the signature contract on its Signing tab, so without that step a row that only opened the contract would have passed on the fault. The Sendy renewal also had to be put away from Prepared for you (`deskDismiss`), or the one-door rule takes it off the card and the row under test is never drawn.

Tests: f395 (8) (seven claims, five red at ba092e2; 8d and 8f are the controls), inspector-checklist-verify 8 (eight checks, all eight red at ba092e2, each landing on the Document tab with no sheet).

## THE FOUR GO-AHEADS (Young, 27 Sep 2026: "Merge to main and it's a yes on the other 3")

**WHAT THE THREE WERE.** Three of the five items the overnight report left for the owner to decide, approved in principle earlier the same day and given their "go" with this message: an alert when the other side presses "Agree to the wording — but don't sign yet"; clearer words on their own bell's signing row; and telling the live server it is running live. The fourth came in the same message, over a screenshot of the side panel's renewal row: pressing Decide should read the contract again before you decide.

**THE LIVE SERVER KNOWS IT IS LIVE.** render.yaml now sets NODE_ENV=production, and the deployment guide says so in its settings table and in both ways of starting the server. Measured before it was set: nothing in the code reads NODE_ENV, the server's own error handler already answers every failure in JSON (added the overnight before), and the server requires only express — so the one real effect is that Render's `npm install` stops installing the three test-only packages. The server was started in production mode against its own routes to prove it still answers. f396 (1c) is the wall: the day somebody requires a test-only package at runtime, a test fails rather than the live build.

**THEIR BELL'S SIGNING ROW.** It said "They are waiting for you to sign", which was not true — nobody had asked them to sign, and the row's press does not sign: it presses their own Ready to sign button, which tells us they are ready. The row now prints that button's own hover sentence, asked by the same key, so the two cannot drift. The old key is left inert in both books.

**THEY AGREED TO THE WORDING.** The answer was always recorded — on the contract, in the comments, on the trail — but its toast is a bare one, which prints nothing, so nobody was told. One reading, `cpAcceptedWording`, decides whether the agreement is still the next thing: nobody has signed yet, the contract is not declined, archived, signed or executed, and no change has been filed since they agreed. That last half borrows the one reading of when the wording last moved rather than writing a second one — see the note below about that reading. The bell row is green (the same kind of news as "ready to sign", ranked directly under it), stands down where they have also said they are ready to sign, and opens the Signing tab, because the next step is a signature.

**A RENEWAL'S DECIDE READS THE CONTRACT AGAIN.** The door every renewal press goes through (the checklist's Decide, Home's renewal row, the bell's renewal rows) now registers the ask before the room opens, and the Overview spends it when it paints — the room's own "do this when you arrive" shape. Starting the reading at the press was the obvious build and the wrong one: a contract chosen from a list is usually a light register row, the room loads it in full a moment later, and loading copies the stored record over the object — so the first answers of a reading already under way would have been overwritten by the old ones. The ask is spent once, only on a record loaded in full, and only within a minute of the press, so a press whose room never arrived cannot start a paid reading the next time somebody happens to open that Overview. What runs is the whole arrival read, with the brief written afresh: it is the one reading with a cache, and without that the reader would be looking at last month's date under "read again". The cost is said on the press's hover in all three places. Plain English is not re-read, because it is made by walking the Document tab's painted page; opening the switch there reads it, and re-reads only what changed.

**TWO THINGS THE RE-READ PUT IN FRONT OF THE READER.** A signed contract had never had the arrival read run over it, so two sentences had never been seen on one. The open-fields box said "This contract is in negotiation" for any contract with stored wording, signed or not; it says "This contract is signed — its wording is final" now (a new reason, `sealed`, asked first). And the head's Copilot fact is built once per render, so it went on saying "Not read yet" above a strip that had just said "Brief written"; the landing now repaints the head with the strip.

**AND ONE THING THE FIRST CUT GOT WRONG, FOUND BY DRIVING IT.** The first commit of this batch let the re-read's last step — filling the open fields — run on a signed contract. On a signed contract drawn from one of HaTi's own templates the record answered a blank (the start date), the step wrote it into the contract's fields, and the server refused the save: a signed contract's fields are locked. The refusal does what refusals do here — it puts the stored record back — so every reading the reader had just watched arrive was thrown away with it. Home's page-error sweep caught it as a 409, and the new browser check reproduces it on that commit (3k: two refused saves). The step now stands down on a signed contract and the tile says why, in the same words as above. A signed contract's wording is final; there is nothing for the step to do.

**NOTICED, THEN FIXED ON THE OWNER'S WORD.** The one reading of "when the wording last moved" (`signCheckBriefAt`) looked for a date field that filed changes do not carry — they carry `createdAt` — so it found no date on any real change. The brief's "out of date" answer, the Overview's out-of-date markers, a signer's read of the brief lapsing after a round, and now the accepted-wording row's staleness could never trip on real data. Fixing it makes the brief hold a signature under the gate after a round until it is re-read, which is what the brief rule was written to do; Young was told exactly that and said "yes, fix the wording date". It reads `createdAt` and `updatedAt` now (`BRIEF_AT_KEYS`), keeping the two old names for any record shaped that way. Every earlier test of it had staged a change carrying `at` — the shape the product does not produce — which is how it passed; f396 (5) files its change through the one funnel instead, and all four of its claims are red at 4f95c09.

Tests: f396 (25 claims, 21 red at ce9cc59; 1c and 2c are walls, 1d and 2b controls; 4i red at 65a4bde too), go-aheads-verify (21 checks in a real browser with both seats, 13 red at ce9cc59; 3g2, 3j and 3k red at 65a4bde). Re-pointed in place: f191 (6)'s list of sentences the bell prints, f280 (3)'s region (it began at a line this batch changed), home-page-verify 12f's staging (its unsaved renewals are put back before the press, because the press now saves).

## A DOOR FROM ANOTHER PAGE LANDS ON FRESH FILTERS (Young ruled 27 Sep 2026)

Young, over a screenshot of the Contracts page reading "Needs your decision ✕  Stage Drafting": *"i was on the home page and clicked on the main graph to take me to contracts and look at the contracts in draft stage. Then i went back to home and clicked on the needs your decision and it took me back to the contracts page but i did not see all the contracts that need my decision because they were filtered still on draft then needs your decision. This is counter productive. When you have chosen a new filter from outside the page and you are landed to the results, the previous filters should not be there."*

**IT WAS THE DOCUMENTED DESIGN, AND THE DESIGN WAS HALF RIGHT.** The named-set door (`regShowOnly`, 11 Aug 2026) said of itself that it was "an ordinary filter in every other respect — the stage, stream and category dropdowns still narrow further inside it, Clear clears it with the rest, and it survives navigation exactly as they do." Narrowing further INSIDE it, on the page, is right and stays. What was wrong is that it ARRIVED inside whatever the reader had left on the page an hour earlier, and nothing on the way said so. Reproduced in a real browser on the parent: the Map's Drafting bar, the rail's Home door, "See all 3" — and the list showed nothing, because every contract on the decision list was signed, with "Stage Drafting" lit beside "Needs your decision".

**ONE SHAPE IN SIX COSTUMES.** Every door onto Contracts from another page wrote its own short list of what to clear, and each list was short of the next filter somebody added: the named-set door cleared nothing but the named set; the Map's stage bar five filters (a category or a search typed on the page survived it); the phone's tiles three; the shell bar's search none; Home's See all fallback four; My Queue's "+N more" two. A door that says one number and lands on a smaller one is the fault the Map's own note ("every figure is a door onto the list that makes it") forbids.

**THE FIX IS ONE READING AND ONE DOOR, NOT SIX LONGER LISTS.** `regFiltersAtRest(R)` is the one reading of "nothing is narrowing", and it is DERIVED from the filter catalogue (`REG_BAR_FILTERS`), so a filter added tomorrow is cleared by every door and by Clear without anybody remembering to list it — f397 (1c) pushes a new filter onto the catalogue and watches it cleared. The rest value is 'all' for every filter and null for the quick-filter tab (`REG_FILTER_REST`), which is exactly what the two Clear buttons had always written; they ask it now, so a door and Clear cannot disagree about what "no filter" means. Sort, direction, density and the amendment fold are kept — they are how the reader LOOKS at the list, not what is on it. `regGoFiltered(patch, opts)` is the one door, the Obligations page's `obwGoFiltered` in the register's clothes (that page learned the same lesson on 31 Aug): the seat goes back to Contracts first, the filters to rest, the patch goes on, the shell bar's box is emptied (it lives above every page and no page repaints it — Clear's own rule, that the box may not say one thing and the table another), and the page opens. `open:false` is for the phone, which opens its own screen.

**WHO PRESSES IT.** `regShowOnly` itself, so every caller lands fresh by construction — the calendar's day, Insights' exposure rows and the graph's dependents, Copilot's worklists (its whole-book door's own comment, "the register's one door, with nothing narrowing it", became true), and Home's Map months and See all. The Map's stage bar. The phone's tiles. My Queue's "+N more" when pressed on My Queue; on the Contracts page's own Board the same button is a press INSIDE the page and keeps what it did. The shell bar's search, typed on another page, asks `regFiltersAtRest` before it writes the query and keeps its own box (it holds what the reader is typing); typed while Contracts is on screen it narrows inside, as every in-page filter does.

**WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT.** A door that carries no new filter — the rail's Contracts door, the calendar's "Open the register", the empty Negotiations page's "Open the register", Home's first-run "Explore" card — leaves the page as the reader left it; the owner's rule is about landing on the results of a NEW filter. The last two clear the stage (and "Explore" the stream) but keep the rest, which is logged for the owner rather than widened. The phone's own Clear still clears only what the phone can show; logged. The other lists already landed fresh: the Obligations page (`obwGoFiltered`) and Templates (`tplGoBucket`), and no door writes the Negotiations seat from outside.

Tests: f397 (17 claims; 14 red at the parent — at the parent the owner's journey lands on NOTHING in the model; 2d, 3a and 5a are walls), fresh-filters-verify (14 checks in a real browser, 7 red at the parent, which prints "door said 3 · list shows 0 (nothing)" and "Stage Drafting" lit — the screenshot; the seven that pass on both are named controls). Re-pointed in place: f281 (3) (the two Clear buttons are asked of the one reading and then of what it DOES, and the region is the handler's own to its closing brace, never a byte count) and f381 (5) (the stage branch presses the one door; the seat-first and named-set claims are asked of that door, where they live now).

## COPILOT'S WORK — THE AGENTS (Young ruled 27 Sep 2026: "Build the agents idea", option 2 of "Work Board Options")

Off four screenshots of other products (a helpdesk's triage agents, a finance team's staged agents with a Run button, a public ranking algorithm, an agent manager's kanban), the owner asked which could add value to HaTi, especially agentic automation. Two were drawn as a playable artifact, "Work Board Options": a Board (every job in a column by where it stands) and Agents (every job under the named agent that does it, with its steps, its rules, a Run button and its earlier runs). The Board was recommended; the owner asked what the agents actually do, was told in plain English, and said *"Build the agents idea, merge to main then move it to be after the home page then move insights to below calendar."*

**WHAT THE DRAWING PRETENDED AND THE PRODUCT DOES NOT.** The artifact's agents ran jobs in the background, drafted answers with a model, took a "Send back with a note" and redid the work, and printed what they spent today. HaTi has none of that machinery and this codebase's rules refuse most of it: a model call with nobody's press behind it is spending that counts against nobody (Copilot's place, refusal 4), and a second way to accept or refuse the other side's change is a second door onto an act that already has one (refusal 5). What HaTi DOES have is five jobs it already does by itself — reading their round against the playbook (the dormant redline co-pilot, js/redlineplan.js), the overnight desk (notices, renewals, late promises), auto-triage on arrival, the overnight renewal memo, the import queue's reading of each file. So the page gathers those under the drawing's five names and adds no machinery at all.

**THE ONE DOOR, KEPT.** The drawing's round review had "File 9 answers as drafts". Building that means calling negoResolve and negoEditClause from a second page, and the negotiation page's own decide path carries the desk rule, the review gate, the accept guard and the live-link catch-up to the other side (`onDecided`). A copy of that path on another page is exactly the drift this codebase keeps paying for. The panel therefore shows the co-pilot's answer per ask — the verdict and the playbook figure it rests on, the same reading the clause panel's "Copilot's read" prints — and offers one door: the negotiation. f399 (1c) greps the page for every decision function.

**READING MUST NOT WRITE, AGAIN.** `negoUnsentAsks` passes through `negoPending` → `negoChanges` → `negoInit`, which creates a negotiation on a contract that has none. The round's last step ("Answered, not sent") needs that count, so it is asked only where `c.negotiation` already exists; f399 (4b) holds a contract with an ask and no negotiation byte-identical across a read of the whole page. The running import is read off `state.mig` raw, because `migState()` creates it.

**THE DESK'S REST, AND ONE STAMP.** Home's Prepared for you draws at most one row of each kind (deskShown) and its note said the desk would one day grow "a door onto the rest". This page is that door: it reads `deskItems` whole. Put away is `deskDismiss`, the desk's own stamp, so a row put away here is gone from Home too — found by driving it: putting a NOTICE away brings the contract's plain renewal row back (deskItems' `hasNotice` reads only rows not put away). That is the desk's existing rule, not this page's, and it is logged in BUGLOG rather than changed.

**WHAT WAS LEFT OUT, said to the owner**: Send back with a note, the Mine/Everyone switch, a spent-today figure, the phone. No band was added; the page head's facts line says "N ready for review · Nothing is sent or filed without you", a fact about what the page does, in the slot every inspector page paints.

Tests: f399 (23 claims in five sections — walls, registration, both books, the readings on a real stage, the page drawn; all 23 red at 231b9fc), agents-page-verify (29 checks in a real browser: the door and its count, the five agents, every panel button pressed and followed, the arrow keys, 1024 wide, the dark theme; every check but the stage and the error sweep red at the parent).

**AND THE DOOR MOVED UP, AND INSIGHTS MOVED DOWN, THE SAME DAY.** The owner's order had three parts — build it, merge it, then *"move it to be after the home page then move insights to below calendar"* — and the last part was done as a second change on top of the first. The place directly after Home had been Insights' since 21 Sep ("Insights tab should be after home page"), which had reversed 19 Sep's "after Obligations". Copilot's work takes that place, and Insights closes the Work group below Calendar. It is markup order and nothing else, as both earlier moves were: every door keeps its data-view, the "New" badge travels inside the Insights block, the four svg colour rules are keyed on the attribute. The note beside the Insights door names the ruling it reverses, which f338 (3f) holds. Two browser claims in four-off-the-screenshots-verify (3a, 3c) had been red since 21 Sep because they still described the 19 Sep place; they are re-pointed in place to the new one rather than left describing a place nobody wants.


### The brief that opened empty, and panels as full as the drawing (27 Sep 2026)

Two reports in one message, the same day the page was built: *"for many cards in there when i click on read brief, the panel comes up but it has no brief in it but when i go through the overview door the brief works. Also, the copilot cards are not comprehensive or detailed compared to the mock up in the artifact."*

**The empty brief.** Reproduced in a real browser on a contract with a brief written: the panel said *"Nothing has been briefed on this contract yet"*. The page is drawn off the LIGHT list, and the brief is transport (`_brief`) that rides only a single contract's own read; the list carries `_hasBrief`, which is why the button was drawn at all. "Read the brief" opened the room and the panel in the same breath, so the panel was drawn before the room's own load came back. The Overview's door worked because a reader reaches it after the room has loaded. The fix loads the whole record first — `agLoadWhole`, the Inspector's loader (`restoreHeavyFields`, which copies nothing over what is on screen), one flight shared by the panel and the door — and it goes into the funnel as well: `openCheckPanel`'s brief branch now loads a light record itself, says it is loading, and draws the brief when it lands. So a door added tomorrow cannot open it empty. The browser check that proves the funnel had to be moved off the Contracts page: that page's side panel loads the first row's record for its own reasons, and the first draft passed at the parent for that reason alone.

**The thin panels.** Measured against the approved artifact panel by panel: the drawing's panel carries the work itself — the letter, the message, the memo, the brief, the departures, the obligations found — and ours carried a handful of facts and a link. Every one of those is already on the record, so each is drawn from the reading that owns it: `noticeDraft(c).text` for the letter; the chase route's own dictionary keys, facts and language rule for the message (`agChaseMail`, and f399 6d pins the route's side so the two cannot drift); the renewal adviser's stored memo (`_renewalAdvice.data`: headline, reasons, what to push on) and the contract's own obligations for "how it went"; the brief, `c.playbook`'s open verdicts (their words beside your standard; a met standard is counted, never listed) and the obligations auto-triage holds, each under the arrival tile's own head; the import batch's files by name. The card gained the drawing's foot — who it is for and when — and NOT its cost, because HaTi books Copilot spend per person and per day, never per item, and a figure there would be invented. Nothing on the panel asks a model anything, and every act is still a door that already existed (adding the obligations found is `runFindObligations`, the one review dialog where each is ticked).

Found on the way and fixed as part of the same screen: the import panel printed "Could not be read" twice (a count, then the list naming them), and the panel's sticky foot stopped 18px short of the edge, so a long letter scrolled through the gap under the buttons.

Tests: f399 (6) — ten claims, all red at faa8f95. agents-page-verify 1i, 2b2, 3a2, 5a2, 6a2 and 10a–10f red at faa8f95, with two gates; 4a re-pointed in place (the tiles are opened sections now).

## THE BRAIN — HaTi AS NEURONS, READ FROM ITS OWN CODE (Young ruled 27 Sep 2026: "Put it as a page before home")

Built from the "HaTi Brain" artifact after rounds of changes on the concept: the three looks (Anatomy, Wiring, Layers) merged into one brain that glides between them (Young: "I want all 3 options in one"); "for every code update it should update brain automatically"; the side panel scrolls inside the stage's height; names that flashed for an instant were background sparks, so only the parts a flow LANDS on are named, each with its step number, and a step lasts 3.2s; zoom by pinch on an iPad, by wheel and by buttons; the caption 25% smaller; the colour key under the brain removed as redundant (the areas are named on the brain itself).

How "updates itself" was made real: the server reads its own files (js/ and server/) on the first request after it starts — which is every deploy — and compares the reading with the last one it kept. Read without a person: every named part and the file and line it lives on, the links between parts that the code really makes, every name the code publishes to window and every server route. Comments are stripped before links are looked for: this codebase explains itself at length, and a name in a note is not a hand-off — measured, the unstripped reading had 22 links and the honest one 14. A name that appears between two readings is a new part, drawn with its code name and "description pending" until someone writes its plain-English name into both dictionaries. Still a person's: the plain-English words, and the six flows, which are stories rather than wiring — the reading checks that every part a flow names is still in the code and says so on the step when it is not.

The one fault found by driving the real app: the page asked `api('/api/brain')`, and api() adds the prefix itself, so it asked for /api/api/brain and the update list said the code could not be read. The two explanation cards on the concept page ("Three views, one brain", "It updates itself") were not carried into the product: a page does not explain itself under its own title; the updates heading's hover carries that sentence instead.

Tests: f400 (22 claims, all red at the parent 972d681 — none of the files exist there), brain-page-verify (25 checks in a real browser, every one but the page-error sweep red at the parent).


# CLAUDE.md AS IT STOOD ON 27 SEP 2026 — SAVED WHOLE BEFORE THE THIRD CONDENSING (owner-asked: "Trim the rulebook back to rules only")

Every section below is verbatim. CLAUDE.md now keeps only the rule, the names that carry it and the tests; the story behind each is here, under the same heading. Where this block and an earlier entry above disagree, THIS block is the later word. New lessons from here on: the terse rule in CLAUDE.md, the full story appended at the end of this file under the same heading.

----- CLAUDE.md, 27 Sep 2026, follows -----

HaTi — Rules for Claude Code

The owner is not a developer. Explain everything in simple English. Keep summaries short and plain.

Do not rewrite the Bug Fix Rules section without asking the owner first. Updating THE MAP to match the code is encouraged and does not need permission — but say in the summary what changed.

THIS FILE IS THE CONDENSED RULEBOOK (condensed 2026-08-11 and again 2026-09-11, owner-approved both times). It is loaded whole at the start of every session and again after every compaction, so its size is paid for on every task: at 1.3 MB it took a third of the working window before any work began, which is why sessions were compacting twice per task. **Keep it small.** The full history — every war story, quoted bug report and design argument behind these rules — is in docs/MAP-HISTORY.md, with matching section headings. Read the matching section there BEFORE changing anything in that area.

**HOW A NEW LESSON LANDS: the terse rule goes HERE, in a few lines; the full story goes in docs/MAP-HISTORY.md under the same heading.** A section here is the rule, the names that carry it (the one function, the stale names to flag, the tests), and nothing else. If a section here runs past about twelve lines it has stopped being a rule and started being a story — move the story.

## Scope rules

- Do only what the current request asks. Nothing else.
- If you notice a separate problem (broken test, bad code,
  missing file, outdated dependency): DO NOT fix it.
  Write one line in BUGLOG.md under "Noticed, not fixed"
  and carry on with the original task.
- Broken tests that were already failing before this session
  are not your problem. Leave them red.
- If the request is unclear, stop and ask. Do not pick
  the wider interpretation.
- At the end, list anything you touched that was outside
  the request. If that list isn't empty, you broke this rule.

THE OWNER'S OWN WORDS, 24 Aug 2026. They sit ABOVE the Bug Fix Rules because they GOVERN them: Rule 2 says find every place a thing appears; this says do not fix the other things you find on the way. The finding still gets written down — one line in BUGLOG.md, never a fix.

**BUGLOG.md IS 8,000+ LINES OF RUN HISTORY — APPEND, NEVER WRITE.** One section per run, newest at the bottom: the defects found, then a "Noticed, not fixed" list. **READING IT IS DENIED ON PURPOSE** (`.claude/settings.json` denies `Read(./BUGLOG.md)` — it is 455 KB and would swallow a session); writing is not — since 14 Sep 2026 the same file's `permissions.allow` pre-approves the two append forms below by name, after a run in which every append was refused.
- To append: `cat >> ./BUGLOG.md <<'EOF' … EOF` or `tee -a ./BUGLOG.md >/dev/null <<'EOF' … EOF` — these two are pre-approved; any other form is not. Verify with `git diff --stat -- ./BUGLOG.md`.
- To read the house style: `git show HEAD:BUGLOG.md | tail -80` (reads the git object, not the path).
- A refusal on one verb is not a refusal on another — try the verb you actually need. `.claude/settings.json` is strict JSON and cannot carry a comment; an unknown key there can take the hooks down, which is why this note lives here.

## NO NEW BANDS ON THE PAGE — ASK FIRST (owner-asked 26 Aug 2026)

> *"I want to add a rule for claude to stop adding such alerts as attached unless I say so. I am talking about alerts that remind you of something minor assuming people are stupid. Think how SAP would manage such things and not unilaterally add these blinding alerts to the page. I asked for the send all stripe so keep that one. If Claude sees a need to add one, ask me first."*

**NEVER ADD A BAND, STRIP, NOTICE, BANNER, CALLOUT OR TIP TO A PAGE ON YOUR OWN INITIATIVE.** If one looks genuinely needed, ASK — say what it would say and why the screen cannot already say it.

**THE TEST, AND BOTH HALVES MUST PASS**, asked about the SCREEN:
1. Does it say something the screen does not already say? A control, count, heading or status word twelve pixels away that carries the fact makes the band that fact printed twice, and the second printing reads as an alarm.
2. Is it about work owed, or a promise made — and does it carry the act?

**THE READER'S OWN CHOICE, READ BACK TO THEM, IS NEVER A BAND.** A control set to something SAYS so by being set to it. **THE SAP RULE**: spend the least attention that does the job — a transient confirmation for something that just happened, an inline state for what a control already carries, a strip only for context that changes what the reader can do, a blocking dialog only for a decision that cannot proceed without them. Amber that is always there stops being read.

**WHAT STANDS**: the "N not sent" Send all (owner-asked by name — since 26 Aug the button alone, in the column head); the counterparty's wall line (decisions stay on their page until Send); a refusal's way forward on the same screen as the refusal; the side panel's "needs you" checklist (owner-picked by name, 27 Sep — see THE LIST INSPECTOR).

**IT CUTS BOTH WAYS: DO NOT DELETE BANDS EITHER.** Removing one is as much a change as adding one — a line in BUGLOG.md and a sentence to the owner, never a fix on the way past.

## THE SIX QUESTIONS, ASKED BEFORE ANY CODE IS WRITTEN (owner-asked 27 Aug 2026)

> *"...first think of how best in class systems in the CLM space approach the issue especially in the integration of AI to support the user, how SAP S/4HANA design in UI and UX would approach the matter, how to make sure it is easy to understand and navigate without adding banners and such for the user, ensuring you are not encroaching on the space allocated to the contract, smartly integrating copilot where copilot is being used and ensuring seamless flows."*

**WHEN THEY RUN**: whenever a change ADDS or MOVES something a person can see or press, or changes what the product SAYS. Never on a fix restoring stated behaviour, a rename, a test. In doubt, run them. **Five of the six carry a REFUSAL — a thing that does not happen without the owner's yes.** Where one bites, say so in a sentence BEFORE building, then build what the owner rules.

1. **THE STANDARD ANSWER.** What does serious contract software do with this shape of problem — where the fact lives, who decides it, what is recorded, what travels, what the reader is asked and when? Follow it or depart on purpose with one sentence of reason. **REFUSES: asserting a named product's behaviour you do not actually know.** Say "the general practice is X".
2. **THE CHEAPEST CHANNEL THAT CARRIES THE FACT.** First rung that works: nothing (already said) → on the control or in the object's header → transient confirmation → strip (only where it changes what the reader can do now) → blocking dialog. Facts in the header, work in a worklist, rules in settings, decisions in a dialog, history in the trail. **REFUSES: a new band, strip, banner, notice, callout or tip** (see NO NEW BANDS).
3. **THE CONTRACT'S PIXELS.** On any screen showing the agreement, measure from the top of the window to the first line of the wording, before and after. **REFUSES: any growth in that number.** Chrome that must grow takes pixels off other chrome, never off the paper. Furniture never follows the reader's text-size setting; the paper always does.
4. **COPILOT'S PLACE.** Beside the wording it is about; resting on something checkable (playbook, precedent, what the other side asked), never its own authority; spending on a press with the cost visible. **REFUSES: any path into the record that is not the funnel a person's edit uses, and any silent failure** — no key, a refusal, a cut-short answer, a cap: each says so where the reader is looking.
5. **THE ONE DOOR.** Does this act already have a way in? Improve that one. **REFUSES: a second door onto an act that already has one** — two doors drift, and two screens disagreeing about what the product does is this codebase's most expensive fault class.
6. **WHERE THE READER ENDS UP.** Walk the whole journey. Is there a way back, does it land where expected, does the number on a door match the list behind it, does a refusal carry its way forward on the same screen?

**THE ANSWERS STAY QUIET.** Work them internally; in the summary mention only the checks that CHANGED what was built, any you could not answer honestly, and any refusal you are asking the owner to lift. **THEY NEVER CHANGE WHAT IS BUILT AND NEVER WIDEN THE JOB**: anything they turn up beyond the request is one line in BUGLOG.md. Refusal 3 is a NUMBER and is not yet pinned in a browser file; the other four are judgements.

## DESIGN OPTIONS, AND THE PAGE CHECKLIST — TWO HABITS BORROWED FROM EMIL KOWALSKI'S SKILLS (owner-asked 24 Sep 2026)

> *"okay i want to borrow this"* — the method of the `prototype` skill and the four questions of the `apple-design` skill in github.com/emilkowalski/skills (MIT), put in HaTi's own words. **Written here, NOT installed**; that repo's other eleven skills are not adopted. "The prototype" elsewhere in this file still means HaTi's own approved reference design.

**DESIGN OPTIONS — how a DESIGN QUESTION is answered**: the owner asks how something should look, or for a new look or a redesign. An exact instruction is built as given, with no round of options.
- **ONE PART OF A PAGE PER ROUND.** "The whole page" is narrowed to the part that matters most; say which, and offer the rest as later rounds.
- **THREE BY DEFAULT, FIVE AT MOST, EACH A REALLY DIFFERENT IDEA** (layout, density, tone, how it is used), **NAMED FOR THAT IDEA** ("Quiet", "Dense"), never A/B/C. Two that differ only in colour or wording are ONE option: replace one, or show fewer and say so.
- **EVERY OPTION IS FINISHED WORK INSIDE HaTi'S OWN SYSTEM** — its tokens, faces and every rule in this file (NO NEW BANDS, THE SIX QUESTIONS, the contract's pixels), realistic HaTi content (contracts, names, figures, never filler text), anything pressable responding. One that breaks a rule is not an option.
- **SHOWN ONE AT A TIME, FULL SIZE, ON ITS REAL PAGE**, all in one Artifact with a switcher to flip between them (a button per option; the number and arrow keys on a keyboard; the flip is instant). Never shrunk side by side: small pictures lie about spacing and size.
- **WITH IT, A TABLE**: each option's idea, when it wins, what it costs; then one recommendation and its reason (who uses the page, and how often).
- **THE OWNER PICKS BY NAME; ONLY THAT ONE IS BUILT.** "Another round around X" draws new options around X.

**THE PAGE CHECKLIST — four questions**, asked of every option before it is shown and of any page the owner asks to have reviewed: (1) Is the most important thing the easiest to see? (2) Are related things grouped together? (3) Does each label say what's behind it? (4) Can you always tell where you are and how to get back? A "no" is fixed before the option is shown, or named as its cost; a review answers the four in plain English, a line each.

## Bug Fix Rules

1. DUPLICATION WARNING: This app draws the same UI in several places. Never assume a fix in one place fixes them all.

2. Before writing ANY code — a bug fix, a new feature, a refactor, or a cleanup — find every place the thing you are changing appears. Do this thoroughly and internally. Do NOT list file paths or locations back to me; I don't need to see them. Just make sure you have actually looked before you start.

3. Fix every place it appears. If you deliberately leave one alone, that decision must reach me in plain English — never silently.

4. Testing rule: test where the USER looks, not where you edited. Verify the result is visible in the actual browser view for every affected place, not just the file you changed.

5. At the end, write a short plain-English summary for a non-developer: what you fixed, whether it is fixed everywhere it appears, anything you deliberately left alone and why, and anything you were unsure about. No file paths, no line numbers, no location lists — just plain sentences about what happened.

## HOW TO TEST ECONOMICALLY (owner-asked 16 and 24 Aug 2026)

**"Do not run the full test suite during incremental edits. Only run the specific test file directly related to the changed code."** Every edit before you believe you are finished is incremental, including fixes to a test you just broke. Run the affected files together in ONE command (`node --test --test-reporter=dot test/<a>.test.js test/<b>.test.js`) until they pass; the full suite runs ONCE when you believe you are finished, and again only if that run found something.

- Full suite: **5m19s**, 8,521 tests in 1,655 suites, 0 red (re-measured 21 Sep 2026; it read 7,056 on 14 Sep and ~4,100 on 21 Aug — the runner is the authority, re-measure before quoting it). The browser set is **39 of 129 red**, the same 39 as the parent (re-measured 21 Sep 2026). A browser file starts a real Chrome and costs 11–40 SECONDS.
- `npm run lint` FIRST — seconds, zero errors is the bar (the ~137 warnings are unused locals; eslint.config.js explains every rule and holds KNOWN_ABSENT). It is the only check that asks "is every name being called a name that exists".
- While working: only the test files the feature's section names. One browser file per screen changed; re-run only after a change to what it measures.
- `node test/chromium/run-all.js` runs the whole browser set (four at a time) — what CI runs, not what you run while working. A file expected to fail is named in KNOWN_RED **with its reason**, printed on every run. **Take a file off that list the day it goes green.**
- **A TEST WHOSE ANSWER DEPENDS ON THE DAY IT RUNS IS WORSE THAN NO TEST.** Fixture dates carrying a calendar claim are built with `monthSpan(off)` or quarter boundaries, never by counting days from today (f183 was red 264 days of 730). Faking node's clock does NOT move jsdom's — rule out the instrument before believing the finding.

## STANDING LESSONS — the defect classes this codebase has paid for repeatedly

Each of these is recorded at length in docs/MAP-HISTORY.md; they are collected here because a new section keeps rediscovering them.

- **THE FILES ARE ES MODULES.** A top-level function is NOT a global; another module reaches it only through the `Object.assign(window, {…})` at the end of its file. A name missing from that list is unreachable, and every caller guarded on `window.foo && …` silently takes its fallback (the rlPaperFootHtml family — a placeholder drew for a year). **f232 is the net**: every `window.foo` READ must be a published name. Its DELIBERATE list is empty; `state` is read BARE everywhere (core.js declares it const; `window.state && …` silently disabled the review gate once). f48 catches the opposite fault (two modules publishing one name) and f232-6 catches one module DECLARING a name another publishes (a hoisted private `lsGet` once captured setView's calls and lost the reader's page on refresh).
- **THE BROWSER HARNESSES DO NOT LOAD index.html.** test/chromium/*.html, test/world.js and test/portalworld.js build their own script lists as CLASSIC scripts — so a new file in js/ is not on them until added, and an unpublished name resolves there when it would not in the product. Run f232 before believing a green browser run on anything that crosses a module boundary.
- **A GUARD THAT IS ALWAYS FALSE, A RULE THAT LOSES A CASCADE FIGHT, AN ATTRIBUTE NOTHING LISTENS FOR, A COMMENT THAT SWALLOWS THE RULE UNDER IT** — four costumes of one fault: nothing errors, nothing logs, the source looks correct. When a rule looks right and the screen looks wrong, MEASURE the computed value in a browser before editing the declaration; fix cascade fights by SCOPE, never `!important`. Never write the CSS comment terminator inside a CSS comment (say "terminator"). Never a backtick in a `<style>` block emitted from a JS template literal — a balanced pair EVALUATES what is between them; f236 is the net.
- **THE COMPILED TAILWIND BLOB IN index.html IS GENERATED.** Never edit it; write overrides in HaTi's own sheet at equal specificity, later in source. Find it by its signature, never a line number. `font-600`, `font-700`, `.sr-only`, `.rounded-full` and four other classes are defined in HaTi's sheet because nothing else defined them.
- **THE GETTER TRAP.** An object literal freezes load-time language; `{...f}` and `Object.fromEntries` INVOKE getters. Use per-key getters and copy by descriptor. A label that is also a RECORD keeps English (RELATION_DOC_WORD, ROLE_LABEL, clauseLabel, audit lines).
- **READING MUST NOT WRITE.** `negoChanges`/`negoAllChanges`/`negoRound`/`negoClauseList` call `negoInit`, which CREATES a negotiation and stamps clause ids. A count or a reading over the book reads `c.changes` and `c.negotiation` RAW.
- **THE LIGHT LIST.** In server mode `state.contracts` is the LIGHT list and HEAVY strips `audit`, an upload's extracted text and more. A reading off the trail is right locally and empty in production (the dashboard's "raised by me", Reports' cycle time, the desk's renewal note). Carry the fact as transport (`_raisedBy`, `_hasBrief`, `_renewalPrep`), stripped on save.
- **THE SERVER IS THE WALL; THE BROWSER IS COSMETICS.** A rule enforced only in pixels holds until somebody sends the request. Guards on PUT /api/contracts/:id are asked as a DIFFERENCE against the STORED record. A route must never read an address out of the body (the open-relay rule) — it looks the person up.
- **"SENT" MUST MEAN SENT.** `mailReport(r)` is the one shape — sent / configured / outbox / error; the outbox is honest delivery, not failure. A `sent_at` stamped whatever the provider did is a lie for the life of the record.
- **A CAP IS A FACT, NEVER A SILENT TRIM.** What was left out is counted and said. An answer cut short (stop_reason) is not an empty answer and is not cached as a whole one. **An absence is stated, never guessed** — null is the honest answer where the record says nothing.
- **A BARE `toast(msg)` PRINTS NOTHING** — kinds are ok / warn / err (TOAST_KINDS, every kind has a dwell, none is zero). An act that leaves the building confirms itself with 'ok'. A stage stub kinder than the real function turns its test into a description.
- **PIN THE RELATION, NOT THE NUMBER.** A test pinning a literal px, colour or count where the claim is a relation costs an edit at every retune and passes on the wrong thing. `test/tokens.js` resolves a token so a test can read a number without typing one.
- **A CHECK THAT PASSES AGAINST THE PARENT IS A DESCRIPTION.** Run a new check against the commit before the fix; a block that hand-writes the shape the product produces passes before the product could produce it. Every driven half of a browser file is GUARDED so a build without the feature REPORTS its failures rather than timing out. A probe that throws proves nothing.
- **PHOTOGRAPH WHAT YOU BUILT.** Read the rendered page, not the source — a card contradicting itself, a dead press, an empty tile with a tick, a rule scoped to the wrong home, are all only visible on screen. Playwright scrolls an element into view before clicking; `.nego-scroll` animates; re-query after a repaint; a probe's own sentinel is not data.
- **THE CLOTHES FOLLOW THE BUILDER.** A control drawn by a shared builder must be dressed by a rule that reaches every home it is drawn in; a rule scoped to one home leaves the other unstyled. Two surfaces may DRAW differently; the READING (which change a clause shows, whose move, is this overdue, which playbook applies) never may — find the question both answer and make it one function.
- **A STANDALONE DOCUMENT CARRIES NO `:root`.** healthreport.js, weekly.js, negoHistoryExportHtml, the memo's clipboard HTML: every value there is a literal; a `var()` resolves to nothing. Charts paint to canvas and need real values too.
- **CHECK THE REMOTE BEFORE MEASURING.** Start from the latest main; "this was already broken" is proved by running the file in a worktree at unmodified main, never asserted.
- **THE COLOUR CENSUS** (theme-tokens-verify, 20 screens × 2 themes) is re-recorded ONLY by somebody deliberately owning a palette change, audited value by value as a SET DIFFERENCE first, in the same commit — never to make a red run go away, and never absorbing somebody else's regression (restore that line by hand). Re-measure before quoting its score.

## THE MAP — how changes get filed (verified 2026-08-03)

Doc Lab is REMOVED — flag any doclab mention as stale.

ONE funnel files every negotiation change: negoFileChange() (js/negotiation.js). Guards that must apply to ALL changes belong here, in this order: deskClaimOnFile, then deskBlockMessage (reversed, no contract can ever start). Wrappers feeding it: negoEditClause, negoInsertClause, negoDeleteClause. Entry paths: direct edit, clause library insert, Copilot (PLUS a shortcut in js/core.js that calls negoFileChange directly — put fixes in the funnel), Playbook (TWO entrances: js/playbook.js and rlFilePlaybookProposal in js/views/negotiation.js), Word DOCX round-trip, the side door in js/views/portal.js that pushes ALREADY-FILED changes wholesale (legitimate — re-verify after any change to the change object's shape).

RULE OF THUMB: a fix touching change objects → `grep -rn "changes.push|negoFileChange(" js/` and account for every hit.

FORMATTING-ONLY CHANGES file with formattingOnly and "Formatting changed — the wording is unchanged". Fingerprints are hashV over the stored rich body verbatim; older versions verify under their own version forever (`NEGO_HASH_VERIFIES` is a SET) — NEVER re-sanitise a stored bodyHtml after filing. Both pending-change renderers (negoDocHtml, redlineDocHtml) carry the formatting-only branch.

THE FUNNEL'S OTHER GUARDS: the no-op guard (nothing changed — also refuses typing the original wording back over a pending ask, and filing the very wording a pending draft already carries); an insertion with no words is refused (a heading alone is not enough); the executed-wording freeze (`negoWordingFrozen = negoExecuted || negoAnySignature`, asked BEFORE the desk rule); the counterparty may not RENAME our clauses (a `modify` from their seat drops `headingText` and keeps the edit); a counter on a clause carrying another side's pending change SUPERSEDES it (see ONE PROPOSAL ON THE TABLE); the clause lock (see ONE CLAUSE, ONE PAIR OF HANDS).

## INTERNAL REVIEW — the step before a change is sent (js/review.js)

A colleague is asked by name, rules on each change (cleared / held on ours, advice on theirs), hands back. A HELD change never travels.
- The hold is enforced in buildSharePayload UNCONDITIONALLY (reviewHeldIds into holdUnsent, no opts flag). THREE send doors ask reviewSendBlock / reviewGateMessage: the share dialog's doSend, reshareToLastRecipient (THROWS), the workbench's #nego-send. A fourth must ask too.
- The counterparty must NEVER learn a review happened. reviewSeatShowsReview() is the one predicate (refuses readonly, side==='counterparty', PORTAL_MODE).
- The gate is a SETTING (admin, OFF by default; per-person since 13 Aug — reviewGateApplies(c,u), rvGateApplies on the server; `reviewChecked(u)` is `!== false`, absence = checked; a named standing reviewer prefills #rv-who). It gates SENDING; the approval chain gates SIGNING; the desk gates REDLINING.
- Traps: read `state` BARE; READING MUST NOT WRITE — only reviewAsk and reviewMark initialise c.review (f59).
- A reviewer may correct wording: folds into the SAME change (revisions[], new fingerprint, revisedBy stamped when reviser ≠ author). f158.
- A review is a CHOSEN SUBSET (rv.changeIds); reviewInOpen(c,ch) is the predicate. SEVERAL REVIEWS AT ONCE, per CHANGE: reviewOpenFor(c,ch) (not reviewOpenOf); one change in at most one review; mark/cancel/return act on a NAMED review; reviewState(c) returns lists from the READER's chair; the banner is a LIST of rows, drawn only while their clauses are pending.
- VISIBILITY: reviewMaySee(rv,u) (reviewer/requester/admin — names flow ONLY through it), reviewMayCancel (requester/admin), reviewActorHeld / reviewActorBlockMessage. Everyone else sees status without a name. The audit trail still names reviewers; it never travels.
- A reviewer is NARROWED while their ask is open (rlActorHeld view-side, asked by FIVE canAct renderers: negoLiveCardsHtml, negoHeadHtml, negoPanesHtml, negoRoomActionsHtml, redlineChangeCardsHtml; the model refuses too). Their column narrows to reviewMyChangeIds / rlMyCardIds (four lists); the DOCUMENT folds to their clauses (rlRvDocClauses, both doc renderers; _rlRvFullDoc per sitting, one delegated listener). Round-governing controls undrawn. ONE hand-back door: the toolbar (openReviewReturnPicker; reviewTagsFor names CHANGE ids).
- reviewInPlay(c,rv) is the ONE population (the review's still-pending changes) for banner, progress, refusal, posture, server rvInPlay. A review with nothing in play is SPENT (reviewSpent) and stops drawing and narrowing; the server keeps the raw rvOpenList at its structural guards.
- Details: RV_NOTE_MAX; the picker is a COMBOBOX (name AND email); reviewCandidates refuses a person who cannot open the contract (folderScopeFor on the server, f160). Never `class="ui-input"` — use HATI_FLD / HATI_LBL (js/review.js keeps its own pair on purpose, reading `var(--field-*)`). reviewDialogHeadHtml builds every dialog head here and in js/desk.js (.rvd-* classes in index.html, f175).
- DELIVERY AND CANCEL: reviewNoteDelivery files on rv.notice and the trail; reviewDeliveryState(rv) is what screens print (null on an older review). The link is contractUrl(req,id,tab) (openFromHash honours 'redline'). Cancel is in the notice (unfolded while reviewWantsAttention) and reviewCardCancelHtml on both card renderers, with reviewCancelCost on the confirm. f186, f155, f172.
- WHO MAY REOPEN: a refusal is reopened by the side that GAVE it, never the side that received it. Our page: Reopen on THEIR refused change; Withdraw on OURS. Their page mirrors.
- Cards: ONE status slot; HELD = ruby, OUT FOR REVIEW = amber; reviewWithheldIds() is the union the payload subtracts. Gate OFF → Send WARNS (reviewSendWarning), never both mechanisms. Every unsent card carries a scoped ask (data-rl-ask-review); the toolbar button is always a door (ask ↔ hand-back); the ask posture opens openReviewEntryChooser ("Assign contributors" / "Send for review"). f171.
- THE SERVER IS THE AUTHORITY: rvOpenList / rvOpenFor / rvWithheldIds / rvActorHeld / rvUnreviewedIds off the STORED contract. POST /api/shares refuses a sender holding an open review, refuses unreviewed content when the gate is on, STRIPS held/out-for-review and returns withheldByReview. PUT guards as a DIFFERENCE (verdict by the named reviewer only, cancel by requester/admin, hand-back by the reviewer, no edits to an open review's ids). DECIDING ≠ RECEIVING: negoResolve records the decider; inbound decisions pass. If browser and server disagree, f162 is right.
- "WAITING ON THEM" HAS TO BE TRUE: negoTheirCopy(c) answers 'live' / 'none' / 'unknown' (PORTAL_MODE always 'unknown'); negWhoseMove asks negoUnsentAsks FIRST (why:'unsent') and where they hold no copy the move is ours (why:'nocopy'). The share cache flag is ON THE CONTRACT (c._shareFetch). f190.
- WHICH LINK IS THEIRS: shareIsStanding(s) (durable, not revoked, not expired — the client's reading of what PUT /api/shares/:token/payload accepts); standingShareFor(shares,contact) for the ROUND SEND ONLY (the link the contact came from, then address, then name, then newest standing); the share dialog matches the typed address and gets NO fallback. A round send catches up every other standing link; a stranded second link is said out loud (reshareStrandedLine, four surfaces). f17.
- Live-link catch-up: refreshLiveShareQuietly (js/core.js) is the one updater; WHOEVER MOUNTS the component supplies onDecided/onWithdraw. Only ANSWERS travel down a live link. f174.

Tests: f154–f159, f161, f162, f164, f186, f190.

## KEY TERMS HAS A DIVIDER, AND THE RIGHT-HAND CARD SCROLLS (owner-asked 19 Aug 2026; **SUPERSEDED 16 Sep 2026 — see THE OVERVIEW. `.terms-grid`, `#kt-resizer`, ktFitSplit and ktWireSplit are STALE; the negotiation page's and the builder's dividers are ports of the same mechanism and are LIVE**)

`.terms-grid` is card · handle · card. The RIGHT column stretches to the grid and scrolls inside itself (`#kt-side`); the LEFT card is its own height. **The column takes the height, the card in it takes its content: `flex:0 0 auto` — SHRINK IS 0** (10 Sep 2026: shrink 1 let cards be squeezed below content height and spill over each other instead of scrolling; `#renewal-host` too). It is the negotiation divider's own mechanism (ktFitSplit / ktWireSplit mirror rlLayoutResizer: pointer position, never distance travelled; KT_LEFT_MIN 320 / KT_RIGHT_MIN 300; `hati.v1.ktLeftFrac`; arrows 2%, double-click resets). Below 980px it stacks and the fraction is READ, NEVER WRITTEN. Bound once per element (dataset.ktSplitBound). Tests: f176, f280 (1)-(2), amendment-journey-verify.

## AN AMENDMENT IS WRITTEN HERE, NOT ONLY FILED HERE (js/family.js, owner-asked 14 Aug 2026)

- Agreement family card sits in the Key terms side column; Obligations moved to a row on the Checks card (its panel BORROWS `obligations-section` by id). `editableFor=kind=>mayEdit&&(kind==='oblig'||kind==='brief'||c.status!=='Signed')`. obligationSurfacesChanged is the funnel that repaints every obligation surface.
- `fa_add_amendment` is RETIRED. Acts in `.fam-acts`: Create an amendment + Link an existing document where a document can have children; "Link to a parent agreement" on a STANDALONE only; a child gets Unlink alone.
- Create MINTS A DRAFT AND FILES IT IN THE SAME BREATH. Carried: counterparty, address, party, stream, letterhead, valueType. NOT carried: value, effective date, obligations, signers. Name keeps ENGLISH (RELATION_DOC_WORD), numbered PER KIND (amendmentOrdinal). Body always written (skeleton of four English paragraphs, or FAMILY_BLANK_BODY).
