## NO BRACE REACHES THE PAGE (Young reported it 20 Sep 2026)

*"where copilot generates information … i see this sign {} being generated. Fix this bug to Remote it from Outputs."* **THE RENDERER IS THE WALL, NEVER THE PROMPT** — `AI_TONE_RULES` is already written as duties with a worked example because asking nicely came back with no markers at all; a tighter sentence is one more thing a model may ignore on any given answer, and the reader would still see the braces.
- **THREE SHAPES, every one reproduced against `aiToneHtml` before a line moved**: DOUBLED BRACES (`{{+78%}}`, `{+78%}}`, `{{+78%}`) — the old pattern matched the INNER pair and left the outer ones standing, which is the owner's screenshot; **BOLD INSIDE A MARKER** (`{+**78%**}`), which the prompt ASKS FOR by instruction (one rule bolds every figure, another wraps the verdict), so `mdParse` makes it `<strong>` and the old body class `[^{}<>]` refused the `<`; and a doubled brace with NO tone character, the model garbling its own emphasis.
- **FOUR PATTERNS, ONE READING.** `AI_TONE_RE` makes both braces optional on each side so all four counts fold to one span; its body admits only NAMED INLINE tags (`AI_TONE_INLINE`) — a BLOCK tag would mean the marker ran across a paragraph, and a span wrapped round `</p><p>` is broken nesting. `AI_TONE_LOOSE_RE` unwraps a doubled pair carrying no tone character to its words and gives it NO colour (which verdict was meant is not knowable, and picking one is the product asserting one nobody wrote). `AI_TONE_ORPHAN_RE` is the last net — anything that HAD a closer is already a span, so a `{` still in front of a tone character is a marker the model never finished. `AI_TONE_SPLIT_RE` runs on the RAW text inside `aiRichText`, because a marker crossing a blank line is cut by `mdParse` and its closer is stranded in the NEXT paragraph.
- **THE WALL: `{{counterparty}}` KEEPS ITS BRACES.** That is this product's own template-blank syntax (`AI_TEMPLATE_RULE` asks the model for `{{lower_snake_case}}`), so the loose unwrap is guarded on the body containing a SPACE — emphasis is a phrase, a blank is one word.
- **TWO SURFACES, ONE READING, MEASURED**: `aiToneHtml` has no caller outside js/aimd.js and `aiRichText` has exactly two — the chat bubble (`aiFmt`) and Copilot's read on the Insights dock (`igFmtRich`) — which are the two screens the owner named.

Sep 2026" with a stepper and wants far more than the 226px share**, so the track grew and the form painted over the contract beside it. `FIELD_GRID_CSS` (js/templatefields.js, published) is the ONE declaration — `minmax(0,1fr)` — read by all three doors that ask these questions (the essentials, the wizard's answer step, the saved-template fill), with the literal as the fallback for a stage that has not loaded that file. **THE OTHER HALF CANNOT BE WRITTEN INLINE**: `.field-grid > *{min-width:0}` lets the item shrink to its track and `.field-grid input,.field-grid select{max-width:100%;min-width:0}` stops the control painting past its own box. The offer card says which shelf it came off, read off the record and never off `why`. **THE LEAD SAYS WHERE COPILOT LOOKS FIRST AND STOPS THERE** — the POP-UP DIET pins `dr_lead` by name, so the other half (that you may ask for another shelf in your own words) rides the ask box's own hover, `dr_shelf_hint`, which is the diet's answer for machinery and the one control where knowing it changes what a reader types.
- **THE PICKER SHOWS YOUR OWN PAPER, AND HAS A WAY OUT.** The note above `lib` in js/wizard.js says company standards "stay pinned on top"; MEASURED, they were not drawn on that screen AT ALL — `lib` and `mine` reached only `rows`, which feeds the folders and the search, so the only paper a reader could SEE was four HaTi built-ins, and reaching your own standard meant knowing its stream or its name. `ours` draws them in ONE section above FOR YOU (one, not two — that screen already carries a curated row, a line of business, a search box and six folders, and the ask was to make it LESS confusing), drawn only when non-empty. ## A DOCUMENT SOMEBODY SENT US HAS BLANKS TOO (Young ruled 20 Sep 2026: "build it", item 9)

MEASURED: `contractHasBlanks` refused every upload BY NAME, so a received document carrying `[Insert Company Name]` twice and two ruled lines answered `[]` — no panel, no count, and the arrival tile reporting "nothing to fill" on the one kind of contract whose blanks nobody in this workspace wrote. `js/uploadblanks.js` is the reading: no route, no store, no new field (f342 (3f) greps).
- **THE PAPER IS THE ANSWER**, as it is for a drafted contract. Three shapes — `[Insert Company Name]`, `{{effective_date}}`, `_{3,}` — and the REFUSALS are the design: a bracket with no letter, a list marker or citation (`[1]`, `[a]`, `[iv]`), over 60 characters, or carrying `<`/a newline (the walk crossed an element boundary — `redlineHangHtml`'s rule); an underscore run flanked by word characters is part of a word.
- **THE MARKS ARE PAINTED ONTO THE CANVAS, NEVER BUILT INTO `docBody`** — `signSpotsPaint`'s and `docDutyPaperPaint`'s own precedent, third on `wireDocCanvas` and for the third time the same reason: docBody TRAVELS (their page, the PDF, the phone), and the C-7 header block was proved doing it on two real links. **Nothing serialises a painted canvas**, so our answers stay a working note on our own screen. `[data-upwording]` scopes the walk to the agreement, so HaTi's own signature block, file strip and seal card are never marked.
- **ONE MATCHER, TWO WALKS, AND THE PAINT NEVER MINTS A KEY.** The READ walks the wording SOURCE (so it answers in Node, at creation, before anything is mounted); the PAINT walks the canvas and takes its keys from `uploadBlankSeq`. **A WALK THAT DISAGREES WITH THE READ BY ONE CHARACTER DRAWS NOTHING** (`ceMarksPaint`'s rule) — count and `raw` both checked — so if a renderer ever did move a word the marks go quiet rather than land on the wrong sentence.
- **THE KEY IS THE PLACEHOLDER'S OWN NAME** (`up_insert_company_name`), so a name said through a twelve-page draft is ONE question answered once and marked everywhere. A ruled line has no name and takes the words in front of it, cut at the last sentence end (`…for one year. Delivery address: ____` asks for an address), with an ordinal where two follow the same words. Its own namespace, so it can never be `counterparty` or `value`.
- **NOTHING IS GUESSED**: `kind:'upload'` is what keeps these out of `fillBlanksFromRecord` (which filters `kind === 'field'`) — we did not draft the document, so we do not know whose side `[Company Name]` names. A person types them, through `contractBlankSet`, the ONE writer.
- **IT STOPS WHEN THE WORDING BECOMES OURS**: `uploadBlanksLive` refuses a redlined or versioned upload (`uploadWordingEdited`), a sealed record, a Viewer and PORTAL_MODE. **It is `docFillable`'s COUNTERPART, never its rival** — that reading refuses every upload by name and this one refuses everything else — which is what makes the panel's `||` one door rather than two. Asserted as a wall.
- The panel says `bf_title_upload`; the one fact about the machinery is a HOVER (`bf_upload_note`), never a band; an unnamed line is `bf_blank_n`. The mark is amber unanswered, the accent answered, and **costs the contract no layout** (measured block by block, off and on).
Tests: f342 (58 claims, **56 red at the parent**; the two that pass are named CONTROLS), upload-blanks-verify (29 checks in a real browser, **26 red**; every claim an empty page would satisfy is GATED).

### AND THE THIRD SHAPE: A WORD FILL-IN FIELD (Young ruled 20 Sep 2026: "Build the last item")

The artifact the owner approved promised *"brackets, underscores, a shaded Word field"*; the build above delivered the first two. MEASURED on a real .docx: a FORMTEXT field and a content control both arrive as ORDINARY SENTENCE TEXT (`"made with Enter buyer name of Click or tap here to enter text.."`) — both readers keep the result and drop everything saying it is a field. There is no pattern in the characters to find, so **THE FILE IS WHAT KNOWS** and `docxRunsHtml` marks it on the way in.
- **`DOCX_WFIELD_CLASS` / `RICH_WFIELD_CLASS` = `hati-wfield`**, admitted to `richSpanClassOk` beside `RICH_TOC_TAIL_CLASS` and for its reason: a SHAPE, not a mark, carrying no value of its own — the prompt is the span's own text. **NOT `hati-field`**, which means a blank on OUR template form routed by `data-field-key`. The drafter's own name (`w:name` / `w:alias`) rides as `data-wfield`, in EXACTLY `RICH_FIELD_KEY_RE`'s machine-safe shape and only on that span — Word's stock prompt is UI chrome, so without the name every gap in a real form would share one key.
- **ONLY AN UNANSWERED FIELD IS A BLANK, and Word says which**: `w:showingPlcHdr` on a control; a FORMTEXT whose result is empty or still its own default. A field somebody filled is their wording and is untouched. A tick box or a dropdown is not a gap for wording.
- **THE TEXT DOES NOT MOVE BY A CHARACTER**: only `html` is wrapped, so the two readers still project the same string (f257's wall, and the one the Word round trip rests on), and marking a field moves the stored projection by NOTHING. A mark begins and ends BETWEEN runs, so it can never cross a bold or italic wrapper.
- **TWO SANITISER PASSES HAD TO LEARN IT, and both were found by driving a real form**: the empty-block sweep deleted the span AND its characters (Word pads an empty box with non-breaking spaces, which do not survive `.trim()`), and the source-indentation sweep took the padding — each leaving `the fee is .` against the plain reader's `the fee is      .`, which is the phantom-change fault. Exempted exactly as `<pre>` is.
- **`report.fields` joins `docxHasStructure`**: a Word FORM is plain paragraphs with grey boxes, so without it the one kind of file this reading exists for stores no body at all.
- **THE PAPER'S OWN SPAN IS MARKED IN PLACE, NEVER UNWRAPPED** (`UP_MADE_ATTR` tells the painter's spans from the paper's); `upNodeHits` is the ONE per-node reading both walks ask, so a field is one unit and its words are never read twice.
Tests: f343 (28 claims, **24 red at the parent**; the four that pass are named CONTROLS), upload-blanks-verify section 8 (10 checks, **all 10 red**). **Noticed, not fixed**: `richToText` collapses a run of non-breaking spaces, so the STORED body's projection differs from the plain reader's on any nbsp-padded document — measured identical at the parent with no field span involved, so pre-existing and far outside this request.

### A FILE THEY SIGN HAS NO BLANKS FOR US TO FILL (Young, 26 Sep 2026)

*"if the contract is being signed out of hati … these fields are irrelevant I would presume."* Right: on the outside route what travels is the agreed WORDING (`outsideAgreedHtml`), never these answers, and the blanks are filled in their own copy.
- **`uploadBlanksTheirs(c)`** (an upload on the outside route; `signRouteOf`, the literal as fallback) is the ONE reading; `uploadBlanksLive` asks it, so the panel, the marks, the count and the arrival read stand down together. A drafted contract on that route keeps its blanks (our paper — its answers are in the words).
- **The tile says why**: `contractBlanksNone` answers `theirs` (asked BEFORE `upload`, whose sentence would be false); `tri_t_fill_theirs` / `tri_fill_theirs`, steel; `triageTiles` asks the route LIVE both ways (a note's open count stops counting; a recorded `theirs` is not believed once switched back).
- **A reading, never a delete**: typed answers stay on the record and come back with the route. **The handover's own check is untouched** (`outsideBlanksOf`: a placeholder written into the agreed words still holds it).
Tests: f342 (7)(8) (14 claims, 11 red at the parent; 7g/8d CONTROLS, 7h a WALL), upload-blanks-verify 9 (the real door pressed; 3 red, the rest GATE and CONTROLS).

## THE BRIEF TILE PULLS THE BRIEF, AND A FIELD'S NAME IS NOT BOLD (Young ruled 20 Sep 2026)

- *"Brief Witten is supposed to pull the brief side Panel but it does not."* It **scrolled to `#brief-card`** — the card ABOUT the brief rather than the brief itself — so the reader landed beside a heading and still had to find its Open button, which is exactly what the tile's arrow promises to have done for them. **TWO DOORS, ONE ACT**: the tile presses `openCheckPanel(c,'brief')`, the very call the card's own `data-kt-brief="open"` button makes, so the two cannot drift about what "open the brief" means and the panel, its 500px width and its filling all stay `openCheckPanel`'s. The door is drawn only where the brief was WRITTEN (`doorFor` asks `x.ok`), so it can never open on nothing. The obligations tile is untouched — a TAB is the right destination for it.
- *"the names of the fields are currently in bold grey letters. They should not be in bold letters. The answered fields should stay in black bold letters."* `.sec-f-l` gives up its WEIGHT alone (`--w-title` → `--w-body`) and keeps the product's own label treatment — the micro size, the uppercase, the `.09em` — so what carries the eye down the card is the ANSWER. **`.sec-f-v` and `.sec-f-v.is-none` ARE UNTOUCHED** and are pinned as walls: an answered field was already `--w-strong` in the page's own ink and an em-dash already light and grey. **`.ov-reads th` is deliberately NOT swept** — a table head is not a field name, and every other table in the product keeps 700.

### THE FOUR EVERYDAY PAGES, AND THE GREY THAT WAS TOO FAINT (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

*"The home page in HaTi, contracts, negotations and calendar need to look exactly like the artifact. Pay attention to the relationship between grey fonts and black fonts in the artifact as well and apply them accordingly. There is a lot of faint grey that makes reading a bit hard. As far as the home page, the the prepared for you card and the needs your attention card have the same width as the space utilized by the combination of the top 4 cards."*

- **THE TWO HOME CARDS TAKE THE TILES' OWN WIDTH, AND THE ARTIFACT ITSELF DOES NOT.** Its `.stack` is capped at 1100 while its KPI row fills the page — the exact mismatch the owner is pointing at — so HaTi's `hmCard` states no width and MEASURES the tiles' (1334 at left 80, both, checked on every render). `hmSec` takes a card flag and `.hm-card` is the shell; the row's left tone bar is the reference's `.hm-rdot` now; the **"My work" heading is gone** (`home_my_work` STALE, inert in both books — four tiles that name themselves need no name above them), and the fourth default tile is `active_value`, not `avgcycle`.
- **THE INK LADDER: HaTi IS ONE STEP DARKER THAN THE REFERENCE WHEREVER THE REFERENCE USES ink-3, AND STAYS THERE.** The reference's `--ink-3` is HaTi's `--color-neutral-400`, which this file has recorded as failing AA as text since 22 Aug. A column head, a row's sub-line, a card head's sub and a tile's detail are all FACTS and read at `--color-neutral-500` or 600. **The faintest step is for an ABSENCE or for FURNITURE** — measured, what is left on these four pages is the idle sort arrow, the em-dash meaning the agreement says nothing, and an adjacent month's day number. Nothing else. **The census is the instrument**: every element that paints its own visible text, with its colour, read off a real page — three of the four Home tile figures were drawing 26px in the faintest grey and no rule in the source looked wrong.
- **THE ROW IS 13px, WHICH IS THE OWNER'S OWN NUMBER.** WO-16 ruled 14 down to THIRTEEN and it was written as `--t-meta`, which the redesign's ladder later made 12 — so the row had gone one rung further than anybody ruled. `.reg-table` is `--t-body` and so are `.reg-mk`, the badge, `.ngl-w` and the four inline sizes in the row region that had been left behind. **The title is `--w-label` in the page's own ink over a 12px sub-line in the quiet ink**, which is the reference's `.tbl td .t{font-weight:500;color:var(--ink)}` and IS the relationship the owner asked for. **TWO `.reg-table th` RULES AT EQUAL WEIGHT IN TWO SHEETS** were folded into one — the winner was whichever was injected first.
- **THE NEGOTIATIONS HEAD IS A SUB-LINE, LIKE EVERY OTHER PAGE'S.** "2 live · 2 waiting on you" under the name, not a steel chip beside it; `.ngl-live` KEEPS its class (four tests reach it by name) and is dressed at `.ngl-head-table .ngl-live` — **by SCOPE, because `.page-facts` and `.ngl-live` both score (0,1,0)** and source order would have decided it. The second half BORROWS `negoBandCounts(negoGroupByMove(…))`, the band's own arithmetic, so head and band cannot disagree. The band count is IN its heading (`· 2`), no pill.
- **THE CALENDAR'S MONTH IS SAID ONCE.** The stepper (`calMonthStepHtml`, the same three ids) moved into the page sub-line, so the grid card begins with the weekday row exactly as the reference's does; `.cal-cardbar` stays for the Horizon. **The agenda window is a segment of four numerals** (`data-cal-days`, id `cal-days` KEPT) — this REVERSES "the heading IS the control" of 24 Aug, whose objection is still written beside the code: the owner has seen the drawing and a window changed four times a sitting is the wrong place to charge two presses. ONE VALUE still answers the heading, the lit half, the reading and the empty state.
- **NOT BUILT, and each would invent something**: the reference's KPI sparklines (a trend HaTi does not hold), a search box on the Contracts page (the shell bar's already narrows it — one door), its own quick-filter tab set, and its Round / Open asks / Last move / Owner columns on Negotiations. The value-stream cell elides because HaTi's stream names are four words where the reference's are one; the whole name is on the hover.

### THE SHELL BAR WEARS THE WORKSPACE'S OWN COLOUR (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

*"The top highlighted bar, make it the color of the color mode the user chooses, Green on blue. Adjust the rest of the features to fit in without disappearing in the background."*

**THIS REVERSES HALF OF DECIDE 4** (20 Sep, "the dark 44px bar is gone"), and only the half about the BAR: the rail still runs floor to ceiling in white with the mark at its top, the bar is still 48px in the page column, and it still keeps every control it had.
- **THE GROUND IS `--nav-bg`, THE TOKEN IT WORE BEFORE THE REDESIGN** — #093733 green, #0F2648 navy, its own answer under dark — stated on the element, because the rest of this bar's geometry is an inline style and no stylesheet rule could have reached past it. Nothing here names a colour; the brand moves and the bar moves with it.
- **FIVE TOKENS ON THE BAR, READ BY EVERY RULE UNDER IT**, because "so they do not disappear" is a ladder and not a list: `--bar-ink` for a control that carries a word, `--bar-ink-2` for furniture, `--bar-line` for an edge, `--bar-well` for an inset, `--bar-hover`. **WHITE AT AN ALPHA over the ground**, so each brand and the dark theme compose their own. **THE FOCUS RING IS WHITE, NOT THE ACCENT** — the accent ramp IS this ground, so an accent ring on it is a ring nobody sees; the one rule that could not simply be re-tokened.
- **THE WELL IS 10%, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT.** At the bar's own earlier 14% the ⌘K chip (a well inside the search box's well) falls to 4.38:1; at 10% it is 5.55:1. Two stacked translucent layers are the thing to measure here.
- **EVERY CONTROL WAS RE-INKED** and each was read off a real page: the title, the crumb and its separator, the search box and its placeholder, the ⌘K chip, the language pair (its own class and its own accent fill, which on this ground would be the bar's colour on the bar), the two swatches and the lit ring (drawn in `--nav-bg`, so it reads as a gap), the theme word, Copilot, alerts, activity, the avatar, sign-out, the divider, the menu toggle and the wordmark that returns under 900px. Measured at seven widths: no dark ink on the dark ground, and under 768 the phone shell draws no bar.
- **THE COMPOSITOR IN contrast-verify WAS WRONG** and is the net for this change: it forced the result's alpha to 1, so 10% white over 10% white answered OPAQUE WHITE and reported 1:1. Over an opaque ground the new arithmetic is identical, so no older reading moves.
- **THE COLOUR CENSUS IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE**, measured: re-recorded at the unmodified parent it differs on six screens over seven values (`.ngl-empty`'s shadow, `#cal-open-reg`, `#rail-user-av`), none in this bar. So it was NOT re-recorded from a fresh sweep — my own difference was taken against the PARENT's census in the same conditions (nine values, every one the bar's) and the seven flaky lines were restored by hand. 34/40 here and 34/40 at the parent.
- **NOT TOUCHED**: the rail head stays white, so the shell's top-left corner is a notch against the band. The owner's highlight covered the bar alone.

## FIVE OFF FIVE IMAGES (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026: "You have not applied my requests")

Measured in a real browser first, because the report was that none of it was built. Three were not; one was built and UNREACHABLE; one was built in the wrong place.
- **THE FILTER CHIPS WERE DEAD.** MEASURED: a chip drew 93x30 and its `<select>` 22x28 in `rgba(0,0,0,0)`, and the centre of the chip hit-tested to `SPAN.reg-f-l` — **a press on a `<label>` does not open a native select's menu**, so four of five filters could only be opened by finding an unmarked 22px strip at the right wall. A rule had shrunk the resting control so the chip would read as a word. **THE SELECT NOW COVERS THE CHIP AND IS INVISIBLE (`.reg-chip-sel`, `position:absolute;inset:0;opacity:0`), AND THE WORD CARRIES WHAT IS CHOSEN** (`selChosen`, ONE reading, so face and control cannot disagree). Nothing shouts `!important`: the builder stopped putting `selStyle` — a whole dropdown's inline dress — on it, which is what the old rules had to shout at. **NOTHING DECORATIVE TAKES THE PRESS** (`pointer-events:none` on the funnel, the word and the caret — a press on the caret landed on the label). **AND THE CATEGORY CHIP WAS A SECOND COPY OF THE MARKUP**, so seven were fixed and it was not; it goes through `selFilter` now — THE CLOTHES FOLLOW THE BUILDER.
- **`REG_VIEWS` loses expiring60 and expiring30**; 90 stays (it is `RENEWAL_WINDOW_DAYS`). **THE FILTERS STAY in `regFiltered`** — the optional Home tiles are doors onto those cuts. Nothing is lit when one is in force and Clear says the list is narrowed.
- **CONDENSED IS DELETED** from `REG_DENSITY`; the segment reads `Object.keys(REG_DENSITY)`, never a typed list. It was the one rung that took the kind and the round off the title, so `twoLine` is gone — with the rung deleted it would be A GUARD THAT IS ALWAYS TRUE. An unknown stored value already falls back to compact: no migration, driven and proved.
- **THE HORIZON GAINED THE ARTIFACT'S DECISION COLUMN** (`300px minmax(0,1fr) 150px` on the ruler AND the row). `calHorizonDecision(r)` BORROWS everything — `renewalDecisionOf` (the one predicate every nag asks) carries the word and the day, the deadline is the nip already drawn — and computes no date. Three states: decided reads quietly, open is amber at the strong weight (the only state here that is WORK), nothing-to-say is faintest. The day prints through `regDotDate`; **`fmtDDay` is not published** and a first draft printed a raw ISO string.

THE SWEEP IS REAL: 16 controls across six pages; the calendar's two were the only ones leaking.
- **EVERY DIALOG FRAME CARRIES A 3px RULE** (`DLG_TOPBAR`, ONE declaration, three frames; danger wears `--danger`). A BACKGROUND, not an element — no markup, no layout, clips to the corner by itself. Written into the INLINE style because the frame states its own `background` shorthand there and a sheet rule would lose while looking correct.
- **HOME'S PREPARED ROW PUTS ITS VERBS AT THE RIGHT** (93px -> 53px; `.hm-row.is-desk` flex, acts `margin-left:auto`, wraps at a narrow card). SCOPED to `.is-desk`: the auto-triage row shares the class names, is a different surface and keeps its stack. The English button said **Discard** where the Swedish has always said "Lagg undan" and the confirm says nothing is deleted — both books say "Put away" now.

## THE SECOND FIVE IMAGES, AND THE NAME, THE TAG AND THE HORIZON (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

Measured against `prototype/hati-redesign-reference.html` rendered SIDE BY SIDE with HaTi before a line moved.
- **ONE DAY PRINTER, AND IT IS THE ARTIFACT'S SHAPE.** MEASURED: the artifact prints `30 Jun 2027` in the figure face at the label size and HaTi printed `30.06.2027` in the body face. `regDotDate` is the one function both register columns already went through, so both moved together and no screen carries two spellings of a day. **THE MONTH FOLLOWS THE LANGUAGE** (`langLocale()`, never `jxLocale`, never a hand-written English name — Swedish reads `30 juni 2027`). **AND IT REFUSES RATHER THAN PRINTING NaN** — the same NaN was reported 13 and 17 Sep at two of four call sites; this is the one printer now. `.reg-day` is the one class both cells wear.
- **INSIGHTS SITS DIRECTLY AFTER HOME** — markup order and nothing else, reversing 19 Sep's "after Obligations" (whose reasoning is kept beside it). **REVERSED 27 Sep 2026**: Copilot's work sits directly after Home and Insights below Calendar (see COPILOT'S WORK). **Comfortable is "Cozy"**, the artifact's own word.
- **PROVENANCE IS NOT A DESCRIPTION.** `Converted from X.docx (original stored: f_…)` was written into the one column every card prints as a DESCRIPTION. **THE ROUTE'S FIX IS THE REAL ONE** (POST /api/templates/upload writes `''`; where a document came from is `origin`/`source_type` and `templateProvenanceHtml`), and `naCardSub` refuses the shape for every row on file, falling back to the CATEGORY — a fact off the record, never an invented summary. `naCardHint` puts the provenance on the hover. **THE SENTENCE SLOT IS ALWAYS DRAWN** and reserves two lines: a grid stretches every cell to the tallest, so a clamp alone caps the long one and still lets an empty card shrink. The describe box is a `<textarea>` (same id, same cap; Enter presses Find, Shift+Enter is a newline).
- **`triageWhy` IS THE ONE READING OF WHY A READING DID NOT HAPPEN** — the four kinds the server's error already carries (noKey · rateLimit · spendCap · provider) worded for a tile, the technical sentence on the hover (`whyRaw`, `hint`). **EVERY step catch asks `triageFail`**: four printed a raw message and one was reported. **`contractOpenFieldNames`** (js/blanks.js, published) names the open fields for BOTH kinds of contract, and `tplFormOpenCount` is derived from `tplFormOpenFields` rather than written twice.
- **THE "WHAT IT FOUND" COLOUR IS THE RESULT, NOT WHETHER IT RAN** — `1 departure`, `1 still open` and `0 found` all drew GREEN. `OV_READ_TONE` gained `look:'amber'` and `bad:'ruby'`; each row works its own out beside the figure. Bold, no rules across the card, the Open links are `.ui-btn`.
- **THE NEGOTIATE HEAD DRAWS NO LINE** (`box-shadow:inset 0 -1px` off `.redline-page #ws-head`; the room's own band never drew one) and **the TERM says its length once** (`termCell=term`; `ct_fact_days` STALE on that row).
- **A CLAUSE'S NAME IS NOT PART OF ITS WORDING.** `pbDropRepeatedHeading` at the TOP of `pbFitWording` — the one reading every proposal goes through. It REFUSES rather than guesses: the WHOLE heading must match, folded free of its number and case; a one-word heading is never cut; words must be left after the cut. THE PROMPT IS NOT THE WALL (it gained the sentence anyway).
- **EVERY PREPARED ROW CARRIES ITS KIND** (`hm-dk-tag`: Notice · Read · Memo · Chase) taking the ROW's own tone, never a second table.
- **A HIDDEN CONTROL MAY NOT COLOUR ITS OWN CHOICES.** `color:transparent` on `.reg-chip-sel` was inherited by the `<option>`s in the NATIVE popup and drew a column of blank rows. `opacity:0` hides the box only; the options state their own ink and surface.
- **THE HORIZON IS THE ARTIFACT'S**: the five bands LEAD, the caption bar is gone (`cal_hz_title`/`cal_hz_head` STALE), the months read as a mono ruler rather than twelve uppercase heads with a box each, the label is who · reference · value. **THE TABLE IS THE SCROLLER** — sticky is relative to the nearest SCROLLING ancestor, so while the page scrolled the header travelled with the rows.
- **AND THE BAR IS A PILL, WITH A CUT RIGHT END WHERE IT RUNS PAST THE RULER** (Young, over two renders: *"These bars are not the same. They do not have round endings in the end"*). MEASURED: every corner of `.cal-hz-bar` computed `0px`. **PIN THE RELATION, NOT THE NUMBER** — the artifact's `4px` is half its own 8px bar, so copying the 4 onto HaTi's 14px bar copies a shallow corner rather than the shape; `999px` is this product's own "as round as this box can be" (`.rounded-full`'s rule) and follows the bar if the bar is retuned. The cut end is the artifact's rule too (`4px 0 0 4px` on an over-run): a pill says *it ends here*, a cut end says *this is where the PICTURE stops, not the agreement*. **ONE READING, TWO READERS** — the flag is the row builder's own `beyond`, which the note under the bar already prints, so the shape and the words cannot disagree. Said out loud and NOT changed: `calHorizonPos` has no floor, so a contract expiring today draws a bar of zero width; and HaTi's 2px `.cal-hz-end` tick (which the artifact does not draw) now stands a little clear of a rounded cap — kept, because it marks the exact expiry day a pill makes vaguer.

## NINE OFF FIVE IMAGES (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

Four of the nine were INVISIBLE IN THE SOURCE.
- **RESERVING ONE LINE DOES NOT FIX A CARD'S HEIGHT.** MEASURED: the New agreement cards drew 103px and 121px. The sentence slot was reserved (21 Sep) and doing its job; the NAME wrapped, and a grid stretches every cell in a row to the tallest. **EVERY LINE IS RESERVED NOW** — name, sentence and foot, one each — and the sentence dropped to ONE line, because "not big either" is measured against the artifact's own ~80px card. `naCardTitle` is the one hover carrying the whole of each cut. **Two `.na-door b` rules were folded into one**: a second rule about one element winning by source order is this file's own recorded fault, and it made the first draft of the claim pass against the wrong rule. MEASURED after: six cards, all 86px.
- **A HEAD AND A COUNT ARE TWO FACTS.** *"the open fields does not tell you how many fields are still open"* — a `none` state forced the count to null, so the one tile with a number worth reading drew a steel dash. **ONLY `working` SUPPRESSES A COUNT**, the strip asks the NUMBER before its three old states (mark and tone alike), and the fill tile's number is how many are OPEN where its head says open. The "— N more" tail came off that branch: two numbers about one thing on one tile is what made it unreadable. f341's count claim is REVERSED IN PLACE; what held it — a `none` tile with no number is a dash, never a tick — is held by the strip.
- **THE STANDARDS TILE IS THE THIRD DOOR**, pressing `openCheckPanel(c,'playbook')` — the Checks card's own act. The 20 Sep note ended "on his word"; this is that word.
- **THE RE-WRITTEN BRIEF IS SHOWN.** The Before-you-sign row already re-wrote it and did not open it. `openCheckPanel(c,'brief')` after a run, and **only where one was really written** — `c._brief` holds the OLD brief after a refusal.
- **"THE ONE PLACE EVERY PROPOSAL PASSES THROUGH" WAS NOT ONE.** The 21 Sep cleaner sat inside `pbFitWording`; `it.draft` is the RAW model string and BOTH "Use Copilot's draft" presses file that. It is cleaned in **`rlPlaybookProposals`**, the one producer the rail, the review window and the batch share, on a LOCATED clause only. Reproduced at the parent: `draftHead: "Limitation of Liability. Each Part"`.
- **A MISSING CLAUSE IS ADDED WHOLE; A PRESENT ONE IS ADJUSTED.** Two holes under one report. `pbFitWording` let an UNADDRESSED whole-clause rewrite count as the smallest change (the owner's *"Replaces all 69 words — keeps none"*) — it now refuses one that would lose unquoted blocks, **asking `pbUnquotedLoss`, the WALL's own reading, so the preview, the lead and the filing door cannot disagree** (a seatbelt in practice: an address is found by the same quote that locates the clause). And on an **EDIT** landing `lead` no longer falls back to the library's stand-alone clause — `lead:null`, both card surfaces say `ng_pb_nofit`, and the three named wordings stay as presses that ask. **An ADD landing is byte-identical.**
- **THE COPILOT DRAFT CAN BE READ**: the 120px cap is the RESTING shape and a press drops it (`ceScanPvToggle`); the control is drawn only where the box really overflows, **measured after the paint** (`ceScanFitPv` — `rowsThatFit`'s own idiom), never a character count.
- **A DROPDOWN THAT WEARS HaTi'S OWN CORNERS.** The list a native `<select>` drops is the OS's and no stylesheet reaches inside it. **THE `<select>` STAYS AND IS STILL THE TRUTH**: `selectMenuWire` intercepts the POINTER and draws `.hati-selmenu`; a press writes the value back and fires the select's own `change`, so nothing downstream learns a menu was involved. **THE KEYBOARD IS LEFT ALONE** (arrows, Home, End, type-ahead) — rebuilding those in a div is how a control loses behaviour nobody noticed it had. Mounted on `document.body` at `position:fixed` so the sticky band cannot clip it (the ladder card's own 18 Sep lesson); the press that opens it closes it. **SCOPE, said out loud**: armed on the Contracts filter bar alone; every other `<select>` still drops the system's list until somebody asks.
- **THE HORIZON BAR IS 8px**, the artifact's own, with the TOP moved so the centre line did not — that is where the expiry tick and the notice nip already sit.

## THE COUNTERPARTY LEADS, AND THE WORK ORDER'S FOUR (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

Two orders in one run: the two tables built to renders he approved, then WORKORDER-five-off-five-images.md built after he read it. *"Important that the columns are well spaced so we can see the most of the counterparty name. Balance is key."*

- **THE ROW'S IDENTITY IS TWO LINES, ONE CELL, BOTH SEATS.** `CELL.name` is DELETED (nothing outside the row builder read it); `CELL.counterparty` carries the counterparty on `.reg-title` over the contract's name on `.reg-sub`, and took the family indent, the ↳ arrow and the `data-fam-toggle` control with it. **`.reg-title` / `.reg-sub` KEEP THEIR NAMES AND THEIR DRESS** — they were never "the title" and "the kind", they are the row's IDENTITY LINE and its sub-line, which is the re-pointing white-band-and-tabs 5d/5e already took; only WHICH FACT each carries moved.
- **CONTRACTS LOSES A COLUMN (10), NEGOTIATIONS KEEPS ITS COUNT (8)** — the owner ruled each page by name. `kind` is the Negotiations seat's OWN column (`reg-typecell`, straight right of the counterparty): a round is what that page is about. On Contracts the same two words ride the identity cell's hover. `kindRound` is the ONE reading both spell them through. **`reg-typecell`, never `reg-kind`** — that class is retired and f240 pins its absence BY SUBSTRING, so even the prefix would have tripped it while meaning the opposite.
- **BALANCE, MEASURED**: `[6,26,13,11,7,9,7,13,5,3]` / `[6,26,14,13,9,13,11,8]` (**since 24 Sep 2026 `[6,39,11,7,9,7,13,5,3]` / `[6,39,14,9,13,11,8]` — the stream column went; see SIX OFF FIVE IMAGES**), both 100, the counterparty the widest column on either table (349px at 1440) and the six shared columns cut identically IN PIXELS. The give moved with the fact: it was the title's, and the counterparty now takes both old shares (13+17 → 26); the four points that did not fold went to value stream and expiry, both measured short.
- **`kind` SORTS** (`REG_CMP.kind`, kind then round) and **`name` is a sort with no column**, which `risk` has been since the dropdown was built.
- **A DROPPED CONNECTION IS RETRIED; A REFUSAL IS NOT.** MEASURED from the owner's screenshot: the brief failed while three Copilot calls in the same breath came back — not the key, not the cap, not the network. `anthropicMessages` had NO timeout and retried only a REJECTED MODEL, so a `fetch` throw went straight to the tile. Now `AI_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` bounds the wait and a THROW — no answer at all — is retried ONCE after `AI_RETRY_PAUSE_MS`. **A STATUS IS NEVER RETRIED, AND THAT IS THE NARROWING**: a first draft also retried a 5xx and turned five green files red (f132, f133, f234, f275, answer-worklist-verify all say a provider error maps to 502 and the loop stops) — any HTTP status is the provider ANSWERING and already carries its own sentence and mapping. spend books off a RESPONSE so it cannot double. ONE PLACE, EVERY metered call; the streaming twin is left alone.
- **A FAILED READING CARRIES THE PRESS THAT RUNS IT AGAIN** (`doorFor`'s `retry`, asked FIRST) — "Try again in a moment" with no way to try again was the half that was breaking the refusal rule. `triageAndPaint(c,{again:true})` is a PERSON asking and the only thing that lifts the once-per-wording guard.
- **THE BRIEF IS THE FIRST BUTTON BEFORE SIGNING** (`#sc-brief`, the card head's own `runCtl` slot, so no band): drawn in EVERY state — *Write the brief* / *Open the brief* — carrying `data-kt-brief`, so `wireKtBriefCard` (which learned an additive `after`) is the one act and the panel is the same panel. The secondary button, never filled; the cost on the hover; `#i-file`, a sprite symbol that exists. **THE HOLD IS NOT WIDENED** to a brief that is current and merely unread — that would re-spend on every signature. Said out loud, the owner's to rule on.
- **THE COPILOT RAIL NAMES ITS CLAUSE** (`.ce-ah-cl`, through `ceClauseLabel`). **AND IT MAY NOT GROW THE ROW**: MEASURED 44 → 61px, because the name took width and the TABS wrapped, then the LABEL wrapped. `.ce-tabs` and `.ce-ah .sp` take `flex:none`; exactly one thing on that row gives, and it is the name. Back to 44px.
- **THE NEW AGREEMENT POP-UP HAS A GROUND**: `.na-body` takes `--color-bg` and the card edges step to `--rule-strong` (the token `.ui-btn` uses). The cards are NOT tinted — six cards each claiming something, when only the chosen one has a claim. `.na-sec + .na-sec` stands clear and the line-of-business control takes `--field-h`.
- **EVERY DROPDOWN DRAWS HaTi'S OWN LIST**: `selectMenuSweep()` armed ONCE on the body, delegated, so every select the product ever paints is covered with no list to keep in step (the filter bar's own call is RETIRED — two roots would open the menu twice). `SELECT_MENU_SEL` names what stays native (`[multiple]`, `[size]`, `[data-native]`); `selectMenuStandsDown` refuses PORTAL_MODE and a phone, asked AT THE PRESS. The `<select>` is still the record and the keyboard is untouched.

## THE DEAL CARD IS EVERY CONTRACT'S, AND EVERY FIELD CAN BE TYPED (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

*"the deal card in the overview page is very sales dimensional. The fields there should be ones that are found in most contracts no matter the Type of contract. Also then you try to edit the details, you should be able to edit all fields."* Then, of the three questions put back to him: *"narrow only, only where something is recorded, take all three."* MEASURED first: of the fifteen fields the card drew, FIVE exist only in a supply or distribution agreement, and `Edit these details` opened FOUR boxes against fifteen values.
- **TWO LISTS, AND THE SECOND IS DRAWN ONLY WHERE IT IS ANSWERED.** `OV_DEAL_FIELDS` is on every contract; `OV_ALSO_FIELDS` (the rebate, its tiers, the price review, the rejection window, exclusivity, retention, warranty) is its own shut card, drawn only where `ktAlsoRecorded` finds something — **NO GUESS IS MADE ABOUT THE KIND OF CONTRACT** (a card headed "Terms for a supply agreement" on a record whose type was read wrong is worse than no card). A field in the fixed grid still prints its em-dash; the second group can never be a row of dashes. A number answers only above zero.
- **THREE NEW TERMS, ALL THE OWNER'S WORD**: `confidentiality` and `disputes` are TEXT (the paper's own words — volumeRebate's reasoning), `assignment` is a select (consent · free · prohibited · unclear). **In the extraction schema too** — a field nothing fills is a dash for ever.
- **ONE CELL BUILDER, TWO POSTURES.** `ktFieldCell(c,k,edit)` decides what a cell draws and is where `ktFactReads` is asked; the grid does not change shape when Edit is pressed — a box is drawn in the value's own place. Nineteen ordinary metadata fields are one generic box driven by META_FIELDS' own type (`data-ktm`, one handler, `change` for everything but free text); the four with a home of their own keep `data-kt` (the value strips its separators, an empty notice DELETES). `term` is derived and is never a box. **Typing over a reading wins** — confidence 'high'.
- **THE RECORD KEEPS ENGLISH**: `metaEnName` derives the audit name from the key, so no second list can drift.
- **A SECTION THIS PANE DRAWS MUST BE NAMED IN `sectionWire`'s ROUTER** or its fold flips and the wrong host repaints — measured the hour `also` was added: the head said "1 term" and drew no field. `Value stream` is deliberately NOT on the deal grid though the artifact drew it: The record already carries it, and it is an admin act with its own confirm.

## BEFORE SIGNING, THE OVERVIEW MARKS THE FIELDS THAT HOLD IT (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

*"before signing, critical fields in the overview page have to be highlighted before signing so that user can go back and fill them in."*
- **CRITICAL IS NOT A NEW LIST.** `signFieldMarks(c)` (js/signcheck.js) TRANSLATES `signReadiness`'s own open rows into the field each is about — a blocker's `key` through `SIGN_FIELD_OF`, a record row's own `field`. It judges nothing, counts nothing of its own, and cannot print a different number from the list it reads. A HOLD OUTRANKS A NOTE on one field: one cell, one mark.
- **NOT WHILE IT IS A DRAFT.** A draft is a form being filled in; an amber *needed to sign* on every blank of a new agreement is the band rule in a new costume. `live` is "this contract is in the phase where a field can be marked", and the Overview reserves its line off `live` ALONE — so within the whole signing phase a mark appearing or clearing moves no pixel, and a draft or a sealed record draws no line at all and is byte-identical to what it was.
- **THE LINE IS OPT-IN**: `sectionFieldHtml` gained a fifth argument the CALLER builds; passing nothing gets the old markup, so the five screens sharing that builder did not move. `.sec-f-n` reserves its height; the cell is dressed by `:has(.sec-f-n.is-hold)`, so the field builder learns no class. Amber has to mean work — a field nobody is waiting on stays quiet.
- **A HOLD IS A DOOR AND IT IS `focusKeyTerms`** (a real `<button>`, `data-ov-fix`), the same act the signing list's *Fix on Overview* presses — two places, one act. A NOTE (the record disagreeing with the paper) is a sentence, never a door: what to do about it is the signing list's own row.
- **THE COUNT RIDES THE HEAD'S OWN CHIP**, not a new line: a shut section still answers, which is the section grammar's rule, and the alternative was a band across the page. Asked ONCE per card, never per cell.
Tests: f352 (16 claims, **15 red at the parent**; the one that passes is a named CONTROL), overview-as-drawn-verify section 10 (6 checks, **4 red at the parent**, which prints `bg rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) · left rule 0px` and `no chip`; 10d and 10f are named CONTROLS). **10e asks the RELATION** — a marked line and an empty one measured in the SAME render — because two renders also measure the value's own text, an em-dash in the body face against a figure in the mono one, which is two real pixels and nothing to do with the mark.

## THE BRIEF IS THE LAST STEP, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

*"write brief should be the last button clicked to verify that a user reads a brief of everything that has been updated before they sign. It should not be the first button in the signing page but last and mandatory."* Then, of the two questions put back: *"follow the gate, every signature."* **THIS REVERSES that same morning's "THE BRIEF IS THE FIRST BUTTON ON THIS CARD"**, whose reasoning is kept where it stands because it is why the control exists at all.
- **A FOURTH STAGE, `sign`, NOT A REORDER.** Putting `read` after `people` would have moved the standards, obligations, record and risk rows too, and those sit where a separate ruling put them. Only the brief moved; `#sc-brief` keeps its id and the card head now draws no control at all.
- **READING IT HOLDS, AND FOLLOWS THE GATE** (`signCheckRowHolds` → `brief-read` is true; `off` holds nothing, which is what off means). It does NOT wait on `current` — it is not a reading the check makes.
- **IT LAPSES WHEN EITHER HALF MOVES.** `briefReadKey` is *when this brief was written* + *when wording was last proposed* — two facts the record answers exactly. **NO SECOND HASHER**: the brief's own inputHash is the SERVER's, and a browser twin would call every brief stale for ever (the trap `signCheckBriefAt` is already kept out of). Each signer's own; `briefMarkRead` is the ONE writer and never back-dates.
- **`signCheckBriefStands` IS ONE READING WITH TWO ASKERS** (the row, and the button's *Read* / *Write* word) — written twice they drift, and the drift is visible: measured, the card offered to WRITE a brief that was already on the screen. **`stale !== true`, NOT `=== false`**: a contract nobody proposed wording on has no dated change to compare with, and asking `=== false` meant the mandatory rule never applied to a contract that went straight to signature. **THE GUARD AGAINST TRAPPING A SIGNATURE IS THE KEY ITSELF** — a brief with no date of its own cannot be stamped against, so it asks for nothing; missing, stale or cut short each keep their own row and their own way forward.
- **READ, IT SETTLES RATHER THAN VANISHING** (an empty stage draws nothing, so without a settled row the one thing the signer was asked to do would leave no trace on the card they did it on).
- **WHAT MOVED WHILE YOU NEGOTIATED** rides the brief panel: `briefMoved` borrows `negoMemo`'s `agreed` list — deterministic, RAW, no model, no spend — capped at 8 with the remainder COUNTED. The foot's *I have read this* is the only act on that panel that writes. **THE WORDS SAY WHAT WAS PROVED**: opened and pressed, never understood, and the trail line says "Read the brief before signing".
Tests: f353 (22 claims, **16 red at the parent**; six are named CONTROLS), signing-flow-verify section 9 (6 checks, **5 red at the parent**, printing `stages: read → people` and `Write the brief · expected Read the brief`; 9e is the CONTROL). **9c pins the RELATION** (the button equals `br_open`'s own words) not the English. The bench itself now reads the brief, guarded — a bench that throws proves nothing about the checks under it. f319 (4b) re-pointed in place.

## SIGNING WITHOUT THE FACTS — THE THREE QUICK FIXES (Young's go, 23 Sep 2026)

Off a review of what a contract could be signed without; the owner took the recommended answers (must/should split, block with an honest one-press answer, anyone with a reason, blanks at the first send AND at signing) and said go on these three. The rest of that plan is NOT built.
- **A VALUE LEFT EMPTY IS NOT "NO MONEY PASSES."** POST /api/templates/:id/contracts writes `'estimated'` for a typed value, `'none'` ONLY for a standard whose category is `nda` (the template answers the silence, as TEMPLATES.ND does), and NOTHING otherwise; the mailroom writes nothing. **The bulk importer still stamps 'none' on purpose** — its review gate reads 'none' as "value not needed" and most imports are already-signed paper. **Stored records are NOT rewritten** (no backfill); the Overview's tick-box is the way back.
- **`metaEffDateOnto(c, m, opts)` (js/metadata.js) IS THE ONE COPY** of a reading's effective date onto `c.fields.effDate` — the field the Overview prints, the record check compares and Copilot's card reads. Fill only; an ISO day or nothing; `overwrite` for the import queue's confirm alone. Four callers: applyMetadata, applyReviewedMeta, migRerunAi, fillKeyTermsFromDocument. **The importer's build is NOT one** (sealed on arrival — an unconfirmed reading would be frozen for good).
- **AN EMPTY BOX IN HaTi'S OWN PAPER IS A READINESS BLOCK, `blanks`** — so the Send screen asks its tick and signBlockers holds, with no new band. `contractBoxesOpen` (js/blanks.js) is contractBlanksOpen narrowed to kind `field`: never `sync` (the counterparty and value have their own rows), never `upload` (their paper is a different question). The row NAMES the boxes (three, then "and N more"), carries `fields`, and the `effective` warning stands down when the start date box is named. `SIGN_BOX_FIELD` marks the one box the Overview owns (effDate). The card's door is chosen at the DRAW: Draft → `data-sc-blanks="docs"`; past Draft with only Overview-owned boxes → `data-sc-fix`; otherwise `data-sc-blanks="nego"` — its own attribute, because `data-sc-nego` is bound with querySelector. **Limit, said out loud**: once a negotiation has stored the wording, an empty box is a dash in the text and is no longer counted.
Tests: f367 (21 claims, **13 red at the parent**; eight are named CONTROLS and WALLS), signing-without-the-facts-verify (26 checks in a real browser, **21 red at the parent**, which prints `Sign as Amina Otieno` over two empty boxes, the draft SENT without a tick, and `Non-monetary` ticked on a skipped value). **FOUR browser files staged a fixture with empty template boxes and are re-pointed IN PLACE** — sign-links-verify, signing-flow-verify (the boxes filled through `contractBlankSet` BEFORE the wording is hashed, for the brief's own reason: every count would be one higher), signers-and-party-verify (the fixture's `material` box), nda-carries-no-money-verify (its heading count asked as the RELATION) — each red here and green at the parent, and green again after.

## WHO IS ON THIS CONTRACT (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

*"when you draft a new agreement, before you create the draft you should have the option to add the other participants to the contract, roles and their access levels. Should you choose to skip this, there should be another door in the contract page."* And of the one decision: *"narrow only."*
- **`js/participants.js` IS A RECORD, NOT A SECOND PERMISSIONS SYSTEM.** `c.participants` is an ordinary field, absent on every record on file; **no route, no server field, no mail** (f354 greps), and it **does not travel** — `buildSharePayload` is an allow-list by construction and who is on OUR side is not the counterparty's business.
- **EVERY ROLE NAMES THE LIST IT FILLS** (`PARTY_ROLES` → `fills`, printed on the row): the signing order, the approval chain, the standing reviewer, a seat at the desk, the three links. A role is an ANSWER, EARLY, to a question the product already asks late.
- **ACCESS NARROWS AND NEVER GRANTS** — four rungs with nothing above `all`; `participantReach` asks the workspace's OWN question (`canAccessFolder`) so the SCREEN can say so on that person's row. A colleague who cannot open the stream is named and told, never quietly added; not-a-colleague-yet is a fact with a way forward.
- **HELD WHILE THE PAPER IS CHOSEN, CLAIMED WHEN IT IS MINTED.** `participantsHold` is in memory; `contractArrived` claims — **BEFORE its own guards** (a contract too empty to read is still one somebody just named three colleagues on) and never on a bulk import. **THE SCREEN'S OWN DISAPPEARANCE IS WHAT DROPS IT** (a MutationObserver on `#modal-root`): Cancel and ✕ are two of five ways out, and hanging the drop off the buttons left people held after an Escape, for the next contract minted anywhere to claim. Create is exempt and spends the hold.
- **`saveSignerPlan` IS STILL THE ONE AUTHORITY**: an EMPTY plan opens on `participantSignerRows`, an arranged one is never touched. Nothing here writes a plan.
- **ONE BUILDER, TWO DOORS** (`participantsPanelHtml` / `participantsWire`, bound once per element): the drafting screen's shut `<details>` and the Overview's own section. The Overview alone carries *Reached* — borrowed from the signing plan and the share cache, with `unknown` where the page has not asked. **`people` IS NAMED IN THE OVERVIEW'S REPAINT ROUTER**, or the fold flips and the wrong host repaints.
- **A BLANK ROW IS A ROW SOMEBODY STARTED**: filtering blanks out of `participantsOf` was the obvious defensive thing and made *Add someone* do nothing at all — the row was minted and hidden by the reading that drew it.
- The namespace is `ppl_`, not `pt_`: payment terms owns `pt_` and fourteen keys collided.
Tests: f354 (32 claims, **27 red at the parent**; five are named WALLS). A missing module READS AS EMPTY there so the file still runs and reports a claim at a time. overview-as-drawn-verify section 11 (5 checks, **all 5 red**) and new-agreement-verify section 8 (6 checks, **4 red**; 8e and 8f are CONTROLS).

## THE SEND SCREEN TAKES SEVERAL PEOPLE (Young ruled 21 Sep 2026)

*"in Door B, you should be able to add multiple people to send the document to."*
- **ONE SEND, ONE ROUND, SEVERAL LINKS.** Everything that happens once still happens once in `doSend` — the round, the handover, leaving Draft, the version capture — and `shareSendExtras` then posts one share per ticked person, AFTER the primary and only inside the branch that landed (a round nobody received is not one to copy to three more people). It advances nothing, hands nothing over and touches no stage; f355 greps it for all five.
- **THE LIST IS THE CONTRACT'S OWN PEOPLE** (`shareMoreRowsHtml` over `participantSendRows`): the other side's, in the role menu's order, each saying which role they have. The primary recipient is NOT offered to themselves (matched by ADDRESS, folded, because that is what a link binds to). Never on the `history` kind — that one travels to a colleague.
- **ONE AUDIT LINE PER ADDRESS**, because a link is a fact about one address; a refusal is COUNTED and SAID and cannot undo a round that has gone.
- **ONE PURPOSE FOR THE WHOLE SEND.** A purpose per row would mean a signing link and an advise link in one press; it is a different feature and the owner has not ruled on it. Pinned as an absence.
- **THE TWO BUILDERS LIVE IN js/participants.js**, not js/core.js: they are about the people, not the dialog, and that is what makes them drivable on a stage with no core.
Tests: f355 (14 claims, **13 red at the parent**; the one that passes is a named WALL), share-recipient-verify's own section (4 checks, **all 4 red at the parent**, which prints `not drawn`). The bench is guarded so the file still runs on a build without the list.

## THE BOOK IS WALKED ONCE, NOT ONCE PER CONTRACT (the performance audit, 22 Sep 2026)

MEASURED in a real browser at 3,000 contracts before a line moved: drawing Home once touched **108 MILLION items in lists**, 99.5% of them from ONE reading. Home 1,035 ms · Contracts 1,293 · Calendar 1,197 · Obligations 1,025 · Insights 958. After: **88 · 157 · 115 · 83 · 115**.

- **`familyChildren` IS A MAP BUILT ONCE** (js/family.js). It scanned the whole book on every call and `effectiveExpiry` asks it about twelve times per contract. **THE GUARD IS THREE O(1) FACTS** — same array, same length, same stamp — plus `familyIndexDirty()`, which every writer of `parentId` and every in-place swap of a contract object must raise. **A GUARD THAT WALKS THE BOOK IS NOT A GUARD**: the first build verified the index with a per-call checksum over every parentId and made Home *slower* (1,035 → 3,442 ms). The empty answer is one shared FROZEN array. f356 (4) is the net on a future writer.
- **ONE COUNT PER PAINT** (`navCounts`, js/app.js): the rail, Home's tile and the phone's bar each asked `negoNeedsYouTotal` for themselves — one navigation walked the book FOUR times for one figure. The memo is dropped on a **microtask**, so it cannot outlive the turn it was computed in and no caller has to remember to clear it. **THE CYCLE WALL**: the first build asked `approvalsDoorCount`, which draws through `hmDashSlices`, which asks `navCounts` — and the memo was written only at the END, so every level recomputed: **1,132 walks of the book for one paint of Home against 3 before.** `navCounts` now asks nothing that draws a screen, and `_navBusy` refuses a re-entrant call rather than recomputing. Every reader keeps its own fallback — these modules load apart.
- **ONE LOOK-UP PER TICK**: `obligationSurfacesChanged` searched the whole book twice for the same contract before asking any surface whether it was even mounted.
- **THE LIST DECORATES ITSELF FROM ITS OWN IDS**: the contracts route read the WHOLE briefs table and the WHOLE renewal_advice table — parsing the JSON of every renewal row in the workspace — to decorate one page of at most 200. `pageIds` + a bounded `IN (?,?,…)`.
- **THE INSTRUMENT**: `test/chromium/_audit/perf*.js` time a real browser at 3,000 contracts. A REALM MISMATCH is what makes `deepStrictEqual` fail on two identical lists — an array born inside jsdom has that realm's `Array.prototype`; compare joined strings. And **the parent baseline is a worktree** (`git worktree add -f <dir> origin/main`), never an assertion.
Tests: f356 (19 claims, 8 red at the parent), f357 (16 claims, 12 red).

## EIGHT HOLES IN THE LIFECYCLE (the process-flow audit, 22 Sep 2026)

Where the product lost track between one screen and the next. Each is a READING the screens already had the facts for.

- **(1) FOUR PLACES AN ADDRESS CAN BE TYPED** and nothing compared them. `contractAddressBook(c, shares)` (js/participants.js) folds the signing route, the people list, the record and the last link into rows with ONE marked `willUse`; `ADDR_SOURCES` is the order, written down once and the send screen's own. It draws NOTHING under two rows — one address is not a disagreement. `shareModalPrefill` gained the people source between route and record.
- **(2) A ROUND LANDS AND NOTHING RE-READS.** `readingStale(c, kind)` (js/signcheck.js) over brief · playbook · obligations. **THREE ANSWERS, and the third is "we do not know"** (never read is not out of date; nothing proposed is nothing to compare with). **THE PLAYBOOK KEEPS ITS OWN AUTHORITY** — `playbookStale` is asked first, because a hash beats a date. The wording-moved date is BORROWED (`signCheckBriefAt`), never computed again — a second hasher drifts. It re-runs nothing and spends nothing.
- **(3) LANES WAITED FOR SOMEBODY TO OPEN A PAGE.** `intakeLaneSweep` on a beat, armed at sign-in beside `loadIntake`; it reads `intakeLanes()` BEFORE loading anything, so a workspace with no lanes costs nothing. **A RULE THAT FIRES WITHOUT A HUMAN MAY NOT MOVE THE HUMAN**: `createFromTemplate(tid, {quiet:true})` mints without stealing the reader's page or toasting at them.
- **(4) A NOTICE DRAFTED BUT NEVER RECORDED.** `noticeMarkServed` is the ONE writer of `c.notice` (absent on every record on file); a served notice IS the renewal decision, so `renewalDecisionOf` leads with it and the chase stops. **IT CLAIMS NOTHING HaTi SAW** — the trail says "Recorded by a person; HaTi did not send it." **AND `todayStr()` IS NOT AN ISO DAY** — see below.
- **(5) EIGHT SWITCHES AND NO SUMMARY.** `stPersonSays(u)` BORROWS every line from the switch below it and decides nothing; an admin is said ONCE, not six times.
- **(6) FOUR END STATES, NO COMPARISON.** `END_STATES` / `endStateSays` is the one place those three sentences live, printed on the hover by the Contracts row and the contract's own menu. **A CHOOSER WAS NOT BUILT, DELIBERATELY** — Young ruled Hold onto that Contracts row BY NAME on 19 Sep, over a drawing, because reaching it meant opening the contract first; folding the three into one door takes that back. The words were the half that was missing. f358 (6d) pins the absence.

### AND `todayStr()` IS A DISPLAY STRING — PAID FOR THREE TIMES (item 4's net found it; the risk scan had it too)

`todayStr()` reads like "today" and returns **"22 Sep 2026"**. Comparing it with an ISO day compares `"2"` with `"0"`, so `day > today` answers false for every date in the future: the wall refusing a notice served tomorrow **never refused anything**, and the date box opened EMPTY with no maximum, because a date input drops a value it cannot read. **THE CALENDAR PAID FOR THIS EXACT TRAP** and wrote it down beside `calToday`, which is the ONE reading — asked through `window` (this file draws on stages with no calendar) with the same LOCAL arithmetic as its fallback, never UTC. **`todayISO()` (js/core.js, published, written DIRECTLY BELOW `todayStr`) IS THE ONE READING**, and three files ask it: the served-notice wall, the calendar's `calToday`, and the RISK SCAN. Each keeps the same LOCAL arithmetic as its own fallback, because none of them is on every stage; `toISOString()` is never the answer — it puts today on yesterday for every reader west of Greenwich after their afternoon.

**THE RISK SCAN PAID IT THE THIRD TIME (Young asked for it 22 Sep 2026).** `runScan` stamped `c.scan.on` with `todayStr()`, so `ktDayDot` — which correctly refuses anything that is not an ISO day — printed an em-dash in the Overview's *What Copilot read* row **on every record ever scanned**. `on` has ONE writer and ONE reader, and they had never agreed. **THE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT WAS ASSERTING THE DEFECT**: f328 pinned the source line `on:(typeof todayStr==='function')?todayStr()` under the message *"and `on` is the ISO day a formatter can read"* — the assertion and its own message contradicted each other. **A CHECK THAT READS THE SOURCE LINE CANNOT SEE THE VALUE**: it is reversed in place and now EVALUATES the `on:` expression and hands the result to `ktDayDot`'s own shape. Its first draft bound only `todayISO`, so `typeof todayStr` answered 'undefined', the expression took its ISO fallback and the claim PASSED at the parent — **the mirror-world trap again; both names are bound with their real bodies now.**

**NO BACKFILL, and the cost is said out loud**: a contract scanned before this keeps a display string in `on` and still prints an em-dash, because `at` beside it is a locale sentence and turning it into a day would be guessing. Scanning again is one press. `todayStr` is right for `c.lastAction`, which is a display field, and that is every other caller. Tests: f358 (4d2, re-pointed to the relation), f328 (three claims, all red at the parent — one prints `the reader refused what the scan wrote: "22 Sept 2026"`).

Both are reversed in place.

- **THREE GRADES, AND EACH IS A COLOUR THIS PRODUCT ALREADY USES FOR THAT MEANING.** `XR_GRADES` = ruby · amber · steel, **the order IS the rank** and `docXrayTone` walks it, so a clause wears its WORST mark by construction. `XR_SEV_GRADE` maps the scan's own high/med/low and is the ONLY thing that hands out ruby. A bare segment is **not "safe"** — `xr_look_none` names no reader (it listed two while there were three) and says silence is not safety.

## FOUR FIXES OFF ONE LONG CONTRACT (Young's order, 23 Sep 2026)

- **A READING'S ANSWER IS CHECKED BEFORE IT IS FILED.** `js/metaclean.js` (module AND window, required by the server) — `metaUnleak(m, keys)` cuts a field at the model's own call syntax (`META_SEAM_RE`), moves an answer written after a seam under ANOTHER known field's name into that field only where it is empty, drops anything else, and files an answer that only says the contract is silent (`META_ABSENT_RE`) as silence. Returns a copy. Asked at the route (`/api/ai/extract`, against its own schema's keys — the wall), at `applyMetadata`, and on the way in (`_repairMetadata` in `migrateContract` and after `ensureFull`'s assign — narrow, persisted only on the next ordinary save). The extract ceiling is 3,000 tokens (nineteen fields with spans).
- **PLAIN ENGLISH PAGES ARE SIZED BY THEIR WORDS.** A page closes at `READ_PAGE_CHARS` (14,000) as well as `READ_PAGE` (60) clauses; the whole-edition `aiDocChars` ceiling is GONE (each page is its own call); `READ_MAX_PAGES` 40 is a runaway guard. A page cut short is asked again in two halves, ONCE (`askAll`). ## THE CONTRACT TYPE IS A CHOICE, AND THE WORDS ARE ENGLISH (Young ruled 22 Sep 2026)

*"make the contract type on the overview a dropdown too"* — the morning after the same ask for a party's role word. **THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME FIELD AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE RULING.**
- **THE FIELD STAYS FREE TEXT ON THE RECORD** (`type:'text'`), because `openMetaReview` and the upload confirm both branch on `type` and a closed list there would DROP whatever Copilot read off the paper. What it gains is **`picks`** — "free text, and here are words to offer" — so the extraction review and the upload confirm are byte-identical.
- **THE WORDS ARE ENGLISH, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE PARTY ROLE.** A party's role word is what THE PAPER calls them, so offering Swedish is right there. This one is a MATCHING KEY: `playbookKeyFor` lowercases it, `copilotPlaybookKey` mirrors it, and f133 requires both hosts to answer the same key — a translated word matches none of the patterns and takes the baseline book instead of the right one, in silence. The RECORD-keeps-English rule, in its third costume.
- **THE TWELVE ARE READ OFF `TEMPLATES`, NEVER TYPED** (`contractTypeKinds`, with `CONTRACT_TYPE_FALLBACK` as the literal for a stage without js/templates.js — `docLibWording`'s own idiom, pinned as a no-drift wall). They are the same words `cKind` writes onto every drafted contract, so an uploaded contract and a drafted one spell one type one way. **EVERY ONE OF THEM RESOLVES TO A REAL PLAYBOOK** and none falls to the baseline by accident — f361 (2) is that measurement, and it is what the English choice rests on.
- **IT OFFERS AND NEVER REFUSES**: the blank leads (clearing a term is an answer), whatever is on the record LEADS the words where it is not one of them (folded, so a reading is never quietly replaced), and the last row types the document's own words through `promptNewName`. `metaPickOptions` is the ONE reading behind all three, so a second `picks` field cannot drift.
- **A SENTINEL NEVER REACHES THE RECORD, AND THE WALL IS IN THE HANDLER** — there is no Save on this grid, every box writes as it is answered, so a cancelled name box returns before anything is written and puts the value back, as `bindFolderSelect` puts a stream back. **THE EVENT IS THE ELEMENT'S**: a `picks` field is text on the record and a SELECT on the screen, and a select answers on `change`.
Tests: f361 (20 claims, **18 red at the parent**; the two that pass are named `[wall]`), overview-as-drawn-verify 14 (7 checks driven with a real pointer, **all 7 red at the parent**, which prints `<INPUT>`). f351 (5) re-pointed in place — it pinned the ternary's own spelling, and **`wireKeyTerms` carries TWO `const evt=` lines**, so the region is the metadata sweep's own. That run's *noticed, not fixed* — `Edit these details` dead on a first paint — was **FIXED the same day**; see THE OVERVIEW'S ACTS WORK ON A FIRST PAINT below.

## THE OVERVIEW'S ACTS WORK ON A FIRST PAINT (Young ruled 22 Sep 2026)

*"fix the edit button bug too."* MEASURED in a real browser on an ordinary contract: open the Overview, press `Edit these details`, **ZERO boxes**; fold any section and press again, **24**. The button was drawn, visible and hit-testable the whole time.
- **ONE STRUCTURAL ODDITY, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DEFECT.** The stack has three hosts and two of them — `#kt-ov-lead`, `#kt-side` — are EMPTY SLOTS their painter fills when the tab is shown. `#kt-ov-terms` interpolated `ktOverviewTermsHtml` straight into the room's template instead, so its markup arrived **without `renderKeyTerms` ever running** — and that function is where every door on the card is wired: Edit these details, Move to another stream, a marked field's Fix, the signers row, the people list, and `wireKeyTerms`' own boxes. A fold calls it through `sectionWire`'s router, which is why a fold woke it and why this had never been seen.
- **THE FIX IS THE PRODUCT'S OWN IDIOM, TWELVE LINES ABOVE IT**: `#kt-triage-slot` is already noted as *"A SLOT, NOT THE STRIP ITSELF"*, with a painter, for exactly this shape of fault. The host becomes a slot, `applyWsTabs`' terms branch paints it beside the sibling painter it already called, and that host has **ONE WRITER** rather than two. No flash — `applyWsTabs` runs synchronously at the end of `wireWsTabs`, in the same tick as the template.
- **THE STANDALONE `wireKtRows` CALL IS GONE, NOT MOVED.** It was the hand-patched symptom — somebody had noticed the rows were dead and armed that one by name. `renderKeyTerms` calls it itself, and `wireKtRows` adds a listener per row **with no bound-once flag**, so leaving both would put two handlers on every row (a blur that writes twice). **ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING**: the side is painted first, so the painter's document-wide row sweep covers what the side drew.
- **`wireKtParties` IS SAFE ACROSS THE REPAINT** because it is delegated on the HOST and carries its own `dataset.pyBound` — `renderKeyTerms` writes the host's `innerHTML` and never replaces the element. Driven both ways to be sure.
- Two orphaned template locals (`ktEditable` / `ktReadable` at the room's own scope) went with it; the lint warning set is byte-identical.
Tests: f362 (12 claims, **7 red at the parent**; the two `[wall]`s pass on both sides by design), overview-as-drawn-verify **section 0** — which is FIRST in that file on purpose, because every other section folds something before it presses and a fold is exactly what used to hide this. `0a` prints `0 boxes before, 0 after` at the parent. `0b` is GATED on something having opened (ungated it passed there, on the fault). overview-as-drawn-verify 14's note re-pointed in place — it recorded this defect as reported-not-fixed, and a false note is worse than none.

## SEVEN FIXES OFF ONE REVIEW (Young's go on the before-and-after preview, 23 Sep 2026)

Diagnosed off a Warehousing agreement and a Maersk SaaS upload; the owner approved the preview and said *"fix all from 1 through 7 and merge to main."* Binding decisions: a highlight across two clauses never edits; the Document tab's highlight menu is untouched; every standard on Our standards is checked; a contract already negotiated keeps its clause split; Plain English starts the first time it is opened; governing law option A.

### 1 · WORD'S NUMBERS AND SPACES, EXACTLY AS WORD SHOWS THEM
- `docxNumbering(xml, stylesXml)` follows `w:numStyleLink`/`w:styleLink`; `docxStyleTable` / `docxStyleChain` walk `w:basedOn` (bounded at `DOCX_STYLE_HOPS` 20) for a style's numbering and outline level; `docxLevelForStyle` takes the level a list links to a style that names none; numbered paragraphs inside tables count in the body's own sequence (`docxTableHtml(tbl, report, numFn)`).
- A list HaTi cannot count all the way through draws NO numbers rather than shifted ones, counted on the file strip. Outline level 9 is body text.
- A space alone in its own bold/underlined run is KEPT (`RICH_KEEP_SPACE`, js/richdoc.js: the dress goes, the space stays — "Order.Unless" was the tell). Tests: f370, upload-structure-verify 8.
- PROVED ON THE OWNER'S REAL MAERSK FILE once it arrived: its "Ikke med" style is `basedOn` Heading 1 and overrides nothing, so Word numbers it in Heading 1's list — main read "48.2 Completion of performance of Project Phase", Word (and now HaTi) reads 57.2.

### 2 · A PAGE BANNER OVER NUMBERED CLAUSES IS A SECTION TITLE
- `_clBanners(blocks, headings)` (js/clausemodel.js): unnumbered headings ABOVE numbered clauses whose numbers run on across them are banners, and a banner rides with the clause after it (`sectionHtml`); `rlSectionHtml(cl)` draws it as a quiet `.rl-sect` title with no pencil on all three negotiate papers.
- ONCE STAMPED, THE IDS DECIDE: a stamped body is read by which headings carry ids, so a rename or insertion cannot flip it and a contract stamped the old way KEEPS its split. `clauseCarryIds` carries only onto headings the fresh read stamped, so Re-read on an un-negotiated contract adopts the new split. Tests: f371, upload-structure-verify.

### 3 · PREPARE REDLINES CHECKS EVERY STANDARD, AND SAYS WHAT IT CHECKED
- `pbStandardsFor(c)` (js/playbook.js) is the ONE list: every standard on Our standards (library positions folded with the book's; a range folds into its standard; the book decides how hard each is held). `pbStandardsSent` is what the route is sent, `pbAlignVerdicts` pairs answers back; both review branches stamp `std.label`.
- FOUR answers — aligned · deviation · missing · `na` (never a departure; `PB_SETTLED_STATUSES`). `pbReviewTokens` sizes the answer and the route says `truncated`; a cut-short or empty answer is REFUSED and never saved. "Every standard is met" only over a FINISHED check (`pbReviewComplete`); a saved check is reused only where finished and current (`pbReviewUsable`); every result names the count checked (`rlPbCheckedLine`, `rlPbOutcomeSay`). Tests: f372, prepare-redlines-verify 9.

### 4 · EDIT WITH COPILOT FROM ANY HIGHLIGHT ON THE NEGOTIATE PAGE
- `rlSelInFront(sel)`: a highlight with both ends in the paper's head or recital is the FRONT REGION's own words → Ask · Edit · Comment, through the editor's door.
- Across two clauses: Ask · Comment only, never Edit. **Ask opens the EDITING Copilot on the first clause** (`askAt`, `passageMode:'ask'`); `rlAskCopilotPanel` remains only where the editor cannot take the words. The Document tab is untouched. Tests: one-copilot-verify, f96, f304.

### 5 · ONE COPILOT LOOK IN THE CLAUSE EDITOR
- `ceRenderScope` draws ONE card, ALWAYS, in four states: the whole clause (`.is-clause`, the pencil), your words (Edit), a question (`.is-asking`), the whole contract (`.is-whole`, after the ✕ — `_ceWhole`, `ceSetWhole`). A probe for "the passage card" asks `.ce-scope:not(.is-clause):not(.is-whole)`. The greeting SENTENCE is gone, its rows stay.
- Whole-contract mode: `context.wholeDoc` lifts the chat routes' per-turn cap to `aiDocChars()` for the LAST user message only; answers name clauses and change no wording. Tests: one-copilot-verify; clause-editor-verify's card probes and redline-verify 3 re-pointed.

### 6 · PLAIN ENGLISH READS IN THE BACKGROUND, A CLAUSE AT A TIME
- `clause_reading_rows` keeps each clause the moment it is read, keyed `readRowHash(lang,row)` (kind · num · heading · text — never the page key); `readRowsKeep` is the ONE writer (INSERT OR IGNORE); deleted with the contract. A cut-short answer and a page more than a quarter misfiled are SHOWN, never kept. The whole-edition cache is unchanged, except one with `unmatched>0` is not served whole: the next press asks for the hole alone.
- THE READING IS A JOB (`_readJobs`, contract+lang): outlives the request; a second press on the same wording JOINS; different wording waits. A failed page is asked again ONCE; only a press where no page answered is refused (502); a tool block of any other name is no answer.
- `GET /api/contracts/:id/reading-progress?run=&from=` — NOT under /api/ai/, no limiter, no spend, scope-checked, about ONE press (`run`).
- THE PAGE: the switch is set FIRST and the column fills (`_docReadJobs`; `docReadPoll` only while `docReadWatching`); "Reading N of M" (`ct_read_progress`) in the head's moved slot; `.doc-read-wait` "Reading…" beside each clause still to come — its own class, placed in the entries' pass. A dropped connection waits on the server (`DOC_READ_WAIT_MS`), then asks once more. Tests: f373, reading-in-the-background-verify.

### 7 · THE CONTRACT'S OWN GOVERNING LAW UNDER THE TITLE
- The negotiate paper's sub-line read "Jurisdiction:" off the WORKSPACE market (`RL_REGION`, deleted). `contractGoverningLaw(c)` (js/metadata.js, published) is the ONE reading — `metadata.governingLaw`, what the Overview prints; nothing read → the line names the kind only, never a guess. `ng_paper_law` in both books; the law is the record's and is never translated. Tests: f374.
