## TWO COPIES OF ONE CONTRACT — THE WORKING COPY AND THE SIGNING COPY (Young ruled 25 Sep 2026, picks 1A 2B 3A 4A 5A 6A)

*"When a contract goes to the document page, the negotiation page as well, it should look like its on Microsoft Word waiting to be edited. But when you go to the signing page it should look exactly like how it was designed."*
- **`js/pages.js` IS THE ONE PAGE-MAKER UNDER BOTH COPIES.** The sheet stays ONE element with exactly the markup it held: a block that would cross a page is pushed down by `margin-top` (a batch-measured correction pass beats margin collapse), and a layer (`[data-pg-layer]`, aria-hidden, its words generated content through `attr()`) paints the grey gap, Word's corner marks and each page's head and foot. Nothing is inserted into the wording, so every reading that walks the painted page (Plain English, X-ray, sign spots, note marks, the field link, a highlight) finds what it found. `pagesPlan` is PURE; a heading keeps with the WHOLE next block; **a block taller than a page GROWS its page — wording is never cut**. `pagesWatch` re-breaks on a resize (`PG_WATCH_MS`); `.pg-sheet::after{height:var(--pg-extra)}` makes the last page whole (never the inline padding — a `padding` shorthand holding a var() answers '' for its longhand).
- **THE WORKING COPY** (Document tab; Negotiate page through `rlPaginate` from `negoAfterPaint`; the clause editor is NOT paged): white pages, `PG_GAP` 20, corners, the letterhead's name FADED in the top margin (`pagesLetterheadName`, 2B), "Page k of n" faded in the foot (3A). Always ONE column; the design lends its typeface only.
- **THE SIGNING COPY** (the Signing tab, every tab once Signed — `docCopyOf`; their signing link; the printed PDF): a fixed 794px A4 page (`PG_SIGN_W/H`, `PG_SIGN_PAD`), the design at full strength — the letterhead on page one, `.pg-run` on pages 2+, the design's footer carrying the number on EVERY page (`pagesSignFoot`); two-column dropped; fields as words and an empty one a ruled line (`docSignBodyHtml`); always white (light tokens pinned on `.pg-sheet.pg-sign`). The size control ZOOMS by transform (`scApplyZoom`, `SC_ZOOMS`, `hati.v1.signZoom`, default fit) and never re-breaks (4A). `docSheetHtml` is the ONE builder per copy; `docRepaintSheet` swaps them on the tab change and re-arms the canvas's listeners.
- **THE PLACES TO SIGN ARE ON THE SIGNING COPY ONLY** (5A): `wireDocCanvas` paints spots and `pagesSignFlags` ("Sign here"; our line index 0, theirs 1) only where `docCopyOf(c)==='sign'`.
- **THEIR PAPER NEVER WEARS OURS** (`signCopyTheirs`): an unedited PDF or scan → their file in the browser's viewer plus an UNNUMBERED signature page (`data-pg-sigpage`); a Word file → `report.layout` (`docxLayoutOf` / `docxReadLayout`: page size, margins, face, size, header, footer — nothing guessed); an edited PDF → the agreed words on a plain page, said in the control row (`sc_src_rebuilt`, 6A).
- **PRINT**: `pagesPrintPages` rebuilds one `.pp-page` box per screen page with the same furniture, plus `@page{size:A4;margin:0}` for the print only (`pagesPrintPageRule`); `fillPrintRoot` and the portal's `exportPDF` use it for the signing copy.
- **REFUSAL 3, SAID OUT LOUD**: the Document tab's first line is unmoved (271.9 — and with a design it moved UP 80px, 352.1 → 272.9); the Negotiate page's is unmoved; **the Signing tab's sits 30px lower** (271.9 → 301.9), the signing page's own 64px top margin against the working copy's 34px. No chrome grew (signing-on-paper-verify 1c re-pointed to that relation). The owner's to rule on.
Tests: f383 (42 claims, 38 red at the parent; the four that pass are named walls), two-copies-verify (28 checks in a real browser; `HATI_SHOT_DIR` for its pictures). **REVERSED IN PLACE by this ruling**: F89 (2)'s flat, warm sheet and redline-verify 2's "it is FLAT" (the Negotiate page's paper is the working copy — white, its own edge, the page shadow, asserted as the three tokens); redline-verify 2b counts gaps between clauses on ONE page (a page break is told apart by the page-maker's own record, never by its size). **Re-pointed**: signing-on-paper-verify 1c (see refusal 3), f225's region (the canvas lives in `docSheetHtml` now — anchor on `#doc-sheet-host`), f278 (1) (a third scroll listener, the signing copy's page number, named). The new Word names sit at the END of docx.js's publish lists (f366 pins `{docxStyledIsWording,` as the first).

## THE COMPACT BUTTON LADDER (Young picked it 26 Sep 2026, off the "HaTi Button Audit" page)

*"Implement compact and merge to main."* The review measured eleven button heights (22–48), three weights, boxes at 28–36 beside buttons at 30, emoji for icons, and dialogs whose buttons scrolled away. **THREE RUNGS, SAID ONCE in `:root`**: `--ctl-h-sm` 22 (`.ui-btn-sm`, rows and cards, 12px) · `--ctl-h` 28 (`.ui-btn`, everything else, 13px) · `--ctl-h-lg` 32 (`.ui-btn-lg` — an area's one big act: Sign, a first password, an empty page's invitation; the filled act, except a HELD Sign, which keeps the rung and wears the secondary face so it never promises — `#sign-btn.sign-held`). Padding `--pad-ctl-x-sm/-/-lg` 8/10/12, icons `--btn-ic` 14 / `--btn-ic-lg` 16 (`.ui-btn > svg`), `--btn-gap` 6 icon-to-word, `--btn-group-gap` 8 between buttons. `--radius` 4 untouched.
- **A TEXT BOX IS THE BUTTON'S HEIGHT**: `--field-h:var(--ctl-h)`, taken as HEIGHT by a one-line box (HATI_FLD, RV_FLD, WZ_ST, the fill forms, `.ui-fld` for the utility-class forms, `.of-amt`).
- **ONE LABEL WEIGHT (500)**; the filled face says which act leads, never the weight. A switch's resting half reads 500 beside the buttons and the lit half stays bold (the 11 Sep ruling stands); tabs keep their own rule.
- **THE ROW RUNG IS A 24px TARGET**: `.ui-btn-sm::after{inset:-2px}` — an absolute box sits against the PADDING box, so -1px added nothing (measured with elementFromPoint).
- **TEXT BUTTONS ARE `.ui-link`** (accent, 500, no underline, ≥ `--tap-min`, a DRAWN arrow; `.ui-link-danger` for Revoke / Remove key). An underline is only for a link inside a sentence, and those were left alone.
- **ONE FILLED BUTTON PER AREA**: a repeated row's main act is `.ui-btn-accent` (the ink, never the fill); a bordered destructive act is `.ui-btn-danger`. Both written AFTER the redesign's white face, one class heavier.
- **DRAWN ICONS ONLY**: no emoji or typed →/▾/✕/↻/➤ in a button's words (f385 sweeps every `<button>`); `plusLed(html)` draws a leading "+ "; ICONS gained chevU · chevL · more · refresh; the writing bar's caret is `RICH_BAR_CARET`, kept OUT of RICH_BAR_ICON (f266's nine tools are all 15 wide).
- **A DIALOG'S BUTTONS STAY IN VIEW**: Cancel then the act, at the right. `.dlg-foot` names a foot; `dlgFootOf` / `dlgPinFoot` (js/core.js, armed in openModal, released in closeModal like the trap and the drag) FIND every other one — the last row of nothing but buttons holding a `.ui-btn`, nothing readable after it — mark it `data-dlg-foot` and pin it; `data-scrolls` on the panel draws the hairline only while it scrolls. "Close" only for a window that just shows information.
- NOT TAKEN, said out loud: the iPad touch step-up (not chosen), the phone's own shell, Reports (off the rail, kept byte-identical), the signature pad's tabs, the writing bar's size (2 Sep ruling), the Copilot composer's 40px send, the Insights ask box, the Compare dialog's mode switch.
- Refusal 3, measured on the same stage at the parent and after: first ink 271.9 / 286.7 / 301.9 (Document / Negotiate / Signing), unmoved.
- **THE COLOUR CENSUS WAS NOT RE-RECORDED**: it is already red on 19 screens at the parent (other people's drift). The uncut set difference against the parent is exactly two moves, both this ladder's own: the approval card's Reject leaves Tailwind's rose for the ruby tokens (`--st-ruby-fg` / `--st-ruby-line`), and a held Sign loses its pale accent wash. Listed in BUGLOG.
Tests: f385 (23 claims, 21 red at the parent; two walls), compact-ladder-verify (29 checks in a real browser, 21 red at the parent); re-pointed in place: f89, f91, f240, f245, f265, f277 (11), f305, f306 (9), f313 (39), f314 (4), f345 (4), f368 (5); in the browser: counterparty-leads-verify 3d, one-door-verify 1a, templates-tabs-verify 9a, flat-rows-and-alerts-verify 3c, nego-redesign-verify 13, pages-read-alike-verify 5 — each asked as the relation (the box height and the icon size read live, one weight across a row, the drawn plus).

## ONE BUTTON: ONE LINE, ONE SIZE PER ROW, ONE LIGHT EDGE (Young ruled 26 Sep 2026, three screenshots)

*"buttons should never wrap text … the same size and likely the size of the needs your decision card … some buttons have dark outlines when the common approach is a light grey outline."* Measured first in WORKORDER-button-consistency.md.
- **A BUTTON'S WORDS NEVER WRAP**: ONE `:is(...)` rule in index.html states `white-space:nowrap` for every family that draws a labelled button (nineteen, from `.ui-btn` to `.rl-pb-btn`). **Each entry is ONE class**: `:is()` takes its heaviest argument's weight, and one id or a second class would lift every family above the rules that dress it. The Contracts row menu's cell takes less side padding so its square fits its column at a 1024 window.
- **HOME'S TWO CARDS, ONE BUTTON SIZE**: `hmRowBtnCls(cls)` (js/views/home.js) is the ONE reading the desk's row and the dormant triage row ask — the ladder's row rung, the lead act `ui-btn-accent` (the ink, never a fill on every row), Put away `ui-link`. `.hm-tri-b` is a HOOK and states no box; the act row no longer stretches its buttons to its tallest item.
- **ONE LIGHT GREY EDGE**: `--btn-edge` is `--color-divider` (#E2E7E5) by day and `--rule-strong` at night, each said once, and every family that named its own edge reads it (the switches and their seams, the chips, the stepper, the secondary button, Add note, the queue tab, the playbook button, the Send dialog's purpose buttons, Insights' Read them now). A switch still FILLS its lit half; a text box keeps `--field-line` (it says where to type); a filled button's edge is its fill.
Tests: f386 (14 claims, 9 red at the parent), button-consistency-verify (17 checks, 11 red); f335 (5) and f364 (9) re-pointed to the relation (the pair shares one edge token).

## THE LIST INSPECTOR — CONTRACTS, NEGOTIATIONS, APPROVALS & SIGNING (Young picked it 26 Sep 2026, option 3 of "Contract List Options")

*"Build Inspector and apply to the approvals and signing pages as well."* A narrower list beside one contract's facts: a press SELECTS, a second press OPENS (the panel's own button, Enter, a double-click), the arrow keys move the selection. The phone is not in it.
- **`js/views/inspector.js` IS ONE PANEL FOR THREE PAGES**: `insPaintPanel(o)` draws the head (reference · kind, the counterparty — every outside party on a multi-party contract, see EVERY PARTY BUT OURS below —, the agreement, status · whose move, the page's own acts and a ⋯) and the sections the caller orders — `lead` (a page's own), `table`, `facts`, `reads`, `latest`. ONE delegated listener per element reads what to do off the element at press time (`host._ins`).
- **THE WIDTH IS MEASURED**: `insFits()` asks `#content`'s own width against `INS_MIN_W` 1040 (the narrowest that holds four columns AND keeps the filter row on one line). Below it each page keeps its full table (every column) and one press opens there (named CONTROLS); the floor, the card and the Display menu below are drawn in both shapes. `data-ins-page` / `data-ins` record the shape and `insWatchWidth` repaints when a resize crosses the line; `insForce` is a stage's override, never stored.
- **THE SELECTION IS PER SEAT, IN MEMORY** (`insSelect` / `insPick`): kept while it is on the list, else the first row, so a filter never leaves the panel describing a contract the reader cannot see. `insListWire` binds once per tbody (roving `tabindex`, `aria-current`).
- **EVERY FACT IS BORROWED AND NOTHING WRITES**: `insFacts` (value only with `canViewValues`, in the contract's own currency), `insMove` over `negoMoveSay`, `insTable` reading `c.changes` RAW (theirs first, `INS_ASKS_MAX` 5 then a count, "past your standard" through the desk's published `deskWorkingDaysBetween` against `deskCfg().staleDays`), `insReads` reading `ktReadingsRows` — the Overview's readings table split into counting and drawing so both read one place. **LATEST IS NOT ON THE LIGHT LIST**: `insLatest` answers null where `audit` is stripped; the panel asks `ensureFull` once, repaints `.ins-latest` alone and only for the same contract, and says a failure.
- **ONE DOOR**: the acts are the page's own. Contracts: Open contract (accent), Open negotiation only where one has started — a change on it, the Document tab's own reading in `wsTabRowEndHtml`, never merely a negotiation object (opening a contract can leave an empty one) — and `negoMayStart` allows it; Negotiations the reverse; the ⋯ is the row's own menu (`regRowActsHtml` / `regRunRowAct`); `regOpenRow` is the one open for a press, Enter and a double-click. Approvals & signing: `apLeadHtml` (the rule, who it waits on, who asked, how long — or what stands before signing, borrowed from `signReadiness`, three then a count) and the lead act `apOpenSigning`; the page still decides nothing.
- **THE REGISTER'S SHAPE**: `regInspecting()` / `regColKeys()` — four columns in plain words (`REG_COL_KEYS_INS`, `REG_COL_KEYS_NEGO_INS`, `REG_INS_COL_PX`; no grips; **the third column is one width on both seats**, so the reference, the counterparty and the value are cut identically in pixels, the full tables' own relation since 21 Sep). **REVERSED, both shapes, by the drawing**: the white band of 24–25 Aug — the title, its facts and the views sit on the page ground and the filter row is the list's own white card's top row, its point kept (the filters and the rows they narrow are one card with no seam); the column headings are the label rung in plain words (12px, `--w-label`), not bold micro caps, with a group's name at `--w-strong` over a lighter count. Table · Board, density and the amendment fold are ONE Display menu (`regDisplayHtml`), so the page carries one filled button.
- **THE DRAWING'S FLOOR, BOTH SHAPES**: a name prints "&" (`regTitleOf` already escapes; the row escaped it twice); "Non-monetary", never "n/m"; days left only within `REG_SOON_DAYS` 90 (`regEndsSay`); plain column names with an arrow only on the sorted one; the resting reference in the quiet ink, the selected one in the accent; "N live" in the head (`ngl_n_live`); a view with nothing in it prints no count (`.reg-vtab.is-zero`); an empty group is not drawn; no Contracts views on Negotiations.
- NOT BUILT, said out loud: the drawing's Owner filter on Negotiations and its Draft new agreement button on the Negotiations head.
Tests: f387 (34 claims, 32 red at the parent; a wall and a control pass on both; 2k and 3d also red at their own parent), inspector-verify (32 checks in a real browser, 28 red at the parent; the stage, 4a/4b and the error sweep pass on both); re-pointed in place: f97, f184, f240, f258, f301, f325, f328, f333, f344, f350, f358, f379. **A browser file that measures the FULL table stages it with `insForce(false)`** (the page's own stage door) and says so beside the line — compact-ladder 1, contracts-page, counterparty-leads, five-images-two 1, negotiations-door, signed-and-columns; flat-rows 5 measures BOTH shapes (the old names for the full table, "5i-" for the Inspector). Re-pointed in place to the relation they meant: adapt-filters (the bar's content height, not its padded box), button-consistency 1a (the words wherever they are drawn), row-density (the segments sit in Display), room-head-fold (opens with the second press), thirteen-screenshots 1c (no narrower than its sibling chip), contracts-page 8/15/15b (the one card is the list's) and 12a (fix 3's edge token).

### EVERY PARTY BUT OURS ON THE PANEL (Young ruled 26 Sep 2026)

*"For contracts that have multiple parties, all the parties apart from the owner should be listed on the right panels."* The head printed the first outside party and "+1"; the rest were on the hover only.
- **`insParties(c)` IS THE ONE READING** (published): `partiesTheirs(c)`, never ours, asked ONLY where `partiesMulti(c)` — so a two-party contract draws its old one-name head byte for byte. Empty means "draw the counterparty as before", never "nobody".
- **`insPartiesHtml(list)` IS THE ONE DRAWING**: a line per party (`.ins-cp-p`, `data-ins-party`), the name keeps its own cut (`.ins-cp-n`), the paper's word for them beside it only where one is recorded (`.ins-cp-r`, the quiet ink), the whole `partyLine` on the hover; no cap (PARTY_MAX bounds it). The heading becomes a column (`.ins-cp.is-many`).
- **TWO HOMES**: the list panel's head (Contracts, Negotiations, Approvals & signing — one builder) and the line under the contract's name on Our standards' departures panel (`sdDevPanelOpts`' `sub`).
- **THE LIST ROWS KEEP THEIR "+1"** — the multi-party build's compact mark; the ask was the panels.
- **NOT SWEPT, said out loud**: the obligation panels ("We owe X this") and the panel's "from X" / "sent to X" name ONE party because an obligation and a proposed change record none; listing all would claim what the record does not hold.
Tests: f391 (14 claims, 12 red at the parent; 2a the control, 2d a wall), every-party-verify (16 checks in a real browser, 10 red at the parent, which prints "SAP East Africa+1"; the stage, the control 1f, the walls 1d/2b/4b and the error sweep pass on both).

### WHAT THIS CONTRACT NEEDS FROM YOU — THE CHECKLIST (Young picked "Checklist" by name, 27 Sep 2026)

*"a nicely designed banner in the contract's inspector side panel that explains what attention is needed … right under the party names and in color."* Picked off "Attention Banner Options"; A BAND THE OWNER ASKED FOR BY NAME (on WHAT STANDS).
- **`needsYouOf(c)` (js/views/home.js) IS THE ONE READING**: Home's own sources asked of `[c]` — deskStaleInboxFor · reviewInboxFor · deskJoinInboxFor · hmMySignings · `hmRenewalDue` (lifted out of hmDashSlices, whose decisions are now built from it) — and Home's own lateness (`hmReviewLate`, `HM_SOON_DAYS` 30, asked by hmDecisionItems too). Late first, then `NEEDS_YOU_ORDER` (quiet · review · join · sign · renewal). **DELIBERATELY NOT HERE**: a contract merely sitting in review, and a renewal on a contract someone else owns (`contractOwnedBy`). **AND HOME'S CARD LISTS THE SAME FIVE KINDS since the same day** (Young: yes) — "Waiting on review" left `hmDecisionItems` (`waitingLongest` stays in the slices: the phone reads it; `home_waiting_on_review` / `home_idle_days` INERT in both books) and a renewal is a row only where `owns(x.c)` (contractOwnedBy, the checklist's question). Measured on the sample book: the card went from 12 "Waiting on review" rows to "Nothing to decide" — no sample contract has an owner. f395 1d REVERSED; f382 (3) drives it. READING MUST NOT WRITE.
- **`insNeedsHtml(c, skip)` (js/views/inspector.js) draws and decides nothing**: in `insHeadHtml` under the name block (party names AND the agreement's name, never split) and above the status line, so all three contract panels draw it; nothing owed draws nothing. Frame in the worst row's tone, a head that counts, one row per item (dot, title, one line from `insNeedWords` — a part marked `hover` rides the hover only), one `ui-btn-sm` verb (Home's verb keys). **The Approvals & signing page's signatures tab passes `needsSkip:['sign']`** (its lead already says what stands before signing).
- **EVERY NUMBER IS BORROWED**: the days their asks waited are the asks table's own (`_insDaysSince`), the standard is `ins_over` and rides the hover, the signature names the Signing tab's first thing (`signReadiness` + `signRowTitle`).
- **`needsYouGo(kind, id)` IS THE ONE DOOR**, pressed by the panel's one listener (`[data-ins-need]`): quiet/review → the negotiation, sign → Signing tab, renewal → Overview, join → the room with `openDeskSheet`. It answers whether it found the contract (true/false). **A RENEWAL READS THE CONTRACT AGAIN** (Young, 27 Sep 2026: *"the 5 checks … should run all over again so that you can see what they say before you go through the steps of deciding"*): the door registers `roomReadOnArrival(id)` BEFORE the room opens, and the Overview (applyWsTabs' terms branch) spends it through `roomReadAgainDue(c)` — once, only on a record loaded in full (ensureFull copies the stored record over the object when it lands), only within `ROOM_READ_AGAIN_MS` (60s) — running `triageAndPaint(c,{again:true,fresh:true})`, the whole arrival read; `fresh` is the brief's own `force`, because the brief is the one reading with a cache. The cost is on the press's hover (`ins_need_go_terms`, reworded; Home's renewal row `title`; the bell's renewal rows' `hint`). Plain English is NOT re-read — it walks the Document tab's painted page. The landing also repaints the head (`roomHeadRefresh` in the onStep), and a signed contract's fill tile says `sealed` (`tri_fill_sealed`), never "in negotiation". **THE FILL STEP STANDS DOWN ON A SIGNED CONTRACT** (`status==='Signed'` or `negoWordingFrozen`): it answered a signed template contract's blanks from the record, the server refuses `fields` on an executed record (409), and the refused save put the old record back over EVERY reading of the run — measured on the first cut (65a4bde) by go-aheads-verify 3k and home-page-verify's error sweep. f396 (4), go-aheads-verify 3. **THREE HOMES PRESS IT SINCE 27 SEP 2026** (Young: *"Yes, make them go straight to the right place"*): Home's rows (`data-dd-kind`, the item's `kind`, else `selectContract`) and the bell's request-to-join row and BOTH renewal rows (`bellGo` in `buildAlerts`, else `openWorkspace`). The bell's review, quiet-desk and signature rows keep their own copies of the same destinations (noticed, logged). f395 (8), inspector-checklist-verify 8 (all 8 red at ba092e2, each landing on the Document tab).

Upload their contract, negotiate it with every tool, hand the agreed WORDS over as a clean Word file, they design and sign it their way, the signed copy is filed and the contract takes its number. The design page is the artifact "Redline Here, Sign There".
- **`js/outside.js` IS THE ONE READING, BOTH HOSTS**: `contractRef(c)` = `c.contractNo || c.id` — PRINT IT wherever a reference is read (≈150 sites swept, guarded `window.contractRef?…:c.id`); **`c.id` IS THE KEY FOREVER** (RL-### stays the key after filing; lookups, data attributes, API paths, dedupe keys stay on it); `contractRefMatches` finds by either (openFromHash, palette, register search, Copilot `aiContractByRef` / `copilotGetJson` by `contract_no`). `signRouteOf` (absent = inside). The clock: `ohWorkdays` = `saWorkdays` (f388 pins), first reminder `HANDOVER_REMIND_WORKDAYS` 5 then weekly, still-live at `HANDOVER_LIVE_DAYS` 60. `outsideCompare` / `outsideReadCopy` / `outsideBlanksIn` / `outsideFileIds`.
- **THE WORKING FILE**: upload asks who runs the signing (admin default `signRouteDefault`, inside at rest); RL ids off `window.rlUid` (server setting, max); **the server gives `contractNo` in the save that files it** (or when the route becomes inside), column `contract_no`; an id that is somebody's number is refused (idTaken). On Negotiations from day one (`negoIsLive` asks `outsideListed`), off Contracts unless searched (the row says where it lives), band `out` "With them for signature". Its uploaded document's blanks panel stands down (`uploadBlanksTheirs` — see A FILE THEY SIGN HAS NO BLANKS FOR US TO FILL).
- **THE HANDOVER IS ROUTE-OWNED**: `POST /api/contracts/:id/handover` (hand · send · chase · check · partial · sendback · live · reopen · filed) writes on the STORED record; the PUT keeps stored `handover` / `handoverHistory` / `contractNo`. `hand` re-asks everything (route, lead, negotiation settled, rule chain, personal approval, check; how they agreed — EVERY negotiating party by name and day where more than one negotiated), READS the Word file (`tplZipEntry`) and refuses a blank; mails it to each address; our own people are told through `hoPeople` (lead, desk, signatory, approvers — NEVER the Overview's Who else list, which the server never reads: f354). While out: `HANDOVER_FROZEN` + route locked (handoverFreeze), no in-app signature, no signing link (theySign), no round (handedOver), their link reads only (`portalHandedOver`) and serves the file; approvals do not lapse (`saStarted`); reopen withdraws them and their link says so.
- **THE SIGNING TAB**: `renderSignButton` hands to `renderOutsideSign`; ONE LIST — `signBlockers` drops turn/signers/spots, cap/folder read OUR SIGNATORY, `ho-signatory` never holds, `ho-blanks` holds. No "Sign here"; the signing order says who signs, no turns, no notices (server: `they-sign`); head acts `ho-hand` / `ho-file`; never on Home's or the bell's signings; alert kind `handover`, ranked after `desk-quiet`.
- **FILING** (Signing tab, or Upload recognises it — `HO_MATCH_MIN` 0.6, the likeliest `HO_MATCH_MAX` 20 compared, a pick-list of EVERY file out; asks, never assumes): the save is guarded as a DIFFERENCE — handed over, `method:'outside'`, `SIGNED_VIA`, copy on the server, **`everyone===true` (filing needs every signature)**, differing words need the approver or an admin with a reason (`srvMayAcceptDiffer` — an approval GIVEN, never a withdrawn request; also on a part-signed copy, which never files); a blank they filled is not differing words (see A BLANK THEY FILLED IN IS NOT A CHANGE). The old paper door is closed on EVERY contract (handoverNeeded): "Signed on paper instead?" now switches the route, and `openPaperSignatureModal` has no caller. v3 seal binds the signed copy and verifySeal re-hashes the stored file; the evidence pack names the copy, the handover and the check; `executedAttachment` sends the signed copy; EXECUTED_IMMUTABLE += signedCopy · contractNo · signRoute; the route cannot move once anybody signed (routeFreeze).

### A BLANK THEY FILLED IN IS NOT A CHANGE (Young ruled 26 Sep 2026: "yes, accept the filled-in blanks without asking")

The signed copy comes back with the agreed words' blanks filled — the date line, `[______]`, "[Customer name]", a Word box — and the word check read each one as changed wording, so filing needed the approver or an admin.
- **A BLANK IS THE UPLOAD PANEL'S OWN READING**: `ohBlankHits` asks `upHits` through the global (names by `upLabel`/`upLead`), narrowed by the handover's `OH_NOT_BLANK` ("[Reserved]", "[Signature]" are not blanks); no copy of the shapes in js/outside.js (f389 (3a)). Where the panel's reader is not loaded no blank is read — the old answer, which asks a person.
- **`ohChunksBlanks` takes a blank OUT of the words and keeps it as a gap**; matching is otherwise untouched (a ruled line was already zero words). `ohFillOps`: a run of THEIR words with none of ours struck, at a gap carrying a blank, at most `OH_FILL_MAX` (20) a blank, becomes `'f'` — kept for every reading (`ohKept`) and listed. A placeholder left as it was is the agreed wording, not a fill. Pass 2's window is widened by what the blanks can hold.
- **A LINE THAT IS ONLY A BLANK** is pinned by its two neighbouring paragraphs (both found, in order, nothing claimed between; one line and 20 words a blank) — a NAMED blank only: a bare ruled line is a line to SIGN on, and a sentence written there is added text.
- **WORD BOXES** are read off the agreed markup by `outsideAgreedParas` (`fields`, found by their own words; an empty box reads `___`). **THEIR COPY IS NEVER READ FOR BLANKS** — a bracket they added is words they added.
- **SAID, NEVER HIDDEN**: `outsideFillsHtml` (open, on the check window and the filing screen), `outsideCompareLine` adds "N blanks filled in.", `signedCopy.compare.filled` + `fills` (first `HO_FILLS_KEPT` 30; the evidence pack takes the compare whole), and the signed record's "the same as agreed" cell counts them.
- Not covered, said: a fill that starts on its paragraph's line and wraps onto the next in a PDF reads its tail as added text; a signing service's stamp on a bare signature line inside the agreement reads as before. **The handover's own placeholder check (`OH_BLANK_RES`) lets `[amount]` / `[Price]` through, so such a blank filled by them is now accepted and listed — logged for the owner, not widened here.**
Tests: f389 (26 claims, 16 red at the parent e2d34ea; ten WALLS and CONTROLS), redline-here-sign-there-verify section 8 (8a0–8e red at the parent, which reads "3 differences from the agreed wording").

## THE OVERNIGHT CLEAN-UP (owner-asked 26 Sep 2026: "review the entire platform … whatever bugs you find, fix them")

About seventy faults, each measured in a real browser or against a real server before a line moved. The rules they left behind:
- **PLAIN ENGLISH**: the mirror stops at the first clause ON THE PAPER (`docReadFront(c, rows)`), never the first one read — a later page lands first on a long contract; a copied preamble is cut at a whole line above the first clause and fades (`.doc-read-mirror.is-cut`); one `docReadSheet` walk per paint, every top READ before any is WRITTEN (~550ms → ~90ms a paint).
- **ONE ESCAPE FOR #modal-root**: `rootEscSet(fn)` (js/core.js) — openModal and openSidePanel hand it their Escape, closeModal takes it off, a declined guard leaves it armed. The opener is read BEFORE a replacing dialog tears the old panel out and handed to the trap. confirmDialog: an explicit `cancelLabel:''` draws no Cancel, `multiline` keeps line breaks; a replaced question is SETTLED (`_settle`), never left hanging. Its only options are confirmLabel / cancelLabel / danger / title / message / multiline — `confirm:`, `okText:`, `confirmText:` were silently ignored. Phone sheets close on Escape (`document._mSheetEscWired`).
- **THEIR PAGE REMEMBERS WHAT IT SENT**: `portalSaveSent` / `portalLoadSent` (`hati.negoSent.<token>`, decisions and withdrawals only — a proposal is re-filed under the owner's own id), not read once `lastResponse.applied===true`, let go when the record catches up; the bell repaints after Send.
- **A SLOW ANSWER LANDS ON ITS OWN CONTRACT**: `contractOnScreen(c)` (js/core.js) is asked before a brief, a scan, a check or a triage result repaints. **The head follows the record**: `roomHeadRefresh(c)` repaints title, status, quiet line, facts and crumb after an Overview or party write — a paint, never a rebuild.
- **PER-SITTING MARKS NEVER REACH THE RECORD**: `SITTING_KEYS` / `dropSittingKeys` (server) and saveContract drop `_messages`, `_msgFetch`, `_shareFetch`, `_signChecking`, `_triaging`. **A signature image is an image**: `sigImageOk` (server, save and respond) and `sigImageSrc` (every screen that draws one). An async route's rejection goes to next(); an unhandled rejection is logged, never fatal.
- **LISTENERS ARE ARMED ONCE** on document (the negotiate page's `document._negoSelKillWired`, the room's `document._wsMoreOutsideWired`, the brief card's `dataset.ktBriefBound`) — a closure bound per paint keeps the whole page alive (125,000 nodes after 100 paints).
- **A RULED LINE'S KEY IS `upLead`, ITS LABEL `upLeadName`** — the label drops an unclosed bracket and a list marker; the key never moves, so an answer already typed is found again. `obRecurLabel` is the one reading of how often an obligation repeats. `m_requested_by` was already a key — **a duplicate key's LAST literal wins**, and lint's no-dupe-keys is the net.
- **SERVER**: the hold guards run on every save (they sat inside the half-signed branch); a bound signing link goes to its row's address (409) and an unbound signature from another address completes no step; a revoked, expired or answered link makes no signing code; the rate limiter keeps each bucket's own window (`rlNoteWindow`); the unused-file sweep is registered BEFORE `/api/files/:id` (Express matches in order); `fileInScope` asks only contracts whose JSON can hold the id; the mailroom writes the browser's own upload shape (`fileName`, `mime`, `fileId`, `fileHash` over the data URL) and counts against the storage ceiling; `executedAttachment` reads an upload's bytes by `fileId`; a deleted contract takes `clause_readings` with it.
- **A REFUSED SAVE PUTS THE PAGE BACK** (`saveContract`, 400/403/409): the reason is said and the record on file is loaded and drawn, so what the reader sees is what is saved. **A BROWSER FILE THAT STAGES A STATE THE SERVER REFUSES MEASURES NOTHING** — signing-flow-verify 6 emptied the route of the contract section 4 had just signed and was reading the refused copy (re-pointed to an unsigned contract, with a guard that the stage landed).
- **A LOOK AT THE TRAIL MAY NOT UNDO AN EDIT**: a light row asks for its trail (`insLatest` answers null), and the Inspector's and the obligation history's loader is `restoreHeavyFields`, NEVER `ensureFull` — that one copies the server's whole record over the one on screen, and a category or status set a moment before read back as the stored one (register-category-verify, home-page-verify 3c). **`restoreHeavyFields` ALSO CARRIES THE SINGLE-RECORD ROUTE'S TRANSPORT** (every underscored key the record lacks — `_brief`, `_renewalAdvice`, `_readings`, `_signNeeds`, `_signState`): it marks the record loaded and the room never asks again, so without them a contract chosen in the list opened with no brief (measured). The same hole closed for saveContract's light-row save.
- **THE OUTBOX IS NOT A FAILURE ON THE SIGNING ROUTE**: `signerNoticeState` answers `outbox`, the row says IN OUTBOX (never EMAIL FAILED) and keeps *Try the email again*.
Tests: f393 (55 claims, 54 red at the parent; the one pass is a named wall); f117, f148, f178, f184, f238, f245, f251, f263, f265, f323, f342, f390 re-pointed in place; in the browser sign-links-verify 4, signing-flow-verify 6 and upload-blanks-verify 9j re-pointed in place.

The first Work door, directly above Home (Home stays the page HaTi opens on); no count. `js/views/brain.js` draws it; `js/brainmap.js` is the ONE catalogue and reader on BOTH hosts (graphwhere.js's pattern).
- **ONE BRAIN, THREE VIEWS**: every neuron carries A (brain) · W (wiring) · L (floors) and the drawing is a blend, so a switch is a glide; six flows (`BRAIN_FLOWS`), `BRAIN_STEP_S` 3.2 a step. **A NAME IS DRAWN FROM WHERE A FLOW LANDED** (`reached`, with its step number), never from a glow — background sparks name nothing.
- **READ, NOT DRAWN**: `brainRead(files)` finds every `BRAIN_PARTS` definition (file, line), the links the CODE makes (comments stripped first — a name in a note is not a hand-off), every published window name and route, and any flow step whose part is gone (`flowGaps`, said on the step, never skipped). `GET /api/brain` (auth; api path `'brain'` — api() adds the prefix) reads js/ + server/ on the first request after a start — every deploy — and keeps the difference (`brainDiff`, fingerprint `brainKey`) in `store` as `brain.builds` (BRAIN_KEEP 12) + `brain.lastMap`. A first reading is a baseline; a new published name is a new part (code name, "description pending", gold ring for BRAIN_NEW_DAYS, at most BRAIN_PENDING_MAX drawn, the rest counted).
- **THE WORDS ARE KEYS**, never in brainmap.js: `brn_p_<id>` / `brn_pd_<id>` / `brn_step_<flow>_<n>` in both books. A new catalogue part owes both.
- The page writes nothing, touches no contract, spends nothing; its frame loop stops when the page is left. Pinch, wheel and ± zoom; not on the phone. The concept's two explanation cards were NOT carried in (a page does not explain itself); the updates heading's hover says it.
Tests: f400, brain-page-verify.

## THE OWNER'S OPEN ITEMS, FIXED (27 Sep 2026)

*"give me a list of the things that need to be reviewed or fixed that are currently listed in the bug log"*, then *"After the latest fixes, run the bug log and update according to the latest code"*, then *"Fix the most serious and worth my attention then merge to main"* — the twelve on the two lists the owner was shown (the private page "HaTi Open Items", v2, re-read against main 3ee647b). Built on claude/beautiful-davinci-4d3cs9, brought level with main 01bf6cc (the rulebook trim) before it was recorded. Every new check was run against the parent before it was believed.

- **THE APPROVAL RULES WERE ONLY A SCREEN (r1).** *"Approval rules — for example 'above a set value the finance director must approve', a foreign governing law, or a playbook departure — are only enforced on screen. The server never checks them, so a request sent straight to the server could send a signing link or sign without them."* Only the named-person approval had a wall; the rule chain had one at the hand-over alone. Now: `srvApprovalChainOpenOf(c, prev)` asks the rules of BOTH the stored and the new record (a save lowering the value in the same breath as it signs is still held by the rule the stored value engaged) and reads the decisions off the new record, checking each approved step's stamp; `srvApprovalChainRefusal` is the owner-side sentence. Asked at the save that starts signing (403 `approvalRule`), at POST /api/shares purpose sign (409 — never once signing has begun, `saStarted`), at their respond (the SAME neutral "not ready" as the named approval — they never learn an approval exists) and at the internal signer's turn notice (`awaiting-approval`). `srvApprovalDecisionRefusal(prev, c, u)`: a step MOVING to approved or refused must be decided by the approver the RULE names (read from the workspace's rules, never the step the client sent — `srvUserCanApprove`, userCanApprove's twin), in the caller's own name, in the chain's order; a move back to pending is a resubmission and passes. The browser's own press (`approveContract` writes `by: u.name` and decides in order) passes untouched. f409: 8 claims, 5 red at the parent; (5)(7)(8) are controls. **THE LEGACY DEFAULT RULE BIT SIX TEST STAGES**: every fixture is ≥ 5,000,000, and a workspace with no saved rules has the old default (an admin's approval at 5M). `seedWorkspace(h, { approvalRules })` states them; node tests that sign a fixture and are not about approvals say `[]` (f118, f123, f205, f375, f388, regression), and so do sign-links-verify (at the seed) and signing-flow-verify (the admin's own settings save, after the browser-only staging it already had). A stage that clears a rule only in the browser measures a signature the server now refuses.
- **A PAPER BUILT FROM THE RECORD FROZE NOTHING (r3).** *"On contracts drafted from HaTi's built-in templates, the key terms can still be changed after the first person signs, so the next signer could see different paper."* Such a contract stores no wording: `docBody` draws the template off the record every time, so the printed terms ARE its wording. `recordDrawnPaper(c)` (no redlineText, not an upload, no execution.html) and `PAPER_TERMS_FROZEN` (template · fields · counterparty · value · party · effDate · expiry, read by `paperTerm` the way docTermSpan reads the days — the record's own field, else what the reading found) join the first-signature freeze's list. The Overview draws those as read-outs with the reason on the hover (`paperTermsFrozen`, `PAPER_TERM_KEYS`, `paperTermFrozenRead`, `ov_paper_frozen`). Once the wording is stored the 21 Aug ruling stands untouched: Key terms stay open between signatures. f408: 5 claims, 3 red; paper-terms-frozen-verify 7 checks, 3 red.
- **DISCARD DELETED WHAT THE OTHER SIDE HOLDS (r4).** *"If you revise a change you have already sent, HaTi treats it as unsent. Pressing Discard then deletes it completely and writes 'never sent' in the audit trail — even though the other side has a copy."* The revision is unsent and the version before it went out. `negoSentVersionOf(c, ch)` is the one reading of which version the other side holds; `negoRetractDraft` restores it exactly — wording, fingerprint, createdAt, heading and formatting flag (a revision now records `headingText`, `formattingOnly`, `revisedBy` and `revisedAt` as well, so the version it is restored from is whole) — slices the revisions filed since, resets `chainHead` where the head went, and writes "discarded the revision that had not been sent … stands again". A never-sent draft is discarded whole, as before. The toast says the same (`ng_retract_revision`). f407: 5 claims, 4 red; discard-keeps-sent-verify 6 checks, 4 red. **Noticed**: a Discard followed by a later filing can leave the fingerprint chain unverifiable (logged).
- **A COMPANY STANDARD DROPPED WHO WE ARE (r6).** The create call sent six of the form's answers and not `party`/`side`, and POST /api/templates/:id/contracts never read them. Both halves: `c.party` + `metadata.party`, and `metadata.category` customer | supplier ("Neither" writes nothing). The standard's own `{{org.…}}` blanks are left as they resolve (the pane beside the questions draws them from the same resolution — f104). f404: 5 claims, 3 red; newcontract-verify gained the two claims.
- **A CONFIRMED REVIEW REPLACED THE RECORD (r7).** Both confirm paths assigned the dialog's answer over every term. `metaMergeReviewed(prev, m)`: keys the review did not carry are kept; a blank answer (empty, `unclear`, `unknown` — `META_NO_ANSWER`) never erases a stored one; sourceSpans merge. The dialog stops choosing for the reader: a list term nothing was read for drew its FIRST option and Confirm filed it — it opens on "—". f405: 6 claims, all red; review-keeps-typed-terms-verify.
- **A VIEW LINK REFRESHED A NEGOTIATION LINK (r8).** The row's purpose decides what its reader may do, and three places put a copy of another kind on a row: the send dialog reused any standing link held by the typed address; the round send's link choice took any standing link; and the round's catch-up pushed the round onto EVERY standing link, a signing or adviser link included. PUT /api/shares/:token/payload refuses a copy whose CHOSEN kind (`purposeChosen`) differs from the row's (409); the browser reuses and catches up negotiation links only (`shareKindOf`, `standingNegotiation`). f406: 5 claims, 4 red; share-recipient-verify 4c.

## NO LINK TO SIGN — CAN THEY STILL ANSWER, THE SIXTH AGENT, AND THE LIST THAT STAYS STILL (Young ruled 27 Sep 2026)

Asked of Copilot's work: *"Does their round came back high all the rounds currently waiting for you?"* — it does not, and the question uncovered a deeper fault. Then: *"why shouldnt we build it as an agent and in the copilots work so that we are notified these contracts do not have a live link and have a resend or reboot button?"*, *"Fix it and build a sixth agent. Afterwards, make sure the highlighted card stays stagnant and does not move when you click around the different agents"*, the name (*"something to do with no live link for the counterparty and therefore they cannot sign"* → "No link to sign", picked by name, with "Both stages"), and *"okay"*.

- **THE FAULT, MEASURED ON THE REAL APP AT e351a91.** `negWhoseMove` asks `negoTheirCopy` before it says "With the other side", and that reading counted only STANDING (durable) links on a share cache that only the negotiation page ever filled, once per sitting, for the one contract on screen. So: a deal whose only link had run out read "Theirs" on the Negotiations list on first look and after every reload (1a/1d red at the parent); an UNUSED one-time link read "Mine · No live copy" the moment the deal had been opened (1c red); the contract head's "Whose move" said Theirs over a dead link (1e). The deal simply stopped, filed under the other side.
- **THE ANSWER IS THE SERVER'S, AND IT IS THE RESPOND ROUTE'S OWN QUESTION.** `srvReach(c, {rows})` (server/server.js, after `shareSuperseded`) asks of each link, in the respond route's own order, off its own predicates (`shareFate`): revoked · expired · a one-time link already answered · overtaken (`shareSuperseded`) or a standing link retired by a later signing link (`shareRetiredBySigning`). A Word row is the one row whose LINK never travelled: it counts where the file really left (`sent_at`) and has not been overtaken, and a file does not expire. Read-only, history and adviser links never carry an answer back (`last.how 'readonly'`). Returns `reply` (live/none), `last` (the newest negotiation copy and what became of it, where reply is none), `sign` (the counterparty signer whose TURN it is — `signerTurn` — and whose link ran out or was cancelled; null where no signing link was ever sent, where they sign outside HaTi, or on a sealed record), and `fresh` ("Link sent": a working link that went out in the last fortnight to a deal whose previous copy had stopped working for a reason of its own — ran out, cancelled, used, never delivered; a copy merely OVERTAKEN was replaced by the new link itself, so the deal was never stuck, 1k).
- **IT RIDES EVERYWHERE THE CONTRACT DOES, AS TRANSPORT.** The list route (`srvReachForRows`: the wanted rows — `srvReachWanted`, a live deal with something pending or a signer still to come — in ONE query), the one-contract read, the share list (`reach`, plus `answersBack` on each standing link), and every send's answer (POST /api/shares both returns, PUT payload, revoke, applied — the applied answer only inside the caller's scope). `delete c._reach` on the server's save and `delete payload._reach` on the browser's; `fillHeavyFrom` lets a fresher one-contract answer win over the list's. `reachTake(c, r)` (js/core.js) is the ONE writer on the browser, called by `contractShares`, `renderSharesSection`, the round send (both sends), the signing links, the dialog's send, the extras, the cancel, the applied poller and the phone's send. `negoTheirCopy` reads `c._reach.reply`; absent is still "unknown" (local mode, a deal with nothing pending) and changes nothing. No second copy of the rule on the browser: it cannot compare wordings, and the server can.
- **A ROUND NEVER GOES ONTO A LINK THAT CANNOT BE ANSWERED.** A standing negotiation link a signing link had retired still passed `shareIsStanding` — so the round send and the share dialog refreshed it in place and reported "sent" onto a copy nobody could reply through. `answerableNegotiation(shares)` is `standingNegotiation` less `answersBack === false`; `standingShareFor` and the dialog's reuse ask it. The quiet catch-up (`standingNegotiation`) is deliberately unchanged: what they can READ stays current.
- **THE INDEX.** Loading a 1,200-contract book went from 0.2s (parent) to 6s with the reading: `shareSuperseded` and `shareRetiredBySigning` find a contract's links by `contract_id` and there was NO index, so each question walked the whole table, payloads and all. `idx_shares_contract ON shares(contract_id, created_at)` → 0.3s.
- **THE SIXTH AGENT, "No link to sign", SECOND IN THE LIST.** `agLinkItems`: a REPLY is stuck where `negWhoseMove(c).why === 'nocopy'` (the list's own reading, so the agent and the "Waiting on you · No live copy" rows are one set), since = the later of the link's death and the round's turnAt; a SIGNATURE is stuck where `_reach.sign.how` is expired/revoked, never outside-route, never sealed; a deal on HOLD is left out (the dispute stops it, not the link). `agLinkDone` reads `_reach.fresh`. Steps: Find stuck deals · Check their link · Your review · Link sent. Card: what is stuck, what became of their link (`agLinkHow`, "today"/"on 24 Sept" through `agOnDay` — "cancelled on Today" was the first draft), stuck N days, last sent to. Panel: situation, what happened, last sent to (name and address), stuck for, and one note. **The fresh link ASKS FIRST, naming who** (the owner's word, so the page's one `confirmDialog` — f399 1f re-pointed): an answer goes by `resendRoundFresh` (js/core.js: the round send, then `roundHandedOver` = `negoHandOver` + `persist` — the two steps the negotiation page's Send and the room's take, published so the agents page stores nothing, f399 1b stands), to `counterpartyContact` over the links LESS Word rows (a Word row sends nothing through the round send — it has no file — so it neither chooses who nor how); the share list is read first and a deal somebody fixed meanwhile sends nothing. A signature goes by `issueSigningAct` ON the Signing tab (`agGo('sign')` first — the act repaints the room, and from the agents page it would have painted over it). The second button is the send screen with the negotiation's own hand-over (`roundHandedOver` in `onSent`), or the Signing tab. A reader who may not send is shown where the work lives and nothing that sends.
- **THE LIST STAYS STILL.** Every press rebuilt the whole page — list and all — and put the scroll back. `agRowInner` / `agPaintList` rewrite what a row SAYS and never replace a row; `agShowAgent` repaints `#ag-main` alone and lands at its top; `agRepaint` after an act does the same under the right side's own scroll. Above 900px the page OWNS ITS HEIGHT (`'agents'` on VIEW_OWNS_HEIGHT; `.ag-root` `--view-h`, `.ag-main` its own scroller, `.ag-main > *{flex:none}` — the Key terms lesson), and the list is no longer sticky on the page's scroller. MEASURED on this stage the parent's list landed on the same pixels after each redraw (3a/3c are CONTROLS); what moved was the redraw itself — 3b/3d prove the rows are the same elements now.
- **Said out loud, not built**: the answer is per CONTRACT, not per party (a multi-party deal with one party stuck reads live if any party can answer); a link row whose EMAIL failed still counts as live (the sender may have copied it — changing that would move many deals); an answered-but-not-signed signing link is not listed (the owner's words were "ran out or cancelled"); the two wording faults on "Their round came back" (logged 27 Sep) are untouched.
Tests: f412 (35 claims, 33 red at the parent; 1f the CONTROL, 4d the WALL), no-link-to-sign-verify (23 checks, 16 red at the parent; 1b, 3a, 3c CONTROLS). Re-pointed in place: f190 (2)–(4) (the staging is the server's answer on the record; "only revoked and ONE-SHOT links is none" REVERSED — an unused one-time link can be answered on), f399 1f (the one question is the fresh link's), 3b and 5a (six agents), F17 and f406 (5) (the reuse asks `answerableNegotiation`), agents-page-verify (the stage, 1d and 7b: six agents, "No link to sign" second, the arrow walks onto it), inspector-verify's stage (it stubbed a standing link on the share cache).

## THE AGENTS DO THE WORK (Young ruled 27 Sep 2026)

Asked of Copilot's work: *"How often are the agents in copilot's work page running to provide the latest information?"* — they were not running at all: the page read what HaTi already held whenever it was drawn, and only Renewals (and New paper's overnight standards review) did anything by themselves, on the 12-hour sweep. Then *"If the other 3 agents aren't doing anything are they even agents?"*, *"Recommend how I make the others be agents"*, a review of the sixth agent against that standard, and the ruling: *"1, your recommendation. 2, yes. 3, yes. Now implement all the fixes and merge to main"* — (1) their changes are answered on the negotiation page, never in the agent's panel (THE ONE DOOR); (2) a bounced email counts as a stuck link; (3) Late promises may send the first polite chase by itself.

- **THE ENGINE ROOM (server).** `runAgent(k, trigger, who, fn, {subject})` is the one way an agent runs: a row in `agent_runs` (why — schedule · now · event · start · sendback — who pressed, the runner's own report of what it looked at, did and skipped and WHY, and its cost). The cost is MEASURED: `recordAiSpend` adds each call's price to the run whose `AsyncLocalStorage` context (`agentRunCtx`) it runs in, so two agents running at once each count their own. `agentCfg(k)` over `AGENT_DEFAULTS` (on, hour `at`, `max`, money `limit`, `soonDays`, `secondAfter`); Renewals' on/max ARE Copilot engine's `aiRenewalPrep`/`aiRenewalPrepMax` (one setting); New paper got its OWN switch (it rode the renewal switch, so turning renewal notes off stopped it, unsaid — f296 re-pointed). `agentMaySpend(k)` asks the workspace ceiling, then the agent's own limit. `agentScheduleTick` (every 5 min) runs link · late · renew · paper once a day at the workspace hour (AI_DAY_TZ); runRenewalPrep and runPlaybookPrep LEFT the 12-hour `reminderSweep` (f275 re-pointed). A run that throws is logged and drops the admin note 'agent run failure' under its own catch (M-6). `HATI_AGENTS_AUTO=off` in test/helpers.js startHati: in a test nothing runs by the clock or on an event unless the test turns it on.
- **ROUTES.** `GET /api/agents/status` (every member; money and settings to an admin only, as /api/ai/spend), with a `stamp` that moves whenever something the page shows may have moved; `POST /api/agents/:k/run` (admin, the SAME runner); `PUT /api/agents/:k/settings` (admin, validated); `GET /api/contracts/changed?since=&reach=1` (rows decorated exactly as the list — `srvListDecorate` was lifted out of GET /api/contracts — and, every five minutes, whether the other side can still answer on every live deal, because a link runs out with nothing written anywhere).
- **THE PAGE UPDATES ITSELF.** js/agentruns.js is the page's ONE door to the server (f399 1b and f413 7d grep js/views/agents.js for any other): `agentsBeat` asks the status every 30s while Copilot's work is on screen (`agentsWatch`), fetches changed rows only when the stamp moved (`contractsTakeRow`: an edit on its way is never overwritten; a whole record held here is read whole again, never shrunk to a list row). Each agent says when it runs next (`agNextWords`), when it last ran and what it did (`agRunResultWords`, every word a key: `ag_rr_*`, `ag_skip_*`, `ag_stop_*`), spent today (admin), and "Earlier runs" (`agRunsHtml`, cost column for an admin). Run now (`agRunNowPress`) asks first for the four that spend, naming who pays. Settings live on the Settings page (`SET_PANELS.agents`, `stAgentsPaint`) — rules in settings, never on the page.
- **NO LINK TO SIGN.** `srvReach` now: a link whose email the provider REFUSED and that was never re-sent is 'bounced' (`shareBounced`: `send_error` set, `sent_at` empty, and NOT the no-provider outbox text — the outbox is delivery); on a deal with several negotiating parties, a party whose every copy stopped working is named (`parties`) while `reply` stays one answer per contract (the list's bands unchanged); a signer is stuck on expired · revoked · answered (a one-time signing link used up without a signature) · bounced (`SIGN_STUCK_HOWS`); `soon` names their only link (or the signer's) that runs out inside `soonDays`. `POST /api/shares/:token/extend` keeps an OPEN link working (same link, the standard length from today, never shorter, a trail line; a cancelled, spent or ended link is refused — send a fresh one). `runLinkWatch` mails each contract's OWNER once per stuck link (reminders keyed on the contract, kind, party and when it stopped); the daily brief carries "The other side has no working link" every morning (`linkStuckBook`, `linkStuckLine`). The bell has a `link` kind (after `handover`), off `agLinkItems`, to the owner (an admin where none). The page: kinds `party`, `soon`, `soon-sign`; "Keep their link working" (`shareKeepOpen`); "Send them a fresh link" opens the send screen with that party chosen.
- **LATE PROMISES.** `runLateChases` (daily): theirs, not done, past due, under 90 days late, not held by an earlier step → the first chase is ready, or the FIRMER one where the last chase is `secondAfter` days old; the promise's owner (assignee, else the contract's owner) is told once per stage. It sends NOTHING to the other side (f413 7c): the owner's "yes" to an automatic first chase was REFUSED by the environment's safety check (Real-World Transactions) and was not built; the switch was removed with it. The firmer chase is a person's press: `obligationChase(cid, obId, {firm:true})` stamps `chaseFirmAt/By` and posts `firm`; `srvChaseSend` (lifted out of the chase route) writes `mail_ob_chase_firm_*` with the first chase's date. The PUT keeps a later stored chase stamp field by field (a save from an older copy cannot undo a chase). The agent's card `chase-firm` (`agLateFirmItems`).
- **THEIR ROUND CAME BACK.** `runRoundPrep(cid)` — on their answer's arrival (the respond route) and on a save that filed new asks of theirs (the PUT), both through `roundPrepKick` (asks `roundPrepNeeded` first so an empty run is never logged) — one Copilot call per contract over every ask with no answer (`roundAsksOf`: the pending changes AND the proposals in answers not yet filed, one-time and standing), against the workspace's standards for its kind: accept · counter (the whole clause wording, the smallest change from THEIR words — AI_REDLINE_RULE) · escalate, with why and the standard it rests on. A counter with no wording is filed as an escalation. Stored in `round_prep` keyed by js/roundprep.js `roundPrepKey(clauseId, newText)` (FNV-1a, whitespace folded) — the server can answer before any browser has filed the change. `_roundPrep` rides GET and the list for asks STILL on the table, stripped on save (both hosts) and from both share-payload routes. Paid by the contract's owner; a cut-short answer is not kept; each ask tried at most once a day. On the page: the card counts Copilot's answers and the tally uses them (one answer per ask, `AG_PREP_PLAN`); the panel shows the answer, its wording and "Send back with a note". On the NEGOTIATION ROW: `rlRoundPrepLineHtml` draws one quiet line on our seat only (`.rl-card-prep`, its own grid row 3, verbs to row 4). Counter opens the clause editor with the prepared wording as the first rail card — Apply is still the only thing that moves words, Save still `negoEditClause`.
- **ARCHIVE IMPORT READS ON THE SERVER.** The browser still reads the bytes, the duplicates, the text and a scan's OCR, and files each contract at once with what the pattern matcher can tell (`migExtractLocal`) marked `migration.reading:'queued'`, then hands the text it chose (buildExtractionPayload) to `POST /api/import/read`. `runImportQueue` reads each with `aiExtractCall` (lifted out of /api/ai/extract — one prompt), the seed wins, a scan is capped (`srvCapForOcr`, line for line js/ocr.js — f413 7b), `migReadNeedsReview` and `folderFromType` from the new shared js/migread.js decide (MIG_CRITICAL moved there from js/views/migration.js), checks the standards, writes a NEW VERSION in one synchronous step, and mails whoever started the batch when its last file is read. A person's check (needsReview false) wins. Thorough mode still reads in the tab. The 25-file cap is unchanged (the browser still holds each file while it works).
- **SEND BACK WITH A NOTE.** `POST /api/agents/:k/sendback` for round (one ask), renew (the memo) and paper (the standards check, a new version and a trail line): `sendBackPrompt(note, before)` rides the SAME prompt the work was first done with; paid by whoever sent it back; logged as a 'sendback' run. The page: one small box (`agSendBackHtml`) — the note is the question, no dialog.
- **Said out loud, not built**: the automatic first chase (refused by the safety check — the owner decides); a per-party answer on the Negotiations list's band; the phone (js/mobile*.js draws no agents page); a cost per ITEM (runs carry cost; items do not).

## INSIGHTS / WHAT COUNTS AS A CLAUSE — ROMAN AND LETTERED NUMBERS, A BOX THAT WRAPS, FORMATTED ANSWERS (Young, 28 Sep 2026)

> *"the clause numbers when in roman numeral numbers they do not appear in the dna strand so review the logic because contracts may have alphabetic or roman numeral numbers. Finally, when you click on a dna and it asks a question, the question field in copilot does not allow for wrap text. fix this too"* — and the logged Explorer markdown fault: *"… and merge all to main"*

NUMBERS. The heading reading (`DOC_READ_HEAD_NUM`, the one every surface shares — Explorer's strip, Risk View's labels, Plain View's citations) read digits only; Roman numerals and letters were deliberately out and logged. It now reads them in the same two safe positions a digit is read: after a self-naming word (clause · article · section · schedule · annex · appendix · part, and now exhibit) or followed by "." or ")"; a dotted Roman or letter heading ("V.2 Notices") needs no separator. Roman numerals I–LXXXIX (`DOC_READ_ROMAN`). Refused, as proved: "A Note on Terms", "I Agree to the terms", "V.A.T. Registration", "U.S. Operations", "Part of the Agreement". f277 13d listed "Appendix A Fees" as a refusal; re-pointed, dated. `cite` is not hashed and not sent to the reading route, so no reading is re-bought. `_docReadSepOf` now finds the number as a whole token first (`_docReadTokAt`), because "PART A:" found the A inside PART.

AND THE PARAGRAPH RULE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED. Tried first: "X.1"/"A.2" paragraphs as their own rows, like "5.1". f384's own fixture (a real warehousing agreement: ARTICLE VI with VI.1 … VI.4) showed the cost — every contract numbered that way would be re-cut, so Plain View's paid reading would be re-asked and Who does what regrouped per sub-clause. That is wider than the ask; reverted, and said to the owner. A Roman sub-clause rides inside its article's block, which now wears the article's numeral.

THE BOX. `#igd-input` was the product's one single-line `<input>` composer, so a question the strip wrote ran off its edge. It is now a `textarea.chat-field` (`chatFieldWire`, `chatFieldGrow`, `chatFieldSubmits`: Enter asks, Shift+Enter breaks the line), grown when the strip fills it, Ask pinned at its foot (inline `right/bottom`, because the generated sheet holds no new arbitrary classes).

THE ANSWERS. Explorer has two answer paths. The chat path already went through `aiRichText`; the GRAPH path (`intelGraphApply`, a portfolio question the map can answer) escaped Copilot's own sentence as plain text, so "**" and "- " showed raw. It now goes through `aiRichText`. And the side panel's answer styles (`#ai-feed .ai-p/.ai-list/.ai-h/...`) were never written for the dock, so even the chat path drew lists with no bullets: `#igd-feed` now carries the same set (headings --t-card, as in the side panel).

Tests: f424 (6)(7); analyze-on-the-graph-verify 0a–0e (0a/0b red at the parent 86260ee on the graph path; 0c–0e red there too); f277 13d re-pointed.


## INSIGHTS — EXPLORER DRAWS A BRAIN (Young, 28 Sep 2026)

> *"review the explorer nodes design and make create options of how to make it similar to the brain option in the brain page without impacting the PAPER page"* — then, over seven rounds of an artifact: *"i hate all the options"* (kept: the brain shape, many small glowing dots, flows that light up, Wiring and Floors views, details "always, but small"); *"it should also be able to bundle … especially when in the brain and wiring mode"*; *"i need to use my mouse to turn them around. Currently only the brain moves"*; *"remove all these filters. the idea is the filters should come from asking a question in copilot"*; and *"Built it but start from the latest main."*

WHAT CHANGED IS THE DRAWING, NOT THE READINGS. `buildGraphModel`, the lenses, `intelGraphApply`, the groupings and the Paper view are untouched. `makeIntelGraph` still makes one SVG `g.ig-node` per group and per contract, with every mark the tests read (`data-ig-fact`, `data-ig-flow`, `data-ig-cp-line`, `.ig-cp-share`, `data-ig-decision`, `.passed`, `.unread`, `hit`/`mut`/`hi`/`dim`), so hover, press, the cliff scrubber and the dock's two-way lighting work as before. What is new: a canvas (`#ig-cv`) UNDER the SVG paints what carries no words — the brain's 2,400 tissue dots (seeded, `igbTissue`), the glow round each group, the dots themselves — and every frame projects each node from three positions (brain `A`, wiring `W3` from the force layout the map always had, floors `L`) mixed by the camera's weights (`igbProjector`, the Brain page's own maths). The words (two small lines per contract, a card per group) are placed each frame where they do not cover another (`igbPlace`: four spots, then the number alone, then nothing — the dot still speaks on hover). A card on the far side of the brain turns away.

DECISIONS. (1) Hybrid, not a pure canvas: a canvas redraw would have taken every node's element away, and with it hover, press, focus and a dozen browser checks that measure painted SVG. (2) The Wiring view IS the old force layout (`igTick` kept, `timeline` hubs kept), fitted to the stage with an eased fit so the drift never shakes the page. (3) More groups than the design's nine lobes take further directions off a golden spiral (`igbSlot`) — none is merged into "everything else", because a card that hides groups would be a silent trim. (4) Small groups (≤3) start folded only where there are more than four groups and only for the reader's own grouping; Copilot's grouping starts open. Folds and the camera are per sitting, in memory. (5) A card press FOLDS (was: filter to that group, `igFilterToGroup`, deleted); the legend's status rows are a key (were: filter buttons) and follow the colour Copilot was asked for. (6) Four map commands are plain arithmetic and are read in the browser before Copilot is asked (`intelMapLocal`): colour by any grouping, size by value / open obligations / nothing, outliers (value ≥3× the stream's median, or paying ≥30 days slower than the stream's median, only where the stream has 3 to measure against; money obeys `canViewValues`; never a score), walk through (the highlighted set, else what is showing; soonest decision first; capped at 24 and said), and show everything. A sentence carrying one of these and more has the rest asked of Copilot. (7) A map answer carries "Open these N on the Contracts page" (`regShowOnly`) and Export (a CSV built from the record). "Save this view" from the artifact was NOT built.

THE HINT BOX CAME OFF THE STAGE. The bottom-right "Drag nodes · scroll to zoom · click a card to explain" box is replaced by the view bar (Brain · Wiring · Floors, zoom, Fold all); its words, reworded ("Drag to turn · scroll to zoom · double-click to reset"), are the bar's hover (the pop-up diet: machinery on the hover). "Clear all" on the head line reads "Show everything"; the head line also says "Showing N of T", what the map is coloured and sized by, and "Walking k of n · Stop".

A BUG FOUND BY THE CHECK, NOT BY LOOKING. explorer-brain-verify 3c (a real drag on the Floors view) turned 0.07 rad instead of 0.72, every time, in that order of presses. Logged pointer events: a `pointercancel` after 13px — the browser had started its own drag of selected SVG text. A reader who double-clicks a label and then drags would have had the same half-turn. Fixed by scope: `.ig-brain #ig-svg{user-select:none}` and a `dragstart` preventDefault. Three runs green after.

SEEDING. A book pushed into `state.contracts` in the page is replaced by the next list refresh; the check seeds its 44 contracts on the server. And "signed in" is waited for as the seeded book being present — before that a demo book sits behind the sign-in screen (the first draft of 1d measured `#auth-root` over the map).

## THE SPELL CHECK — A MISSPELT DEFINED TERM; EDIT WITH COPILOT — SAVE LIVE WHILE TYPING (28 Sep 2026)

Young: *"fix the greyed Save button while typing too And also fix the spelling error issue as it is not working"*.

Now `ceBoxNow()` reads the box as `cePullText` would, writing nothing; `ceCanFile(d)` takes that draft (no argument = the old answer, clauseEditorDirty's question written out) and Discard asks its own question of the same draft; the typing listener calls `ceRenderFoot()` (patched in place, the button identity the 30 Aug fix rests on kept). f245 and f264 re-pointed from the literal `ceCanFile()` line.

Two real gaps found: (1) a capitalised word inside a sentence was always a "name", so "the Suplier shall" — a slip of the contract's own defined term — was never checked; contracts are written in capitalised terms. `spellTermsFrom` collects the words the contract capitalises inside a sentence (possessives folded), `spellTermSlip` checks a capitalised word one slip (two for 7+ letters) from one of them; a new name is a slip of nothing and still passes (measured: Wanjiru, Kamau, Nairobi, Mandy, Lars pass).
