## THE SPELL CHECK — THE RED UNDERLINE WHILE TYPING (28 Sep 2026)

Young: *"yes add the red underlines while typing too"* (after being told the check ran at Save only).

ONE READING, TWO SURFACES. The underline marks exactly what the Save would list: `spellSuspects` over the Save's own `before` (`ceSpellBefore`, lifted out of `ceSaveChecked` so the two share it; the narrow panel passes its `spellBefore`) and its own `after` (`ceSpellAfter` reads the box as typed through `ceBoxNow`; the panel passes `spellNow`). A word underlined is a word the Save stops on; a word the Save lets through is never underlined.

NOTHING IN THE BOX. The marks are a CSS Custom Highlight (`CSS.highlights`, name `hati-spell`, `::highlight(hati-spell)` wavy `--st-ruby-dot` in `spellEnsureStyle`): ranges over the box's text nodes, never an element — the draft the Save reads, the caret, and `ceMarksPaint` are untouched. Because the marks' repaint replaces the box's text a beat after typing, the underline is drawn again at the end of every `ceMarksMount`; cleared when the paper leaves typing and on close. Words inside a struck run (`del`, `[data-ce-mark="del"]`) are never marked; a word split across inline tags gets no mark rather than a wrong one. The browser's own underline is turned off on a box HaTi underlines (another dictionary, in the reader's browser language, would disagree on the same word); where the browser has no highlights, HaTi draws nothing and the browser keeps its own. The word list is now fetched on the first keystroke rather than the first Save. `Highlight` is read through `globalThis` (f232 reads `window.foo` as a module publication).

Tests: f428 (red at the parent 1cc4df5 on every claim); their-edit-page-verify 3a3, 6f, 6g, 7 (the narrow window's panel) — 3a3, 6f and 7 red at the parent. Driven in the real app too: "Suppleir", "recieve", "paymnet" underlined, the box's own spellcheck off.

## INSIGHTS — EXPLORER: THE VIEW RECIPE (Young, 28 Sep 2026)

> *"copilot has limitations. Think of all variations of how people can ask questions to segment different requests for review and advise on how we can build hati to show the contracts in different ways."* — over a screenshot where "divide the floors by payment terms" was answered "I can see MK-411, but I'm not sure what you mean… The contract doesn't discuss building floors". Then, of the seven-step plan: *"Let's go with this instead and merge to main after."*

WHY IT FAILED. Two faults. (1) The routing guessed from words: "payment terms" was on `IG_QA_RE` (a reading of one contract) and neither "divide" nor "floors" was on `IG_GRAPH_RE`, so the sentence went to the reading chat, which answered about the contract in hand. (2) Even routed right, the map's tool knew only group, filter and highlight.

THE RECIPE. Everything the map shows is one short list on `intel`: the lenses (which contracts), `groupBy`/`groups`, `floorsBy` (the stage at rest), `columnsBy` (the grouping at rest), `colourBy`, `sizeBy`, `labelBy`, `timeBy` (the renewal decision at rest), `sortBy`, and the view. `igRecipeNow` snapshots it, `igRecipeSet` puts it back, `igRecipePush` keeps one undo point per sentence (`IG_UNDO_MAX` 30), `igRecipeUndo` goes back, `igRecipeSays` is the head line's read-back. A saved view is a saved recipe in `hati.v1.igViews` (this browser, like the template builder's drafts; ids kept so a view shows the same contracts next week).

ONE LIST OF FACTS. `GRAPH_GROUPINGS` grew five facts, each ONE existing reading: liability (`metadata.liabilityCapped`), law (`contractGoverningLaw`), owner (`contractOwnerName`), obligations (open count bands), read (`graphNodeFacts().unread`); the server mirror and its description grew with it (f299 pins the set). `igRoleSet(role, fact)` accepts any fact on the list for any role — that is why "floors by payment terms" works with no special case. `igFactOrder` puts a fact's buckets in their natural order (stages in order, time in time order, bands low to high, largest first otherwise, the none bucket last).

THE FREE READER. `igRecipeParse` reads a sentence into changes, in English and Swedish: role words (`IG_ROLE_RE`) + "by/per/efter" + a fact (`IG_FACT_WORDS`, longest first); two facts "against" each other make a grid; "only/hide/which" read conditions off the record (`igConditions`: stages, money over/under in the home currency via `fxHome`, renewal and expiry windows, signed in a year, overdue, whose move, not read, off standard, capped/uncapped, payment days, laws, streams, types and counterparties by the names the book holds); top N (optionally per group); sort; compare two sets (a custom grouping of the two); connections (dependents, a party's linked contracts, families); undo, show everything, save, open. Follow-ups ("of those", "and", "now only", "av dem") AND onto what is showing; a fresh "only" starts again; "same but…"/"instead" change the role changed last (`intel.lastRole`). A sentence opening with summarise/explain/describe/quote… is not the map's. A grouping by something no fact names ("by region") goes to Copilot (it can place contracts by reading them); a colour, size or floors by an unknown thing is answered with the nearest things the role can do (`IG_NEAREST`).

COPILOT DECIDES. `intelAsk` now: the reader first; two named contracts → side by side; the compliance sweep and the template adviser keep their own doors; EVERYTHING ELSE → `intelGraphAsk`, whose tool (`render_graph`) now carries `kind` (map | wording), every role, `view`, `top` and `ask`. `kind:'wording'` hands the question to `intelChatAsk` and leaves the map alone. Cost said plainly: a wording question on Explorer now makes one small map call before the chat. `intelGraphApply` judges each role like the grouping (a fact on the list, or nothing) and composes its sentence from what was set.

ASK BACK. An answer may carry `choices`: up to three presses (`data-ig-choice`), each a list of recipe changes; a bare fact ("payment terms") asks "What should payment terms do on the map?" with Group / Floors / Colour; an unknown fact offers the role's nearest; a refused grouping offers three the map can cut; with no Copilot at all, the fallback offers three.

GRID AND TIMELINE. `IGB_VIEWS` has five; every weight list carries five (`IGB_NV`); `igbMix`/`igbHeart` mix five positions; cards and folds belong to Brain and Wiring only (`igbCardW`). `igbAxes` builds the floors (any fact, ≤`IGB_FLOORS_MAX` 10), the columns (the grouping's cards, or `columnsBy` buckets ≤14), the grid (one cell per column × floor, each knowing how many and how much) and the timeline (dates along `timeBy`, one lane per group, today marked, the undated counted in their own strip, "no contract has a … on file" when none). The canvas's own words are reserved room (`G.reserve`) the contract words keep clear of.

THE PHRASE BOOK. f427 holds ~225 lines (≥40 Swedish), each with the recipe it must produce; line 1 is Young's sentence. First run: 16 misread — commas swallowed by the normaliser merged "group by stream, colour by risk" into one clause; "timeline by expiry" also grouped; "signed in 2025" also read the stage Signed; JavaScript's `\b` does not see a boundary before "över" (non-ASCII), so "över 20 miljoner" read nothing; "Summarize my highest-value contract" read as top 10. All fixed in the reader; three lines were re-judged ("make them all the same size" IS size by nothing; a bare "by owner" groups).

Tests: f426 and f427 (red at the parent b2586354: 1 of 13 passed, the one counting the book's lines), explorer-recipe-verify (red at the parent 0 of 5 — the question reaches no floors). Re-pointed: f425 (1) five views, (6) the unknown colour now offers presses; f148 SAME_IN_BOTH gains two placeholder-only sentences.

## INSIGHTS — EXPLORER: FLAT VIEWS TURN, FLOORS OF ANYTHING (Young, 28 Sep 2026)

Young: *"In the explorer page, i seem to have difficulty rotating the screen when it comes to the floor, grid and timeline pages. They seem to get stuck. Also, allow the ability to create different types of floors like floors by stream simply by prompting. Make it possible to prompt every version of shapes and patterns but the landing state can be the stages."* Then: *"the state when you click into it can be what it is today as in the four floors of in review, drafting etc. but that should not be the only way to have floors. Maybe i want copilot to create floors of value stream or floors of owners etc"*.

What was found: the drag DID change the angles on all three views (measured `rotL`/`rotG`/`rotT` before and after), so "stuck" was what the eye saw. (1) A drag starting on a contract lit that contract's neighbourhood on the way in, and the turn never let go — the rest of the map stayed dimmed (47 nodes at 49ae5241) until the pointer happened to leave and re-enter a node. (2) Grid and Timeline stood upright in the screen plane, so turning them only narrowed them like a door on a hinge; the tilt was nearly locked. (3) "floors of owners", "rows by stream", "stack by owner" were not read; "reset" kept whatever floors were set.

What was built: the turn raises `IG.turning`, drops the hover and repaints undimmed, and the pointer's own enter/leave do nothing while it turns. Grid and Timeline now lie on the ground plane (x,z), the same way the floors do, with their own tilt ranges (`IGB_TILT`, clamps in `igTurnBy`), so a drag turns them like a table top. Grid column headings are trimmed to the width the cell is DRAWN at, so a turned grid never piles its headings. The reader: a role word (floors/rows/stack/lanes/columns/colour/size/label) finds its fact ANYWHERE in the sentence (`igFactAnywhere` after the role word is cut out), "by/of/per/on/into/with/efter/enligt/på/med/av" all introduce the fact; "reset", "start over", "back to the start", "återställ", "börja om" go back to the landing (stages on the floors, grouped by value stream; `int_did_landing`). When the floors ARE the grouping ("floors of value stream" while grouped by stream) the floors are not split again into the same columns — one column, no empty headings.

Checks: f427 phrase book grew the new phrasings; explorer-recipe-verify section 8 (8a–8f) — red at 49ae5241 on 8a, 8b, 8c, 8d (the dim left behind), 8e, 8f; green after.

## A REFRESH LANDS AT THE SAME SPOT (Young, 28 Sep 2026 — a new standing rule)

Young: *"New rule. If you are on a specific page and you refresh the page, you should land at the same exact spot you were in when you refreshed or reloaded the page."*

What was measured at 5448c132, on eight pages with a real reload: every page came back (setView already recorded view, contract and folder in `LS.ui`), and everything inside it was lost — the Contracts list's and the Negotiate page's scroll, the Document tab's scroll, the room's tab (History came back as Document), the Insights tab (back to Portfolio), the Settings tab (back to People), the Templates tab, the Calendar's Horizon, the Negotiations list's search, and the Explorer's floors and turn.

What was built: ONE STORE — the place rides in `LS.ui` as `place`, beside the page it belongs to; both writers of `LS.ui` (setView's and `persist`) keep it through `uiPlaceKept`. `placeNow` reads the page's own part plus every id-carrying scroller under `#content` and the shell's `#content-scroll` (keepScroll's sweep). `placeSave` runs on `pagehide`, `beforeunload`, the tab going hidden, and 250ms after any scroll. `placeResume` runs in `startApp` BEFORE the first paint, only when the stored place is for the same page (and, on a contract's pages, the same contract), and hands the part to its page's writer so nothing is drawn twice. `placeScrollBack` then re-asserts the scroll every 120ms for up to 6s because a page fills in after its first paint (a contract's full record, the paper's pages); the first wheel, touch, pointer press or key stops it — the reader's hand always wins. While a place is still being put back, a save keeps its scroll (the scrollers may not have filled in) and reads everything else live, so a tab changed straight after a reload is kept — found when the check changed the room's tab inside those six seconds and the save was being skipped.

The parts (`PLACE_PARTS`): register (`regPlace` — scope and the list's whole filter state), room (`roomPlace` — the tab; a reload is NOT an arrival, so the Document tab keeps Plain English or X-ray through `_docViewAt`, where the owner's 23 Sep landing rule still resets it on a real arrival), Insights (`intelPlace` — the tab, and on Explorer the recipe and camera), Settings (`settingsPlace`), Templates (`tplPlace`), Calendar (`calPlace`), Obligations (`obwPlace`), Negotiate (`rlPlace` — the list with its search, or the contract on the bench).

Not kept, on purpose: an open drawer or dialog (it is a step, not a place — it closes on a reload as before); a press that navigates to another page still lands at the top (7a).

Checks: refresh-keeps-your-spot-verify (14 claims) — red at 5448c132 on every claim except 7a (the behaviour kept) and 9a.

## INSIGHTS — EXPLORER: FINGERS, AND EVERY VIEW SHOWS THE WHOLE BOOK (Young, 28 Sep 2026)

Young: *"It seems all pages in explore have the same issue with trying to rotate and spin the screen. But i wonder if it just my iPad so please review. Also, brain and wiring seem to show a lot more contracts on the screen at a time especially when i am looking at 179 contracts in my portfolio. The other screens do not seem to show the magnitude of the portfolio."*

THE iPAD. The stage already carried `touch-action:none` (index.html, `#ig-svg`), and Chromium's own touch input turned every view — so the fault is not the browser taking the gesture. What IS iPad-only is the finger bookkeeping: (1) the pointer map `_igTouch` never forgot a finger whose lift it missed (a system gesture from the screen edge takes the touch), so from then on every one-finger drag arrived as the second finger of a pinch — the map zoomed by nothing and never turned again until a reload. That matches "gets stuck on every view". Now the first finger of a new touch (`isPrimary`) clears the count. (2) Two fingers only zoomed; an iPad reader twists or drags with two. Now a twist spins the view one radian per radian (`IGB_TWIST` is the drag's own scale) and moving both turns and tips it, while the pinch still zooms. (3) Lifting one of two fingers left the other doing nothing; it now carries on turning. Safari itself cannot be driven from this container — the check stages the finger sequences an iPad produces. Measured on the way: frame rate at a tablet's pixel density is fine (40–52 fps here without a GPU); not the cause.

THE MAGNITUDE. Two faults. (1) `INTEL_CAP` was 120 and silent: a 179-contract book drew 120 (the largest by value) in EVERY view with nothing saying so — against the standing rule that a cap is a fact. Now 300, chosen by measurement (420 contracts turned at 20–30 fps in this container; 310 at 45–52 on the flat views and 30 on the Brain; 175 at 47–59), and the head line says "Drawing the 300 largest of N by value" when it bites (`int_map_capped`). To buy the headroom the force layout idles at a quarter of the frames when the Wiring view is not showing, and `igbHexA` parses a colour once. (2) Floors, Grid and Timeline packed contracts into piles: the floors' columns sat 0.4 apart in the middle of a 3.4-wide floor and every cell stacked three abreast (each floor's contracts covered 33–45% of the stage); a quarter-end crowd on the Timeline landed on one spot (29 of 29 overlapping). Now the columns share the whole floor (`FW` 3.1) and each cell lays its contracts over its own patch, as square as the patch allows, `IGB_PITCH_MAX` apart at most (53–72% of the stage); on the Timeline a contract that would land on another's spot takes the nearest free one around its date (`IGB_TL_SPOTS`, a packed cluster inside its lane, the across-lane step `IGB_TL_ZS` longer because the plane is seen at an angle). Found on the way: a check that measures a dot must measure the circle — the node group's box includes its name label.

Checks: explorer-magnitude-verify (11 claims) — red at 47b48c1c on 1b, 1c, 1d, 2a–2d, 3b; 1a, 3a, 9a are the kept behaviour.

## INSIGHTS — EXPLORER: EVERY VIEW MOVES, AND TURNING / STILL (Young, 28 Sep 2026)

Young: *"Why are floor, grid and timeline not on a moving state at all times? Floor should be spinning just like brain and the others should be moving. Also add a turning/still button like in the brain page."*

Only the Brain turned by itself (`igbStep`: `cam.view===0`). Now the Floors turn at the Brain's own rate (`IGB_TURN_RATE`, on `rotL`). Grid and Timeline carry words laid on the ground — a full turn would show the axis, the headings and the lane names backwards half the time — so they SWAY `IGB_SWAY` (0.32 rad) each way once every `IGB_SWAY_S` (24 s) round whatever angle the reader has set; the sway is display-only (`cam.sway`, added in the projection), paused while the reader holds or points at the map, and eases back to the set angle when stilled. Wiring already drifts through its physics and is left as it was. THE BUTTON is the Brain page's own (its mark and its two words, `int_turning` / `int_still` mirroring `brn_turning` / `brn_still`), on the Explorer's view bar between the zoom and Fold all; `cam.spin` is the one switch for every view, starts Still for a reader who asked for less motion (as the Brain page's `autoRot` does), and rides the refresh place with the camera. Two older checks had pinned an exact angle while the Floors stood still (explorer-brain-verify 3d, refresh-keeps-your-spot-verify 3b) — 3d now allows a frame's drift, 3b holds the map Still and also proves the choice comes back.

Checks: explorer-magnitude-verify section 4 (4a–4g) — red at ac2c7d5b on 4a, 4c–4g; 4b (the Brain's own turn) is the kept behaviour.

## INSIGHTS — FOUR TABS REBUILT TO THE OWNER'S PICKS (28 Sep 2026)

The owner asked for three "world class" designs each for Portfolio (and "kill the bottom 3 cards"), Negotiation Friction ("leave the copilot feature"), Obligations and Exposure ("significantly improve"), with Payment terms left alone. Three named options per tab were drawn full size on a design-options page; the owner picked by name — Overview, Clause Ledger, Reminder Line, Pattern Grid — and said build. Each was built in its own worktree and merged here.

### PORTFOLIO IS THE OVERVIEW
What this slice says, What needs attention (with its pager) and the grey honesty note were deleted, not stubbed, the way `pfBiggest` went on 19 Sep. Two facts were saved from them: the contract past its end date became a headline tile (read through `contractExpired`, so it cannot disagree with the Expired chip), and the findings the attention card listed now colour the risk map in place of the old risk band — a contract with no scan is drawn HOLLOW, because unread is not safe. Every figure became a door; ids are recorded as the page draws and read at the press, so the number on a door and the list behind it are one reading. The runway's ids come only on the page's own request (`pfRenewalRunwayData({ids:true})`), so Copilot's copy did not grow. Value by stage counts stored statuses in the list's own words and dots and is a third filter. The map redraws at its card's real width. The old page's "Out with the other side" tile is no longer drawn (the design has four fixed tiles) — said to the owner. Checks: f429 (19 of 22 red at the parent), portfolio-frame-verify rewritten and taken off KNOWN_RED, f183 (7), f251 4a/6, keeps-your-place-verify re-pointed.

### THE FRICTION TAB IS A CLAUSE LEDGER
The 26 Aug brief (three hard-coded English sentences, bars, a counterparty table, four KPI cards) became a strip of six figures and one ranked list with a details panel. Every fact the brief carried survived: its figures are the strip, its costliest clause the first row, its refused-and-open count the amber figure, its slowest counterparty the first row of the counterparty lens. What went is the prose. New readings (asks by clause and side, refused-open by clause, contested-by) are plain counts collected on `intelFrictionStats`' existing walk and shaped by `intelFrictionLedgerData`; every old field keeps its value because Copilot's snapshot, the health report and the Explorer read them. The clause list is the same eight names reordered by extra rounds, so Copilot and the page agree on which clauses are listed. The 19 Sep "not buttons" ruling is reversed only for the three figures that now have a list. Copilot's read (`intelFrictionCopilotHtml`, key, wire, ask) is byte-identical. Checks: f430 (20 of 23 red at the parent), n8 (2), f337 (1), five-screenshots-verify 1, insights-panels-verify 10.

### WHERE OBLIGATIONS GO QUIET — THE REMINDER LINE
Every open obligation is a dot on its due date in a lane for the person carrying it, with a window for when that person is mailed; a hollow dot will never be mailed about. The page's other readings shrank to six tiles; the hero, cards, chase list and footer are no longer drawn (keys inert). The rule that sat inline in `intelObligationsData` moved into ONE function, `obReminderOf(o,c)`; the count, the fill and the window all take its answer, so the picture and the headline cannot disagree, and f247's silence pins pass unchanged. A lane's window is drawn only when everyone on it is reached, so a hollow dot never sits inside one. The page had never had doors; now every figure opens the Obligations list narrowed to exactly its rows (the register's `only` pattern: `obwOnly`, chip `#obw-only`), and a dot opens its own obligation, picked. Checks: f431 (17 of 17 red at the parent), f247, f253, f254 (6), obligations-report-verify 2/3/5.

### THE EXPOSURE TAB IS THE PATTERN GRID
The ranked table became a grid: the five exposures against category, value stream or owner, so a pattern like "every supply contract lets them change the price" — a playbook fix, not a one-contract fix — shows at a glance. ## INSIGHTS — WHAT CHANGED RIDES THE PAPER (Young, 30 Sep 2026)

Young asked, in three steps: does the paper update as redlines are approved (yes — `negoResolve` rewrites `c.redlineText` through `negoCommitBody` at once; the Document tab and the Explorer paper both draw from it, and the background poller re-draws the page when the other side's answer lands); could Explorer's Copilot summarise the changes from the original paper to the current one; and then: *"I want to be able to ask copilot in explorer page to summarize changes while the paper is open. It should have answers related to the paper as I read it with no limitations."* Picked all three recommendations: the ORIGINAL is the wording when the negotiation started; the record rides EVERY question on the open paper; EVERY change is in it, each labelled.

WHY IT COULD NOT: `igPaperAsk` sent `contractPlainText(c)` — the agreed wording only — under `IG_PAPER_RULE`, which said "from THE WORDING and nothing else". The negotiation's history was never on the message. The only other route to it, `get_contract` → server `copilotNegotiation`, clips each wording to 600 characters and keeps the newest 60 changes — the owner asked for no limitations, so that route was not the answer (and is untouched; it serves every other Copilot).

WHAT WAS BUILT: `igPaperChanges(c)` reads RAW (`c.changes` + `c.negotiation.rounds[].changes`, never `negoInit`) and writes, per clause in first-touched order: the clause's wording WHEN THE NEGOTIATION STARTED — `rounds[0].baselineBody` when a round has closed, because `negoAdvanceRound` moves the live baseline to the agreed wording, so the live one is not the original — then every change oldest first, whole: who (side named), when, the status now (`IG_CHANGE_SAYS`: agreed/on the paper, waiting, rejected, parked under a counter, replaced — each saying on or off the paper), the heading proposed, the proposed wording, the reason asked (`negoReasonOf`, never the provenance note) and what was said with the decision. `IG_PAPER_CHANGES_RULE` rides only when there is a record; a contract with nothing negotiated sends byte-for-byte what it sent before. `IG_PAPER_RULE`'s first sentence now admits the record. The one ceiling left is `aiDocChars` on the route, and a cut there is already stated (`aiInputCapped`).

A PIN IS LIT ON THE PAPER, so `igQuoteOnPaper` drops a quote found in the record and NOT in the wording (the old wording quoted back would have made a chip that points at nothing); a quote found in neither keeps the pin's own lost state. The rule tells the model to quote old/unagreed wording inside the answer, labelled, never as a citation.

THE SIX QUESTIONS: no new control, band or door — the existing ask box; the cost is visible where it was (the hover), re-counted at every ask because the paper redraws as changes are agreed (`igPaperCost`, `int_ask_contract_cost_changes` in both books).

Checks: f441 (10; 9 red at the parent 2654ad5, one [wall]); explorer-paper-knows-what-changed-verify 10/10 on the real app (two changes filed through `negoEditClause`, one agreed; the paper carries only the agreed one; the provider received the record after the wording; the old wording quoted back took no pin); analyze-on-the-graph-verify 39/39 unchanged.

## THE DEAL BOARD IS AN INSPECTOR (Young picked it, 3 Oct 2026)

Young: *"The deal board design is still not clear as some information is hidden and you do not get a full picture."* Three designs were drawn in an artifact (Ledger · Briefing · Inspector, beside the board as built). Young: *"Build Inspector, no Accept/Counter/Reject, no walk-away."*

What was hidden, measured on the board as built: the "Their last" and "Yours now" cells cut wording at 40 characters (`summary.slice(0, 40)`), the fallback wording at 32 (`db-fbw`), the Walk-away column could only ever print "—" (the playbook holds none and HaTi invents none, ruled 14 Sep), Rungs was a bare count, and nothing said why they asked or whether their ask sat inside the playbook.

What was built:
- `dealBoardHtml` draws a list (`#db-list`) and a pane (`#db-pane`); each scrolls in its own column, the head line stays put. Below 1000px they stack and the page scrolls as one.
- THE LIST is grouped Needs you · With {counterparty} · Closed (`dealBoardGroupOf`; our own unsent draft is OUR move, as the old board's fifth word said). Each row: name (wraps, never clipped), whose move, the small bar (the old Distance column's object), the verdict. THE LIST INSPECTOR'S GRAMMAR: a press selects, a second press on the shown row (or the card's button) opens the clause (`rlBoardGoClause`, the old row press, now the one door). Arrows move the pick (`document._rlBoardKeysWired`).
- THE CARD (`dealBoardCardHtml`) borrows every reading: the scale is `rlScaleHtml`; both wordings are `rlChangeWordingHtml` inside `.rl-cp-src` so they wear the clause panel's marks; the precedent sentence is `rlPrecedentSay`, lifted out of `rlPlaybookSecHtml` so the panel and the board say one thing; notes are `negoNoteCounts`; every move is listed oldest first with who, round, when, its tag, its summary and its own reason (`rg.say`).
- THE VERDICT (`dealBoardVerdict`) is arithmetic on the playbook's figures: meets your standard · within your fallback, you could accept · beyond your fallback by N · outside your standard by N (no fallback figure) · argued in wording · only you have moved · agreed · back to agreed. No model.
- THE HEAD LINE'S COUNTS ARE ITS FILTERS (`RL_BOARD_FILTERS`, `rlBoardFilterSet`); a zero is said, never pressed; a filter that empties falls back to everything. Not a new band: it is the head line the board always had.
- Pick and filter are per sitting and are forgotten with the contract (beside `_rlBoardOpen = false` in the arrival reset). Like the board's open flag before it, they are NOT in `rlPlace`: a refresh with the board open still lands on the paper (BUGLOG line).
- Refused by the owner and absent: a Walk-away column; Accept · Counter · Reject on the board (the Redlines column's acts; the board is not a second door onto them).
- `ng_board_note`, `ng_board_col_walk`, `ng_board_col_rungs`, `ng_board_col_fb`, `ng_board_col_clause`, `ng_board_col_std`, `ng_board_col_theirs`, `ng_board_col_ours`, `ng_board_col_gap`, `ng_board_col_move`, `ng_board_sorted_cap` and the `.db-t` family are STALE (keys kept inert in both books; `ng_board_col_prec` is live as the card's "Settled before").

### A room is a party, and the drawer is 460 (Young ruled 3 Oct 2026)

Young, of the notes panel: *"You can see how the notes panel looks like which is it is just too compact."* Then, having picked option 1 off the design round and asked for it wider: *"Let's improve the option 1 by increasing the panel size to be as the natural landing width of the redline panel."* Then: *"Build option 1 at 460."*

**THE COMPACTNESS WAS THIS SESSION'S OWN.** Measured on Young's iPad: `--shell-panel-w` is 330 below 1440 and he was on that rung, and the note's acts row was carrying SEVEN controls — Seen · Seen-by · Reply · Reopen · Delete · the given chip · Done-by. Four of the seven predate 3 Oct; **three arrived that morning with f443 and f444, built without measuring the row they were joining.** It had wrapped into a stack of single words.

**AND UNDER IT WAS SOMETHING WORSE THAN THE LAYOUT.** `negoNoteRoom` was `m.visibility === 'shared' ? 'external' : 'internal'` — a boolean — and a note carried NO party anywhere: `partyId` appeared on no message in js/ or server/server.js, so there was nothing for a payload to filter on. `share_messages` is keyed to the CONTRACT, deliberately, so the thread survives every reshare; `contractMessages` served the whole table to every link holder, walled only against advisers. On a two-party contract that is exactly right and always was. **From the moment a contract held a second outside party — which `partiesMulti` shipped in late September — a note written for one outside party was served to the other.** Young's own MK-411 reads `Jumenza LLC +1`. It was reported in the design artifact and recorded in BUGLOG before any code, because it needed his ruling on whether three or more parties get a room each or also a joint room; he answered by picking option 1, whose drawing is one room per party.

**NO MIGRATION, AND THE RULE IS THE SERVER'S OWN.** `srvPartyOfShare` already said a share row with a null `party_id` is the first outside party, "which is what every link on file is". `negoNoteParty` applies that same fallback to a note, so on every contract that existed before this not one note moves room, and `share_messages.party_id` is NULL on every row with nothing to backfill. A party named on a note that the contract no longer holds falls back to the same answer rather than being quietly re-homed to somebody else.

**THE SERVER IS THE WALL**, in the shape the adviser wall already had beside it: `srvMsgScope(contractId, shareRow)` resolves a link's room, `contractMessages` drops rows belonging to another party, and both sides of the comparison go through the same normalising so the migration is a rule rather than a backfill. A link's party is the LINK'S and never the body's — the open-relay rule in its room costume — and `srvPartyIdOn` validates the one a colleague names, because a colleague does legitimately choose the room. An adviser's rows are past the token wall already and are deliberately not narrowed by party, or an adviser would lose sight of their own notes.

**THE MENTION ROSTER IS A WALL TOO.** `negoPostComment` resolves mentions against `negoTagPeople`, so whoever is not on that list cannot be tagged; before the rooms it was one list for every outside party at once, which on a multi-party contract would have offered — and filed — the names of people at a different company. `opts.partyId` narrows it, using the signer row's own absent-means-first rule rather than a second one invented here.

**ONE BUILDER WHERE THERE WERE THREE.** The room tab row was written out three times (the change's panel, the embedded panel, the chat face) and kept in step by hand. `rlNpRoomsHtml` is the one builder with three callers, and the pin's own two-button switch was folded into the same room list — otherwise the pin and the chips would have been offering different places to put one note.

**THE WIDTH IS NOT A NEW NUMBER.** 460 is `RL_RIGHT_W0`, the width the redlines column rests at and the width its cards were approved at. MEASURED in a real browser at a 1500px window: drawer 460, column 460, **paper right 1000 against drawer left 1040** — on the negotiate page the drawer lands on the cards and the contract keeps every pixel, which is the whole argument for the number. It is the NOTES face's own token (`--shell-panel-notes-w`), because Activity and Alerts are one scrolling list and were deliberately left alone; the face is written once, in `applyPanelLayout`, which both doors already call, and `#context-panel[data-face="notes"]` beats the base rule by weight (1,1,0 against 1,0,0) so nothing needs `!important`. Two rungs, and the line is `BP.laptop` 1024 — an existing named rung of this product's, the one `clauseEditorFits` asks — rather than a number invented for this. The precedent for a per-face treatment was already in the code: the notes face owns its own LAYOUT, with a comment beside it saying why.

**THE ACTS ROW IS SPLIT BY KIND, NOT BY COUNT**, so it keeps working however many controls are drawn: a verb is a thing you press and a fact is a thing you read, and they were competing for one line. Nothing was removed and nothing moved to a hover — the pop-up diet's own rule is that a fact a reader needs stays on the face. The given chip is a fact that is also a door, so it sits on the facts line and keeps `data-rl-np-give`; the separator is its own element rather than a `::before`, because a pseudo-element inside that bit would put the dot inside the button and underline it on hover.

**WHAT THE NETS COST, and two of them taught the same lesson twice.** f444 (5) sliced 400 characters BACKWARD from the tick's own attribute and so was really asserting "nothing root-gated is drawn just above the tick"; re-ordering the row put Done inside that window and it went red while its claim stayed true — re-pointed to capture the tick's OWN guard. f333's adviser wall pinned a whole ternary including its `: undefined` else branch, which now carries `srvMsgScope` — re-pointed to ask each branch. **PIN THE REGION, NOT A BYTE COUNT**, for the third and fourth time in a fortnight. Six more nets reached for the outside room by the literal key `"external"` and were swept to `[data-rl-np-room]:not([data-rl-np-room="internal"])` — the relation, not the key. f304 (1)'s ruling was REVERSED IN PLACE: round two ruled the pin says Internal / External, and the second half of that is gone, because a contract can hold several outside parties and "External" cannot say which.

Tests: f446 (45 claims, **32 of 35 red at unmodified main**, and the three that pass are named controls). Its section 9 drives the real server with two outside parties and two links; at the parent it fails on `AND NOT THE OTHER PARTY'S`, which is the leak reproduced. notes-two-rooms-verify gained the pixels (the width as a RELATION to `RL_RIGHT_W0`, read off the page rather than typed; the paper ending before the drawer; the verbs on one line). Re-pointed in place: f173, f264 (8), f302 (1), f303, f304 (1), f333 (9g), f444 (5).

## HOME — THE CHART FAMILY (4 Oct 2026)

The owner, the morning after chart-first landed: "the charts seem to only be in bar charts which can be very boring. Please fix this… and also, how would a timeline chart appear? Show me a render first." A design question, so four named ideas were drawn on the real board in one artifact with a switcher — Ring, Blocks, Timeline, Bubbles — with a table and one recommendation: not one chart but a family picked by the question's own shape, Bars kept on the switch. The owner: "Implement your recommendation and merge to main."

WHAT WAS BUILT. `hbChartHtml(D, cs, view)` dispatches on the dig's `chart.mode`: `groups` → `hbRingSvg` (slices and a legend over the field the question did not fix; past `HB_RING_MAX` the rest is one grey slice with no door), `values` → `hbBlocksSvg` (a column per group as wide as its value, the biggest contracts named tiles in rows the column is wide enough for — a tile's width blends an equal share with its value's so nothing is a sliver — and the rest one band at the foot), `months` → `hbTimelineSvg` (months across, a lane per stage, every contract a pill from `hbStartOf` to `hbEndOf`, the today line amber, past end ruby with the word drawn ONCE as a key, a month with an ending a `qm:` door, a lane a `qg:` door; pills pack into rows per lane and a crowded set past `HB_TL_PACK` keeps only the last `HB_TL_SHORT` months of each pill and takes 16px rows; past `HB_TL_ROWS` the rest is said), the new `attention` → `hbBubblesSvg` (days to the end date across, value up, the bubble grown by `hbObOpen`, stage colour; quadrant words; the top six by value named). `attention` is picked when a condition's FIELD matches `HB_ATTENTION_RE` (move · owner · overdue · not read yet · off standard · liability) — the field, never the label's words. Money hidden (`canViewValues`) folds Blocks and Bubbles to the Ring.

THE DOORS. SVG pieces are not buttons, so `_hbSvgDoor` gives each `data-hb-dig`, `tabindex="0"`, `role="button"` and a `<title>` (the native hover), `hbOnKey` presses one on Enter or Space, and every group carries a solid or clear rect under its whole area — Playwright's click on a legend row timed out while the row's centre fell on a gap between text and track, which is the same as a reader's press landing on nothing. Colours are the board's own `--hb-*` through `.hb-sv-*` classes (a `var()` in an SVG presentation attribute is not honoured; `style=` and classes are); stage hues are `hmStageTone`, other groups `HB_HUES` literals. The stagger is an inline `animation-delay`, not a per-piece token (f447's token sweep reads every `var(--…)` the sheet names).

MEASURED where the owner looks: the Ring for "Show me all Juno contracts" (dark, light, expanded), the Blocks for a value range, the Timeline for "end in the next 12 months" (74 contracts, a crowded fixture with four end dates: 681px packed) and for expired contracts, the Bubbles for "contracts with no owner" (120, after unowning two in three — the server stamps `_raisedBy`, which `contractOwnerName` reads). Tests: f447 (the family, the attention question, Enter digs, Bars on the switch, the Ring when money is hidden), home-board-verify 13a/13h/13i/13b/13d/13f/13g/13j. The Explorer's own Grid and Timeline views are untouched.

EXPAND TAKES THE ROOM. An SVG grows only with its width, and the expanded card's width was the board's column beside the dock, so the ⤢ button grew the figures and the padding and little else (home-board-verify 13j: the timeline's width did not move). Now `hbPaintBoard` puts `hb-dig-big` on the page while the focus card is expanded, and the dock and its divider step aside the way they do in Present (`.hb-dig-big #ig-dock`), coming back on the same button; `igFitSplit` is asked after the toggle. The expanded ring measured 385px tall against 271px before.

## HOME — THE COUNT FOLLOWS THE QUESTION (4 Oct 2026)

The owner, 3 Oct: "I think the top constant 6 cards should also change based on the results of the latest output. Thoughts?" The advice: the Counting chip already exists and everything on the board follows it, so the latest answer becomes what is counted; what moved and the watches stay on the whole book; only answers that are a SET of contracts count, not panels. 4 Oct: "Build it."

WHAT WAS BUILT. No new state: the count is DERIVED from the trail. `hbCountKey()` walks the path from the end and takes the last key whose root (`hbRootKey`, unwrapping qg/qm/qv) is a question (`q:`) or the list an answer came back with (`ls`); a card opened from the list keeps the list's count; the book's own doors (f:, st:, cp:, panel rows) never recount — pressing "Past end date" must not turn the book into the 23. `hbCounted(lens)` is the raw `hbBook(lens)` narrowed to that set, read by `hbBookData` (the six figures and the stage bar), `hbPanelData` (every panel) and `hbLensOnMap` (the `hbcount` lens, applied on the flip to Explorer and when "Show these on the map" is pressed, which no longer adds a twin chip for the same set). `hbBookData(lens, {whole:true})` is the whole book: the watches, the daily baseline (`hbSeenTick`) and the "what moved" chips, which are not drawn while a set is counted. The head's chip (`hbCountChipHtml`, patched in place by `hbPaintHead` on every board paint) reads "Counting Juno ×" — the × is the trail's own close (`data-hb-crumb="-1"`); "All contracts" is not drawn beside a counted set, the side lens keeps its own chip. Your book's sub-line names the set.

A LOOP WORTH NAMING: `hbDigData` reads `hbBookData` for every key, and `hbBookData` was asked to carry the count's LABEL (`hbCrumbOf` → `hbDigData` → `hbBookData` → …: "Maximum call stack size exceeded" in f447). The label is read by the one builder that prints it, not by the data reading; the ids are read under a latch (`_hbCounting`) so the count's own dig is computed off the raw book. Tests: f447 (the count, every panel and the map, the chip), home-board-verify 14a–14c.

## HOME — THE RECIPE: WHICH · SPLIT · PICTURE · MEASURE · TREND (4 Oct 2026)

The owner, after the chart family landed: "The chart family is still not working well. My prompts are still not creating the outputs I desire or want to see. Advise how we can create a better solution… for instance when I ask for a timeline by month the charts do not come out as I asked." Then: "How do we include trend lines as well especially since we want to learn from the data in the platform?", "Both" (month columns for "by month", contract bars for "timeline"), the render, "Build it".

MEASURED BEFORE: 20 chart questions in the owner's style through the live board. Only 3 drew a chart and none drew the chart asked for. Four causes: the board never read picture words ("timeline", "pie", "bars"); "by month / by owner / by stream" were taken by the HIDDEN map (`igRecipeParse` regrouped Explorer while the reader looked at the board, and the dock said "Grouped by value stream"); a question naming no set ("timeline by month") drew nothing; Copilot could only send back a list, always drawn as the default ring.

WHAT WAS BUILT. `hbRecipeRead(q)` reads the chart words first (`HB_RC`: time units, group splits, pictures, measures, trend words, and a filler list of words that name nothing to count), takes them out of the question, and hands the rest (`condText`) to the map's one conditions reader; `left` is what neither understood. In `hbParse` it runs before the conditions block, so a figure's door never answers a question that asked for a picture, and a chart question that cannot be read whole goes on to Copilot with its picture words kept (`_hbPendingRecipe`). The `q:` dig carries the recipe; no conditions means the whole book (`D.whole`), which the count never follows. The date a time split uses is the date word nearest the time words, else what the measure implies (time to sign, rounds, payment days and an unprompted trend lean to the signing date), else the end date. `hbPlan(D)` = the dig's defaults (`hbPlanBase`, which also maps the older `mode` charts) + the person's presses (`s.recipe[key]`, `hbRecipeSet`, cleaned on load by `hbRecipeClean`; the 3 Oct Chart·Bars·List switch migrates as `pic`) made drawable by `hbPlanFix` (columns need time, ring/blocks need a group, a reader without values never sees money).

THE PICTURES. Month columns (`hbColsSvg`): buckets by month/quarter/year on the chosen date (`hbBucketOf`, `hbInBucket`), a door per column (`qm:` key + unit + bucket + date), a window of `HB_COLS_MAX` around today for forward dates or the latest for past ones with Earlier/Later columns that are doors too, a No date column — except on a signing chart, which draws what was signed and says how many are not signed yet. Contract bars stay `hbTimelineSvg` (now naming every second or third month on a long span, red only for a SIGNED contract past its end, closed ones faded). Bars for a group split take any measure (`hbGroupBars`).

TRENDS. `hbTrendOf` is a least-squares line over the columns: averages need `HB_TREND_MIN_N` (3) contracts in a column (fewer: drawn hollow, left out), a past-dated chart leaves the unfinished current column out, and a line needs `HB_TREND_MIN_PTS` (6) points — fewer is said in words ("Not enough history yet for a trend. It needs 6 months with at least 3 contracts each; there are 3."), never drawn. The sentence ("Average days to sign: 47 days → 55 days over 6 months · getting slower") is worked out by HaTi from the line's ends; steady within 5%.

THE MONTHLY PICTURE. "How many live contracts did we have each month" is not on the contracts, so it cannot be rebuilt. `book_snapshots` keeps one picture a month per stream (taken the first hour the server runs in the month, or on the first read; an empty book is not a picture; never rewritten). `GET /api/book/snapshots` adds up only the streams the reader may open and drops value for a reader without values. `hbLiveSvg` draws the points, where the line will start and when, and offers "contracts signed per month" instead. A browser check caught the first draft calling `api('/api/book/snapshots')` — api() already prefixes `api/` — and leaving the card on "Reading…" for ever on the failure; a failed read is now "no pictures yet".

COPILOT. The graph route's tool may return `chart` {pic, split, date, measure, trend}; `graphChartClean` keeps only the board's own words (never a number). On the board the typed words win and Copilot fills the parts they did not say (`hbFoundChart`).

MEASURED AFTER: 18 of the 20 questions draw the picture asked for, free; the other two ("top 10 contracts by value as bars", "a bubble chart of what needs attention") go to Copilot and land in the picture their words named. Tests: f448 (the phrase book — 41 questions with their four parts, 7 that keep their old road — the dropdowns, the columns, the trend rules, the snapshot states and the stream wall, Copilot's chart), f447 updated to the Picture menu, home-board-verify 13b/13c/15a–15g, home-page-verify 6.

## HOME — THE BOARD AND THE MAP: a card pressed while counting stays inside the count (4 Oct 2026)

Young: *"When I am looking at Juno contracts the top 6 cards show the numbers as it should but when i press any one of the cards, the numbers return to the whole list of contracts in the platform."*

Cause: the count is the focus card's set (`hbCountKey` scans the trail for a `q:`/`ls` root). A press on a Your-book figure, a stage bar or a panel row called `hbDig(key, false)`, which REPLACED the trail with `[key]` — so the question left the trail and the count with it; the six figures went back to the whole book and the list under the card was the whole book's.

Fix: the press carries `keep` (`hbDig(key, deeper, keep)` from the click and the SVG keyboard press). While a count stands (`hbCountLabel` non-empty) and the key is not itself a question or an answer list, the trail is cut back to the count key and the press is added after it: Board › Juno › Live contracts. A typed question still starts afresh (hbAsk, the contract card and `hbShowFound` pass no `keep`). Two readings that still read the whole book under a count were brought in: a stage's "Open these" opens the counted list instead of every contract at that stage (`stage` is set only when nothing is counted), and a counterparty row (`cp:`) reads `hbCounted`.

Tests: f448 (6) "a card pressed while counting Juno opens WITHIN Juno" (red at the parent: "f:live nests under the count"); home-board-verify 14d (asks "Show me all Juno contracts", presses Live contracts, the six stay on Juno, the trail names Juno). Photographed: 14d-card-within-the-count.png.

## THE BAR SAYS ONE THING (Young ruled 4 October 2026)

Young sent a photograph of a contract page with a box drawn by hand in the
empty space to the left of the word Contracts, and wrote:

> *"In contracts, the circled arrow next to contracts is missing in HATI but
> please make sure it is included now both in the documents and negotiate page.
> Also kill the the wordings that come after Contract as they are redundant
> because they are already below it in the page. Please advise you understand
> first. No coding"*

**THE ARROW WAS NEVER MISSING.** It was ruled on 15 September — *"there should
be a back button but in sign format not words"* — and built that day. Six days
later the second pass of the redesign moved the crumb out of the page head and
into the dark bar, and one line went in with it:

```css
#shell-title .room-crumb-back.in-crumb svg{display:none;}
```

So the sign survived only on `.room-crumb`, a row that hides itself the moment
the bar takes its button (`.room-head .room-crumb:not(:has(.room-crumb-back))`)
— which is to say nowhere a reader has ever seen it. Nineteen days of a ruling
in force and invisible. Told this, Young did not restate the ask; he changed
it, and improved it:

> *"In negotiations, back takes you to document page. In contracts, there
> should be no back button"*

**WHY THAT IS THE BETTER ANSWER**, and it is his, not mine. A back button earns
its place only where the rail cannot make the journey. On the contract room the
rail already carries Contracts, lit, one press away — so an arrow there was a
second door onto a trip the shell makes for free, which the One Door question
refuses. On the negotiate page the rail's Negotiations door goes to the LIST,
never back to the contract you were just inside, so the arrow is the only way
out. One rule, two different answers, and it is the rail that decides.

That REPLACES the 17 August ruling (*"when I am in the document page and click
the back button it should always take me to the contracts page… It should never
take me to the negotiations page which sometimes it does"*): there is no arrow
on the room to land anywhere now. The claim that survives — a reader who
reached the room from a negotiation gets out to Contracts and not back into the
negotiation — is asked of the door that does it, the rail's own
(negotiations-door-verify 7b).

**THE WORDING WAS REDUNDANT, exactly as he said.** The bar printed
`Contracts / MK-398 · Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement` while the page under it
printed the name in 28px type and the reference in the quiet line thirty pixels
below. Both crumbs lost it. On the room the word left behind is
`nav_contracts`, not `ct_back_register`: it has stopped naming a destination
and started naming where you are, and in Swedish those are two different words
(*Avtal* against *avtalslistan*). On the negotiate page the Negotiations door
went with the rest of the wording — the rail carries that too.

**THE TRAP, which is the whole reason f449 exists.** The room draws no button
now, so `wireRoomHead`'s old fallback —

```js
const back=document.querySelector('.room-head #ws-back')||document.getElementById('ws-back');
```

— would answer with the NEGOTIATE page's button, still parked in `#shell-title`
from the last visit. `shellCrumbAdopt` reads `data-back` off whatever it is
handed, so the room would have worn another page's arrow, landing on another
page's destination, on every second visit. Silent, second-visit-only, and
invisible to a screenshot. The fallback now refuses anything the bar is
holding.

**MEASURED, not assumed.** The two heads' crumbs stopped starting at the same
height the moment one became a sign and the other a word (pages-read-alike 1:
negotiate 16 against room 14.4): the row took its tallest child's height and
the 48px bar centred two different boxes at two different tops. Fixed by giving
`#shell-title.is-crumb` a `min-height` of `--ctl-h-sm` so the row's box stops
depending on what is in it — both read 12.5 after.

**WHAT WAS RE-POINTED, and why each one was a reversal rather than a break.**
f184 and f317 both pinned `${backC ? ' data-back="contract"' : ''}` — the
ternary that gave one head the destination and withheld it from the other.
There is no second head to withhold it from; both now pin that the button is
the negotiate page's and lands on the contract. negotiations-door-verify 7b and
nego-redesign-verify 1/1c pinned the room's arrow and the reference-as-word in
the bar. nego-redesign 1c is the interesting one: it is a RESTORATION, because
what it had been re-pointed to on 21 September was *"no arrow is drawn before
it"* — the check had been taught to assert the very fault Young reported.

**A SELF-INFLICTED ONE, recorded because it is the rule this codebase keeps
re-learning.** f449's first run failed its own "one button" claim: the comment
I had just written above the button quoted `id="ws-back"` verbatim, so the file
declared the id twice as far as a regex could tell. Strip comments before
sweeping source, or do not put the pattern in them.

**Pre-existing and left red** (proved in a worktree at unmodified main):
negotiations-door-verify's two "four tabs" checks (the room has five tabs now)
and nego-redesign-verify 1's hairline measure.

Tests: f449 (new, 17 claims, 6 of them red at the parent), f184, f317,
pages-read-alike-verify 1, negotiations-door-verify 7b, nego-redesign-verify
1/1c.

## ONE LIST, ONE PLACE (Young picked it by name, 4 October 2026)

Idea 4 of the seventeen — one "waiting on you" page — with one change made in
passing: *"Idea 4 but this should be included inside the newly built
dashboard."* Asked to confirm before anything was built, he wrote: *"confirm
that we are aligned that waiting on you will be in the home page dashboard and
will have it as a suggestion prompt."*

Three options were drawn, named for their ideas: **A card of its own**, **One
list, one place**, **Top of the morning**. He picked the middle one.

**WHY IT IS ONE CARD AND NOT A THIRD.** Nearly everything still to be built
PRODUCES something that waits on you — a named guest's invitation, a
colleague's held suggestion, a status page going stale. One list means each of
those adds a row. Three lists mean each invents its own way of nagging, and
somebody spends a week pulling them back together. So Prepared by Copilot
became **Your work**, and the only difference between two rows is who raised
them.

**THE ONE THING I PUT BACK TO HIM BEFORE BUILDING.** "Suggestion prompt" could
have meant Copilot writes the sentences. These are worked out from the record —
free, instant, and they cannot say something the contract does not. Copilot
sits in the same card offering to do the work and writes none of these words.
home-one-list-verify 6a counts every generative route from the sign-in to the
moment the card is painted and requires zero; it was failing at first for an
honest reason that is worth keeping — opening a contract from the card starts
Copilot reading it on arrival, which is a different feature paying for itself,
so the count is snapshotted before anything is pressed.

**THE FAULT THIS BUILD FOUND, and it was found by measuring rather than
reasoning.** The first run of the stage reported an empty list on a book with a
renewal plainly due in it. hmDecisionItems strikes a renewal out of its own
list when the DESK card is already showing it, so one decision is not asked
twice on one page — a correct rule written on 27 September, when Home drew
both. The desk card left the desktop with the 24 September redesign and the
board has never had it, so the subtraction was quietly deleting rows nothing
else drew. The fix uses the parameter that already exists for saying "no desk
here": `hmDecisionItems(null, [])`. The phone, which still draws both, calls it
with neither argument and is untouched. The stage seeds TWO renewals on
purpose, because with one it is impossible to tell an empty list from a
subtracted one.

**A ROW THE BOOK-WIDE LIST HAD NEVER BEEN TOLD ABOUT.** Giving a note to a
colleague was built on 3 October and the side panel's checklist has carried it
since that day; `hmDecisionItems` had not. So a note handed to you on Friday
was findable only if you already knew which contract to open — exactly the
fault one list exists to fix. Its lateness is the only date on either list a
PERSON typed, so it is the only one that can be wrong, and the row stays quiet
until it is actually late.

**AND THAT TURNED A TEST RED, correctly.** f395 1b pins that lateness is one
rule with two askers and that *"the card no longer carries its own copy of
today"*. The note row needed a day comparison, so the card said `todayISO()`
again. The claim was right and the build was wrong: `hmNoteDue` now holds the
rule, both readings ask it, and the check is stronger than before — neither
reading carries its own copy, and both are named.

**A SELF-INFLICTED ONE.** The card drew nothing and the whole app failed to
boot on `Unexpected identifier 'DESK'`: a paragraph added to the top of a
comment block had been pasted AFTER its `*/`. Lint catches it in one second and
had not been run since the edit before. Run lint after every edit, not after
every few.

**Left for the owner** (BUGLOG): a contract can appear twice on the card — once
as a waiting row and again inside Copilot's own count for the same contract.
They are different things and the sub-lines differ, but it reads as a repeat,
and suppressing the Copilot row per contract would make its count lie.

Tests: f450 (new, 26 claims, 20 red at the parent), home-one-list-verify (new,
19 checks driven in a browser), f395 1b re-pointed in place.

## WHERE THE DEAL STANDS — THE OWNER'S OWN TAB (idea 15, part one, 4 October 2026)

Young picked idea 15 after being shown five whole screens — what each side sees
today, the shared page at its own link, and the same page on each side — and
then said *"Build all your recommendations."*

**THE RULE THE WHOLE IDEA STANDS ON is a subtraction.** Every other feature in
this product adds something to a screen one side owns. This is a single page
with no owner, read by people who are negotiating against each other. So a fact
goes on it only if it can be shown to EVERY party; if it cannot be shown to one
of them it is not on the page at all — not hidden for that reader, not greyed,
not there. Anything else would need the page to know who is reading, and the
whole value is that it does not.

Each thing it rules out is a wall somewhere else that one careless line here
would have walked through: the internal review the counterparty never learns
happened; who on our side was asked to do what; any party's notes, walled into
one named party's room eight hours earlier; money not put to every party;
anything that reads as advice.

**AND PEOPLE — including our own.** This is the subtraction that is not
obvious. A change's author already travels to the counterparty, so naming them
would have been defensible. But a third party that only signs has never been
told who argues on our side, and this page is read by all of them at one
address. So "Lately" says the SIDE and the act: *"Highland Corporate Ltd asked
about 9. Liability Cap"*, never *"Elin accepted CHG-3"*. The browser stage
seeds three names on purpose — an author, a reviewer and a word that appears
nowhere else — and looks for each of them by name in what was painted.

**NO SEAT WORD, which is the other half of the same rule.** "You" and "them"
are the only words on a HaTi screen that mean different things to different
readers. negWhoseMove answers in seats, so the reading turns the seat into a
NAME before anything is drawn, and the stage greps the whole painted sheet for
you/your/them/their/us/our and requires none.

**READING MUST NOT WRITE, and here it is load-bearing.** negoChanges,
negoProgress and negoRound all run negoInit, which CREATES a negotiation on a
contract that has none — and this reading is asked for every contract with a
status link, including imported signed paper that never negotiated. The server
then freezes the wording it just invented, and every later save of that
contract is refused. Everything reads the raw fields, and the stage proves it
on a contract with no negotiation at all.

**IT SPENDS NOTHING**, which is what lets the same page be served later to a
stranger at a public address with no key, no budget and no wait. The stage
counts every generative route while the tab is drawn and requires zero.

**THE TAB WENT IN SECOND, not first,** so `roomOpenOnTerms` is untouched: a new
draft still lands on the Overview and f170 still asks it of the same key. Three
tests pinned the tab list by its exact shape and were re-pointed to what they
were each really about — f148 to the six translated words, f184 to the ORDER
the three original tabs stand in, f253 to Obligations sitting after Signing and
before History. Each is now a relation rather than a list, so the next tab
costs no edit.

**ONE SELF-INFLICTED FAULT, and f232 caught it.** The pane was built with a
`head` hook for the owner's own line about the link — who can see the page,
copy the link, switch it off — and nothing fills it, because the link is part
two. A hook nothing fills is a guard that is always false, which is the exact
fault that check exists for. The hook came out; `opts.head` stays as the seam
it will go through the day there is something true to put in it.

**WHAT IS STILL TO COME** (part two): the public address itself, the `status`
purpose on the send screen, the counterparty's page drawing the same sheet, and
the export buttons moving off their landing page into More.

Tests: f451 (new, 30 claims; the whole file is red at the parent, where
js/dealstands.js does not exist), deal-stands-verify (new, 19 checks driven in
a browser), f148 / f184 / f253 re-pointed in place.

## THE STATUS LINK — ONE ADDRESS, EVERY PARTY (idea 15, part two, 4 October 2026)

Part one built the reading and the owner's own tab. This is the address.

**A STATUS LINK IS THE ONE PURPOSE WHOSE LINK DOES NOT OPEN HaTi.** Every
other kind — negotiate, sign, view, history, advise — hands the holder a copy
of the contract and opens the application around it. This one is a page the
server builds from the stored record on every open: no account, nothing to
press, and no copy of the contract anywhere behind it.

**THREE WALLS, because one would not have been enough.**
 1. The browser stops building early: `buildSharePayload` returns the
    contract's **id and nothing else** for a status purpose. Not a stripped
    copy — the id, so the server knows which contract the address is for and
    can check the sender may reach it.
 2. The server reduces a hand-built payload to that same shape, because a
    payload is the thing under suspicion and the wall belongs to the route
    every path goes through.
 3. `GET /api/shares/:token` — the route that serves every other kind —
    refuses a status token outright with a 403 that names the right address.
    Without that line it would hand over the counterparty's whole working
    payload to anyone holding a link that was never meant to carry one.

**IT IS ONE MORE ANSWER, NOT A NEW DOOR.** The send screen already asks what a
link is for; `status` is a sixth answer on that control. The One Door question
would have refused a button of its own, and the owner's own line about the
link is a LINE in the head rather than a strip across the page — his rule
refuses a new band without being asked, and the head says the same thing for
less.

**MEASURED, and three of the four faults were only visible by driving it.**
 · The row behind the address had no `contract_id`, because the first version
   of the server wall deleted `payload.contract` outright and the id is read
   off it. The page answered *"This contract is no longer available"* and the
   owner's tab said no page was shared. Keeping `{ id }` fixed all of it.
 · The public page named ONE party and said *"A party asked about 9. Liability
   Cap"*. `srvContractParties` builds our row out of `c.party` — the entity on
   this agreement — and a contract that never named one leaves it blank, so
   the row fell out of the list. The browser's reading falls back to the
   workspace; this one now falls back to the same fact out of the org record,
   or the two readings disagree about who the deal is between.
 · f390 3b broke in a way that had nothing to do with it: that check slices the
   server between `TRACK_STAGE` and the tracker's route and evaluates the
   slice, and the new page had been written between them. It moved below the
   tracker. A test that evaluates a slice of a file is a test that owns the
   space between its two anchors.

**THE TWO READINGS ARE PINNED AGAINST EACH OTHER** (status-link-verify 4d),
the way copilotNegotiation and negoCopilotRecord are: the owner's tab and the
public page are asked about the same contract and must agree on the round, the
open and total, whose move, every open clause, every settled clause, every
party and the live step. Two surfaces may draw differently; the reading may
never differ.

**A SELF-INFLICTED ONE worth recording**: f451's own check for "no person is
named" passed `ch.author` to `includes`, which is a PREFIX of `ch.authorSide`
— the side, which is allowed and is the whole mechanism. The check failed on
the correct code. It asks on a word boundary now.

Re-pointed in place: f333 9a and its sibling pinned the purpose list as a
literal and now ask that `advise` is on it, so the next purpose costs no edit;
f148 took `co_purpose_status_label` into SAME_IN_BOTH, because "Status" is the
same word in Swedish and the sentence under it IS translated.

## THEIR PAGE DRAWS IT TOO, AND THE COPIES GO BACK INTO MORE (idea 15, part three, 4 October 2026)

The third surface. The owner has the tab, a stranger has the address, and the
counterparty's own page now draws the same reading under a quiet rule.

**WHAT IS ABOVE THE RULE KNOWS WHO IS READING; WHAT IS BELOW DOES NOT.** Their
two cards — what is waiting on YOU, and who to talk to — are theirs alone and
could never go on a public page. Everything under the rule is the same
dealStands reading the owner's tab draws and the address serves.

**AND THE COPIES WENT BACK INTO MORE**, which Young asked for in his own words:
*"for space limitations, in the home page, you will have to delete the export
button and keep it under the more button as it is designed today."* This
REVERSES the 29 September decision that emptied that menu — Notes and Focus
moved onto the page and the copies onto a Copies card, which left nothing in
More, so it was switched off. The argument then was sound and is no longer:
nothing else wanted that column in September, and the shared page wants it now.
**Nothing was written for it**: portalMoreMenuHtml has sat there in full the
whole time, same Export heading, same two rows, same wiring, with nobody
calling it. This was turning something back on.

**A JUDGEMENT I MADE AND THEN REVERSED, in the same hour.** The sheet drew its
own journey and its own Lately, so their page had two of each. My first answer
was to delete theirs and let the sheet carry both — which read well and lost
something real: THEIR journey can say signing is under way on their link, and
THEIR Lately carries the exact words that moved. f440's check caught the first
loss by name ("Under way"). So theirs stay, and the sheet leaves both out on
that surface alone. `standsHtml` takes `{journey:false, lately:false}` and
nothing else can be switched off — the parties, whose move, the counts and the
two lists ARE the page.

That also made the rule's own label honest. It said *"The same page every party
is reading"*, which stopped being true the moment one surface drew less of it.
It says *"What every party can see"*.

**AND ONE THING THE RULEBOOK CAUGHT.** The rule's label was
`color:var(--color-accent-700)` — the raw accent ramp as text, which measures
2.35:1 at night against AA's 4.5, and f238 sweeps every view file for exactly
that. It is `--accent-ink-700`, the only accent token with a dark answer. The
same fix went into the sheet's own eyebrow and the owner's line in index.html,
which that sweep does not cover but the eye would have.

Left red, pre-existing on main: portal-header-verbs-verify's "the Send is ON
TOP OF THE REDLINE CARDS".

the rule); f439's More claim reversed in place — what it was really about,

## A NAMED GUEST'S LINK ASKS WHO IS OPENING IT (idea 8, built 4 Oct 2026)

Young picked **"The guest list"** by name from three options in the decision
pack: *several named people per outside party, each with their own link and
their own code.*

### Two thirds of it was already built, and the first draft did not notice

- **The guest list.** `js/participants.js` has held several named people per
  contract since September, and the send screen has minted one link each
  through `shareSendExtras` since the day it learned to copy a colleague.
- **And the code.** `share_otp`, `POST /api/shares/:token/otp` and
  `/verify-otp` have minted a six-digit code, mailed it to the address ON THE
  ROW, hashed it, counted wrong guesses and handed back a ticket since the
  signing work.

The first draft of this build wrote a **second pair of routes anyway** — four
new columns on `shares` (`code_hash`, `code_at`, `code_tries`, `code_ticket`),
two new rate-limit buckets (`codesend`, `codetry`), its own twenty-minute
expiry, its own five-guess cap, its own ticket. The full suite answered with
**f358 (7e)** by name:

> `assert.ok(!/shares\/:token\/code'/.test(SRV), 'a second door onto an act
> that already has one');`

and that test exists because the same mistake was made once before and
reverted. Its own heading is *"the guest's one-time code was ALREADY built"*.
Every line of the second pair was removed. What the build actually added was
**one question asked in one more place**: the code gated SIGNING and nothing
gated OPENING, so a link addressed to Elin opened for anybody she forwarded it
to.

### One code, one proof, two gates

The proof the door wants is exactly the proof the signature wants — this
address, this person, this link — so a guest who proved their inbox to open the
link does not prove it again to sign. Minting a second code for the same
question would have been the weakening: two codes in one inbox, neither meaning
anything in particular.

`shareDoorOtpOk(token, t)` reads the one code table, compares the ticket in
constant time (`timingSafeEqual`, lengths asked first because it throws on a
mismatch), and requires `verified && verify` so a null can never be a ticket.
The ticket deliberately outlives the code: `share_otp.expires` is ten minutes
to type six digits, while `verify` is the proof that was earned with it, and a
reader should not be asked again eleven minutes into reading a contract.
Asking for a fresh code clears it (`verify=NULL` on the `/otp` upsert), which
is what shuts a previous opener out — driven by named-guest-verify 5a.

### The escape, and why it reverses nothing

`/otp` and `/verify-otp` carried three refusals that are about SIGNING: a
read-only pass cannot sign, an adviser's copy cannot sign, a spent one-shot
link cannot sign again. f144 measured the first of those — a view token could
make the server email a signing code — and that wall stays. But where the
link-code rule is on, this route is also the only way the holder can OPEN the
link at all, and those three would then lock a legitimate reader out of their
own link with no way forward. So **one escape, gated on `shareNeedsCode(s)`**,
which is off by default and never true of a status link or a link with no
recorded address. A revoked or expired link is still refused, for everybody,
and that check sits outside the escape: dead is dead.

### Where the gate stands, and the two measured corrections

The 401 stands on `GET /api/shares/:token` — the route that hands over the
contract — and **below** the two "gone" answers. It was written above them
first; a withdrawn link would then have sent its holder off to fetch a code the
code route itself refuses, which is a door asking for a key to a room that is
not there.

**The mask was measured and loosened.** The first draft masked the domain too
and printed `e…g@n…g.example` for `elin.hallberg@nordbygg.example` — which
tells somebody with three inboxes nothing at all, so the wall was doing no work
and the help was gone with it. It now does what every sign-in screen does:
first characters of the name, whole domain (`el…@nordbygg.example`). The domain
is the company whose link this is; the part worth hiding is which person at it.
The server draws it on its refusal (`shareCodeMask`) and the screen redraws the
same shape from the whole address `/otp` has always returned
(`portalMaskAddress`), so one screen cannot read two ways.

**And a hole was found and closed on the way past.** The comment above
`shareIsReadOnly` says, in those words, *"adding the purpose without adding it
here is how a fifth purpose becomes a hole"* — and the `status` purpose, added
two commits earlier the same night, had not been added. Measured: a status
token, which opens a page with no account and no copy of the contract on it,
could make the server mint a six-digit signing code and email it to the
recipient. It could never have spent it, but generating signing traffic to
somebody's inbox from a link issued to show a progress bar is exactly f144's
fault in a new costume. `shareIsStatus` is now on `shareIsReadOnly`, with its
own sentence in `refuseIfViewOnly` because the view link's words ("it can show
the contract") are untrue of it.

### The screen

`portalCodeScreen` holds **nothing of the deal**, and not as a design choice:
the payload was refused, so the page has not been given a contract to show.
There is nothing to skip to. It sends the first code on arrival (opening the
link IS the ask) and marks the sitting so a refresh does not spend the mail
again; every later code is a press. The ticket lives in `sessionStorage`, not
`localStorage`, so a borrowed laptop is not still inside somebody else's deal
tomorrow morning. "Sent" means sent, in `mailReportPublic`'s own four states.

Measured off the rendered page (named-guest-verify 2g/2h): the card is 420px,
the box and its button share one line, the box is what `elementFromPoint`
returns at its own centre, the face is 14px, and at 390px there is a 24px
gutter and no sideways scroll.

### The setting, and the group it forced

An admin's switch, OFF by default, in the same `appSettings` blob every other
wall lives in. It was first put in **The agreement** group — and that made a
group of five, which settings-groups 1c holds to four, measured on the first
run. It is also the truer home elsewhere: the three rules in that group decide
**who must say yes before a step**; this one decides **who may open what has
already left the building**. So a sixth platform group was declared, **"Links
you send"** (*who may open what leaves the building*), and settings-groups 1a,
1e and 4h were re-pointed from the numbers five and two to the relation — every
group `ST_GROUPS` declares is drawn, and a caption appears on exactly the ones
that declare one. That file had already learnt the same lesson on 30 September.

### And f354 learnt the house rule from the other end

`f354` swept the whole of server.js for the word `participants` to prove there
is no route to the people list. It went red because a comment about THIS
feature mentioned the browser module by name — so a sentence explaining one
wall was breaking another, and the only way to keep it green was to stop
writing the word. The rulebook's own rule applies: **strip comments before
sweeping code**. The claim is unchanged and still catches a real field.

Tests: **f452** (30 claims, all red at the parent), **named-guest-verify**
(28 claims, 15 red at the parent, runs to the end either way).
