## THE AI'S READING RULES

- `aiDocChars` (200,000) is the ONE ceiling for one contract on every route and client send; a cap marks the text and says so. An answer cut short (`truncated`) is not an empty one. `anthropicMessages` bounds the wait and retries ONCE only on a thrown connection, never on a status.
- COPILOT READS EVERY CHANGE, WHOLE (Young, 30 Sep 2026): `copilotNegotiation` (server) and `negoCopilotRecord` (browser; f47 pins them alike) clip no field and cap no count; the one bound is the document ceiling over the list, newest first (`aiDocChars` / `NEGO_COPILOT_CHARS`), `changesOmitted` states a cut. `NEGO_COPILOT_CAP` is STALE. Tests: f47, copilot-reads-every-change-verify.
- A line break written out as text is a break: `mdParse` reads `\n` (`AI_ESCAPED_BREAK_RE`) for every Copilot answer; a doubled backslash stays. Tests: f459 (E).
- `AI_QUOTE_RULE`, `AI_REDLINE_RULE`. Commentary is not wording (`AI_MODEL_VOICE` / `AI_MODEL_INSTRUMENT`); the builder refuses a remark as wording (`tbCardWording`). A reading's answer is checked before it is filed (js/metaclean.js `metaUnleak`, at the route and on the way in). No brace reaches the page (`AI_TONE_RE` family in js/aimd.js; `{{blank}}` keeps its braces).
- THE COPILOT AUDIT: money per contract with home-currency totals (`copilotMoneyOf`, `COPILOT_MONEY_KEYS` walled); archived off lists; `graphWhereHit` one predicate both hosts; paging and search bounded; tool-name sets equal on both hosts; `get_obligations`, `get_contract_history`.
Tests: f53, f135, f229–f235, f305, f328, f367.

## TWO LANGUAGES ≠ TWO MARKETS

LANGUAGE is the person's (js/i18n.js); MARKET is the company's (js/jurisdiction.js, admin). A month follows the language (`langLocale()`); numbers follow the market; CONTRACT TEXT IS NEVER TRANSLATED. `i18t()`/`i18tn()`, never `t()`; never inside a regex; never branch on translated words; a RECORD label keeps English; getters not literals; `srvMsg` translates a server sentence inside `api()`. Tests: f148.

## WHAT COUNTS AS A CLAUSE (js/clausemodel.js)

A HEADING's number may be Roman or a letter (`DOC_READ_HEAD_NUM`, `DOC_READ_ROMAN`; after a self-naming word or before `.`/`)`); the PARAGRAPH rule `DOC_READ_NUM` stays digits ("X.1" rides in its article). `clauseSegment()` is the ONE splitter (headings mark clauses or they don't); `CLAUSE_KINDS` the one vocabulary; `clauseKind` reads the heading only; page banners over numbered clauses ride with the next clause (`_clBanners`, once stamped the ids decide). `clauseCarryIds` keeps ids across a re-read. `applyNegoProposals` never drops what it cannot place. `redlineHangHtml` is the one gutter walk. Tests: f131, f163, f285, f371.

## HOME — READ, THEN ASK, AND A BUTTON THAT SAYS "MAKE SMALLER" (Young, 4 Oct 2026)
- Two screenshots. First: *"the expand button should turn into contract button when the card is already expanded."* The button drew the same outward arrows in both states; only its hover changed, and its aria-label said "Make bigger" even when enlarged. One builder now draws it in its three places (the dig-in, a board panel, a kept view): arrows in, "Make smaller" to the hand and to a screen reader. It was pointed out that the owner's picture was probably at normal size (the Copilot panel was still showing; enlarging hides it), which is why the button looked wrong.
- Second: *"the cards when expanded should have some sort of summary explaining the charts. I have no idea what this is saying for instance. Maybe that could be a differentiator for Hati. Short copilot summaries of what the analytics or data is saying."* The card read "Count: −2 → 4 over 24 months · rising" — the trend line's arithmetic, and wrong (a count below zero; logged in BUGLOG, not fixed). Four named options were drawn on the owner's own card (Plain reading · Copilot's read · Read, then ask · Notes on the chart); Copilot's read spent on every enlarge, which the rules forbid without the owner's yes. Young: *"let's go with read then ask but the output of the ask should have colors like copilots read"*, then *"build it and merge to main"*.
- WHAT WAS BUILT: on an enlarged chart, HaTi's reading (teal) replaces the trend sentence: what was counted, where most of it sits (the busiest one or two neighbouring columns, "Most of them…" when they hold half), the longest empty stretch, what falls before/after the columns, what has no date, what is not signed yet; for an average, the highest, lowest and latest; for a grouping, who has the most and what the top three hold. Every contract count is a door onto exactly those contracts. Under it one press asks Copilot, with what it reads said beside it; the answer lands in the amber box (Copilot's read's own look), checked by the map's rule (a sentence stating a number of contracts the chart does not hold is left out, and the box says how many were). Kept per chart and per day; a different count is a different chart; a failure or a missing key is said in the box. At normal size nothing changed.
- Not read yet: the timeline, the bubbles, live-per-month and list pictures keep their own lines (no reading is drawn for them).

## TODAY'S INSIGHTS — THE SHELF COMES BACK WHOLE AFTER A REFRESH (4 Oct 2026)

- Young: *"fix the shelf refresh fault and merge to main"* — the fault noted in BUGLOG on the "Yours, measured" build.
- THE FAULT: the board record's loader (`hbS`) kept only bare shape names in `s.ins.list` and dropped `scope`, `young` and `usual`. After a refresh, a "yours" finding (`pay.mine`) was thrown away, the day's choice was already made (same day, same book signature), so the reader's own findings stayed off the shelf until tomorrow, and an opened "usual pictures" closed again.
- THE FIX: the loader keeps any id `hbInsOf` can read (a shape or its `.mine`), at most `HB_INS_MAX`; `scope` must be one of mine · few · co (anything else reads as co); `young` is a boolean; `usual` must be an ISO day. An unknown word in the list is still dropped.
- Also made real: f461's "the kept answer survives a reload" set `_hbS = null` through `eval`, which did not reach the module's binding in jsdom, so it passed without reloading. Both f460 and f461 now reload for real by switching to another person's sitting and back.
- Tests: f460 "a refresh keeps the day's shelf" (2 tests, red at unmodified main); insights-shelf-verify stage 2a reloads the real page and finds the "Yours · 40" picture still on the shelf (24/24).

## THE BOARD ANSWERS THE QUESTION ASKED (4 Oct 2026)

- Young sent a screenshot of Home's board: "All contracts · by month · signed · Value · Trend". It read "Value: SEK -367.66 → SEK 851.41 over 24 months · rising", "29 contracts · SEK 6K" and "148 contracts not signed yet are not drawn". In the panel Young had asked *"why does the dashboard say on 851 SEK when we have over 1 billion sek under management"*, and Copilot answered *"Nothing changed on the map. … The 851 SEK you're seeing likely points to a single contract's value or a filtered subset"*. Then: *"fix the stage bug then review this bug where dashboards are still not working well as far as the relationship between prompting and the output. Review this as a whole and fix it. Then merge to main."*
- THE STAGE BUG (BUGLOG, 4 Oct): `hbGroupsOf` keeps stages in stage order, so the reading's "has the most" named the first stage. It is now measured (sorted by size); "the three largest" too.
- THE REVIEW: 25 everyday questions were put to a book shaped like the owner's (177 contracts; the money in 86 drafts; 47 signed, 18 of them with no signing date), in a real browser, and each card was recorded. Mismatches found:
  1. Executed contracts with no signing date were said to be "not signed yet" (148 instead of 130), and the headline counted only the dated ones (29 contracts · a few thousand).
  2. The trend line was fitted through 24 months that were mostly empty; its ends went below zero and were printed to the cent as if they were figures ("SEK -367.66 → SEK 851.41").
  3. Copilot in the panel was never shown the board: on Home, a question the board's reader did not take went to the MAP's route with only the map's screen. It answered about the map and opened with "Nothing changed on the map".
  4. The reader missed money questions and everyday words: "how much value did we sign each month", "total value signed by month", "average days to sign by month", "how long does signing take", "value of contracts in review" (drew a count), "how much is signed", "total value under management".
  5. A default split put everything in one group ("how much is signed" → one ring slice, "Executed 100%").
  6. "my contracts" drew the attention bubbles, because "owner" is in `HB_ATTENTION_RE` for "nobody owns".
  7. A ring by owner was captioned "by stage" (`hbGroupWord` had no owner).
  8. The card title read "over 1million".
- THE FIXES:
  1. SIGNED IS THE STAGE: an executed contract with no date stands in the "No date" column. Only the not-yet-signed are left off, said with their money ("14 contracts not signed yet (KES 520M) are not drawn"). The reading's totals include the "No date" column, like the headline.
  2. A trend on a total or a count needs `HB_TREND_MIN_PTS` columns that hold contracts, else it is said in words (`hb_tr_few_any`). It is clamped at zero, and its ends are "≈", rounded (`hbTrendFmt`) and said as "Trend line, value per month: about … → about …".
  3. `hbBoardNow()` describes the board in words: Your book's figures, the count, the open card (set, picture, headline, columns, the trend sentence called the ends of a fitted line and not totals, what is left off, HaTi's reading), and the panels. It rides as `screen.board` to `/api/ai/graph`, where `graphScreenSays` tells the model it was asked on the board and to change nothing on the map. It also rides at the head of the chat question. On the board, the answer is printed without "Nothing changed on the map", and a sentence with a count the board does not show is left out (`hbWhyCheck`).
  4. A why/explain/what-does-this-mean question (`HB_WHY_ASK_RE`) is never read as a new chart; it goes to Copilot with the board.
  5. `valueLead`: a question that leads with money asks for money, and the money words are read. "how", "much", "total", "average", "sign", "under", "management" are filler. "did we sign" is the signing date, and "how long does signing take" is time to sign. A money question's panel line carries the money (`hb_found_n_value`).
  6. `hbUsefulGroup`: a split the board picks itself moves to one that divides the contracts; a split the question named is drawn as asked.
  7. Attention only for "nobody owns". `hbGroupWord` knows owner and value band. Value labels shorten their unit ("over 1M").
- Ruling changed: f448 (4) had pinned "no 'No date' column on a signing chart". The undated EXECUTED ones now stand there; the not-yet-signed are still said apart. read-then-ask-verify 1b and f461 (B) now expect no line through one burst after a long quiet.
- Tests: f482 (24 tests; 21 red at unmodified main, the other two guard what must not change). board-answers-the-question-verify 12/12; at main it was 3/12, and drew "KES -94.28571428571428" on the chart.

## "THIS" IS THE OPEN CHART, AND COPILOT PRESSES THE BOARD'S BUTTONS (4 Oct 2026)

- A review of how the board and Copilot talk was compared with four open-source projects on GitHub, and their own pages were checked:
  - CopilotKit gives the copilot what is on screen (`useCopilotReadable`) and the app's own buttons (`useCopilotAction`).
  - Microsoft LIDA turns a question into a goal, draws the chart, evaluates and repairs it, and takes edits like "convert this to a bar chart".
  - NL4DV surfaces an unclear part of a question as "ambiguity widgets", small dropdowns.
  - Metabase's Metabot keeps the current question as context, and its interface sends the dashboard and question being viewed.
- The review found three faults. Copilot was told it was "filtering and clustering for a graph view" even on the board. A chart-only answer ("make it a pie", "show this by stream") was thrown away, because the board only drew answers that came with a list. And the board and the server kept two word lists.
- Young: *"build 1 and 2, run full suite then merge to main"*.
- WHAT WAS BUILT, (1) "this" is the open chart:
  - `hbFollowUp` reads a follow-up while a list card is open on the board. Edit words ("make it monthly", "as a pie", "by stream", "show value", "add a trend", "remove the trend") change THAT card through `hbBoardEdit`. That is the dropdowns' own `hbRecipeSet`, part by part, with the picture last.
  - A monthly/quarterly change keeps the card's date unless another date is named.
  - "only X" (or a condition plus a refer word) nests a `qn:` card: the open card's contracts narrowed by `igConditions` + `igIdsWhere`. It sits in the trail and in `hbRootKey`, so the count follows it.
  - "all contracts" or "the whole book" start fresh, as does a question with no refer, edit or lead word.
  - The board's own commands win (`hbParse` non-`q:` acts).
  - "that" and "those" are NOT refer words. home-board-verify 11c caught "agreements that are past due" being read as a narrowing.
- WHAT WAS BUILT, (2) Copilot presses the board's buttons:
  - On the board, the `/api/ai/graph` prompt OPENS with `boardJob`. Its order of preference: change the open chart (`chart.target` "open", only the parts asked for, in the board's own dropdown words); a new chart over a set ("new"); or an answer from the board's numbers. The map's own fields stay empty unless the map is asked for.
  - `hbBoardNow` adds "Open chart settings (chart{} words)", so "this" can be changed exactly.
  - `graphChartClean` keeps `target`, keeps `trend:false` ("remove the trend"), and takes `live`. f483 pins the server's `GRAPH_CHART_*` lists equal to the board's `HB_PICS`/`HB_DATES`/`HB_MEASURES`.
  - In the panel, `hbBoardTakes(res)` takes a chart-only answer BEFORE the map sees it: it changes the open chart, or draws a new one over the whole book. The panel says "Changed the open chart, "…": now …", followed by Copilot's own sentence.
  - On the board, the map's ARRANGING reader (`intelMapLocal` regroup/floors/colour) stands aside (`boardUp`). Its list-making acts (top N, narrow, compare, linked, families, sort, outliers, walk) still answer, so "top 10 contracts by value" still lands on the board.
- Re-measured: the 25-question review shows no regressions. One gained: "total value under management".
- Tests: f483 (17 tests; 15 red at unmodified main, the other two guard what must not change); this-is-the-open-chart-verify 12/12 (3/12 at main). The pinned line in f425 (6) and f426 (4) now reads `(igPaperUp()||boardUp)`.

## RISKS TO LOOK AT — THE RISK SCAN LIVES IN THE REDLINES CARD (4 Oct 2026)

The owner asked why a risk-scan finding ("No injunctive-relief clause" on an NDA) never became a prepared redline. Answer: Prepare redlines reads only Our standards; the scan is a separate, fixed rule list per template, and the NDA book had no remedies standard. Then: *"shouldnt there be an option to prepare a rebuttal or choice to add language to the contract as redline to cover the potential risk?"* and *"i also think copilot scan is very much hidden."*

Three options were drawn in an artifact for each round. The owner picked by name: **"A pile to look at"** (open risks listed at the foot of the Redlines column, kept after the first redline) with **"Read in place"** (Copilot's wording drawn as tracked changes in the row; "Add to redlines" files it), then ruled **the separate Risk scan panel away** (*"would it make sense to get rid of the risk scan panel and keep it in the redlines card?"* — yes: read in Risk View, act in the Redlines card), then **"Risks found" replaces the Overview's "Filed" tile** (*"so the scan is never missed"*). "Go with your suggestions" settled the four open points: both sources (scan + the brief's watchouts/unusual terms, de-duplicated), the rename "Prepare redlines" → "Draft from our standards", one "Risk scan not run yet · Run it" row on an unscanned contract, and "Add a note instead" on every risk.

Built in js/risks.js. Points worth keeping:

## ONE RECIPE LANGUAGE (work order Part 1, built 4 Oct 2026 overnight)

The owner asked Copilot to "build almost anything I need in the dashboard with precision". Before, a card was four parts and a switch (split · picture · measure · trend). Now it is ONE recipe: which · split · split2 · measure · pic · sort · top · window · compare · title.

- ONE cleaner (`hbCardClean`) for a press, a question, a stored board and Copilot; the server mirror `graphChartClean` reads the model's words into the same shape, and f483 pins every list equal (pictures, dates, measures, sorts, directions, comparisons, units, the top N and title limits, every group word).
- ONE planner (`hbCardPlan`) holds today's rules (`hbPlanFix` runs inside it) and the new ones: time always runs across; averages are never stacked (they go side by side); a value band or live contracts cannot be split again; a comparison draws columns or bars over a period (the last 12 months when none is named, said); the order and top N belong to ONE group split. Anything it cannot draw is listed in `P.dropped` and said under the chart ("Not drawn: …").
- ONE writer (`hbCardSet`): the dropdowns, the free reader (`hbCardEdit`) and Copilot. Before this, the shelf, a kept view's paint and the brief sync each seeded `s.recipe` by hand; they now call `hbCardSet(key, recipe, { seed: true })`, and the load path reads the 3 Oct `digView` switch through the cleaner instead of writing into `s.recipe`. f496 (C) counts one writer.
- ONE run (`hbChartRun`): the period cut, then the picture, then the notes. The card, its reading, the board described to Copilot (`hbBoardNow`, now in recipe words via `hbRecipeWords`) and the shelf all use it, so they can never disagree.
- New pictures: stacked columns, side-by-side columns, heat grid (`hbStackSvg`, `hbHeatSvg`), and the comparison (`hbCompareSvg`). Every bar, cell and segment is a door: `q2:<card>§t1§v1§t2§v2` (a token is a group field, `d.<unit>.<date>`, or `w` with cur/prev), and `qr:<card>§field§kept§mv` for the rest past a top N. Both read the card key from the END, because a card key can itself hold `§`. A dig under a card counts within its period (`hbWinCs`).
- Found while photographing: (1) the colour key's position was written after the door attributes, inside the `<title>`, so every label stacked at the same spot; (2) "this year compared to last year" held January–September against all of last year — a running period is now compared like for like (`hbWinOf` `soFar` cuts both at today's date) and says "so far" for this month/quarter/year; (3) "this year" made the follow-up reader think "this" meant the open chart — `HB_FU.refer` no longer takes "this" before month/quarter/year/week/period; (4) "top 3 counterparties" ranked by money while the chart counted contracts — the ring now ranks by the card's own measure.
- The dropdown row carries its card's key (`data-hb-rkey`): before, a press on a kept panel's row wrote to the open dig-in's recipe and opened the menu on both cards.
- The free reader learned: a second split ("by month and by stream", "by stream and stage", "then by"), stacked / side-by-side / heat-map words, "top 5 counterparties", "the 3 smallest streams", order words, periods ("last 12 months", "this quarter", "next 6 months" — an ending or renewal "in the next N" stays the map reader's set), comparisons ("compared to last year", "against the previous quarter") and a name ("… called Renewals watch"). "top 10 contracts by value" still goes to Copilot (the phrase book's own line).
- Red at main: f496 28 of 29; the browser check stops at "the one recipe language is not on this board".

## SEVERAL BUTTONS AT ONCE — COPILOT BUILDS THE BOARD (work order Part 2, built 4 Oct 2026 overnight)

The CopilotKit pattern: the copilot acts through the app's own controls. Before, Copilot on the board could fill ONE `chart` (target open/new). Now, asked on the board, `/api/ai/graph` hands the model `actions` instead — a list of the board's buttons: add_card {which, recipe, title}, change_card {card, recipe}, remove_card {card}, arrange {order, sizes}, name_card {card, title}, filter_board {which}. The route stayed the map's (one route, the tool's fields swap on `onBoard`), so the map side is unchanged and the older stubs still answer.

- ONE applier, `hbBoardApply`, presses them in order through the writer a press uses: `hbAddCard` (a kept view, `cd:<pid>`, holding its set in `which` — the whole book, the map's own reading of plain words, or ids — and its recipe through `hbCardSet`), `hbCardEdit`, `hbPanelAct` (the panel buttons, lifted out of hbOnClick so a press and Copilot share it), `hbCrumb` (the trail, likewise), `hbArrange`, `hbPanelName`, `hbDig`. f497 sweeps the applier's body for any write of its own.
- What it did is said one line each in HaTi's words, then Copilot's own sentence. What it cannot do is said and not done: an unknown step, a card not on the board, a ready-made panel (it keeps its picture and name), words that name no contracts, more than 12 steps.
- `hbBoardTakes` became a caller: an older `chart` answer is read as change_card "open", or add_card over the whole book (before, "new" replaced the open dig-in with an `ls` card; f483's line was re-pointed to the card).
- The board Copilot is shown (`hbBoardNow`) lists every card with its ref and recipe words; the open chart is ref "open". A card can also be named by its title.
- Found by the browser check: "build me a renewals dashboard" never reached Copilot — the free reader read "dashboard" as "back to the board". `HB_RX.build` (build/make/create/design … dashboard/board/cards/charts/overview) now hands it on. Cards added together are arranged in the order asked (the board otherwise draws the newest first).
- Photographed: with nine dropdowns a half-width card wrapped its row onto four lines and the chart shrank. The row now shows the first four, any newer part the card uses, and ONE "More (n)" (per sitting, `hbRcMoreToggle`). Copilot's cards say "Built by Copilot" where a kept view says "Kept view".
- Red at main: f497 12 of 12.

## DATA GUIDE (work order Part 3, built 4 Oct 2026 overnight)

So Copilot builds cards on fields that work: every board question now carries `screen.guide` beside `screen.board`. `hbDataGuide(lens)` writes one line per field a recipe can use — the stage split (live · drafting · signed), each date (end, signed, start, created, decision: "22 of 24 signed have one", first and last month), each group (streams, counterparties, owners, types, sides: how many groups, the top eight with their counts, "+n more", how many have none), value (filled count and range), and the measures (days to sign, payment days, rounds, the monthly live pictures). Every count is the board's own reading (hbDateOf, hbGroupsOf, hbMeasureOne, hbValueOfOne), so it cannot describe a different book.

- Walls: no amount for a reader without canViewValues ("Value: not shown to this reader — do not use measure value"); a stream outside visibleFolders is counted as "in streams this reader cannot open", never named.
- A cap is a fact: the browser stops at HB_GUIDE_MAX (3000) and says how many lines it left out; the server clamps at GRAPH_GUIDE_MAX (3200) and says the guide was cut, and adds one instruction — build cards on fields the guide shows as filled.
- Board only: off the board no guide travels and the server prints none.
- Red at main: f498 6 of 6.

## CHECK AND REPAIR (work order Part 4, built 4 Oct 2026 overnight)

The LIDA pattern: nothing wrong reaches the board quietly. ONE checker, `hbCardCheck(D, raw, spec)`, reads a card's recipe against the book and returns problems in plain words: no contracts ("no contracts could be found for …" when the words name nothing); nothing in the period; a picture or split that cannot be drawn as asked (a ring split by month — the planner quietly moved the split, so the asked split is compared too); parts the planner dropped; money this reader may not see; more than 25 groups with no top N; a date missing for more than half the set (the signing date is measured over signed contracts; a start date falls back to signing, as hbStartOf does — the test first expected 40 of 40 and the checker rightly said 34); a trend with fewer than six months that hold contracts; a word the cleaner dropped.

- Copilot's answer is checked before it is applied (`hbBoardTakesChecked`): the good actions apply; the bad go back to Copilot ONCE through the panel's own payload with the failing recipes and reasons (`hbRepairNote`); the retry costs one more call and the panel says "One retry ran: n cards went back to Copilot to be fixed"; what still fails (or never came back) is not applied and is said one line each ("Could not add “Starts by month”: the start date is missing for 20 of 20 contracts."). HaTi's lines come first, Copilot's sentence last. No band, no dialog.
- The free reader's cards go through the same checker: drawn as asked, no retry, and the answer adds "Drawn, but …".
- Red at main: f499 7 of 8; the browser check stops at "the board has no checker".

## PREVIEW AND UNDO (work order Part 5, built 4 Oct 2026 overnight)

A big build is the owner's choice, and any change can be taken back.

- Preview: an answer that would add two or more cards, or remove any, is offered as a list with ticks — "Add all" / "Add chosen" ("Do all" / "Do chosen" when a removal is in it) — and nothing is applied until pressed (`hbIsBig`, `hbBoardAnswer`, `hbPreviewPress`). The panel's message then becomes what was done ("2 were left out, as chosen") with Undo. A list is pressed once; an old one says "no longer open — ask again". One card, or a change to the open card, applies at once as before. No band, no dialog: the cheapest channel that carries the act.
- Found while building: the panel strips buttons and inputs from an answer's text (`IG_UNSAFE_TAGS`, its security wall), so the first version drew text with no buttons. The presses now ride as the message's own parts — `hbTakeMeta()` hands `preview` / `undo` to the message intelAsk pushes, and `igMsgHTML` draws them with `hbPreviewHtml` / `hbUndoHtml` (rows escaped).
- Undo: ONE store `s.undo` (the last ten board shapes — cards, trail, recipes) and ONE writer, `hbUndoMark`, inside `hbSave`, so every change is caught whatever made it — a press, the free reader or Copilot. Changes made in one go are one step (the step closes on a microtask; test/world.js runs timers at once, which first split one answer into five steps). An answer's Undo goes back to before that answer; Ctrl/⌘+Z on the board takes the last step, never inside a box being typed in. Kept on the person's own board record, so a refresh keeps it; the trim to ten is not said (it holds only their own views).
- Red at main: f500 8 of 8.

## CHOICES WHEN UNCLEAR (work order Part 6, built 4 Oct 2026 overnight)

The NL4DV pattern. Three known places where the free reader's words can mean more than one thing: "by month" with no date named (end · signed · created), "by value" (value bands · the contract value), and one word matching two or three counterparties ("Juno" → Juno Logistics Ltd, Juno Fresh AB). The work order said "two or three buttons instead of guessing"; the phrase book (the pass mark) and home-board-verify both expect "Show Juno contracts by month" to draw month columns by end date, so the board draws the likeliest reading AND SAYS IT ("Drawn by end date; you may have meant another date:"), with the other readings as presses — NL4DV's own ambiguity widgets do the same (show the default interpretation, offer the alternatives). Nothing is guessed silently.

- The presses are the map's own choice buttons (`m.choices`, drawn by igMsgHTML); a board choice carries `board` actions and its press goes through `hbChoicePress` → `hbBoardApply`, with Undo.
- Copilot may answer `choices` on the board (up to three, each a label and the board's actions; `graphBoardChoicesClean`); nothing is applied until one is pressed.
- A clear question offers none (pinned for four questions).
- Red at main: f501 11 of 11.

## HOME — THE BOARD AND THE MAP (js/views/homeboard.js)

- Desktop Home IS Explorer's page (`renderIntel` `onHome`; `renderDashboard` → `hbRender`); the PHONE keeps the old Home (`hmMapData`, `hmAgentsCardHtml`). Head `hbHeadHtml`: greeting · Board | Explorer (`data-hb-face`) · counting chip `hbCountChipHtml` (nothing at rest) · Present · the board's own Dark | Light (LITERAL `--hb-*`). `#hb-board` covers the map's stage; the map is built only on Explorer (`igMapUp`).
- Your book: six figures + stage bar (`hbBookData(lens)` = `hmDashSlices`, f447). PREPARED BY COPILOT (`hbPrepHtml`, `#hm-agents`): Copilot's rows (`hbAgentsData`) and the shelf, nothing else. WAITING ON YOU IS NOT ON HOME: the checklist (`needsYouOf`), the bell, the phone (`mNeedsYou`), off `hmDecisionItems`. Every number/bar/row is a door with a trail (`hbDigData`, `data-hb-dig`); a whole-book stage opens Contracts (`regGoFiltered`); what moved: one baseline a day (`hbSeenTick`, `hbMoved`).
- ASKING: `hbParse` (`HB_RX` en+sv) before Copilot, on the BOARD only. WHICH CONTRACTS = `igConditions` (field+hit; OR within, AND across; "my contracts" = `owner` by `contractOwnedBy`) → the `q:<question>` dig, re-read every paint; a list answered elsewhere lands on the board (`ls`, `hbShowFound`); "Show these on the map" narrows (`hbShowOnMap`). THE RECIPE `hbRecipeRead` (`HB_RC`; leftovers → Copilot, `_hbPendingRecipe`/`hbFoundChart`, server `graphChartClean`): which · split (date by `hbDateOf`, or a group) · picture `HB_PICS` · measure `HB_MEASURES` · trend (`hbTrendOf`). Dropdowns `hbRecipeRowHtml`/`hbRcOptions`/`hbRecipeSet` (`s.recipe`); live per month `hbLiveSvg` (`book_snapshots`); defaults ring · money blocks · attention bubbles (`HB_ATTENTION_RE`, "nobody owns" only); an axis never repeats a label (`hbAxisTop`).
- THE COUNT FOLLOWS THE QUESTION (`hbCountKey`/`hbRootKey`; `hbCounted` narrows Your book, panels, map; a door pressed while counting nests). THE BOARD ANSWERS THE QUESTION: signed is the STAGE (undated executed = "No date"; the not-yet-signed said with their money); a trend needs `HB_TREND_MIN_PTS` filled columns, ≥0, said as a line (`hbTrendFmt`); a default split must split (`hbUsefulGroup`); `valueLead`; a why-question is Copilot's (`HB_WHY_ASK_RE`), with the board (`hbBoardNow` → `screen.board` and the chat). "THIS" IS THE OPEN CHART: `hbFollowUp`/`HB_FU` (never "that"/"those"; the board's commands win) → `hbBoardEdit`; "only X" nests `qn:`. COPILOT PRESSES THE BOARD'S BUTTONS: server `boardJob`, `chart.target` open/new, word lists = the board's; `hbBoardTakes`; on the board the map's arranging reader stands aside (`boardUp`, `mapListy`).
- ASK COPILOT FROM THE BOARD puts the question READY in the panel (`hbAskInPanel` → `intelAskReady`), never `openAI`. Analyze (`data-hb-analyze`, `HB_RX.analyze`) → `hbAnalyze` → `igAnalyze`. ## A NEW CLAUSE IS HELD IN EDIT WITH COPILOT (Young chose to build it, 5 Oct 2026)

- The overnight work order stopped Part 8's screen 5, "A new clause": the clause editor was built around ONE clause already on the paper, and holding one that does not exist yet was a big change. The morning summary put the choice to the owner; Young answered "Build these" (option 1).
- HOW IT HOLDS A CLAUSE THAT DOES NOT EXIST: `rlOpenClauseEditor(c, null, { newClause: { afterClauseId, heading } })` sets `_ceNew` under a placeholder id (`CE_NEW_ID` = 'cl_ce_new'). `ceClause()` answers a placeholder clause (`ceNewClause`, `_ceProposed`), so every reading the page already has — the box, the heading box, the marks, the foot — works unchanged. The paper is drawn from a VIEW: `ceNewView()` is a shallow copy of the contract carrying the record's changes plus ONE unsaved insertion where the clause will go, so `redlineDocHtml`'s own insert block draws it in place with the typing box. The record is never written; f503 (D) pins it.
- No lock is taken on a clause that does not exist yet (`ceLockable`); the lock is taken the moment it is filed. The paper's step chip counted the unsaved insertion as "Step 1 · your ask · not sent", which is untrue before Save — `ceNewBadge` makes it read "new clause" (found in the photograph).
- THE FIRST SAVE is `ceFileNew` → `negoAddNamedClause` (the same add-a-clause door the standards use, with its duplicate wall; a refusal is said in the page). Then `_ceClauseId` becomes the real id, `ceSeedDraft` reads the record, and the page is on a clause we proposed — every later save is `negoReviseInsert`, as before. f245 (7) now allows exactly one `negoAddNamedClause(` call, inside `ceFileNew`.
- THE RISKS SIDE: `riskEditTarget` answers `{ newClause, afterClauseId, heading }` where no clause of the risk's topic is there — after `_rkLastTerm` (the last clause ahead of Signatures / Execution / Signed by / In witness), named from the risk. The Risks tab shows "Where it goes" (`_rkWhereHtml`: only places before the signatures, and "Never after 6. Signatures.") which moves the held clause on the paper (`ceSetNewPlace`). Copilot is asked with the new-clause prompt. The walk no longer skips such risks.
- THE CARD DRAFTS NOTHING NOW: `riskDraft`, `riskFile`, the open row, its target select and its handlers are removed; f484 (4) re-pointed ("the list files nothing itself"). `riskFiled` repaints the column so the row says "from the risk scan" at once (the old browser check measured it before the next repaint).
- Tests: f503 (16; the three new ones red at unmodified main), f245 (7) re-pointed, f484 (4) re-pointed, one-door-for-edits-verify (screen 5 driven: held in place, moved, saved as one insertion, "new clause" until saved), risks-in-the-redlines-card-verify sections 3, 4 and 6 re-pointed to the window.

## THE THREAD — THE DOCUMENT TAB'S ONE CARD FOR READING A CLAUSE (Young picked it 5 Oct 2026)

- THE ASK, over three rounds. First: *"I need to simplify the use of contract view, plain view and risk view. Imagine a view where all of them are in the same screen. Maybe for the plain view it should be at request per clause as opposed to whole contract which currently slows down the process when trying to translate an entire large contract."* Three options were drawn on the real Document tab (Facing · Marked · Ledger); the owner asked what became of the Checks card and the Activity & comments card, then asked that scrolling and ‹ › one-clause stepping never disagree and glide. Second round, on Facing: *"Is there better design approaches to facing that make it elegant maybe even the approach to the DNA strands? I also believe we should get rid of the image 1 features [the Checks card and Activity & comments] as they are essentially redundant."* Three more (Thread · Strand · Quiet). The go: *"Build Thread with Quiet's typography, merge to main once done. Start from the latest main noting that add note feature has been deleted from the worth a look panel."*
- WHAT WAS THERE. A three-position switch on the control row (Contract View · Plain View · Risk View, `docReadSwitchHtml`, `DOC_READ_KEY`, `docViewSet`/`docViewMode`), the Plain English column laid over the right column (`#doc-read`, a mirror of the paper pushed down entry by entry, with amber bars `docReadFlags`, the duty tick-box, wheel and touch forwarded to the paper), the X-ray panel (`#doc-xray`, `docXrayPaint`, the DNA strand `docXraySpineHtml` in the margin), and under them the Checks card (`renderChecksCard`, `checks-card`) and Activity & comments (`renderFeed`, `wireComments`). Three ways in to one job, and a whole-contract translation on every press of Plain View.
- WHAT IS BUILT. ONE card `#doc-thread` in the right column, drawn by `docThreadPaint` on the sheet's own funnel (`wireDocCanvas` after `docPaginate`, `applyWsTabs` on every tab change, the readings as they land; `docReadPaint`/`docReadOn` kept as its aliases so every other caller — the negotiate page's type stepper, the clause editor, js/ai.js, js/obligations.js, templatelib — presses the same name). Every clause a row (`docXrayRows`: label, words, share, marks, tone) with a bead in the worst mark's tone; the row's state says "N to look at" · "Read" · "Reading…" (`docThreadStates`).
- THE LINE. One line 24px below the paper's top (`DOC_THREAD_LINE`) decides the open row: `docThreadAtLine` measures live (the last row whose element has reached the line), never remembers. The paper's scroll opens the row at the line (`docThreadFollowArm`, passive, one answer per animation frame, off `_docThreadCache` — a scroll never re-walks the sheet). A press on a row or on ‹ › GLIDES the paper until that clause is at the line (`docThreadGoTo`: `scrollTo smooth`, instant under prefers-reduced-motion); the row opens at once so the page never waits; the scroll handler stands aside while the glide is in flight and `docThreadSettle` RECONCILES — what the line says is what the page says — except for a clause the paper cannot bring up to the line (the last ones on the sheet), which `_docThreadHold` keeps open until the reader's next scroll. Measured in a real browser: press row 0 from scroll 1013 → 253, line 0; › twice → row 2 at 766, line 2; ‹ → row 1, line 1. A plain press on a clause in the paper opens its row without moving the paper.

## RISKS TO LOOK AT — A RISK FINDS ITS CLAUSE, AND WHERE HaTi CANNOT TELL THE READER POINTS (Young, 5 Oct 2026)

- The owner, over a screenshot of Edit with Copilot's Risks tab on "Product standard not cited" (Risk 2 of 2, MEDIUM, "Where it goes: New clause after 4. Governing Law", and Copilot's red "Copilot could not draft this: … the selected wording passage is empty … I need to see what the quality clause currently says"): *"find a solution to this but do not fix. Just proposal for situations like this one"*. Three ideas were offered — "Find the clause", "Ask Copilot where", "You point" — with two small fixes; the recommendation was "Find the clause" first with "You point" behind it. Then: *"Build the recommendation and merge to main"*.
- THE FINDING: the risk is `rm-kebs` (js/ai.js, the raw-material template's rules), anchored to template clause `c3` ("Quality & Rejection"). About thirty such rules name a template clause by its tag; the tag is `data-anchor` on the template paper (`clause()` in docBody) and does not survive into the negotiation copy, which is built from the paper's TEXT (`negoBodyOf` → `docPlainText`). "Product standard" was none of Our standards' six kinds (payment, liability, law, conf, dp, term), so `riskEditTarget` found no clause and offered a new one after the last term. Copilot was then sent `passage: ''`, and `copilotPropose` still wrote "The selected wording is:" over an empty quote and "The passage comes from <label> and is ONE clause", so the model asked for the wording; `riskEditorDraft` printed its answer in red as a failure. Measured at unmodified main (a-risk-finds-its-clause-verify 1a/1b): "Product standard not cited" opened a new clause "Product Standard Not Cited" and Copilot was asked to "Draft ONE new contract clause".
- BUILT:
  - FIND THE CLAUSE: `templateClauseTitles(c)` (js/views/contract.js, beside docBody, published) reads `{ tag: title }` off the template's own paper — docBody on a copy with no stored wording, read only — so the paper the reader saw and the lookup cannot disagree. `riskEditTarget` asks, in order: the quote's clause (`rlPbFindClause`), the tag's clause (`_rkAnchorClause`, title matched by `_rkHeadNorm`, numbers and "&"/"and" ignored; a clause the negotiation renamed finds nothing, never a guess), then the topic's clause. `_rkOnClause` carries our own pending redline as before.
  - MORE TOPICS, FOR RISKS ONLY: `RK_TOPICS` (insurance · quality · warranty · delivery · ip) read in `_rkKind` only AFTER `clauseKind`, so Our standards' CLAUSE_KINDS and every standards reading are untouched. "specification" was left out of quality on purpose ("Supply & Specification" is not a quality clause). Side effect, by the existing rule: a redline of ours on an Insurance clause now COVERS an insurance risk (f503 (A)'s "no known topic" test re-pointed to "Audit rights").
  - YOU POINT: where no clause is found, a new clause is still offered where HaTi knows one is needed — the topic is known and has no clause, or the scan's kind is `missing` ("No injunctive-relief clause", the owner's 5 Oct choice). Anything else comes back `choose`: the window holds the place, the box reads "Which clause is this about?" with nothing chosen (`rk_choose_ph`), every clause to change (`chg:<id>`, `rk_change`) and every place for a new one (`rk_after`), never at or after the signatures; Copilot is not asked and the quick asks are grey until the reader chooses (`_rkWaiting`, `riskEditorArrive`, `riskChipsHtml`); a typed ask says "Choose the clause … first" (`rk_ce_pick_first`). `riskWherePick` opens the chosen clause (or holds/moves the new one) and asks Copilot once; the box keeps the choice so it can be changed. With no Copilot the waiting window says so at once (found by risks-in-the-redlines-card-verify 6a: "Assignment not restricted" became `choose` and said nothing until a choice).
  - COPILOT WROTE NOTHING: an answer with no wording is `_rk.say`, drawn as the quiet "Copilot could not draft this: …" with the way forward under it ("Choose the clause this is about above, or ask Copilot again below.", `rk_ce_refused_way`), not in red, and turns the box on with the clause in front selected. A thrown failure stays red.
  - THE REQUEST: `copilotPropose` with an empty passage (`fresh`) says "There is no existing wording: this is a NEW clause … do not ask for existing text to revise", and drops "The selected wording is:", the empty quote and the "passage comes from" line. With wording the request is unchanged (f98's tests and f509 (F)). This also serves a held new clause asked about from the editor's Suggestions tab.
- Noticed, not fixed (BUGLOG): the template paper's scan-flag tags ("Deviation", "Check", "High") are read into the negotiation copy's TEXT as the first line of a flagged clause (seen in the photographs: "3. Quality & Rejection / Deviation / Consignments…"), so they show on the paper, in the "Selected" card and in Copilot's suggestion.
- Tests: f509 (22; 17 red at unmodified main, the 4 green ones guard what must not change, 1 added after the browser run), f503 (A) re-pointed; a-risk-finds-its-clause-verify (21 checks, photographed; at main the guard reports "a risk cannot find its clause on this build", and driven past the guard 10 fail).

## THE THREAD — A DRAWER OVER FORM & LINKS (Young picked "Drawer", 5 Oct 2026)

THE OWNER'S REPORT, the same day the Thread shipped (three screenshots of "Kwetu - V2", MK-314, a credit application made from a template form): *"Image 1 and 2 show that the panels are breaking. Image 3, the plain english translator sometimes does not work. Finally, I want to have the opportunity to simply filter to the amber, blue or red clauses as opposed to going through all the clauses in the right side of the page."* Then, over five rounds of drawn options in the Thread Repair Options artifact (Tabs, One home, Drawer, Inline, Stack; Fold refused — *"I do not like the folding"*): *"The explain why button is supposed to be a button for converting the clause to plain english"*; *"a button that says plain which converts the clause to plain english"*; and the pick, *"when you land to documents page, form and links is the landing panel but you click on a button above which then brings you the clauses"* — *"Implement drawer and merge to main"*.

MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX (a staged copy of MK-314 at 1440 × 900):
- THE PANELS BROKE because the Thread build gave the right column's docs wrapper `flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0` so the Thread could fill it — and every card in that column carries `overflow:hidden`, whose automatic floor is ZERO. The form, 1107px of content, was drawn 136px tall with its own scroll bar inside a column with another, beside the Thread's rows with a third (and the open row's capped body a fourth).
- PLAIN STALLED because the readings prompt TOLD the model to return an EMPTY reading for "a cover page, a table of contents, … counterparts, severability", and the route kept every paired row, empty or not (D-1, 11 Sep), in clause_reading_rows with INSERT OR IGNORE. "3. Delivery Information" came back empty once; press 1 made one call, presses 2 and 3 made none (the table answered "nothing" for the life of the wording), and the row drew nothing and said nothing.

WHAT WAS BUILT:
- THE DRAWER. The docs column lost its flex (cards `flex:none`; the column is the one scroller); the provenance became a card of its own (`#doc-prov`) so the panel can be asked whether it holds anything (`docPanelHas`: the form, the provenance, the links card, the rounds card, `c.rounds`, the share cache, the share overview). A "Clauses · N to look at" door leads the tab row's slot (`#ws-th-door`, drawn shut by `wsTabRowEndHtml`, shown and counted by `docThreadDoorPaint`), and brings the Thread over the panel (`docThreadDrawerSet`; `#doc-right.is-clauses` hides the cards, the Thread takes the column, a short slide-in and a shadow say it is over something). It opens on the clause at the paper's line. × and Escape go back (Escape bound at load, so heard before focus mode's and stopping it — one key, one act — and never past a dialog, an open menu or from a box) and the hand returns to the door. ONE answer, `docThreadShowsClauses`, decided ONCE PER LANDING so a links card that fills a moment later never pulls the list out from under the reader: a refresh puts back what was open and which colours (`docThreadPlace`/`docThreadPlacePut` through roomPlace/roomPlacePut), a risk door opens it, anything else lands on Form & links. Landings: arriving on the tab (applyWsTabs), arriving in the room from another page (a line in setView). renderSharesSection tells the drawer when it fills (`docThreadPanelMoved`).
- THE DECISION NOT ASKED (said to the owner): a contract with no form, no link and no round has nothing for a drawer to cover, so there the clauses ARE the panel — no door, no × (the "One home" behaviour, for that case only).
- ONE SCROLLER. The open row's capped body (`--th-max`, `DOC_THREAD_BODY_MIN`) is gone: the row grows, the list scrolls, and only a CHANGE of open row brings its head into view (`_docThreadRevealed`), so a reading landing never yanks the list.
- A PART TITLE IS A LABEL: a section row draws as a small uppercase label (`.doc-th-sec`), no bead, no button, never opened; the line on it opens the shown clause it belongs with (`docThreadNearest`).
- THE COLOUR FILTER: All · Red (could hurt you) · Amber (worth a look) · Blue (worth knowing), any together, each counting the clauses whose WORST mark is its colour (so the list behind a chip is as long as its number); a colour nobody carries is greyed with "No clause is marked blue." unless pressed. While it filters, ‹ › and the paper's line step only through shown clauses (`docThreadVisible`), the meta line says "k of n shown", a hidden open clause gives way to the next shown and the paper glides there (`docThreadFilterSet`), part titles step aside.
- PLAIN: the button says Plain (`th_plain`), "All N clauses in plain English" beside it; `th_explain*` are inert in both books. The prompt's WHEN TO SAY NOTHING became EVERY CLAUSE GETS A READING (the tool's `plain` description too); an empty answer on a CLAUSE row is not landed or kept (`refuse(…, true)`, so the second pass asks again and a clause still empty counts as unmatched); a stored empty clause row is no answer (`readEmptyClauseDrop`); an edition holding one is never served whole (`readEditionHasEmptyClause`); and a real reading HEALS the stored empty row (`readRowsKeep`'s UPDATE … WHERE json LIKE '{"plain":""%' — "never rewritten" still holds for every real reading). REVERSED: D-1's "every paired row is kept, reading or not" now holds for SECTION rows only.
- A PRESS NEVER ENDS IN SILENCE: after Plain (or All) a clause still without a reading is marked for the sitting and the walk (`docThreadCannotMark`), its row says "Could not read" and the open row "Copilot could not read this clause. HaTi shows nothing rather than a reading it cannot place on this wording. Press Plain to ask again."

PROVED: at unmodified main f507 (6)–(10) fail every claim (20) and thread-drawer-verify fails 22 of 25 (the 3 that pass are controls: the contract does not move, a bare contract shows its clauses, no page errors) — including 1b, the form at 136px. After: f507 36/36, f277 120/120, f314 + f335 106/106, thread-drawer-verify 25/25 photographed light and dark, thread-verify 27/27, and the 22 browser checks that open the Document tab green. Re-pointed: f277 (1) (the slot is clauses+step+focus+door), (5) (every clause gets a reading — reversed), (6) (an empty answer is asked again, by itself), (10) (the open row grows — reversed); f314 (7), f335 (7) (no bounded scroller — reversed), (12); f507 (2) and (5); f278 (1) and f373 (7) (they pinned the follow's and the Plain press's old lines; both red at main as re-pointed). The full suite once: 11,528 tests, the only red f364 (5), which was red at main before this work (its own line in BUGLOG) and is untouched.

## HOME — THE BOARD AND THE MAP (js/views/homeboard.js)

- Desktop Home IS Explorer's page (`renderIntel` `onHome`; `renderDashboard` → `hbRender`); the PHONE keeps the old Home (`hmMapData`). Head `hbHeadHtml`: greeting · Board | Explorer · `hbCountChipHtml` · Present · the board's own Dark | Light (LITERAL `--hb-*`). Your book `hbBookData` = `hmDashSlices` (f447); PREPARED BY COPILOT `hbPrepHtml` (`hbAgentsData` + the shelf); WAITING ON YOU IS NOT ON HOME (`needsYouOf`, bell, `mNeedsYou`). Every number is a door (`hbDigData`, `data-hb-dig`); what moved `hbSeenTick`/`hbMoved`.
- ASKING: `hbParse` (`HB_RX` en+sv) before Copilot, board only; `igConditions` → `q:` dig re-read every paint; `ls`/`hbShowFound`; `hbShowOnMap`. "THIS" IS THE OPEN CHART: `hbFollowUp`/`HB_FU` → `hbBoardEdit`; "only X" nests `qn:`. THE COUNT FOLLOWS THE QUESTION (`hbCountKey`/`hbRootKey`/`hbCounted`). THE BOARD ANSWERS THE QUESTION: signed is the STAGE; trend needs `HB_TREND_MIN_PTS` (`hbTrendFmt`); `hbUsefulGroup`; `valueLead`; why → Copilot (`HB_WHY_ASK_RE`) with `hbBoardNow`. ## RISK CARD TITLES — THE CARD HOLDS ITS COLUMN, A BRIEF ITEM HAS A NAME, A CARD GOES TO ITS CLAUSE (Young, 5 Oct 2026; built overnight 5–6 Oct)

**THE ASK.** Two photographs of the Negotiate page's "Risks to look at" on Kwetu - V2: the cards ran off the Redlines column and severity, Why and Re-scan were pushed out of view. The plan (https://claude.ai/artifact/56Xp7U4BfQzNXgjLoPJgFW) found two faults together and the owner answered *"Build both fixes with your recommendations"*; the same day: *"For risks, where possible, when i click on a risk card it should take me to the clause being impacted just like in redline cards."*

**FAULT 1 — THE CARD TOOK ITS TITLE'S WIDTH.** `.rk-row` was `display:grid` with an automatic column, so the one-line title (`white-space:nowrap`) set the column's minimum width and the ellipsis never engaged. Measured on a Kwetu-shaped list at 1366 px: the list 427 px, every card 985 px, the column scrolling sideways 459 → 1005 px (risk-card-titles-verify reproduces it at unmodified main: 766 px cards, 327 px sideways). One rule, by scope: `.rk-row` and `.rk-ce-card` are `grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)`. The same rule covers the Covered and discarded rows, built the same way. "Re-scan" sitting 4 px past the edge is `.ui-link`'s hover wash, on purpose, left alone.

**FAULT 2 — A SENTENCE WAS THE TITLE.** Scan findings arrive named ("No data-protection terms detected"); the brief's watchouts and unusual terms arrived with a sentence only, and the card used it as the title, cut mid-thought. The brief now asks for `title` (`BRIEF_TITLE`, two to six words, required on both lists, one sentence in the prompt), the light list copy carries it (`briefLiteOf`), the readers carry it (`docXrayBriefWatch`/`docXrayBriefOdd`, '' when absent). `riskItemsOf` shows the title and keeps the sentence in `say`; THE KEY STAYS THE SENTENCE, so every discard, drafted mark and Risk View foot already stored keeps working. One reader of what a risk is ABOUT, `_rkTopicText`, keeps de-duplication, cover, Edit's lookup, the audit line and provenance on the sentence exactly as before — a short title loses nothing. The hover and the opened Why print the whole sentence. Decision 2: a brief written before this falls back (its sentence on one line ending "…") until it is read again — nothing is re-read on its own. Decision 3: the Document tab's Worth a look leads with the title in bold, the way scan marks lead with theirs (`_xrBriefMark`/`_xrOddMark` `lead`). The Explorer's Analyze strip reads a mark's lead first (`igStrandPoint`), so it now names brief items by their title too — one risk, one name.

**FIX 3 — A CARD GOES TO ITS CLAUSE.** The redline card's own press (`rlLinkFocus`): the clause to the middle, the card a faint 1px accent ring, no line on the paper (the owner's ruling earlier that day). The lookup at the top of `riskEditTarget` is split out as `riskClauseOf` — quote, then template tag, then topic ahead of the signatures — so the press and Edit can never disagree; asked at the press only (it reads `negoClauseList`). The door is the card's head (`.rk-head`, `data-rk-act="go"`, role=button, tabindex, Enter and Space), on open and covered rows; never the verbs, never the opened Why, never a discarded row, never a risk about something the contract does not say (`it.missing`). A covered row goes where its "Go to change" goes. With a quote, `scrollToQuote(it.quote, {root: clause})` brings the words into view and flashes them. Where HaTi cannot tell: `toast(rk_go_none, 'warn')`, both books — never a silent press. `data-rk-go`/`data-rk-target` stay stale.

**ON THE WAY.** f510 (D) pinned the brief's `required` list literally — re-pointed to allow `title` (its claim is that `wording` is required). one-door-for-edits-verify 1f/1g gathered "every risk button but Why", which now met the head door — re-pointed to exclude it (its claim is the three verbs). Tests: f522 (13 of 15 red at main; the two green are controls for old briefs), risk-card-titles-verify (12 red at main).

## COPILOT PANEL TIDY — PREPARED QUESTIONS, NEVER MORE THAN FOUR (Young, 5 Oct 2026; built overnight 5–6 Oct)

**THE ASK.** *"I believe the playbook scan tab is redundant since it is already addressed by the drafted redlines. The solution should be deleting the tab and keeping the use our standard, fall back and copilot as the prepared questions above the copilot entry field."* Then *"Also delete the Figure tab feature and the title name at the top of the panel that appears after copilot name … Plus ladder should be the last tab after risks."* Then *"prepared questions here or in risk should never be more than 4"*, and *"Go with the recommendations."* Plan and decisions: https://claude.ai/artifact/QDBjRfjDVfiAwNZJRYgWcc.

**WHAT WENT.** The Playbook scan tab (its count, its run button, its failure note, the Add buttons for missing standards, the preview's "more" control) and the Figure tab (the slider, the box, "Write it into the clause") — and the same Figure box in the Negotiate page's narrow clause panel (`rlFigureSecHtml`, `data-rl-fig-write`; `rlScaleHtml` stays for the Deal board). The clause name after "Copilot" in the rail head (`.ce-ah-cl`) — THIS REVERSES the owner's 21 Sep 2026 ruling ("it is not clear which clause copilot is working on"); the clause stays named in the top bar ("Edit …", `shellCrumbLayer`) and on the Selected card over the box. On their seat the rail head was always hidden (`#clause-editor.is-theirs .ce-rail > .ce-ah{display:none}`), so nothing changed for the other side: their clause is the one marked on the paper beside their Redlines column, and nothing was added to their page (no-new-bands rule). Tabs now read Suggestions · Risks · Ladder; Risks shows only where there are risks, so most clauses read Suggestions · Ladder.

**WHAT CAME.** One ordered list of eight prepared questions, the first four that apply drawn (`CE_CHIPS_MAX`): their ask (the work owed) · Use our standard · Use our fallback · Use Copilot's draft · the risk · softer (not on a deletion) · plain English · the playbook. The three standard ones are not questions to Copilot: `data-ce-std`, never `data-ce-chip`, so they never reach `ceAsk`. A press (`ceStdPress`) puts a "you" turn and a Suggested wording card in the thread through the ordinary card builder, badged Our standard / Our fallback / Copilot's draft (`ceWordingLabel`), with the reason (`pbVerdictWords`) and a quiet line saying what it changes (`ceCostLine`, `.ce-card .cost`, the label shade the scan cards used); each question carries the same cost on its hover. One wording reading (`ceStdWording`): "Use our standard" takes the smallest change where HaTi found the figure (the old "Use the smallest change", folded in), else `pbFitInto` puts the wording in the block the finding quoted, else the whole wording. **One call made without the owner:** where a clause departs from more than one standard, the questions act on the FIRST open one (`ceStdItem`), and the card's reason names it. The three questions do not appear on a contract never checked against the standards (the check stays on the Overview's Standards tile and the Negotiate page).

The dead `.ce-rule`/`.ce-scan-h` styles were left (f245 (13) still pins the quiet cost rule there) and the i18n keys of both tabs are inert in both books. ## HOME — THE BOARD AND THE MAP: CHARTS THAT EXPLAIN (5 Oct 2026, the overnight run)

**THE ASK.** Young: "review this artifact and build what is suggesting in totality as an overnight run and merge to main as well" — the doc "HaTi Board: Charts That Explain", eight recommendations ranked: new measures; a fact sheet and a safe summary; four answer packs; analyst mode with one Copilot; show the working; Summarise my board; chart what contracts say (key terms read once, the playbook check across the whole book overnight); test the new answers (the four questions and about twenty more in the precision book, the weekly run checking every number).

**WHAT WAS BUILT.**
- Part 1: measures `exposure` (value × worst open risk, high 1 · medium ½ · low ¼; unread left out and said), `avgValue`, `medianValue`; `show` running / share (only of a measure that adds up); the `standards` split (off · met · not checked); "act by" / "give notice" words read the renewal decision date (`renewalDecisionDate`, expiry minus notice) — the date existed, the words did not.
- Part 2: `hbFactSheet` in one fixed format (title, totals, HaTi's reading, the data lines, coverage "risks read on X of N (K not read); checked … (K never checked)", the contracts behind it); `hbSummaryPrompt`; `hbFactCheck` drops a sentence holding a number not on the sheet; both checks run (the old count check `hbWhyCheck`, then the sheet).
- Parts 3, 5, 6: `HB_PACKS` risks · ending · standards · next12, read FIRST on the board (`hbPackOfQ`), free, the same way every time: cards, a ranked list with a reason per row, "How HaTi worked this out" (`details.hb-how`), next questions, the summary press. `pk:name`, `pk:name.c1`, `pk:name.k:id` are doors ('.' inside, so '§' keeps its meaning). "Summarise my board" (`HB_BOARD_KEY = 'board:all'`) on the board's top line.
- Parts 4, 5: Dig deeper. Young's comment on the doc asked whether analyst mode should run by itself; it runs ON A PRESS (CLAUDE.md: Copilot spends only on a press, its cost beside it). The press rides under Copilot's board answer as `m.deeper` (the panel's `igSafeHtml` strips buttons inside a reply's text, so it is drawn beside Undo and the marks). POST /api/board/analyst is stateless: the browser carries the steps, the server replays them as tool_use / tool_result pairs, each re-cleaned; tools calculate · pack · finish; at most five, then finish is forced; 'deep' tier. Each step is the board's own arithmetic (`hbDdCalc` builds a list D with the cleaned recipe as its chart — a key in no store, so nothing is written — and reads it through `hbReadOfList`, lifted out of `hbReadSrc`). The run is a focus card `an:<id>` kept in `s.an` (three; one cut short by a refresh says so; its lines come back as words, never markup); its cards are OFFERED, one press adds them through `hbBoardApply`.
- Part 7: `runBookReading` (agent 'book', `AGENT_DEFAULTS.book = { on: false, … }`, not one of the page's agents — like 'board'), nightly by `bookReadingTick`. Key terms once per wording hash (`aiKeyTerms`, fast tier): a state that asserts something needs a quote that is IN the wording, else 'unclear' (`bookTermsClean`). An open contract with no check takes the verdicts as its ordinary playbook record (as the new-paper agent writes it); an EXECUTED one is never written — its check is kept beside it. Both live in `book_readings` and ride as `_book` (list: states and verdict statuses only, `bookLite`; single GET: the quotes, to a reader with the money). Splits `liabcap` · `autorenew` · `priceup`; `hbVerdictsOf` reads the record's check, else the overnight one. The switch sits in the Copilot's agents drawer — a fifth Copilot row broke f467's "four to a group" (the wall).
- Part 8: 24 requests in the book (141), `want.pack` judged by the pack that opened, `want.answer` by words; `numbersOutside` in server/boardjudge.js; `runBoardAccuracy` returns `numbers {answers, flagged, examples}`; the accuracy drawer says it.

"act by dates by month" was handed to Copilot because the conditions reader did not know "act by": the decision date's words are taken where the date split is made. The number check read "11 and 14, 25 in all" as one number "1425" and dropped a true sentence: a run is now its pieces (`hbNumPieces`, and the same in `numbersOutside`).

## HOME — THE BOARD AND THE MAP: THE ANALYST'S PHRASEBOOK (6 Oct 2026)

**THE ASK.** Young asked how HaTi answers "compare the value of our contracts between last 2 quarters" and "what is the trend growth of our contracts the last 12 months?" — both were handed to Copilot (one word each: "compare … between", "growth"). Then: "think like an analyst and all the formats and ways an analyst would ask questions when it comes to analyzing numbers … teach Hati. Be expansive as possible … Build now and then merge to main."

**MEASURED BEFORE.** 163 analyst questions in eleven families (period comparisons, growth, rolling and to-date periods, aggregates, rankings, distribution and share, cumulative, time to sign, renewals, risk and wording, combinations): 69 read free, and several of those WRONG ("median time to sign" drew the median contract value; "cumulative contract value" a pie of counts; "who are our biggest suppliers" narrowed the whole board to suppliers; "contract value this year vs last year" counted by the CREATED date).

**HOW.** One rewrite pass, `hbAnalystWords` over `HB_ANALYST_WORDS`, between the company's words (`hbWordsApply`) and the reader (`hbParse`), so the one reader answers both and the preview line says the same. Rules are plain rewrites into words the reader already reads; nothing counts. Copilot is still sent the words as typed (intelAsk keeps its own `q`). A card's name ("… called X") is set aside and put back. Case is kept; every rule reads case-blind.
- DATE: a comparison or growth question with no date of its own reads the SIGNING date (the placeholder `\u0001` becomes "signed"); unsigned sets (pipeline, drafts, in review) read the CREATED date; a date the question names wins.
- PERIODS: "last quarter/month/year" with no number is the WHOLE previous period (`_hbAwPrevRange`), not the one in progress (the reader's own "last 1 quarter" still means this quarter; nothing in the book used the bare form). Q2 2026, H1, "January to March", "in March 2026" become exact ranges, read by a new `HB_RC.winRange`. QoQ / MoM / "between the last 2 quarters" / "change from last quarter" compare the last two COMPLETE periods; "this quarter vs last quarter" stays like-for-like so far (`hbWinOf`'s soFar). `hbWinOf` now holds an exact whole month/quarter/year against the whole one before (it used the same number of days, so Q3 was held against 31 Mar–30 Jun).
- FOUND ON THE WAY: "Q2" in capitals was read as quarter 0 (the helpers lower-case now); the Swedish "trend" rule ate the English "remove the trend" (narrowed to "trenden"/"trend för").

**MEASURED AFTER.** 159 of 163 free (the four left are lists of single contracts: "top 10 contracts by value", "biggest contracts", "largest contract" are the map's own reader's on the board, free; "smallest contracts" goes to Copilot); a second wave of 131 other wordings (casual, CFO, combinations, Swedish): 131 free. The precision book: 141 → 201 requests, 201/201 (f502's bound 150 → 240).

**DECIDED WITHOUT ASKING (the owner said "build now").** "Value of our contracts" in a period comparison means SIGNED in that period (offered to the owner as the recommendation the turn before). "Median time to sign" draws the AVERAGE time to sign — the board has no median of days; the reply says what is drawn.

## THE MISSING CALCULATIONS (6 Oct 2026)

Young asked "Can copilot build the charts or comparisons for all these questions?" over the analyst's question list, and the answer named three things neither HaTi nor Copilot could count: a median time to sign (the phrasebook read "median time to sign" as the AVERAGE, said nowhere), two periods that are not next to each other ("Q1 2025 vs Q3 2026" drew six quarters side by side with no change said), and a ranked list of the smallest contracts (the map's reader knew only the top). Young: "Add the missing calculations and merge to main".

- MEDIAN DAYS TO SIGN: a measure of its own, `medianDaysToSign`, in HB_MEASURES and GRAPH_CHART_MEASURES (f483 keeps them equal). Every place that treated `daysToSign` as "the signing measure" (the signed date, the trend's faster/slower, the unsigned said apart, the ambiguity offer) now asks `hbSignM(m)`. The median shares `hbMeasure`'s middle-one arithmetic with medianValue. The phrasebook rule that mapped the median to the average now says "median time to sign".
- ANY TWO PERIODS: compare gains `range`; the other period rides INSIDE the window (`window.vs {from,to}`), so every recipe list that carries `window` carries it untouched (hbCardClean, the server's graphChartClean, the pending recipe, the next questions, the kept board). `hbWinOf` holds the window against `vs`; over time the columns pair up `hbBucketGap` buckets back. A range with no other period is dropped and said. The press menu offers "Against another period" only on a card that already has one (a press cannot name the dates). The phrasebook's two-quarter, two-half, two-year and new two-month rules go through `_hbAwTwo`: two periods that touch stay side by side, as before (f531 pins "Q4 2025 vs Q1 2026"); otherwise the LATER period is the card and the earlier the comparison, so the change reads forward in time. A period held against another is named as an analyst names it (`hbPeriodWord`: "Q3 2026", "Mar 2026", "2026", else two days WITH years) on the chip, the legend, the reading and the reply — never lower-cased.
- THE SMALLEST CONTRACTS: the map's top N read from the other end — `smallest`, `lowest`, `least valuable`, `bottom`, `minsta`, `lägsta` — as `top.dir:'up'`, only by value (a payment, obligation or renewal question is not a smallest list). `igTopIds` takes `dir`; a contract with no value on record is in neither end. On the board the list arrives as the List picture ordered smallest first (`listChart`), from the free reader and from Copilot's `top.dir`. "Biggest contracts" is unchanged.
- Measured: the three in a real browser on Home with the AI routes blocked — all answered free; the one AI call seen was the usage read. f532 is red on unmodified main except its guard that touching periods stay side by side.

A story is a focus card `sy:<topic>`; its four chapters are ordinary chart cards (`sy:<topic>.c1…`) or, for "which clauses get redlined", the friction tab's own ledger (`intelFrictionStats({days:365}).clauses`, which now also carries each clause's contract ids so the bar is a door — additive, nothing that read it before reads differently).
- THE WORDS: asking for the story is the press that spends ONE Copilot call (the proposal's "one call"); the prompt is every chapter's fact sheet (`hbStorySheet`, each cut at `HB_STORY_CH_SHEET`), the reply a fixed shape (LEAD / C1…C4, `hbStoryParse` reads past bold and dashes), each piece checked by `hbFactCheck`; the count left out is said in the foot. The words are kept for the day in `s.sy` with the numbers' `sig`; when the book moves the card says "The numbers have moved since this was written" with Write it again. The run stays on the story (`hbStoryDeeperSet`), is kept while the story keeps it (`hbDdKeep` and the refresh both skip it when trimming), and its deeper chapters are cards counted again from the step's own calculation (`sy:<t>.dK`, `hbStoryDeepD`). ## HOME — RISK EXPOSURE OVER TIME DRAWS (6 Oct 2026, Young: "Fix the risk exposure crash and merge to main")

Found while building the seven story topics (#147): asking the board "risk exposure by month signed over the last 12 months" threw inside `hbReadingCore`. The column chart's renderer `hbColsSvg` hands the reading COPIES of its columns (`cols`, `edges`: b, y, n, k, dig) and keeps the measured object `M` to itself; the exposure branch of the reading then asked `c.M.left` on those copies — on every column, so any exposure-over-time card threw, not only one with edge columns. ## THE THREAD — PLAIN READS ONE CLAUSE, ONLY, AND SAYS WHY; THE OPEN CLAUSE RISES (Young, 6 Oct 2026)

Young, over "3.4 Termination for Change of Control. · 1 to look at · Could not read": *"Hati keeps having a hard time translating a clause to plain english. Review why that is. Also, there should never be an option to translate all clauses so please delete."* Then, over "5.9 Interests on late payments." opened low in the drawer: *"the translation is supposed to be one clause at a time only … when i click on the next topic, it should go to the top pushing all the ones before it up the scroll so it is then the first one. Add these to a work order"* — and *"Go, build all three parts"*. Work order: docs/WORKORDER-plain-one-clause-and-the-list-glides.md.

MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX: Plain already sent ONE clause, but the route judged the model's copy of its heading against EVERY heading in the contract (`readEchoJudge(r.heading, list, i)`), and `readEchoScore` divides shared words by the SHORTER heading — so a short heading whose words all sit inside the copy ("1.5 Change of Control") scores a perfect 1.0. An exact copy passed; one word off ("on" for "for", "upon a") lost to the short heading, was called a shift, refused, asked again, refused again, and the row said "Could not read" press after press. f536 (A) reproduces it at the parent (two calls, nothing landed). The row's one sentence ("HaTi shows nothing rather than a reading it cannot place") said the same thing whatever happened, and the press's tidy-up marked the row even when the press had returned early without asking.

WHAT WAS BUILT:
- ONE CLAUSE ASKED, ONE ANSWERED: a page of one row (`solo`) pairs its answer by being the answer — the key and the echo no longer decide; a page of several (none is asked any more) is judged among its OWN rows (`readEchoJudge(r.heading, pg.rows, k)`), never the whole contract.
- NEVER THE WHOLE CONTRACT: "All N clauses in plain English" (`data-th-explain-all`, `.doc-th-all`, `th_plain_all*` inert in both books) is gone; `docReadRun` makes no press that names no clause or several; the ROUTE refuses one (400, `oneClause`, after the scope and empty-wording answers). Nothing else in HaTi called the readings route.
- A PRESS WHOSE CLAUSE NEVER GOT AN ANSWER FAILS (502 with the provider's reason), even where other clauses were read before — it used to come back 200 and say nothing of why.
- WHY IT COULD NOT: `docReadRun(c,{only,out})` raises `out.asked` only past every early return and sets `out.why` (`docReadWhyOf`: empty · noai · limit · failed); the drawer marks the row only after a real ask, with the reason (`DOC_THREAD_WHY` → `th_cannot_empty|noai|limit|failed`; `th_cannot_say` inert). The pop-up stands down for a row that says it (the pop-up diet); the 429 toast the api layer raises itself still shows.
- THE OPEN CLAUSE RISES: `docThreadFill` used to move the list only when the row was out of sight (`top > scrollTop + clientHeight - 120`, then 40px below the top). Every change of open row now glides the list until that row's head is the first thing under the drawer's head, as high as the list allows (scrollTo clamps; nothing padded). A reading landing in the same row still moves nothing (`_docThreadRevealed`). The paper's own glide is untouched. The phone does not draw the Thread (below 1024 it stands down — thread-verify 6a).

SIX QUESTIONS that changed what was built: (2) the cheapest channel — the reason went INTO the existing sentence on the open row, no new band, and the toast stood down for it; (5) one door — Plain stays the only press.

RE-POINTED IN PLACE (each says "RE-POINTED 6 Oct 2026"): f277 (6) the route — one clause per claim, a new refusal claim and the owner's reworded-echo claim; f300 rewritten to the one-clause world, the shift/quarter claims RETIRED with a proof (R); f315 any clause of a 130-clause contract, the multi-page claims retired; f367 (2) driven; f369 (6); f373 (1–7) one clause, the job joined; f507 (3)(8) and its words list; thread-verify 1e + new 8a–8e; thread-drawer-verify 4a; reading-in-the-background-verify rewritten to one clause's press; five-screenshots-verify 5d reads three clauses one at a time.

PROVED: f536 — 9 of 9 red at unmodified main; thread-verify 27/32 at main (8a–8d and 1e red; 8e is a control: the last row cannot rise), 32/32 after.

## EXPLORER — FOLD IN EVERY VIEW (CELL BUBBLES) (6 Oct 2026)

Young: "fold all only works in the brain and wiring tabs but it should work across all of them." Young picked CELL BUBBLES by name from the mock-up.

Why it did nothing: every fold was multiplied by `igbCardW(w) = max(0, 1 - w[2] - w[3] - w[4])`, the weight of the views that draw cards, so on Floors, Grid and Timeline the hub fold, the bubble and the card glow all came to zero. Only the button's words changed.

What was built:
- `igbAxes` gives every contract a cell per axis view (`n._cell`): the floors' and grid's column × floor, and the timeline's lane × the timeline's OWN tick stretch (`tStep`, the same month/quarter/year the ticks use — never a second bucketing). The no-date strip is one cell per lane.
- `G.cellsBy[v]` holds one entry per group × cell, with where the bubble sits: the middle of its own dots on Floors and Timeline, the cell middle (a little under the cell's own count) on the Grid. A bubble is capped to its cell, or to its lane on the Timeline.
- `igbStep` eases each contract's per-view fold (`n.cf`) with Brain's own easing (reduced motion jumps). `igbShade` takes the axis views' fold from it. Brain and Wiring keep `igbCardW` exactly.
- `igbDrawCells` paints each bubble in the group's colour, sized like Brain's (`igCellRadius` against the biggest group, by count or by value), with its count inside. `igBubDoors` makes each one a press target (touch-sized on a finger) that opens THAT bubble only (`igCellOpen` → `intel.cellOpen`).
- ONE fold store: `intel.folds`, written by `igFoldHub`, which also forgets a group's opened cells whenever the group is folded or opened again. Fold all asks `igAllFolded` for the view on screen. A walk-through reaching a folded cell opens that cell.
- Copilot's words, read free in `igLookRead` before any call: "fold everything" / "open everything", "fold <group>", "open <group>", "fold only <group>", in both books. Every fold goes through `igFoldHub`. The reply is counted after the rebuild (`igFoldSaid`): "Folded X on Floors: 4 bubbles holding 31 contracts." An unknown group is said with the groups that exist. `IG_CLAIM_RE` now also catches "unfolded", "collapsed", "opened up" and the Swedish "fällt ihop".
- `BRAIN_PARTS` names it `cellfold` (igbDrawCells) in the ask flow beside the Explorer.

Tests: f539 (cells per view add up to the book; Fold all, one press, kept across views; Brain/Wiring unchanged; every phrase acts and its reply's numbers match the drawn bubbles; both books; the walk). fold-every-view-verify (22 checks, real presses, painted pixels, 1500 and 1024 wide).

## THE FORM FILLS THE DOCUMENT ON A PRESS, AND PROGRESS RINGS (7 Oct 2026)

Young, over two screenshots: *"Implement progress ring. Also, add the button in image 1 to the bottom of the panel in image 2 so that once someone has filled out a form they need to press this button so that the platform fills in the document. All add the color to the button both in the cover tab and document tab. also, when moving from one entry field to the next, make it one press to get into the next entry field as currently i have to do it twice."* Answers: "Fill the document" and "Light blue".

- THE DOUBLE CLICK, MEASURED: `tplFormCommit` regenerated the wording and repainted the whole panel on every `change`; `change` fires on blur, so the click on the next box blurred the first, the panel was rebuilt and the box under the pointer was thrown away. Now the commit writes only the form and patches the count and the field's error line in place (`tplFormPaintRow`). A file/image field still redraws (its row shows what it holds). The built-in template's blanks panel (`wireBlankForm`) was already patched in place and was one press already — measured, left alone.
- THE PRESS: `tplFormApply` is the panel's one writer of a form's wording; `form.filledSig` remembers the answers the wording last carried. Owed (`tplFormPending`) = answers moved since AND the wording they would make differs from the stored wording — so a regeneration elsewhere (repair on open, a counterparty's response, the portal) never leaves a false "owed". The in-paper popover is a door IN the document, so it fills as it closes. REVERSES f106's "value lands, wording regenerates".
- A FORGOTTEN PRESS NEVER TRAVELS: `linkRefusal` returns kind `form` for every link carrying wording (sign · negotiate · view · history), and `signBlockers` adds `form-fill`. Kept out of LINK_ASKS on purpose: the server cannot know a press is owed, and it walls nobody out — it is the sender's own unfinished step with its way forward in the sentence.
- LIGHT BLUE: `.ui-btn.hati-fill-btn` (accent-50 wash, `--accent-ink`, accent-100 edge) on the Overview's `#kt-fill` and the panel's button. Read the brief stays the one filled button.
- PROGRESS RINGS: `ovMapSvg` redrawn on an 880×380 stage (400×600 stacked), two parties side by side, more below with lanes bowing above; each party a tinted circle with a ring of its duties in state colours (`ovMapRingSegs`, grouped by state past `OV_MAP_RING_EACH`), a key over the map. Card measured 429px with the panel at 429px at 1440. f442 (4) re-pointed.
