The work order is WORKORDER-signing-amendments-playbook.md (O-1..O-42, decisions D1–D10 all taken as recommended).

## SIGNING — ONE LIST BEFORE THE SIGNATURE (signing with the other side)
Reported off screenshots of the counterparty's signing: comments typed at signing went nowhere visible, the signature never appeared on the paper, the title box emptied, a refresh read "read-only, ask for a fresh link", Sign stayed live while a point was still open and while the order said wait. Built: the share route returns the live signatures (also on a dormant link) so the page paints them as marks after the render (`pagesSignMarks`), never inside the paper's HTML, because the paper's HTML is fingerprinted; the respond route refuses a signature while an owner's ask that was in the payload is still open (409, `srvSignOpenAsks`); the Sign button greys with the reason (`portalSignHold`); the comment box was removed (D1) and the reason box lives in "Something else"; the page ends on a receipt.

## AN AMENDMENT IS WRITTEN HERE (creating one)
Gaps A1–A10: an amendment could be started on a draft; the dialog asked for a name and nothing else; nothing said which clauses changed; the value and end date never followed a signed amendment. Built: Create only on an executed agreement; a dialog that asks what should change and offers blank or Copilot (D2, quotes checked against the signed wording, dropped ones counted); one numbered item per change remembered as `c.amends`; the proposed facts kept as suggestions to confirm, never applied by themselves; the deal as amended read live (D3) on the list and the Overview; an "As amended" view on the Document tab (D4). Found on the way and fixed in the same work: the "change the wording directly" link went to a tab key that does not exist.

## THE NINE FLOW RULES (8 Oct 2026)

Young asked, after the process review was re-walked over the merge "Copilot prepares, you press": *"if I wanted to build rules based on one seamless flow that makes all the flows green, what would be the rules?"* — and then: *"i need one more rule which is for every change the brain should be updated accordingly"*, *"both, then merge once CI is green"*.

The eight rules are the lessons of the 4 Oct process review (sixteen findings, six gaps) written as tests a change must pass: one fact one home (the address book, the ask record); one way to do each thing; every hand-off tracked until answered; every step starts the next; the check is on the server; tell the right person once where they look; Copilot prepares and a person decides; every act leaves a record the server writes. On 8 Oct four of them were broken by the new merge and are on the review page as recommendations 1–4: "Send for review" is an email only (rule 3), the "Sent to a colleague" History line is written by the browser (rule 8), the link agent starts on "Just do it" (rule 7), approvals waiting on you are back on Home (rule 6).

Rule 9 existed as a sentence under THE BRAIN ("a new feature is named in BRAIN_PARTS and put in a flow") and the 8 Oct merge still landed js/copilotacts.js, POST /api/contracts/:id/pass and seven new acts with none named. So it became a test: f561 reads the code and fails on a new file with no named part, a new js/ file with no area, a new route not named, or a part in no flow. What was uncovered on 8 Oct (69 files without a part, 32 without an area, 173 routes, 6 parts in no flow) is test/brain-known.json, which may only shrink: an entry that gets named must come off it. At the parent f561 fails on js/copilotacts.js and the pass route. The same change named the merge's ten parts (copilotask, draftcard, paperjobs, papermark, homepaper, citedoor, passroute, agentlevel, linkkeep, readings), each joined to an existing flow step, and put js/copilotacts.js in the AI area.

## THE NINE FLOW RULES — RULES 3 AND 8 MENDED, AND THE FOUR RED CHECKS (8 Oct 2026)

Young: *"fix the two broken rules and the 4 browser test issues, then merge"*.

RULE 3 (every hand-off is tracked until answered) and RULE 8 (every act leaves a record the server writes) were broken by Copilot's Send card: "Send #MK to @Jane" was an email only, and its History line was written by the browser after the send. Now POST /api/contracts/:id/pass opens a `look` question on the one ask record (js/asks.js gains the fifth kind, `look`, with no older field to mirror) and writes the trail line itself on the STORED record, the srvShareExtend way (no version bump; the save merges both back). It does both even when the colleague has no email address, because the hand-off reaches them in HaTi. The colleague sees it in the side checklist (`needsYouOf` kind `look`, verb Done → `lookDone` → `askAnswer` + save), the bell (`look`) and the phone (`mNeedsYou`). srvAsksMerge lets only the person asked answer it; no ordinary save may file one. The answering save writes "Looked at it" on the server (`srvLooksDone`) and mails whoever asked (`lookTell 'done'`). One still open after SA_REMIND_WORKDAYS working days is reminded once (`runLookReminders`, on the sign-approval sweep). f562 is red at 85c0ad0 (9 of 10); a-pass-is-a-hand-off-verify drives it as the colleague.

THE FOUR RED CHECKS. nine-jobs 2/3/3b and owners-fifteen 13b/d/e were tests left behind by deliberate redesigns: the Constellation Overview (party rows at rest are `.ov-pty`; the people list opens with the ONE Edit), and Paper as Home's own side (`hbAnalyze` lands on face `paper`). share-recipient 4 was a REAL regression: the Constellation had moved the record's rows behind "Filing and stream", so a signing route naming another address than the contact row was quiet at rest — the 16 Sep rule says it may never be. It is now said on the outside party's own row (`data-ov-route`). fill-the-document 4 was a REAL defect that only a slow machine showed: the form panel's listeners were bound to the contract object as drawn; when the full record landed afterwards and replaced it in state, "Fill the document" wrote to a copy nobody keeps. The listeners now act on `getContract(c.id)` at the press, and the check stages the late record every run (red before the fix).
FILL-THE-DOCUMENT, CONTINUED (8 Oct 2026). The live-record fix was right but not the CI cause. The check was taught to say what the press met: on CI the button was on top, enabled and pressed without error, both answers were committed, and the paper was never filled — the click itself was dropped. Leaving the box for the button commits the answer and repaints the button's insides between mouse-down and mouse-up; CI's browser (Playwright's own Chromium, not the container's) dropped the click. Not reproducible here even pressing on the icon. Fixed at the root: Fill does its act on POINTERDOWN, committing the box still being typed in through the same writer first; the click that follows is let go (a keyboard press still arrives as a click); and the button's insides are rewritten only when its words change.

## THE LINK AGENT ASKS FIRST, AND THE WAY TO COPILOT IS A DOOR YOU CAN SEE (8 Oct 2026)

Young: *"set the link agent to Ask me first. Also, when in this view in image 1, there is no clear door to going to the view in image 2. Fix this."* Image 1 was an enlarged Board card ("What this shows", the chart full width); image 2 the same Board with the Copilot panel open beside it.

THE LINK AGENT: `AGENT_DEFAULTS.link.level` was 'auto' (Just do it) — Copilot kept the other side's links open by itself out of the box. Now every agent starts at Ask me first; Just do it is still OFFERED for keeping links (AGENT_AUTO_OK), never assumed. f560 2a pins the default; 3a now chooses Just do it before driving it. The nine flow rules' rule 7 ("starting at Ask me first") is now true of every agent.

THE DOOR: two faults. (1) `.hb-dig-big #ig-dock{display:none}` hid the whole panel, door and all, while a card was enlarged — "the dock steps aside, as it does in Present, and comes back on the same button" meant the reader had to know to make the card smaller first. (2) Folded, the door was a 46px strip with a 16px gold mark and "Copilot panel" in 9px faint monospace written sideways — not read as a door. Now the enlarged card FOLDS the panel to its door (`igDockStepAside`, which remembers an open panel and opens it again when the card is made small), and the door is a tinted button (`.igd-door`: accent wash, accent mark, "Ask Copilot" at 12px, 600, top to bottom) at the same 46px, so the board does not move. Pressing it presses the card's own "Make smaller" first and opens the panel with its ask box — image 2. copilot-door-verify drives all of it (red at the parent on 1, 1b and 2); read-then-ask-verify 2b now expects the door, not a hidden panel. Present still sets the panel aside; not asked.

## AN AMENDMENT IS WRITTEN HERE — ITS BLANKS, ITS CLAUSES, ITS STANDARDS (8 Oct 2026)

Young, off MK-449 (Amendment No. 1 to a Mutual NDA, Drafting, Document tab): *"when you are creating amendments and so forth, you will have fields that need to be updated. In a draft contract, usually there is a field on the right panel that appears for you to fill in. That needs to happen for amendment process as well … Also, this amendment was found to have 4 risks but they are not appearing on the side panel either."* Then, with a Signing-tab screenshot: *"When narrowing the panel, wrap the words so they do not disappear on the sides."* Reviewed first without code ("Review but do not code yet"), then "Build and start from the latest main".

WHAT WAS FOUND. (1) The amendment's paper is wording written once (`amendmentSkeletonBody`), so `contractHasBlanks` refused it on `c.redlineText`, and the upload reader (which does read ruled lines) refuses everything that is not an upload — the "made on ____________" date had no box anywhere. (2) The side panel's clause walk (`docReadSheet`) takes headings and DOTTED paragraph numbers only ("1." is refused on purpose, 10 Sep); the amendment has no headings and numbers its changes "1. Term." — zero rows, "Nothing on this page reads as a clause", and every risk (placed by its quote on a row) had nowhere to land. (3) The head's "Read · 7 to look at" was 4 risks + 3 standards "not in this document" — an amendment checked against the full NDA's standards. (4) `.ui-link` is on the "words never wrap" list, and the Signing tab's "Signing it their way …? Hand it over instead" is a sentence: it ran off both edges.

WHAT WAS BUILT. (1) A third blanks reading in js/blanks.js, for HaTi-written amendment paper only: ruled lines are keyed `own_N` in one walk shared by read, paint and write; answering one writes the answer INTO the wording as the keyed span a company standard's answered blank already is (both on the rich sanitiser's allow-list), because this is OUR paper and the answer must be signed — the upload's "working note" model would have kept the date off the document. Live only while nothing is on the table (no change filed, no round, no fingerprint — negoFreshenBaseline's own guards, read RAW), so a measured baseline never moves; past that the wording changes in Negotiate. Not a signing hold: once the paper leaves Draft the panel stands down, and a hold whose way forward is a panel nobody can open is a door onto nothing (said to the owner). A date-shaped blank ("… made on") is a date box and is printed the way the paper writes dates (fmtDocDate). (2) `docReadOwnPaper(c)`: on amendment paper every paragraph is a part; a bold "N." lead is its number; an untitled paragraph is named by its own first words. Uploaded paper is untouched. (3) A document filed under an agreement (parentId + relation) is never "missing" a standard — `na` with `inParent`, said "Doesn't apply here · it is in the agreement this amends"; a deviation still counts. Applied in runPlaybookReview's stamp (every browser writer goes through it) and at the four server writers. A check already stored before this keeps its old verdicts until it is run again. (4) `.ui-link.ui-link-say` wraps and centres; f386's wall names it as the one exception.

Proved against unmodified main in a worktree: 10 of 12 checks in amendment-blanks-and-clauses-verify fail there.
